## The artist pictures' relay (2.1.32)

Phase 8's server change B (notes/ios-specs/phase8-managing.md on `ios`, sections 4 and 12, decision 1): the app's
Artist images (slice 5) draws the candidates `POST /library/artist/images/preview` offers, and their `preview`s are on
other hosts - the web's ArtistPanel loads `candidate.preview` straight into an `<img>`. The app talks only to deadwax,
so deadwax passes them on. The web doesn't change.

- **The route**: `GET /deadwax/library/artist/picture?url=`, Edit albums' like the preview that names those
  addresses (`dependencies=EDIT` on the library router, which is included with `current_user` - never middleware;
  tests/test_logins.py ROUTES, "edit"). `url` is required, at most PICTURE_URL_MAX (2048) characters (422 otherwise).
  Answers: 200 with the picture as `served_image_type()` names it - and refused unless that is one of
  SERVED_IMAGE_TYPES (jpeg, png, gif, webp, bmp: never an SVG) - with `Cache-Control: private, max-age=604800` (a
  week: fanart.tv's and TheAudioDB's addresses carry the upload's own id, Commons' the file's title); 400 for an
  address the relay won't ask, before anything is asked; 404 when the host has no such picture (a 404 or a 410
  anywhere in the chain); 502 when it couldn't be had; 503 when PICTURES_PENDING_MAX asks are under way already,
  nothing asked; 504 when the host was too slow. Every refusal `no-store`, its `detail` one of routes/library.py
  PICTURE_WORDS - the phone draws the words either way. A 502 has two sets of words (the review's): "deadwax couldn't
  get that picture just now." when the host is away or in trouble, or deadwax faulted - worth asking again - and
  PICTURE_REFUSED_WORDS, "That picture's site won't let deadwax pass it on.", for a PictureRefused - a 403
  (Wikimedia's robot policy), a redirect elsewhere, not an image, too big - which asking again won't change. No ETag:
  nothing is kept to make one from cheaply. Under GuardMedia's headers and never gzipped: the path is in app.py
  MEDIA_PATHS (an exact path - the existing guard applied to one more route, no rule changed). FastAPI's own 401, 403
  (NEEDS' words) and 422 are as every route's.
- **With logins off** (the review's): anyone on the network is the implicit admin, so any page a browser on it opens
  can make deadwax fetch these pictures; the same-origin Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy GuardMedia sends stops that
  page reading what comes back. That is the cover relay's position too, and it stays: the fetch is of the five hosts
  alone, and the caps bound it.
- **The fetch** (src/api/artist_images_endpoint.py `ArtistPictures`, `artist_pictures`; closed with the app): its own
  httpx client beside ArtistImagesClient, `follow_redirects=False`. **Not a general proxy**: `picture_address()`
  parses the address once (the same parse is checked and fetched) and `passes_on()` lets through only `https`, no
  userinfo, no port but https's own (`:443` is normalized away), and a host - read from `raw_host`, never decoded,
  since httpx's `.host` raises for a malformed international name - exactly one of PICTURE_HOSTS. So
  `https://commons.wikimedia.org@evil.example/` (host evil.example), `https://evil.example\@commons.wikimedia.org/`
  (a user to httpx), an address by number, a subdomain, a trailing dot and the sources' API hosts are all a 400
  with nothing asked. `picture()` checks again, so nothing reaches the network unchecked. Each redirect is followed by
  hand, its target `passes_on()` or the answer is refused (502) and the target never asked; at most
  PICTURE_REDIRECTS (4) hops. A Location that isn't an address is refused the same way - httpx reads it itself even
  with redirects off, as its RemoteProtocolError "Invalid URL in location header", or idna's ValueError for a name
  that can't be decoded; a RemoteProtocolError of any other kind (the host broke off) is an outage. Only a declared
  `image/*` is read (anything else refused unread). **Undecoded** (the review's): every hop sends
  `Accept-Encoding: identity`, and an answer with any Content-Encoding but none or `identity` is refused unread
  (`sent_as_it_is()`, in coverart_endpoint.py) - before, httpx asked for gzip and `aiter_bytes()` inflated it, so the
  cap counted bytes after decompression (141 MB from 269 bytes of nested gzip, in the review); the cover relay had
  the same flaw, fixed in the same commit (above). So a Content-Length past PICTURE_MAX_BYTES is refused unread, a
  body read a piece at a time is the bytes that came and is refused as soon as it passes, an empty one refused.
  PICTURE_DEADLINE_SECONDS (7) for the whole fetch - the wait for a turn, every hop and the body - with httpx's 5 s
  between pieces and 4 to connect. The agent is `image_user_agent()`, moved out of ArtistImagesClient.user_agent
  (which now returns it): the MusicBrainz one with its contact, else `deadwax/<version>` - what Wikimedia, TheAudioDB
  and fanart.tv are already sent by Artist images. The outcomes, as ArchiveFronts': a picture (a memoryview of what
  was read - the answer goes out with no second copy), None (404 or 410), PicturesBusy (503), or PictureHostDown
  (unreachable, broken off, 429, 5xx: 502), PictureHostSlow (the deadline, an httpx timeout: 504), PictureRefused
  (this answer's own: off-list or broken redirect, not an image, encoded, too big, empty, another status - 403
  included - too many redirects: 502). A fault in deadwax while fetching is a 502 with its traceback in the log.
  Nothing is kept: no folder, no memory of a failure, each ask asks again.
- **Bounded**: at most PICTURES_AT_ONCE (6) fetches at once (a semaphore per event loop, as the cover relay's), and
  at most PICTURES_PENDING_MAX (64, the cover relay's PENDING_MAX - the review's) asks under way, waiting for a turn or
  fetching; one more is a 503 at once, nothing asked or remembered, and counted down whatever ends it. What is true
  of memory: **at most 6 bodies are being read at once, each refused past 8 MB - 48 MB being read, at most**; a
  waiting ask holds nothing but itself. A picture once read leaves both counts and is held until its answer is handed
  to the server to send, which neither count covers: in practice at once, but a phone reading slowly keeps its picture
  (at most 8 MB) alive that long. (The first cut's notes said "at most 48 MB is held", which wasn't so.)
- **The hosts** (PICTURE_HOSTS, where each came from):
  - `commons.wikimedia.org` - every Commons candidate's preview (`artists.commons_file_url`: the `image` relation's
    and Wikidata's P18/P154, Special:FilePath with `?width=`), and its own first hop.
  - `thumb.wikimedia.org` and `upload.wikimedia.org` - where Commons sends it: **seen by hand, 2026-11-16, with curl
    (not deadwax)**, `Special:FilePath/<file>?width=600` answers 302 to
    `commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?title=Special:Redirect/file/<file>&width=600`, which answers 301 to
    `thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/…/960px-<file>` for a file wider than asked (a 960px JPEG, 127 KB;
    an SVG logo as a 960px PNG, 60 KB - Wikimedia now rounds a thumbnail up to its own sizes) or to
    `upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/…/<file>` for one no wider (Example.jpg, 9 KB, served as it is). The code
    named only upload.wikimedia.org (the robot-policy comments); **thumb.wikimedia.org was found only by asking**, and
    without it every Commons thumbnail would have been a 502.
  - `r2.theaudiodb.com` - tests/test_artists.py's fixture, and **seen by hand**: every image field of a row asked
    with TheAudioDB's public test key (Coldplay) is an `https://r2.theaudiodb.com/images/media/artist/…` address,
    which answers 200 at once (a thumb 89 KB, a background 178 KB). `www.theaudiodb.com/images/…` answers 404, so the
    API host isn't on the list.
  - `assets.fanart.tv` - **assumed**, from fanart.tv's API documentation: no code or fixture names it (the fixtures
    use `https://f/…`), there is no project key here to ask with, and on 2026-11-16 the host couldn't be reached
    from where this was built (something on that network answered for it with a certificate of its own). Whether the
    host redirects is unseen.
  - **fanart.tv over https** (the review's): fanart.tv's v3 API is known to name its pictures
    `http://assets.fanart.tv/…`, so every fanart.tv preview - fanart.tv leads SOURCE_ORDER - would have been a 400.
    `artists.from_fanarttv` now upgrades exactly that prefix (`fanarttv_https()`, case-insensitive) to `https://`,
    for the candidate's `url` and so its `preview` - one address, so the choice apply checks against the candidates is
    the same URL the picker offered, and apply fetches it over https. No other host's scheme is touched, nor disc
    art's (`fanarttv_cdart`), and fanart.tv's `/preview/` paths aren't used (unverified). The web's Artist images
    loads those pictures over https now too - assumed to work, since the same host serving https is what everything
    else that uses fanart.tv relies on, but not seen here.
- **The cap**: PICTURE_MAX_BYTES, 8 MB - more than the cover relay's 4, because only Commons' preview is a
  600px thumbnail: fanart.tv's and TheAudioDB's `preview` is the picture itself (`artists._candidate`), and fanart.tv
  offers 4K backgrounds (`artist4kbackground`), a few MB each. Under it, no more than a picker should be sent.
- **The deadline**: 7 s, the cover relay's ANSWER_SECONDS: nothing carries on past the ask here, so the deadline is
  what the phone waits, under its 8 s (ios/App/URLSessionTransport.swift `timeoutIntervalForRequest`). A 4K background
  on a slow host may not make it; the phone then shows that candidate as words.

### Decided here (the spec didn't say)

- **https only**, as asked - unlike the cover relay, which allows http on the Archive's hosts. Every hop seen was
  https.
- **One list for the first address and every hop**: the spec's "the hosts the previews are on, plus where they
  redirect"; a phone may send a `thumb.wikimedia.org` address directly, and gets it.
- **No cache, no single flight**: the spec's "nothing kept on disk". The phone's own URL cache (a week) is the cache;
  a picker shows a picture once.
- **A turn's wait inside the deadline**, unlike the cover relay (whose fetch carries on to keep the cover): here a
  picture queued past 7 s would be thrown away anyway.

### Review (before it shipped)

A review of the first cut found no way off the host list - forty tricky addresses and thirty-one redirect Locations
all handled - and five things, each fixed in the same commit: fanart.tv's `http://` addresses (upgraded in
`from_fanarttv`, above); the cap counting decompressed bytes, in this relay and the cover relay's (identity only,
above); the six at once covering only the fetch (PICTURES_PENDING_MAX, and the memory claim corrected, above); the
words (a 410 a 404; a refusal's 502 said for good, not "just now"); and the logins-off position, written down above
and unchanged.

### Verified, and not

- **pytest**: tests/test_artist_picture_relay.py, through start() with no lifespan, the hosts an httpx MockTransport
  shaped as they were seen (above): each source's preview, Commons through its own two redirects (thumb and upload);
  every preview the `from_*` functions make passing `picture_address()`; fanart.tv's `http://` pictures end to end -
  the images preview offering them as https, the relay passing each on, apply honouring that address and fetching it
  over https; forty addresses refused with a 400 and nothing asked; redirects followed within the hosts and refused
  off them (seventeen targets - an undecodable name and a broken address among them - a chain leaving part way, none,
  too many); the cap declared, streamed, at the cap, and a 6 MB picture under the real one; identity asked on every
  hop, eight encodings refused unread (a nested-gzip bomb), `identity` passed on, the bytes counted the bytes sent;
  the deadline over Commons' three hops; 404 and 410, 403 and the other statuses said for good, 429/5xx, unreachable
  and broken off said for now, timeouts; non-images (an SVG, AVIF, an icon, HTML, an untyped answer refused unread
  whatever its bytes); six at once over twenty; a turn's wait as a 504; the pending cap a refusal at once, nothing
  asked, asked once they drain, the count back to 0 after a picture, an outage, a refusal, a 404 and a timeout, and
  the route's 503; nothing kept; the agent, with and without a contact; GuardMedia's headers and no gzip; logins off
  as the implicit admin. tests/test_artists.py: `from_fanarttv` upgrades fanart.tv's `http://` (any case) and

## The scan without its tracks (2.1.28)

Phase 8's server change A (notes/ios-specs/phase8-managing.md on `ios`, sections 3.1 and 12): the app's album editor
finds an album's folder from the scan's albums, as the web's does (`albumEdit.ts` `editFolders`), but every field it
reads of an album is album-level, and `/library/albums` carries every track of every album - most of the body even
compacted (notes/performance.md, "Tracks travel compact"), twice a visit. So `GET /deadwax/library/albums` and `POST
/deadwax/library/rescan` take `tracks` (a query parameter, default true). `?tracks=false` sends each album as
`compact_for_wire()` would, less its `tracks` and `track_defaults` (`library.albums_without_tracks()`: the same keys in
the same order, the server-only fields dropped as ever, new dicts so the cache is never trimmed); everything else is
the same answer - the scan, `queue`, `issue_types`, each album's issues, the `X-Scan-*` headers, the snapshot form.
The ETag is of the body, so the two forms never answer each other's If-None-Match. The web never sends it, so nothing
it reads changed; no route was added (tests/test_logins.py ROUTES as it was) and no permission moved (`/albums` a
user's, `/rescan` Look after the library's).

- **Not chosen**: the full scan on the phone (megabytes a visit), and a one-folder route (`edition_count`,
  `split_discs` and `disc_label` are worked out across the whole scan, and Needs a look and Library care read the list
  anyway).
- **Verified**: tests/test_library_cache.py - the lean body equals the full one less the two keys, key for key; its
  own ETag is a 304 and each form's ETag a 200 for the other; the snapshot form stale and from the saved scan; rescan's
  form, and an unchanged library's forced read the same lean answer. **Not seen**: the phone asking it (slice 1).

## Edit album on the phone (Phase 8, slice 1 - 2026-11-16)

James: "nothing in the app should take you to the web app", and "maybe some dropdowns instead of big lists". The
design is notes/ios-specs/phase8-managing.md (sections 1-3, 13-15); this is its slice 1, **Edit album: the folder,
what's wrong, Release**, on the `ios` branch at 2519279 (main's 2.1.31 merged). The app stays 0.13 (13);
src/__init__.py untouched; no server or web change (server change A, the scan without its tracks, shipped as 2.1.28);
the player engine has no diff.

### Decided here, and where the phone departs from the spec

- **Apply goes ahead through the plan's problems**, as the web's does (`MetadataEditor.tsx:1049`: off with no plan, an
  empty one, or while planning, applying or a release loads - never for a problem); the spec's section 2 said "and no
  problem". The problems are amber above it.
- **The cover switch says the web's words** ("Download cover art" / "Replace cover.jpg", with its hint and size), not
  the spec's "Save the release's cover"; Compare covers' button is the web's "Replace cover only" / "Save cover only".
- **Needs a look's section is Edit albums'** (the web draws the issues and the marks on its Release tab), and It's fine
  as it is and Ask about it again in it need Look after the library too (decision 2; AlbumEdit.marksFine is the web's
  `marksFine`, composed with the editors in the App) - both, as main's 2.1.31 docs say. The spec's 3.2 tied the whole
  section to Look after the library; its checks 338 and 342 (Edit albums alone: no marks; Look after the library
  alone: Delete album… only) are what this does.
- **The follow outlives the sheet**: closing it doesn't stop the looks for the album's new id (the web's panel lets go
  as it closes) - the album page under it is the one that would otherwise be left on a gone id. A sign-out does stop
  it (after review, below).
- **The album is followed to where the apply said it left it** (after review): the apply's own plan's `target_path`,
  worked out again on the server, once `moved_to` says it moved - the preview's target only for an apply that never
  answered (or moved it without saying where). The web takes the preview's alone (MetadataEditor.tsx's apply:
  `results.moved_to && plan?.target_path ? plan.target_path : album.path`, `plan` the preview in state); the folder can
  change between the two, and the apply's is what happened. The web is unchanged.
- **A mark that fails is said in the phone's words** (`markFineFailed`, `askAgainFailed`, through EditWords.said); the
  web leaves its rejection unhandled.
- **No preview while the folder must be read again**: after an apply, `RetagFlow.due` holds the debounce until the
  re-read lands, so a preview never plans against the folder as it was.
- **The editor's search is the web editor's**, without `quick` (MusicBrainz's ten attempts), given 60 s.
- **The retag payload is buildRetagRelease, not the download's** (the spec's 3.3): the credit's `?? ... || null`, the
  country's `??`, no `album_artist`. The vectors hold each case beside its download payload; whether the two should
  differ is the web's question (reported, unchanged).
- **The cover alone waits 120 s, not 90**: the contract test found two fetches (the full size's fallback) can take 110.
- **Tags, Artwork, Lyrics and Delete album… open the web app** (WebAppRow: the album's page, or the web app's Library
  for a folder with no album page) until slices 2-4; the line under them says so.

### After review (16 Nov)

A review of the slice (the payload vectors, the URL encoding, the Codable keys, the double-Apply guard, the permission
gates and the newest-answer tickets confirmed) found nine things, all fixed in one commit:

1. **A 5xx from Apply was taken as a refusal.** `RetagFlow.outcome(of:)` took every answered failure as `.refused`, but
   `_retag_apply` answers 500 for an exception raised after the files are written and the folder moved, and a reverse
   proxy answers 502 or 504 while the scan wait runs on. Now only a 4xx is a refusal; any other answer goes the
   unanswered way - said as maybe finished, the folder read again, the album followed. deadwax's own words, when a 5xx
   carries some, are said under it (`EditWords.writeFailure`).
2. **A failed read after an apply spun for ever** ("Working out the changes…" while `needsRead` stayed set, and the
   sheet hid `scan.failure` with an album held). `LibraryScanModel.read` now says how it ended (`landed`, `failed`,
   `dropped`); a failed one calls `RetagFlow.couldNotRead()`, which ends the wait (`readFailed`: `planning` false) and
   keeps Apply and the cover off until a read lands. The root, whenever the scan's read has failed, and Release, while
   `readFailed`, draw `ReadAgainFailed`: the failure in the phone's words and Look again.
3. **Back in reach didn't search again.** `RetagModel.cameBack` now searches again when the last search failed or none
   ever finished on a folder that searches as it opens (`RetagFlow.searchesOnReturn`, with `searched` and
   `searchFailed` moved into the flow), else loads the tagged pressing's tracklist if the search found it and it never
   came (`Retag.currentToLoad`).
4. **A cancellation was shown as a failure** - the search's (the list wiped, searchError set), the preview's (wentAway
   cancels one in flight: `flow.failed`) and the scan's read (`failure` set). Each now checks
   `APIFailure.isCancellation` first and leaves what was there; a cancelled search stops its spinner only
   (`searchCancelled`).
5. **Close could come back on mid-apply.** `RetagFlow.due` is false while a write runs (and `planning` with it), and
   `EditAlbumModel.settle` touches neither the album held nor its Release while one does (`writing`: an apply or the
   cover alone) - the write's end reads the folder and decides; the Folder menu and the marks are off meanwhile. A
   refusal reads the folder only when a gap during it asked for a read.
6. **The follow used the preview's target.** `RetagResponse.pathAfter(_:)` takes the apply's own plan's target when it
   moved the folder (nil when it moved it without saying where - then the preview's, if the scan lists it). A departure
   from the web, which takes the preview's (above).
7. **Save cover only had no guard** against a folder still to be read or a write under way, and took a timeout or a
   5xx as a plain failure. It is now a write in the flow as Apply is (`beginCover`, `canSaveCover`, `coverEnded`):
   off while the folder is to be read again or a write runs, Apply off while it runs, and a timeout or a 5xx said as
   maybe finished ("deadwax may have finished this - looking again", announced) with the folder read again.
8. **The apply's timeout.** Worked out from the server: the cover fetched twice (fetch_front_why's full-size 1200 px
   fallback; 10 s to connect and 45 s between chunks each, 110 s), then Navidrome's two baseline getScanStatus calls
   (5 s each) and either the wait on its scan (90 s, plus one last 0.5 s sleep and 5 s poll started just before the
   deadline: 105.5 s with the baseline) or - the baseline unreadable, or no Navidrome - RETAG_RENAME_WAIT's fixed sleep,
   up to RENAME_WAIT_RANGE's 300 s (310 s with the baseline). Worst case 420 s; the phone waits **480 s**, 60 s for the
   plan, the tag writes, the move and the bookkeeping. test_ios_edit_contract.py works the 420 out of the server's
   source and constants and holds the timeout at least 60 s past it. (A second apply of the same folder queued behind
   another on the server's lock - from the web, say - can still outlast it: said as maybe finished, and read again.)
9. **An apply's follow outlived sign-out**: an apply in flight at a sign-out carried on, and its follow could write
   `albumMoved` into the next person's pages (AppNavigation.reset didn't stop it). AppNavigation has a `session`,
   moved on by `reset()`; the model keeps the one the sheet opened in (`attach`), and nothing after a write - the read,
   the page refreshes, each look of the follow, the move - runs once it has moved on.

After the review, on the Mac: `swift test` (1759 Core tests in 186 suites, 158 Audio in 17, 12 more, all passing);
the unsigned generic-iOS Debug build, BUILD SUCCEEDED, its one warning appintentsmetadataprocessor's own, none in a
touched file; the full pytest suite, 4649 passed and 1 skipped; all 92 sims with Node 22. Not verified: a real 5xx or a
proxy's 504 mid-apply, a failed read and Look again on screen, a sign-out during a long apply, and the search asked

Before it (the slice's first commit): `swift test` (1753 Core tests in 186 suites, 158 Audio in 17, 12 more, all

## Edit album's Tags on the phone (Phase 8, slice 2 - 2026-11-16)

The spec's 3.4 (notes/ios-specs/phase8-managing.md): Edit album's **Tags** - the folder's files, a track's page, and
Edit tags with its preview and Apply - on the phone, the WebAppRow for Tags gone. On the `ios` branch after slice 1's
review (92ccccd); the app stays 0.13 (13); src/__init__.py untouched; no server or web change; the player engine has
no diff.

### Core (DeadwaxCore)

- **AlbumInfo.swift**: `AlbumFile` reads every field `/library/tracks` sends (read_album_details) - `filename`,
  `format`, `size`, `length`, `bitrate`, `sample_rate`, `bits_per_sample`, `channels`, `codec`, `position`, `pictures`
  - each loosely, so a file with one odd field is kept; `title` (the non-empty title tag). `EmbeddedPicture`
  (describe_pictures: index, type, label, mime, size, description).
- **TagEdit.swift**: lib/tagEdit.ts - `TagEdit.fields` (TAG_FIELDS: the eleven, labels and short/numeric flags, the
  web's order, which is track_tags.EDITABLE_TAGS'), `sections` (the phone's four groups of them), `shared`
  (sharedValue: the value every file holds, or `mixed`), `edits` (only the fields typed over, trimmed, "" to remove,
  one draft to every file), `problem` (fieldProblem: UTF-16 length over 1000, a control unit, a number or a date by
  JavaScript's ASCII `\d`), `removes`, `placeholder`, `note` (fieldNote), `trackLabel` (albumEdit.ts's). `TagEditWords`
  (TrackTagEditor.tsx's and EditPanel TagsList's sentences, `saved`, `problems`, `canApply` - the web button's
  `disabled` turned round). The wire: `TagEditBody` (TagEditRequest), `TagEditPlan`, `TagEditFile` (each file's
  changes in the form's order), `TagEditResults`, `TagEditResponse`. `EditWords.pictureFailed` (the phone's own).
- **TrackInspector.swift**: lib/trackInspector.ts and trackFields.ts as a track's page reads them with its file read:
  `groups` (Tags, Audio, MusicBrainz, File - every TRACK_FIELDS row the inspector shows, its value, the data face, the
  default's reason), `place` (trackPlace), `trackTime`, the picture's facts and bytes, the page's words.
- **RetagFlow.swift**: `canApply(_ plan: TagEditPlan?, problems:)` and `beginApply(_:problems:)` - the tag editor is
  the Release page's flow again (a preview and an apply of one body: tickets, `due`, `needsRead`, `readFailed`,
  `mayHaveFinished`, `outcome(of:)`), so its review lessons hold for Tags as they are. `EditWords.inWebAppLine` names
  Artwork, Lyrics and Delete album… only.
- **EditClient.swift / Routes.swift**: `tagsPreview`, `tagsApply` (POST `/library/tags/preview|apply`) and
  `trackPicture` (GET `/library/tracks/picture?album&file&index`, a 404 as nil) - 73 routes now. Timeouts: the

**Held to the web**: ios/scripts/export-edit-parts-vectors.cjs (seed 8330) compiles lib/tagEdit.ts,

pages. ui/test/iosedit.sim.cjs runs both exporters with `--check`. Slices 3 and 4 add their sections to it.

### The app (ios/App/Edit/)

- **TagsModel** (one per folder EditAlbumModel holds): the files as `/library/tracks` reads them (the first time Tags
  opens, then whenever the scan reads the folder again - `albumRead`; newest read only, a cancellation changing

  TrackTagEditor's effect does), `beginApply`/`applyEnded`.
- **TagsPages**: `TagsListView` - a List, a section per disc on a set ("Disc 2", by the file's own disc number), rows
  "3 · Title" with the artist under it when it isn't the album's; **Select** / Done in the bar, the List's own
  selection (EditMode), and the bottom bar's **Select every track** / **Deselect every track** and **Edit 3 tracks…**
  (or **Edit all tracks…**); the footer "3 of 12 selected" or the web's note. `TrackPageView` - the head (title, "No
  title tag…", place), **Edit this track…**, an `InspectorSection` per group, **Pictures in this file** (a
  `PictureRow` each: the picture at 56 pt, `Corners.artShape`, its facts once loaded; a tap is FullCover's new
  `.picture` source), **All tags in this file (N)**. `EditTagsView` - a Form: what is edited (one track's title, or a
  disclosure of the tracks), the four sections of fields (each a TextField over what the files share, its note in
  amber for a problem, Undo), the web's hint under the last, **What would change** (`TagFileChanges` each: the label,
  from struck through, to), Apply.
- **EditAlbumModel.applyTags()**: as `apply()` - BackgroundHold ("Edit album: Edit tags"), RetagFlow's outcome, the
  maybe-finished announcement, `samePerson` before anything after the write, the folder read again only when it wrote
  or a gap asked, `wrote(before:)` so the album page asks again. `holdsWork` takes typed tags; `applying` takes the tag
  apply (Close off); `becameActive` reads again for Tags' `needsRead` too; reach and a failed read reach TagsModel.
- **One write at a time**: Release's Apply and the cover alone are off (and guarded in the model) while Tags applies;
  Tags' Apply is off while Release applies, saves a cover, or a mark runs. **And each waits for the other's write**: a
  tag edit that wrote (or may have) tells Release's flow the folder changed (`RetagFlow.folderChanged`: `needsRead`,
  no preview landing, no "may have finished" of its own), a release applied tells Tags' - so neither page offers an
  Apply on a preview of the files as they were. A Tags never opened has nothing to wait for (a read lets it go).

### Decided here, and where the phone departs from the spec

- **"" removes a tag**, as the web sends it (TagEditBody's tags are strings); the spec's 3.4 said null. The server takes
  both alike (TagEdit's model: `str | None`, "" or None removes).
- **A file's changes are listed in the form's order** (Title first), a tag the form doesn't offer after them by name -
  the web lists them in the order of the server's dict (the order typed), which JSONDecoder doesn't keep.
- **The track's page shows only the fields the file has** (the web draws a dash for each empty one), its place without
  the disc's title (that's Tags' Disc title row), and has no Previous/Next - Back and another row are the phone's way.
- **Edit this track…**, the web's words, not the spec's "Edit tags…".
- **After a clean apply the fields go back to what the files now say** (the draft cleared); the web leaves what was
  typed in them. On the phone the next edit then starts from the files, and the sheet holds no "unsaved" work that is
  saved.
- **The hint names the Release page**, not the web's Release tab.
- **Track, Disc, Year and Original year have the numbers-and-punctuation keyboard** (a "/" or "-" is part of them);
  Done above the keyboard, as on Release.
- **Another set of tracks over typed work asks "Discard changes?"** (the web's editor simply starts again on the new
  selection); the same set keeps what was typed.
- **Select is the bar's Select / Done**, Select every track in the bottom bar, the selection cleared on Done; the web's
  Shift-click runs aren't the phone's.
- **"Couldn't load this picture."** - the phone's own words when a picture full screen doesn't load (the web's viewer
  leaves the image broken).
- **The fields carry the web's labels** (Track, Disc, Disc title, Year, Original year), not the spec's.
- **The web's rule is stricter than the server's in three places** (tests/test_ios_edit_parts_contract.py holds it):
  a digit of another script (Python's `\d` takes it), a NEL after a number (Python's strip removes it), and a length
  over 1000 UTF-16 units but not characters. Each refuses something the server would have written - never the other
  way - so the phone never offers an Apply the server refuses for a field. Reported, unchanged.

The spec's 3.5 (notes/ios-specs/phase8-managing.md): Edit album's **Artwork** - the folder's cover, Get cover, its CD
art in a grid, Get CD art - and **Lyrics** - the count, Get lyrics - on the phone, their WebAppRows gone; Delete
album… is the one row left in the web app. On the `ios` branch after slice 2 (4452f5c); the app stays 0.13 (13);
src/__init__.py untouched; no server or web change; the player engine has no diff.

### Core (DeadwaxCore)

- **GetResults.swift** (new): lib/getResults.ts (`GETTING`, `GET_FAILED`, `getProblem` - ErrorWords with the Get's
  own lead and the page's Try again, the error's own words in brackets for whoever runs deadwax - `lyricsResult`),
  lib/lyrics.ts (`describeLyrics`, `lyricsOnDisk`), the three buttons as components/LibraryParts.tsx draws them -
  when each is offered (`offersCover`, `hasOwnDiscArt`, `offersDiscArt`, `offersLyrics(album, ran:)`) and its words
  by its last run (`label`) - and the two tabs' lines lib/albumEdit.ts has held since 2.1.30 (`coverNote`,
  `coverPointer`, `discArtPointer`, `lyricsLine`, `allLyricsNote`, `COVER_MISSING`, `DISC_ART_BESIDE`,
  `NO_DISC_ART`, `RETIME_POINTER`), the headings and VoiceOver's words. `GetRun` is LibraryParts' `run` - keyed to
  the folder it ran for - with the phone's outcome split: `working`, `none` (a 404: a fact, Look again), `failed` (a
  refusal: nothing written), `unanswered` (no answer, or a 5xx: it may have written - RetagFlow.outcome's rule, as
  Release's apply), `done`; `wrote` is done or unanswered. `LyricsSummary` (fetch_album_lyrics' counts, loose),
  `LyricsFetchBody` (LyricsRequest, `replace` and `retime` always false), `DiscArtFetchBody` (DiscArtRequest),
  `DiscArtFetched`.
- **EditClient.swift / Routes.swift**: `getCover` (POST `/library/art/fetch` with `replace: false` and no
  `release_mbid` - GetArtButton's body: the folder's own release), `getLyrics` (POST `/library/lyrics/fetch`),
  `getDiscArt` (POST `/library/disc_art/fetch`) and `libraryDiscArt` (GET `/library/disc_art?album&file`, a 404 as
  nil) - 76 routes. Timeouts, worked out from the server's own (tests/test_ios_edit_parts_contract.py does the sum):
  **Get lyrics 600 s** - LRCLIB's two asks for a track's artist name (connect 10 + read 30 each), CONCURRENCY 2 at
  once, a 12-track album: 6 x 80 = 480, and a margin; **Get CD art 360** - the Archive's listing (55), fanart.tv's
  (25), and four discs' pictures at the slower source's 55: 300, and a margin; a CD art picture 30, as the cover.
  Get cover is the cover alone's route and wait (120). A longer album may outlast its wait: then it is said as maybe
  finished and the folder read again, never asked again unseen.
- **EditWords.inWebAppLine** names Delete album… alone: "Delete album… opens the album in the web app, in Safari,
  until the app has it."

**Held to the web**: ios/scripts/export-edit-parts-vectors.cjs gains an artwork section - lib/getResults.ts and
lib/lyrics.ts compiled and run over 21 made errors (the web's own ApiError, fetch's TypeError, a TimeoutError, any
Error) x three kinds x admin or not (126), 46 lyrics summaries (six fixed, 40 seeded), albumEdit.ts's lines over 81
made folders (the art, the release, a dozen CD art listings including Turkish dotted capitals, the counts), and
LibraryParts.tsx's three buttons - when each is drawn and the JSX of its words, read by pattern and hashed into
made_from, so a change there fails the sim. The fixture is 387 KB. EditPartsVectorTests replays it (5 tests more).

### The app (ios/App/Edit/)

- **ArtworkLyricsPages.swift** (new): `ArtworkPage` - **Cover**: the folder's cover at 96 pt (a tap: FullCover's
  folder source, full screen) or the empty square, `coverNote` beside it, `GetButton(.cover)` when offered, and the
  pointer as a row - pushing **Compare covers** (with a cover) or **Release** (no release); **CD art**: `NO_DISC_ART`,
  or `DISC_ART_BESIDE` over a `LazyVGrid` of `DiscArtPicture`s (`/library/disc_art` for each of the scan's
  `disc_art`, square on the empty cover, a thumbnail at 360 px) with their names, each a button opening FullCover's new
  `.discArt` source; `GetButton(.disc)` when offered, the pointer (a row to Release with no release, else the words).
  `LyricsPage` - `lyricsLine`, `GetButton(.lyrics)` while offered (and after a run, saying what it came to),
  `allLyricsNote`, and `RETIME_POINTER` as the section's footer. `GetButton` - the label by the run, a spinner while
  it works, the line it left under it. `GetWait` - over both pages: "deadwax may have finished this - looking again"
  after an unanswered Get until a read lands, and Couldn't read the library with Look again.
- **EditAlbumModel**: `runs` (one GetRun per kind), `run(kind)` (only the held folder's), `getting`, `canGet`
  (in reach, an album, no write - `writing` takes `getting` through `applying` - no mark, the scan not being read, and
  the Release's `needsRead` clear: the folder read since the last write or gap), `unansweredGet` (cleared when a read
  lands). `get(kind)`: a BackgroundHold ("Edit album: Get cover"...), the route, `GetRun.done`/`failed`; anything that
  may have written tells Release's and Tags' flows the folder changed (their previews wait for the read), then -
  still the person the sheet opened for - says it (VoiceOver: maybe finished, or the line), reads the folder again and
  asks the album page beneath again (`wrote(before:)`: now, and once Navidrome has scanned). A 404 or a refusal reads
  nothing.
- **One write at a time**: Release's Apply and the cover alone are dimmed (and guarded) while a Get runs, Tags'
  through `model.writing`; a Get is dimmed while any of them runs. Close is off while a Get runs, as for an apply
  (`applying`), and the sheet can't be swiped away.
- **The root**: Artwork ("Cover, CD art") and Lyrics ("8 of 12") are NavigationLinks under Edit, as Tags is; the Edit
  section has no footer now; Delete album…'s section always has the web-app line under it.

### Decided here, and where the phone departs from the spec

- **The re-timing pointer is words, not a row**: the spec asked for a row to Server settings > Lyrics with Settings
  and the log. Server settings is still the web app's (Phase 8's slice 8), so a row could only open Safari at the
  settings page, not its Lyrics group; the web's own sentence ("…see Lyrics in Server settings (Library).") says where.
- **The pointers name the phone's pages**: the web's "in the Release tab (Compare full size…)" is "on the Release page
  (Compare covers…)" (`GetResults.onThePhone`), and each pointer that names a page is a row pushing it - Compare
  covers with a cover, Release with no release; "deadwax never replaces CD art it saved." stays words.
- **No cover is the web's line** ("No cover is saved with the album."), not the spec's "No cover", beside the empty
  square - the root's row keeps "No cover".
- **A Get that never answered (or answered a 5xx) reads the folder again** and says "deadwax may have finished this -
  looking again" over the page, as Release's apply does; the web just says the error. Its button still says Try again
  (the web's), and the route's own words stay under it. A cancellation counts as unanswered, as a write's does.
- **A Get is a write**: off while another write, a mark or a read after a write runs, and Close off while it runs - the
  web lets you close its panel mid-Get. Kept to slice 1's review rule (one write at a time, nothing drops the held
  album mid-write).
- **Get cover says nothing on success** (as the web, whose button goes once the scan has the cover) - the cover
  appearing is the answer; Get CD art likewise (its pointer appears). VoiceOver hears only the failures and Get lyrics'
  line.
- **CD art pictures aren't cached across openings**: each grid asks deadwax for its thumbnails (the route keeps them five
  minutes in a browser; the phone's transport keeps nothing). They're small, and a grid is rarely more than four.
- **The web's `&v=` cache-buster isn't sent** with a CD art picture (the server takes only `album` and `file`, and the
  phone keeps no cache to bust).

## Edit album's Delete on the phone (Phase 8, slice 4 - 2026-11-16)

The spec's 3.6 (notes/ios-specs/phase8-managing.md): Edit album's **Delete album…** - what deleting the folder takes,
read live, who holds it, the warning and Delete permanently, asked once more - on the phone, the last WebAppRow in Edit
album gone. On the `ios` branch after slice 3 (310c21f); the app stays 0.13 (13); src/__init__.py untouched; no server
or web change; the player engine has no diff.

### Core (DeadwaxCore)

- **DeleteAlbum.swift** (new): `DeleteWords` - DeleteAlbumDialog's words, lib/albumEdit.ts's since 2.1.30
  (`DELETE_TITLE`, `DELETE_CHECKING`, `DELETE_READ_FAILED`, `DELETE_FAILED`, `DELETE_WARNING`, `DELETE_CONFIRM`,
  `DELETING`, `deleteCounts` through Sources.size - the web's formatSize - and `deleteOthers`), myLibrary.ts's
  `holdersText` (with its `listed`; `holders_unknown` said as unread, never as "nobody"), editStatus's "Deleted …."
  for VoiceOver, and the phone's own question ("Delete Dummy?", "There is no undo.", Delete, Cancel) and page title.
  `AlbumEdit.deletesAll` - albumEdit.ts's rule for whether the album page goes back. `DeletionSummary` (loose: the four
  counts, and with logins on `holders`, `yours`, `holders_unknown`), `DeleteAlbumBody` (DeleteRequest's `album_path`),
  `AlbumDeleted`. `DeleteFlow` - the page's state: the summary keyed to its folder, read with tickets (only the newest
  lands; a cancelled read says nothing; a failed one leaves no summary), `canDelete(path)` only with this folder's
  summary and nothing reading or deleting, `deleteEnded` by RetagFlow.outcome's rule (a refusal said; no answer or a
  5xx said as maybe finished), `went(scan, path:)` (gone from a scan that read the library - nil for a scan with a
  `problem`, which says nothing either way) and `settled(gone:)`.
- **EditClient.swift / Routes.swift**: `deletionSummary(path:)` (GET `/library/deletion_summary?album`) and
  `deleteAlbum(path:)` (POST `/library/delete`) - 78 routes. Timeouts from the server's own work (the contract test
  checks them): the summary walks the folder once, nothing on the network - **60 s**, twice the track listing's; the
  delete walks it again, removes it, saves the scan and writes the store index - **120 s**.
- **EditWords.inWebApp** and **inWebAppLine** are gone (nothing says "in the web app" in Edit album now);
  `EditWords.deleteAlbum` ("Delete album…") is the root's row.

**Held to the web**: ios/scripts/export-edit-parts-vectors.cjs gains a delete section, appended after the others so their
output is unchanged - lib/myLibrary.ts compiled with the rest, albumEdit.ts's words and `deleteCounts`/`deleteOthers`
and myLibrary.ts's `holdersText` run over 112 made summaries (ten sizes from 0 to 13 GB, other-file counts past the
twelve listed, holders from none to four - an accent, an apostrophe - with and without `yours`, and `holders_unknown`
with and without holders beside it), `deletesAll` over 241 cases (each folder source x 0-3 folders x track and song
counts, and no folders), editStatus's deleted line, and DeleteAlbumDialog.tsx's flow read by pattern and hashed into
made_from (the summary read as it opens, the button off until it, a failed read's and a failed delete's words, the
holders line, the Cancel button). The fixture is 454 KB. EditPartsVectorTests replays it (3 tests more).

### The app

- **Edit/DeletePage.swift** (new): `DeletePage`, pushed from the root's **Delete album…** (Palette.danger, under
  `if edit.delete` - Look after the library's gate alone). Under the heading "Delete this album?": the album, its byline
  and its path; then "Checking what's in there…", the counts, the other files (the lead in amber, the names quiet), who
  holds it (amber), or the read's failure with Look again; then the warning in red over **Delete permanently**

  looking again" after a delete that never answered, and Couldn't read the library with Look again. The summary is read
  by `.task(id: path|online)`: every time the page opens, for a folder the album is followed to, and back in reach -
  never kept from before.
- **EditAlbumModel**: `deletion` (DeleteFlow), `deleted`, `deleting` (in `applying`, so Close is off and the sheet can't
  be swiped away while it runs), `canDelete` (in reach, an album, no write, no mark, the scan not being read, Release's
  and Tags' `needsRead` clear, and the flow's own), `readDeletion()`, `delete()`: `deletesAll` decided before the
  folder goes (from the folders as they are, as the web's dialog is given it), a BackgroundHold ("Edit album: Delete
  album"), then - still the person the sheet opened for - gone; refused (said to VoiceOver, nothing more); or
  unanswered: said as maybe finished, Release's and Tags' previews told the folder changed, the folder read again. The
  next read that lands settles it (`lookUp`, by `DeleteFlow.went`): gone, it went; still there, "Couldn't delete it."
  (or the 5xx's own words), the album followed and its summary read again. `gone()`: `deleted` (the sheet's
  `.onChange` dismisses it), "Deleted …." to VoiceOver, the Library's lists asked again now and after
  AlbumEdit.settleMs, and with an album page beneath - `deletesAll`: `AppNavigation.leaveAlbum(id)`; else
  `wrote(before:)` (the page asked again now and once Navidrome has scanned). Apply, the cover alone, Tags' Apply and
  the marks are guarded by `!deleting`, and Release's Apply and cover buttons dimmed by it.
- **AppNavigation.leaveAlbum(id)**: the album's page popped from the tab shown, only while it's on top (App.tsx's
  `else if (showing) router.back()`).
- **LibraryModel.albumDeleted()**: the store's album index forgotten (asked again by the screen showing it), and with
  a library of your own yours too, and your library asked again (the deleting admin's own entry is put away by the
  server as the folder goes).
- **EditAlbumSheet**: `EditPage.delete`, the root's row (the WebAppRow, its line and `webURL` gone), the LibraryModel
  from the environment passed to `attach(_:library:)`, and the dismiss once `deleted`.

### Decided here, and where the phone departs from the spec (or the web)

- **The question's title isn't italic**: the spec's "Delete *Album*? There is no undo." - a confirmation dialog's title
  is plain text on iOS, so the album's name is plain, and "There is no undo." is the dialog's message under it.
- **The phone asks once more; the web doesn't** - its dialog is the confirmation, Enter deliberately not confirming.
  On a phone the button is a tap away from a scroll, so the spec's action sheet is the second step, Cancel the default.
- **A failed summary read has Look again** - the web's dialog has none (reopening it reads again); the phone's page
  would otherwise have to be left and opened again.
- **A delete that never answered, or answered a 5xx, is settled by the library's next read**, said as maybe finished
  until then - the web just says the error. A 5xx can come after the folder has gone (the store index written after
  the rmtree), so a 5xx is never taken as "not deleted". A read whose scan has a `problem` (the library unreadable)
  decides nothing: the delete stays maybe finished until one that read the library lands.
- **Its failure words sit under the button**, not at the top in red as the web's do - beside what was pressed, as the
  Gets' are.
- **A delete is a write**: never beside an Apply, the cover alone, a Get or a mark, off until the folder has been read
  after one, and Close off while it runs (the web's panel can be closed mid-delete). Slice 1's review rule.
- **The album page goes back only on the tab shown, and only while it's on top** - App.tsx's rule. A page of the same
  album open on another tab stays; it shows what Navidrome says the next time it's looked at.
- **The Library is asked again twice** - now (the store's list, and yours with a library of your own) and once
  Navidrome has scanned (EDIT_SETTLE_MS, 10 s): Navidrome lists the album until its watcher scans the folder gone, so
  the first answer may still have it. The web's album index isn't asked again on a delete at all (it ages a minute); the
  spec asked for the phone's.
- **Managing.albumURL stays in Core** with its vectors, though the app no longer opens an album in the web app;
  WebAppRow stays for Manage's rows and Change password.
- **Check 341 needs nothing new**: a downloaded album gone from the collection already plays from the phone and says
  so (DownloadChoice's `gone`, the album page's line).

4695 passed and 1 skipped; all 92 sims with Node 22 (iosedit running both exporters' `--check`).

Not verified - only the phone can tell (docs/ios.md checks 338-342): the confirmation dialog's look and its Cancel in

### After review (16 Nov) - slices 2-4

A review of slices 2-4 (the permissions, the query and picture-URL encoding, the Codable keys against pydantic's
fields, one write at a time, Close, the newest-answer tickets and the cancellations confirmed) found five things and
three smaller ones, and four mutations that survived; all fixed in one commit on top of slice 4, with nothing on the
server or the web changed.

1. **Delete's question wasn't tied to its folder.** `delete()` read `album.path` when Delete was tapped, so a scan that
   followed the page to another folder while the action sheet was up would delete that one. The question now keeps the
   folder and the summary it was raised over (`asking`, handed to the sheet's buttons by `presenting:`), goes away when
   `album.path` changes, and `delete(path:summary:)` starts only through `DeleteFlow.beginDelete(_:over:holding:)` -
   the page still holding that folder, and that summary still the one in hand (a summary read again into something
   else meanwhile deletes nothing).
2. **"Several values" could become "Will be removed" with no typing.** `set` guarded on `draft[key] != value`, and a
   field over files that disagree shows "" - so a "" SwiftUI's TextField hands back (as it can on focus, without a key
   pressed) went into the draft as emptied, and Apply would have stripped every track's own value. `TagEdit.typed`
   (Core) now takes only text that differs from what the field shows (what was typed, else what the files share);
   typing and then clearing still reaches "", the draft then holding what was typed. A field the files agree on, handed
   its own value back, isn't an edit either (it used to make a preview of nothing).
3. **Delete was off with no reason after a failed Tags read.** `canDelete` waits for Tags' read as well as the
   Release's, but the page said only the Release's failure. `EditAlbumModel.readBlocking` says whichever is waited
   for - Tags' own read of the files first, else the scan's failure - and ReadAgainFailed (Release, Delete, the Gets'
   pages) shows it with Look again; Tags' TagsReadState shows the scan's failure too when it is what Tags waits for.
4. **After a clean apply the fields showed the old values until the read.** The draft was cleared at once, so each field
   fell back to what the files said before the write, under "Saved 12 files.". `TagsModel.refreshing` (set as the draft
   goes, cleared only as a read of the files lands) keeps the fields away meanwhile: "Saved…" and "Reading the files…",
   or - the read failed - its failure with Look again, never the stale values. Typed work isn't kept in them instead
   (the phone's departure from the web stays): a field would then disagree with its note, which reads the files.
5. **The long writes' waits were under the server's worst case.** Get lyrics' 600 s assumed one name a track; LRCLIB's
   `find` tries the track's artist and then its album artist, each by `/api/get` and then `/api/search`, with up to 15 s
   of busy pauses a request on top of 10 s to connect and 30 s to answer - twelve tracks two at a time are 22 minutes at
   worst. Get CD art's 360 s counted one request an Archive address, but the Archive answers through two redirects
   (coverartarchive.org, archive.org, the item's server), each its own 55 s silence - a single disc 355 s, four 850.
   Tags' 120 s ignored that mutagen writes a file whole when its new tags outgrow the room before the audio. Rather than
   one bigger fixed wait each (the sheet's Close is off while one runs), `EditWaits` (Core) works the wait out for the
   album in hand, a minute's margin on top, rounded up to the minute (URLSessionTransport keeps one session per wait)
   and never under `Routes.timeouts`' floor: lyrics by the tracks without a lyrics file, `ceil(n / 2) * 2 names * 2
   requests * 55 s` (twelve: 1380 s); CD art by the discs, `165 + 25 + discs * 165` (one: 420 s, four: 960); Tags'
   Apply by the files' size, `120 s + bytes / 20 MB a second` (3 GB of hi-res: 300 s). EditClient's `getLyrics`,
   `getDiscArt` (handed the album now) and `tagsApply(_:bytes:)` set the request's timeout from it.
   tests/test_ios_edit_parts_contract.py reads every figure against the server's source (the clients' timeouts,
   RETRY_PAUSES and `_retry_after`'s cap, `lookup_from_tags`' two names, `find`'s two requests a name, CONCURRENCY,
   `has_lyrics_file` on both sides, `fetch_disc_art`'s order) and works the pinned waits out again; the Archive's two
   redirects and the disk's 20 MB a second are assumptions, said there. A wait that still runs out is unchanged: said
   as maybe finished, the folder read again, never sent again unseen.

Smaller: a track's pictures are drawn by place (`enumerated()`'s offset), not by the server's index, which a missing or
malformed field reads as 0 for two pictures alike; a refused tag apply marks its preview out of date at once
(`changed()`: the spinner, then a new preview) rather than leaving the refused plan drawn; and a read after the files
were renamed filters the editor's files (`editing`) as it does the selection, so Apply never names a file the folder no
longer holds.

Mutations that survived, now killed (each run against the new tests, then put back): **M1** TagEdit.problem's `<= 0x1F`
as `< 0x1F` - the exporter now asks the web's rule about the separators 0x1C-0x1F (inside a value and alone; 72 more
problem vectors, 471), which also showed the web stricter than the server a fourth way: Python's strip removes those
separators at either end, JS's trim keeps them and its control check refuses them (the contract test counts the values
the web refuses and the server would take: 18 now, 11 of them these, at most 21); **M12** beginRead keeping another
folder's summary (A read, B's read called off: nothing deletable); **M13** canDelete without `!reading` (the same
folder read again with its summary drawn: off); **M14** settled(gone: false) overwriting a 5xx's words (deadwax's own
words stay; ours only when it gave none).

Tests: DeleteAlbumTests 4 more (11), TagEditFlowTests 1 more, EditWaitsTests (new, 4), GetResultsTests and
TagEditFlowTests' client tests with the waits; tests/test_ios_edit_parts.py 1 more (Tags' fixes) and the Delete,
Gets and apply tests moved to the new calls; test_ios_edit.py (readBlocking); the contract test's waits rewritten.
docs/ios.md: Edit tags' "Saved…" and "Reading the files…", a "Several values" field left alone by a tap, the Gets' and
Apply's waits, Delete's question and its unreadable library; checks 330 and 331 reworded.

Verified on the Mac: `swift test` (1805 Core tests in 191 suites, 158 Audio in 17, 12 more, all passing); the unsigned
generic-iOS Debug build, BUILD SUCCEEDED; the full pytest suite, 4696 passed and 1 skipped; all 92 sims with Node 22
(iosedit running both exporters' `--check`); each of the four mutations run against the new tests (all four failed
them), then put back. Not verified - the phone's: whether a TextField over "Several values" really hands back "" on
focus (the guard holds either way), the action sheet put away when the page is followed elsewhere, and "Reading the
files…" after an Apply; nor any wait against a real LRCLIB or Archive at their slowest.

## The artist tools on the phone (Phase 8, slice 5 - 2026-11-16)

The spec's section 4 (notes/ios-specs/phase8-managing.md): an artist page's **Artist images…**, **Which artist is
this?** and **Move albums to {name}…** on the phone, from a bar ••• the page didn't have, each a sheet. On the `ios`
branch after the merge of main's 2.1.32 (fd86014), whose relay (`GET /library/artist/picture`, "The artist pictures'
relay (2.1.32)" above) the pictures come through - decision 1. The app stays 0.13 (13); src/__init__.py untouched; no
server or web change; the player engine has no diff.

### Core (DeadwaxCore)

- **ArtistManage.swift** (new): lib/artistManage.ts - `libraryNames` (over the `/library/owned` index the page reads
  already: a collaboration never theirs, a folder of one artist theirs by its id, else by name or by a release
  Navidrome lists under them; a steady order by the web's collation), `namesToMove`, `imagesFolder` (with the summary's
  `Said` - answered or unread - for the web's Map of summaries), `bestUrls`, `toggleChoice`, `byKind`, `slotLine`,
  `imageNotes`, `savedLine`, `matchLine`, `refileView` (two names planning one target: the later shown staying),
  `canMove`, `moveLine`, `moveButton`, `refileAfter`, `refileOutcome`, `listed`; and ArtistPanel.tsx's own, held by
  pattern (below) - `others`, `refileSubtitle`, `namesApplied`, `showing`. The answers, each read loosely as the rest
  of Core decodes: `ArtistSummary` (`/library/artist`), `ArtistImagesPreview` with `ArtistImageCandidate`,
  `ArtistImageKind` and its sources' keys, `ArtistImagesApplied`/`ArtistImagesResults`, `ArtistMatchesAnswer` (the
  search; `MBArtistMatch` reused), `ArtistRefilePlan` with `RefileMove`, `RefileRetag`, `RefileRefused`,
  `ArtistRefileApplied`/`ArtistRefileResults`; the bodies `ArtistImagesBody`, `ArtistSearchBody`, `ArtistRefileBody`
  (no id is no key - the model's `None`). `searchWords` and `sameAddress` for the app (WebText is internal).
- **ArtistManageFlow.swift** (new): `ArtistImagesFlow` - the look and the search by tickets (only the newest lands), a
  look with no id opening the search (the web's), the choices starting at `bestUrls`, `canSave` (the web's - an id
  settled, something chosen, nothing loading, no problem - and section 2's: a folder, in reach, read since the last
  gap, not saving), `holdsWork`, Save by RetagFlow.outcome's rule (a 4xx said; no answer or a 5xx: maybe finished, the
  folder looked at again before Save comes back), out of reach and back. `ArtistRefileFlow` - every name's preview as
  one round, `changed(ask)` (the page's names, id or name now different: the previews asked again rather than applied
  blind), `beginMove` (the names `namesApplied` gives), `moveEnded` (refileOutcome and refileAfter; a name that never
  answered: what is known to have moved said with "maybe finished", the previews asked again). `ArtistWhoFlow` - the
  search, newest only, a failed one searched again once deadwax is back. `ArtistWaits` (below) and
  `ArtistManageWords` - ArtistPanel's and ArtistPage's words, and the phone's own (the menu, "More for this artist",
  a picture as words, the relay's failure words, "In their folder now").
- **ArtistManageClient.swift** (new): the eight calls - `libraryArtist(name:)` and `artistArt(folder:kind:)` (each a
  404 read as none), `artistImagesPreview`, `artistImagesApply(_:commons:)`, `artistPicture(url:)` (`mostBytes` the
  relay's own cap, Accept `image/*`), `artistSearch`, `refilePreview`, `refileApply(_:bytes:)`. **Routes.swift**: the
  eight (86 routes) and their floors - `/library/artist` 120 s (the scan's, as `/library/albums`), `/artist/art` 30,
  images preview 240 (the scan, one MusicBrainz lookup, three sources and Commons' widths), images apply 600, search
  60, refile preview 240, refile apply 480 (as Release's apply: every file read, tagged and moved) - raised after
  review to 660, 600, 120 (and facts 120), 480 and 600: "After review (16 Nov) - slice 5" below. **Managing.swift**:
  `artistManaging(permissions)` (permissions.ts's, vectors over all 64 sets). **Models.swift**: `looseMap`.

**The waits** (`ArtistWaits`), as EditWaits works Edit album's out: Save's is the scan (120) + one MusicBrainz lookup
(60; 111.5 at its worst, worked out again after review - below) + the three sources and a width for each Commons candidate (25 s each: JSON_TIMEOUT's 10 + 15) + each picture
chosen fetched through Commons' two redirects (3 x 40 s: IMAGE_TIMEOUT's 10 + 30) + the minute's margin, rounded up
to the minute, never under 600 s. Move's, a name at a time: 480 s + that name's albums' size (its summary's
`total_size`) at 20 MB a second, for a retag that outgrows its room and rewrites a file. The relay has no wait of its
own: the transport's 8 s is past its 7 s deadline. tests/test_ios_artist_manage.py reads each figure from the server's
source; Commons' two redirects (seen by hand when the relay was built) and the disk's pace are assumptions.

**Held to the web**: ios/scripts/export-artist-manage-vectors.cjs compiles lib/artistManage.ts with lib/artistPage.ts
and lib/owned.ts and runs it as it is - libraryNames over 76 cases (folded and accented names, collaborations,
folders with and without ids, pages with and without one, by release), namesToMove, imagesFolder over 17 (one name,
several, the current among them or not, unread, no folder), the slot and save rules, 13 refile cases (two names, one
target; applies that stayed, failed or emptied a name), listed - and reads out of app/ArtistPanel.tsx what the panel
works out itself, each by a pattern evaluated as written (the subtitle, the names Move applies, a slot's other
pictures) or a sentence checked as written (Showing…, canSave, the slot's pictures in order, a look choosing the
best, no id opening the search), and every word the phone says that the panel and ArtistPage.tsx say. The fixture is
142 KB; ui/test/iosartistmanage.sim.cjs runs it with `--check`. export-managing-vectors.cjs gains `artistManaging`
over the 64 sets.

### The app (ios/App/Artist/)

- **ArtistView**: a bar ••• (`ellipsis.circle`, "More for this artist") only while it has something - in reach, the
  artist not gone, and by `Managing.artistManaging`: **Artist images…** once the library files albums under a name of
  theirs (dimmed until deadwax has said which folder: the sheet asks by it); **Which artist is this?** once the
  artist's answer and `/library/owned` are in, while nothing says who they are (the web's `said`) or it was chosen
  here; **Move albums to {name}…** while their name now is known and a library name isn't it. Who they are is `said ??
  chosen` (the web's): a pick is kept by the page's artist id in ArtistsModel (`chosen`, cleared for a new person),
  and the page says "You chose who this is, for this visit." under their name. Their name now comes from
  MBArtistModel's `loadFacts` (the MusicBrainz artist page's own, made reachable), asked only for someone who
  manages. The hero is the square from their folder once Artist images saved this visit, or where Navidrome has no
  picture (the web's `square`). After a move: the page's kept answer forgotten, `/library/owned` and the summaries
  asked again, the page loaded again now and after AlbumEdit.settleMs - never past a sign-out.
- **ArtistToolsModel** (with `ArtistManaged`, what the page knows for the tools): the library's names (made again only
  when `/library/owned` or who they are changes) and `/library/artist` for each, asked together, newest round only,
  only for someone the ••• has something for. **ArtistPictureCache**: every picture the tools draw - a candidate's
  `preview` through the relay, a folder's through `/library/artist/art` - in memory only (NSCache, 32 MB, scaled to
  900 px), one fetch however many views wait, four at a time, a 503 (the relay busy) asked again twice 1.5 s apart, a
  failure held a minute (CoverCache.againAfter) with deadwax's words. **RelayedArtistPicture** draws the candidate in
  words (its label and source, then why) when it couldn't be had - never blank; **ArtistFolderPicture** the folder's.
- **ArtistImagesSheet**: who the pictures are of ("Showing Ye (rapper)") with Not them? and the search, the notes and
  problems, a section per slot (the preview's `kinds`): the chosen picture large (or the one on disk), `slotLine` in
  the header, **Use another picture (N)** pushing **ArtistPictureGrid** (lazy: the slot's own kind first, then the
  rest, a tap choosing, a second taking it back); Replace; **In their folder now**; Save and `savedLine`. Close asks
  when `holdsWork`; Close and the swipe are off while Save runs.
- **ArtistWhoSheet** (in ArtistMoveSheet.swift): the note, the search (asked as it opens for the page's name), the
  matches (**ArtistMatchRow**, `matchLine`); a pick hands the page the match and closes.
- **ArtistMoveSheet**: the subtitle ("Kanye West → Ye"), the note with the folder in bold (an AttributedString),
  Albums that move and Albums that stay, Move N albums; then the outcome, the failures in amber, Done. Cancel and the
  swipe are off while it moves.
- **ArtistToolModels.swift**: `ArtistImagesModel`, `ArtistMoveModel`, `ArtistWhoModel` - the asking; Save and Move
  each held by a BackgroundHold, a cancelled write taken as unanswered, VoiceOver told what became of it, and nothing
  after a write (the page asked again) done past a sign-out (AppNavigation's session when the sheet opened). Back in
  front with a read owed (`becameActive`), it is asked.
- **ReadAgainFailed** (Edit/EditAlbumSheet.swift) takes a failure, a dimming and an action as well as Edit album's
  model: the look's and the preview's failures, with Look again.

### Decided here, and where the phone departs from the spec (or the web)

- **ArtistPanel.tsx's own rules stay in the .tsx, held by pattern** - the Move albums subtitle, the names Move applies,
  a slot's other pictures, "Showing…" and `canSave`. The brief said a rule living only in a .tsx should stop the work
  for a no-change web refactor on main first, as slice 1 did; slices 2-4 instead read such pieces out of the source by
  pattern (`piece`, `says`), each hashed into made_from so the sim fails when one changes, and this slice does the
  same. Moving them into lib/artistManage.ts is a small no-change refactor on main whenever wanted; the exporter would
  then run them as it runs the rest.
- **One ••• in the bar**, as the spec says, where the web puts each button beside what it acts on (under In your
  library, in About's Now known as, in the "doesn't know who" line). It's there only while deadwax is in reach - every
  item needs it - and Artist images… is dimmed until the folder is known.
- **The chosen picture large, the rest a pushed grid** (the spec), where the web lays every picture of a slot in a row
  and Use another picture/Fewer adds the others inline. The grid lists the same pictures in the web's order. The phone
  shows a picture's label and source under it (the web shows the source, the label in its tooltip); VoiceOver reads
  the web's "label, from source", and "Chosen".
- **In their folder now** is the phone's own section (the spec's "what's in the folder now"); the web shows a slot's
  file on disk only when nothing was found for it.
- **A picture the relay couldn't pass on is drawn as words** - its label, its source, and deadwax's words (the
  relay's 502 is "deadwax couldn't get that picture just now.") - never a blank or a broken image. Four at a time from
  the phone, under the relay's six and its 64 waiting.
- **A choice is kept for the app's life, by the page's artist id** - the web's `kept.chosen` is the page's cache, "for
  this visit". The phone's Which artist is this? stays in the ••• after a pick (the web's Change).
- **The page doesn't follow a move.** The web's page of an old name every album of which moved becomes their page by
  their MusicBrainz id; the phone's pages are Navidrome's artists, so once Navidrome has scanned, the old name's page
  says the artist isn't here any more. Not ported: it needs a way from an MBID to Navidrome's artist id. docs/ios.md
  says so.
- **Move applies only the names whose albums the preview shows moving** (the web's skip), in turn, stopping at the
  first that fails; a name that never answered keeps what is known to have moved on screen with "maybe finished".
- **Move's previews are asked again when the page's names, id or name now change under the sheet** (`changed`), and
  Move is off until they land - an apply sends only what its preview showed.
- **The menu item has an ellipsis** ("Move albums to Ye…"): it opens a sheet. The web's button has none.
- **A cancelled write is unanswered**, never a refusal: it may have written.
