### After review (16 Nov) - slice 5

A review of 8ea5bfc found eight real problems and a handful of small ones. All are fixed in one commit on the `ios`
branch's worktree; the app stays 0.13 (13), src/__init__.py untouched, no server or web change.

1. **A gap no longer throws away the person's picture choices.** `ArtistImagesFlow.looked` used to start every look
   from the best of each kind - so deadwax going away and coming back (or Look again, or the read after a save that
   may have written) undid an edit and made Close stop asking. Now a look of the SAME artist (the same id as the
   pictures in hand) keeps each choice the new look still offers, what the choices started from (`baseline`, so
   `holdsWork` still holds) and what the last save said; a choice no longer offered is dropped and said in amber
   above the slots (`notOffered`: "The picture you chose for the banner isn't offered any more, so it won't be saved
   - choose another."), cleared by the next save. A look of ANOTHER artist starts from the best, as the web's does.
   The web never looks again unasked, so this is the phone's own rule.
2. **A Move that never answered is checked, never stuck.** Its previews asked again used to 404 on the name it had
   emptied ("no such artist" - the preview failed, Look again failing the same way), and once the page's names lost
   it, `preview()` asked for nothing and Look again did nothing. Now `moveEnded` records what is being checked
   (`settling`: the name whose answer never came, the albums its preview showed moving, where to, what the names
   before it said); a name's 404 is read as nothing left under it (`gone`, ArtistMoveModel.preview), and the check
   (`settle`) counts the name as moved when it is gone, the page's names no longer hold it, or none of those albums is
   under it any more. Had finished: "deadwax had finished: N albums from X moved into Y/." with the outcome and Done -
   or, with names after it still to move, over their plan with Move offered again. Hadn't: "deadwax hadn't moved the
   albums under X - they're below, to move again." or "deadwax had moved M of the N albums under X - the rest are
   below, to move again." over the plan, Move offered. With no name left `preview()` settles without a request, so
   Look again always does something. A check whose preview fails keeps "maybe finished" said.
3. **Each guard has a test of its own that fails without it** (each mutation run alone against ArtistManageFlowTests,
   the source put back after): `canSave` without `loading == nil` fails saveWaitsForALookUnderWay; without
   `problem == nil`, saveWaitsAfterALookFailed; `beginSave` sending `lastAsked.mbid`, saveSendsTheIdTheLookAnswered;
   `canMove` without `outcome == nil`, moveIsOffOnceItIsOver; `ArtistManage.offered` with `may.images` and `may.move`
   swapped (either side), theMenuOffersEachToolByItsOwnPermission.
4. **A replaced picture is drawn as the new one.** The folder pictures' cache key carried a per-sheet counter
   (`flow.wrote`, the page's `tools.version`) while the cache lives for the app: a sheet or page opened again started
   at 0 and found the old picture under the old key. Now `ArtistFolderVersions` (an @Observable singleton, as long-lived
   as ArtistPictureCache.shared) counts the writes to each folder by server and path - bumped by every save that wrote
   or may have, and by a Move that moved (it carries the pictures into the folder of their name now) - and
   ArtistFolderPicture keys on it. The hero's square comes from the folder once that folder's count is past nought
   (was: saved this visit).
5. **Move's wait reads each name's size when Move starts.** The sizes were taken as the sheet opened; one the page read
   later was never seen, and an unread one was waited for as nought. The sheet now passes the page's sizes on as they
   come (`onChange(of: sizes)`, merged), and `move()` asks `/library/artist` for any name still without one
   (`ArtistRefileFlow.unsized`; a 404 is nought - nothing filed under it). If that fails, Move doesn't start: nothing
   sent, "Couldn't read their folders just now, so nothing was moved - try again." under Move, Move offered again
   (`moveNotStarted`).
6. **The look's wait is past the server's worst case, every term summed.** One MusicBrainz request at its worst
   (`ArtistWaits.musicBrainz`): its ten attempts (RETRIES), each waiting out the rate limiter's 5 s window and then
   paused at its longest - a 429's `sleep(6)`, a 503's 3 s, or a failed connection's `2.0 + attempt * 0.5` (6.5 and 7
   at the last two attempts, and paused after the last as well) - 50 + 61.5 = 111.5 s. Artist images' look: the scan
   (120) + a search and a lookup (2 x 111.5) + the three sources in turn and a width for each Commons picture (25 s
   each, JSON_TIMEOUT's connect and read), at least five Commons pictures (the next look may be someone else's) + the
   minute's margin = 603, so 660 s (was 240, then 600); with the last look's Commons count when it found more (nine:
   720). An artist's facts and the search, one request each, are given 120 (were 60). Move's preview 480, its apply
   600 at least plus the size term. tests/test_ios_artist_manage.py reads every pause from `MusicBrainzClient._ask`'s
   own source, holds each Swift constant to it, sums the same terms and checks each route's floor and the formulas.
   **Assumed, not waited out**: each answer comes promptly - a network silent to its timeouts on every attempt (10 s
   to connect, 30 to read, ten times) would be over eight minutes; an attempt waits at most one window for its turn
   (more only with other MusicBrainz work queued ahead of it); five Commons widths before a look has said; JSON's
   write and pool timeouts (the requests send nothing and the pool isn't contended); Commons' two redirects; the disk's
   20 MB/s for a rewrite. A look past its wait writes nothing and says so with Look again.
7. **"Use another picture (N)" counts as the web counts**: N is the other kinds' pictures (`others.length`), and the
   button is there only when N > 0 (`ArtistManage.anotherPicture`, the sheet's only call for it). The exporter reads the
   web's condition and template out of ArtistPanel.tsx by pattern ("use another picture, when") and the fixture's
   `others` cases carry the label the web draws - ten cases now, a slot with no other kind among them - so the call
   site can't drift. Where the phone departs: it draws only the chosen picture in a slot (the web draws every one of
   its own kind in a row), so a slot whose pictures are all its own kind still needs the grid - "Pictures for this
   slot (N)", N its own. **"Showing …" names the page's name** when MusicBrainz gave none (`ArtistManage.showingWho`,
   the web's `preview?.facts?.name || request.name`, read out by pattern into `whoShown`), never a pick's or a
   search's. **Move's subtitle names the page's name** too (`request.name`; was the first name moving).
8. **Move checks the person before each name.** The samePerson guard ran only after the loop; now it runs before each
   name's apply, and a change stops the rest - "Stopped before the rest - someone else signed in." with what moved.

And the small ones:

- The ••• offer rule is Core's (`ArtistManage.offered`), table-tested.
- The outcome screen's subtitle keeps naming what the Move was for (`shownFor`, from `movedFor`) as the page's names
  empty under it - it used to go blank.
- Picture fetches nobody waits for any more are cancelled: ArtistPictureCache counts each fetch's waiting views, and
  the last one leaving (the grid or the sheet closed) cancels it - or, still waiting its turn among the four, it is
  never sent. Nothing is kept of a cancelled fetch, so it is asked afresh when drawn again.
- "deadwax may have finished" after a Save that never answered stays said when the look after it fails (it was inside
  the section a failed look hides).
- A look while Save runs is never sent: deadwax coming back during a save owes the look, asked once the save is over
  (`saveAnswered` and a refused `saveFailed` say so) - one sent before could land after it with the folder as it was,
  and clear "Saved …".
- `ForEach(id: \.self)` over words (problems, notes, failures) and over the grid's candidates keyed by place instead:
  two the same would have been one row.
- Which artist is this?'s failed search is asked again trimmed, as it was searched (`ArtistWhoFlow.failed`).

Left alone, and why: the waits outside the artist tools that cover a MusicBrainz request asked with all ten attempts
are under the 111.5 s worked out above too - Edit album's search (`editorSearchTimeout`, 60), a release group, its
pressings and a release (60 each), an artist's albums (`discography`, 60, up to five pages). The review named the
artist tools' waits; raising Phase 6's and slice 1's is a change of its own, for James to decide. An artist's facts
(`artistFacts`), which the artist tools ask, went to 120 here - the artist page and Info's artist card are given that
too now (SearchSongsTests follows).

Checked again on the Mac: `swift test` - 1836 Core tests in 193 suites, 158 Audio in 17 and 12 more, all passing; the
unsigned generic-iOS Debug build, BUILD SUCCEEDED; the full pytest suite, 4865 passed and 1 skipped; all 93 sims with
Node 22 (iosartistmanage's `--check` against the regenerated fixture). Not on a phone: docs/ios.md's checks 344 and
347 now ask after the kept choices, the redrawn picture and a lost Move's check.

## Add to Queue: the swipe, and the menus' one item (2026-11-16)

James: "Can we also add swiping to add to queue", then "it should be intelligent so the first swipe is play next, and
then the next would be play last. In fact I'd prefer if instead of next and last, we could just use 'add to queue' that
just puts it at the end of the queue." Asked whether the ••• menus should change to match, he chose **"Only Add to
Queue"**: every ••• on the phone offers one item where it had Play Next and Play Last. The web app keeps both. The app
stays 0.13 (13); src/__init__.py untouched; no server change; the engine files (QueueController, UpNext) have no diff.

### What Add to Queue is

**The web's Play Last, under the phone's own word** - checked first, because the ask depends on it: `withLast` inserts
at `layout(queue, state).addedEnd`, past the song playing's Repeat One copies and every `.added` unit after them (the
group Up Next draws as Playing Next), so each song added goes after the ones already added and still ahead of the
album, playlist or shuffle; with none added it lands at `copiesEnd`, straight after the song playing - it plays next.
That is exactly "the first swipe is play next, then the next play last", and Spotify's Add to queue. With nothing
playing (or a queue played out) `QueueController.addSongs` plays the songs instead, as Play Next did.

**Where it isn't strict order** (found in review; the engine left as it is, docs/ios.md "Adding to the queue" says
both and checks 401-402 ask after them, `AddToQueueOrderTests` holds them):
- **After a roll-back** (Previous, or a History row tapped): `addedEnd` counts only the `.added` units straight after
  the song playing's copies. Going back leaves the songs added after the song gone back from, so a song added then
  lands before them. An album of 6 played to song 5, a and b added, Previous at 1 s: 4 plays, then [5, a, b, 6]; c
  added: [c, 5, a, b, 6]. The web's Play Last (layoutAt, the same port) does the same.
- **In a song's last ~2.5 s** (D4): the next song is already scheduled on a player node, `replaceUpcoming` refuses,
  and the controller holds the add and makes it at the join, against the queue then - so it lands after the song that
  was next, not straight after the one ending. With an added song next, the order comes out as usual.

- **Core** (`ios/DeadwaxKit/Sources/DeadwaxCore/AddToQueue.swift`): `AddToQueue.words` ("Add to Queue", title case as
  the menus' other words), `choice` (`.last`), `symbol` (Play Last's, `DownloadWords.playLastSymbol`), `fill` and
  `glyph` (below), and **`AddToQueue.pick(_:online:gone:here:)` - the one rule** for both the ••• and the swipe:
  the pick while deadwax answers; offline, or for an album gone from the collection, only its songs on this phone in
  their order; none, or no songs at all: nil (not offered). It is QueueMenu's old private `playable` moved into Core,
  so the menu and the row can't drift. `QueueSwipe` holds the hand-drawn swipe's numbers and decisions (below).
- **One call**: `PlayerModel.addToQueue(_:album:)` = `choose(AddToQueue.choice, …)` - the path the menu's Play Last
  took (`QueuePick.choose` at the level an album's ••• or a song's says, Levels' QueuedHow, the album or the playlist's
  stubs remembered, the songs shelved, the notice when the music didn't start, the retry kept). The menu, the swipe and
  the swipe's VoiceOver action all call it, through `QueueAdder` (AddToQueueSwipe.swift), which asks `AddToQueue.pick`
  again at the moment of the add.
- **The menus** (`QueueMenu`): one Button, `AddToQueue.words` with `AddToQueue.symbol`, then Add to a playlist… in the
  same titled section - the order fixed, Add to Queue first. Every ••• is a `QueueMenu` (a song row's on an album, a
  playlist, Songs and Search; an album's and a playlist's bar •••), so every one changed at once. Now Playing's ••• never
  had Play Next or Play Last.

### The swipe

**Where**: every row whose ••• is a `QueueMenu` with Add to Queue offered - the song rows of an album's page
(`TrackRow`), a playlist's (`PlaylistSongRow`), the Library's Songs page and All songs (`SongRow`), and Search's library
songs (`SearchRowView`'s `.song`, Top results included). Each passes its own •••'s `QueueMenuRequest` (pick, album,
`gone`), so the swipe adds exactly what that ••• would. **No album or playlist row in a list has a ••• today** (the
Library's, Artists' and Search's album rows, Playlists' rows), so none gets a swipe; one that gains a `QueueMenu` gets
it by passing its request. Not on Up Next's rows, the grids' tiles, MusicBrainz's songs (no •••), a playlist in Edit
(its edit rows are others), or a song the rule leaves out.

**Two mechanisms, one look**:
- **A List's row** (album, playlist) takes SwiftUI's `.swipeActions(edge: .leading, allowsFullSwipe: true)` - one
  Button, `Label(AddToQueue.words, systemImage: AddToQueue.symbol)`, `.tint(Palette.queueSwipe)`. UIKit's own swipe:
  it already lives with the List's scroll, the back swipe and the pull to shuffle (which reads scroll geometry and
  phase, no gesture of its own), and closes on any touch. Its VoiceOver action belongs to the row, which is two
  elements (the song's button and the •••), so the song's element carries `addToQueueAction` too (after review).
- **A ScrollView's stack** (Songs, Search: `.swipeActions` does nothing there) is drawn by hand, `HandSwipe` over Core's
  `QueueSwipe`: the row follows the finger rightwards (`moved`, never left of shut, never past the row); past half the
  row (`fullAt`: max(2 x 74, half the width)) a light tick, and letting go there adds (`release` -> `.add`); let go with
  the button half out or more, or flung right (500 pt/s), and it stands open on one 74 pt button; less, or flung left,
  it shuts. Standing open, a tap on the button adds, and a tap on the row (swallowed - it plays or opens nothing), a
  swipe back, another row opening (`OpenQueueSwipe`, one open row in the app), the row moving on screen (a scroll,
  rows landing above, the Library's page turning: `onGeometryChange` of its global frame's origin), a touch going down
  anywhere outside its band (`TouchDown`, below) or its list's songs changing (`shutsQueueSwipes`) shuts it. Drawn as
  a List cell's: the purple from the screen's edge (`inset` 16, the stacks' own padding) to `offset`, the symbol in
  its last 74 pt, beside the row - which keeps its 16 pt gap, as a cell's content keeps its inset; always in the row's
  background, so it shrinks with the row as it shuts (no width and no hits while shut). Opening and shutting slide
  (`.snappy`, 0.25 s), at once under Reduce Motion. VoiceOver: every row puts `.accessibilityActions { Add to Queue }`
  on its song's own element (the opener, the song's button) via `addToQueueAction`, offered by the same rule; the
  drawn button is hidden from it.
- **The pan is UIKit's** (`UIGestureRecognizerRepresentable`, iOS 18), because it can refuse to begin: its delegate's
  `gestureRecognizerShouldBegin` is `QueueSwipe.begins` - sideways more than up or down (so the list's vertical pan
  keeps every vertical touch), rightwards, or leftwards only while open, and never from within 24 pt of the screen's
  left edge (`backEdge`: UIKit's edge back swipe, which this never makes wait). `shouldBeRequiredToFailBy` makes every
  other UIPanGestureRecognizer on the same touch wait for the row's to begin or fail, but two: a
  UIScreenEdgePanGestureRecognizer (the edge back swipe) and a scroll view that scrolls only up and down (the list's
  own, as wide as its content). It isn't only sideways pans, then: iOS 26's back swipe from a page's content and a
  horizontally scrolling scroll view's pan - the Library's pager (below) - are the ones meant, but any other pan
  above the row (a SwiftUI drag, if SwiftUI makes it one) waits too - for no longer than the row's pan takes to decide,
  its first few points, where `begins` refuses anything not sideways-rightwards (or leftwards on an open row) from away
  from the edge. A SwiftUI DragGesture can't refuse that way inside a ScrollView (as `.gesture` it takes the scroll's
  touches on iOS 18; as `.simultaneousGesture` both move - SwiftUI's behaviour as known, not measured here).
- **A touch elsewhere** (`TouchDown`, after review): while a hand-swiped row stands open (or is being swiped) its
  pan's coordinator puts a gesture recognizer on the window that only watches touches go down - it fails as each
  begins, never cancels or delays a touch, and recognizes beside every other - and a touch outside the row's band
  (its global frame's top to bottom) shuts the row, as a List's row shuts on any touch. Inside the band the row's own
  views decide (the button adds, the row's overlay shuts). Taken off the window as the row shuts; one whose row went
  without shutting takes itself off at its next touch. Touches in another window (the keyboard's) aren't seen.
- **Why not Lists for Songs and Search**: both would have had to be re-laid-out as List rows - Search's sections, slots,
  More buttons and disclosures most of all, its rows inside other views' bodies - and "styled to look exactly as they
  do now" checked on nothing but the phone. The hand swipe changes nothing about how either screen looks at rest.

### Decided here, and where the phone departs from the web

- **The purple is the primary button's, not the tint**: `AddToQueue.fill` is `PrimaryButton.bottom` (#8a2ee0, the
  foot of --dw-primary-bg) under a white symbol, 5.9:1. The app's tint (#C084FC) under white is 2.64:1 - the very pair
  James couldn't see on the album page's Play (Phase 4, slice 3b), and SwiftUI draws a swipe action's label white.
  `Palette.queueSwipe` / `onQueueSwipe` carry it to both mechanisms.
- **The confirmation is the menu's own**: the notice the menu's Play Last said, "Added to Up Next: Roads" (`queuedWords`,
  held to the web's fixture), over the mini player for 5 s and announced to VoiceOver by `PlayerModel.say`; nothing when
  the music starts from it (the mini player says so). Plus `.sensoryFeedback(.success)` when something was queued, on
  both mechanisms, and the hand swipe's light tick at the full-swipe line. The notice's "Up Next" is the screen's name;
  "Added to Queue: Roads" would be the phone departing from the web's words again - left for James.
- **The Library's Songs page** (logins off, a page of the horizontal pager): a swipe right that starts on a song adds
  it, as on every other song list, and the pager waits for the row's pan to fail; a swipe left (the row's fails at
  once while shut) and a swipe from the screen's left edge turn the page. With most of that page rows, turning back a
  page is by the edge or the switch there. The other way round (the pager winning, no swipe on that page) is one line
  in `shouldBeRequiredToFailBy`; docs/ios.md check 398 asks James.
- **iOS 17**: no hand swipe (UIGestureRecognizerRepresentable is iOS 18); the rows keep their VoiceOver action and •••.
  The List rows swipe on 17 too.
- **Play Next stays in Core and the engine** (`QueueChoice.next`, `withNext`, `QueueController.playNext` and its tests,
  the history and resume vectors that drive it, the web's fixture) and `PlayerModel.playNext` stays beside
  `addToQueue`; nothing in the app calls either now.
- **Held against the web, on purpose**: `ScreenQueueTests.thePhonesOneItemIsTheWebsPlayLast` - the fixture's items are
  still the web's ["Play Next", "Play Last"], the phone's one is the web's Play Last (`AddToQueue.choice.label` is the
  fixture's second item) under a word the web hasn't got, and every fixture drive of the web's Play Last (its call, each
  song's level, the albums remembered, the notice) is what `choose(AddToQueue.choice, …)` answers. The fixture and
  `theMenusWordsAreTheWebs` are untouched: `QueuedHow.label` is still the web's two words, which the phone no longer
  draws.
- **Normalization's Automatic line** names the phone's item: "…a song you add with Add to Queue…" (`Normalization
  .addedWith`), where the web's says "with Play Next". `LevelsTests.theChoicesAreTheWebsWordsButOffsClause` holds it as
  it holds Off's dropped clause: the web's line must still say "with Play Next", and the phone's is the web's with that
  phrase swapped - so a change to the web's line fails until it's looked at. No exporter or sim reads the phone's
  words for either, so neither needed a change.

### Tests

- **AddToQueueTests** (new, 6): the words, choice and symbol; that it is Play Last's call, level, albums and notice;
  online every pick whole; offline and gone only the songs here, in order, label and level kept, a song not here not
  offered; no songs never offered; the purple's 5.9:1 against the tint's under 3:1.
- **QueueSwipeTests** (new, 5): a pan is the row's only sideways (vertical, diagonal and leftwards-when-shut refused,
  leftwards-when-open taken); the screen's edge is the back swipe's; the row follows the finger rightwards only; the
  full swipe is half the row, never under twice the button; letting go (add, open, shut, flings, a fling never adds) -
  and the fling's bounds exactly: 500 pt/s either way is a fling, 499.9 isn't (after review: `<` for `<=` or `>` for
  `>=` in `release` passed every test before; each now fails `lettingGo`, tried both ways).
- **AddToQueueOrderTests** (new, 6, in QueueControllerTests over the fake engine): the first plays next and each after
  it in the order added, an album's songs after them, the engine's entries the same; once the added are playing, the
  next goes after those still waiting, and with none waiting plays next again; with nothing playing the first plays;
  Repeat One's copies stay ahead, where Play Next put songs too; and (after review) the two places it isn't strict
  order - after Previous [c, 5, a, b, 6], and added in a song's last seconds after the next song.
- **SongsTests.aRowIsKnownByItsSongNotItsPlace** (after review): `SongsList.rowKeys` - a song replaced in place is
  another row, a song twice is two rows, no id passes for another's second time, a page landing leaves the rows above.
- **ScreenQueueTests.thePhonesOneItemIsTheWebsPlayLast** and the Automatic line in **LevelsTests** (above).

### After review (16 Nov)

A review of the first commit found nothing serious; each point fixed in a second commit:
- **Reduce Motion**: the hand swipe's open and shut animated regardless. Now `settle(at:)` sets the offset at once
  under `accessibilityReduceMotion`, as LibraryTop, the pager, the EQ and PullShuffle do. (The List rows' motion is
  iOS's own.)
- **The order's two exceptions** (above): said plainly in docs/ios.md instead of promising strict order; checks 401
  and 402; two tests. The engine is unchanged.
- **An open row could carry over to another song on Songs**: rows were keyed by place (`\.offset`) and the open state
  is a row's `@State`, so Refresh's first page replacing the list in place left row 3 open on whatever song was now
  third, its button adding that song - the minY watcher never fired, nothing having moved. Rows are now keyed by
  `SongsList.rows` (the song, and which time it appears - a song can be in a page twice), and `shutsQueueSwipes(on:)`
  on the Songs scroll view shuts any open row when the songs' ids change (`OpenQueueSwipe.shutAll`). Search's rows
  were keyed by `row.key` already. Check 403.
- **The fling mutation** (Tests, above).
- **VoiceOver on the List rows** rested on SwiftUI handing the row's swipe action to the song's element. Now the song's
  button in `TrackRow` and `PlaylistSongRow` carries `addToQueueAction` itself. Whether iOS also lists its own (from
  the swipe) on that element - which would make two - can't be told from here: check 400 says to expect it at least
  once, possibly twice, and to say if twice (then ours goes).
- **iOS 17**: docs/ios.md says where the swipe is that the Songs, All songs and Search rows have none below iOS 18.
- **The purple disappeared on shutting** rather than shrinking with the row (it was drawn only while `offset > 0`,
  so it went with the shut's first frame). It is now always in the background, `offset` wide, `allowsHitTesting`
  only while open.
- **An open stack row stayed open through touches elsewhere**: now `TouchDown` (The swipe, above) and the origin
  watcher (a page turn moves the row sideways, which the old minY watcher missed).
- **`shouldBeRequiredToFailBy`'s comment** said sideways pans; it is every pan but the two (The swipe, above). The
  comment and these notes now say so; the behaviour is unchanged.
- **The success haptic with nothing queued**: `PlayerModel.choose` answered true when no engine could be made (older
  than Add to Queue - its only reader is `QueueAdder`). It answers false now; no engine file touched.
- **Check 395** promised a tick at halfway on every row; on an album's and a playlist's page the swipe is UIKit's, its
  full-swipe point and any tick its own. Reworded.
- The notice still reads "Added to Up Next: …" - James hasn't said.

### Verified, and not

Verified on the Mac, after the rebase onto 67480d5 and the review's fixes: `swift test` (all of it, passing: 1855
tests in Core's 196 suites, and 12 and 158 in the others); the unsigned generic-iOS Debug build, BUILD SUCCEEDED, no
warning in the files touched; tests/test_ios*.py with tests/test_source_bytes.py (400 passed, 1 skipped); all 93 sims
on Node 22 (iosartistmanage's among them). The order was read from `withLast` and `layoutAt` and is held by the tests
above.

Not verified - only the phone can tell (docs/ios.md checks 392-403): the swipe's feel on a real finger on all four
screens, and that the List's and the hand-drawn swipe look and feel alike; that vertical scrolling, a row's tap and its
•••, the pull to shuffle, the edge back swipe (and iOS 26's content back swipe) are untouched; that SwiftUI keeps the
coordinator as the pan's delegate and the pager really waits; that `TouchDown` on the window shuts an open row and
leaves the touch to what it was for; Reduce Motion; the haptics; VoiceOver's Add to Queue on each row's song (once or
twice on a List row).

## Needs a look on the phone (Phase 8, slice 6 - 2026-11-16)

The spec's section 5, with 3.1-3.2's queue mode (notes/ios-specs/phase8-managing.md): Settings > Manage > **Needs a
look** is the app's own page now, the review queue with its facets, each album opening Edit album in queue mode, and
the count as the row's value. Built on the `ios` branch at 375b3cf (Add to Queue after its review). The app stays 0.13
(13); src/__init__.py untouched; no server or web change; the player engine has no diff.

James's two decisions, kept: the count is on Settings > Manage's row only, never on a tab; and "It's fine as it is"
shows only with Look after the library - which main already does (EditPanel.tsx's `const fine = marksFine(permissions)`
since 2.1.29) and the phone's Edit album already did (AlbumEdit.marksFine, slice 1), so nothing changed for it here.

### Core (DeadwaxCore)

- **NeedsLook.swift** (new): lib/needsLook.ts as it is - `facets` (All; Newly added; one per kind of issue, the most
  albums first and then by label under the web's collation, a JS Map's first-set order breaking ties; Marked fine),
  `facetAlbums`, `facetShown`, `summaryTotal`, `isIgnoredOnly`, the session (`Session`, `SessionRow`, `startSession`,
  `markFor`, `FolderChange`, `rowChanged` - the current row first, as two rows share a path after a disc folder
  merges - `StepTarget`, `stepTarget`, `leavingAtEnd`), `RowMark` and its words, `ignoresUnsaved`, `navidromeNote`
  (Navidrome's own words for whoever runs deadwax only), `label` (needsLookLabel) and the page's sentences.
  NeedsALook.tsx's own rules beside them - `DrawnRow`, `Ending` (`ending`, `released`), `real`, `facetGivenUp`,
  `readsAgain`, `asRows`, `sessionRows`, `drawn`, `chips`, `showing`, `pressed`, `rows`, `title`, `byline`, `chipWords`,
  `markedFineTitle`, `lead`, the `state` and `status` ladders; MetadataEditor.tsx's queue footer as `Nav` (`place`,
  `back`, `on`, `done`, `nextAlbum`, `forward`); the phone's own words (`NeedsLookWords`: the Show menu, its header,
  the bar, a step said, a row read once); `chip(_:pressed:)` (the header's chip) and `lists(_:)` (the scan's paths as
  go()'s `Set.has` - code unit by code unit, never Swift's canonical equivalence). `QueueSummary` and `QueueReviewed`,
  read loosely (`tracking_enabled` absent is true, as the web reads it); `QueueCount`, useQueueSummary.ts's rule (one
  request out, one more after it when asked meanwhile, a failure keeping the number, nothing while unknown, never
  without Look after the library); `queueSummary()` and `markReviewed(path:)` (QueueMarkBody with no `issues` key).
- **ScanAlbums.swift**: ScanAlbum's `severity` and `disc_label`; ScanAnswer's `review_tracking_enabled` and
  `navidrome_check` (`NavidromeCheck`); MetadataQueue's `isNewImport` and `queueAlbums` (metadataQueue.ts: new imports
  first, then severity, artist, album - the web's collation - and the scan's order).
- **Managing.swift**: `asksQueueSummary` (permissions.ts), `needsLook` (App.tsx's `allowed` and `canEdit`),
  `Tool.native` (Edit an album and Needs a look), and the footer's `othersOpen(_:)` naming every native row drawn
  ("Edit an album and Needs a look are the app's own; …").
- **Routes.swift**: `queueSummary` (GET, 30 s) and `queueReviewed` (POST, 20 s) - 88 routes.

### The app (ios/App/Manage/, and Edit album's queue mode)

- **QueueCountModel** (new): the count, asked through QueueCount - only while Settings' root or Needs a look shows
  (since the review, below): as either comes on screen, on either's pull, back from the background with one up, when
  Look after the library becomes the person's, and after every managing write (`AppNavigation.managed()`, MainTabs'
  onChange of `managingWrites`): Edit album's `told` (every apply, Tags' apply, the cover alone, a Get, a delete, a
  mark), an album noted as looked at, and the artist tools' Save and Move. A ticket per person; `reset` with the rest
  when the person changes. Nothing polls.
- **ManageSection**: Needs a look pushes `AppRoute.needsALook`, its count as a `LabeledContent` value ("99+" past 99,
  nothing at 0 or unknown), read once by VoiceOver as `count.spoken`.
- **NeedsLookModel** (new): the page's state - its own LibraryScanModel (`GET /library/albums?tracks=false` with its
  ETag; READ_FAILED words for a first read, CHECK_FAILED after), the facet chosen, the session, the facets held, the
  ending, and `steps`. The first read as the page shows; again underneath as it shows anew (another tab and back, the
  app back in front, deadwax back in reach) with no session and no ending (readsAgain). `settle()` after any read of the
  scan ends - the page's or the editor's (the screen's onChange of `scan.reading`) - lets an ending go and gives up an
  emptied facet. `open` begins a session and opens Edit album over the tabs with the request's `queue`; `heard` takes
  the editor's FolderChange; `go(by:gate:)` notes the album left (`markReviewed`, then the count), steps (the step
  said to VoiceOver) or ends the session and closes the sheet; `editorClosed` ends it however the sheet went. The
  ending's read waits for the note, as the web's does. Nothing past a sign-out (`samePerson`). Since the review every
  move of the session is Core's `NeedsLook.Run`, carried out by `carry` (below).
- **NeedsLookScreen** (new): the lead (by Edit albums), NEEDS_EDIT, the ignores warning; the state ladder; the list's
  header (the facet and its count) over the status line, a line held even when empty; rows keyed by the path they
  were listed at, each `NeedsLookRow` (FolderCover, the title, the byline, its words in amber - or its mark in green,
  the row faded), the open one shaded; Show as a toolbar Menu with a Picker. Without Look after the library,
  NO_PERMISSION and nothing asked; opened out of reach and unread, Managing needs deadwax; out of reach with a list,
  rows off. Reduce Motion takes the list's animations away.
- **AlbumEditRequest** carries `queue` (equal by its id); **EditAlbumModel** takes the session's folder and the page's
  scan (`target:`, `scan:`) in queue mode, tells the page and the count after every write (`told`), keeps a deleted
  folder's sheet up in queue mode (`deletedPath`, "Deleted …" from AlbumEdit.status), and has `stepGate` and
  `canStep` (since the review, below). **EditAlbumSheet** in queue mode: `.task(id: queue.steps)` builds the next
  album's model in the same sheet (its pages popped); a bottom bar on the root - ‹, "2 of 9", Skip › / Next album › -
  off unless `canStep`; a step over typed work asks Discard changes? (`pendingStep`); a delete pops to the root
  instead of closing. The session ended with `.onDisappear` until the review; now where the sheet is dismissed.

### Decided here, and where the phone departs from the spec (or the web)

- **NeedsALook.tsx's own rules stay in the .tsx, held by pattern**, as slices 2-5 did: the pieces read out of
  NeedsALook.tsx, MetadataEditor.tsx, You.tsx, useQueueSummary.ts and App.tsx (each hashed into made_from - the sim
  fails when one changes) and run as written where they are expressions. Moving them into lib/needsLook.ts is a small
  no-change refactor on main whenever wanted.
- **The real scan only, never the saved one first** (the web's useLibrary draws `snapshot=true` at once, then the real
  scan): the phone's managing shows nothing stale as live (LibraryScanModel, slice 1), so `stale` is always false and
  the status line's "Checking the library…" is a read again under a list, never a saved scan's.
- **The page's own count never stands in for the server's** (setPageQueueCount): the row isn't on screen while the
  page is, and the count is asked again as Settings shows.
- **Not asked when a download is filed** (App.tsx's `onAlbumsFiled`): the phone's Requests don't say so to the
  Settings tab; the count is asked again the next time Settings shows, which is the only place it's drawn.
- **"Marked fine", not "Ignored"**: the spec's check 350 says Ignored; the web renamed it (2.0.8) and the phone says
  the web's word.
- **Skip becomes Next album once any write was told of the album** (a mark, an apply, tags, a Get, a delete), where the
  web's Apply becomes Next after a release applied and its delete shows a Next album button: one rule for every write,
  from the session's own `heard` and `mark`. The last album keeps Skip, off, as the web's keeps its plain buttons.
- **A delete leaves the sheet up** saying "Deleted …", with Next album (the web's folder request after a delete); the
  spec said the editor moves on.
- **The bar is on Edit album's first page only**: a pushed page (Release, Tags, …) has its own back; stepping from deep
  in would throw its state away unseen.
- **A step is off while a write or a mark runs and out of reach** - since the review, until everything done to the
  album has settled (Core's StepGate, below) - and over typed work asks Discard changes? first: the web's footer steps
  whatever is typed, whatever is under way.
- **The count is asked only while Settings or Needs a look shows** (since the review, below), where the web asks it as
  the page comes back from hidden and after every Edit panel change, whatever shows.
- **A note that fails is said nowhere**, as the web's isn't: the album stays new and comes back.
- **Show is a menu**, the web's chips its items with their counts; a chip's hint (its title) isn't shown.
- **"›", not "▷"**: the web's arrows are drawn glyphs; the phone's words use the chevron the bar's ‹ matches.
- **Navidrome's note wraps** where the web keeps it to one line with the rest in its title: the phone has no title.
- **The care exporter holds asksQueueSummary and the page's permissions** rather than the managing one, so one fixture
  holds the whole slice.

### After review (16 Nov)

The review of 4c67368 found nothing that loses data, but two real queue-mode bugs and a gap in the tests.

- **A step could go between a write ending and its follow-up read.** `canStep` was `online && !writing && !marking`,
  and an apply clears `applying` before it awaits the folder's read and tells the page (the cover alone, Tags' apply, a
  Get and an unanswered delete the same). A Skip in that gap sent the note for the old path, the next album's open
  bumped the scan's ticket so the old read was dropped, `told` then sent a stale album (its Fixed lost), and ‹ could
  open a folder that had gone. Now **Core's `NeedsLook.StepGate`** decides - shut out of reach, while a write or a mark
  or its follow-up runs (`EditAlbumModel.following`, held by each of apply, saveCoverOnly, applyTags, get, delete and
  mark from before they send until `told` has run), while the scan is read, while Release or Tags waits for a read
  (`needsRead`, which a failed read keeps - Look again opens it), and while a delete that never answered waits for the
  read that says whether it went (`unansweredDelete`, now watched). `canStep` is `stepGate.open`; the step itself
  takes the gate as it is at that moment (`go(by:gate:)`), so Discard - asked before a write began - is checked again
  when pressed.
- **A full-screen cover from Edit album could end the session.** The sheet's `.onDisappear` ended it, and presenting a
  `.fullScreenCover` over the sheet (Compare covers, the cover or CD art full size, a track's picture) takes the sheet's
  content off screen. The session now ends where the sheet really goes: MainTabs' `.sheet(item:onDismiss:)` calls
  `AppNavigation.editorDismissed()`, which tells the queue of the editor last presented (`presentedEdit`) unless that
  same opening is still up; Close (and Discard over it) ends it before dismissing; `editAlbum` in place of another
  opening (up, or going with its onDismiss yet to come) ends that one's, unless it is the same page's new session -
  which its Run began only once the last had ended; a sign-out ends it after `session += 1`, so nothing is noted, read
  or asked for the next person; a step to an album gone ends it and closes the sheet. However many say so, the Run ends
  it once.
- **The session controller is Core's, and tested** (`NeedsLook.Run`): `begin` (no session while one lasts or an
  ending's rows are held), `heard`, `step(by:gate:present:live:)`, `closed`, `facetChosen`, `endingRead(ticket)` and
  `settle(reading:)`, each move answered as an `After` - the album to note, stepped, the ending's ticket, close the
  editor. NeedsLookModel holds a Run and only carries each After out (`carry`): the note sent, then the count; the
  editor closed; the ending's read once the note is written, then `endingRead`. NeedsLookTests run it by hand, and
  CareVectorTests replays all 90 of the web's sessions through it - every note the web's `leaving`, every end once.
- **QueueCount's failure path** has its own test (an ask queued meanwhile goes after a failed one, as the web's
  `finally` sends it), and the facets' first-set tiebreak its vectors: a `same` set of issue words, two facets of one
  label and count met in each order (seeded on their own, so every other vector is as it was).
- **The exporter reads a row's chip order out of NeedsALook.tsx**: the whole chips block hashed (`a row's chips, in
  order`), the mark first standing in for the rest, and New, the issues and Marked fine put in the order they sit
  there - no longer written by hand.
- **The count is asked only while a page that uses it shows** - Settings' root or Needs a look (QueueCountModel's
  `shows`/`hides`): as one comes on screen (once, however often SwiftUI says it appeared), on either's pull (Settings
  asks before /me, so Look after the library given by its answer asks once, not twice), back from the background with
  one up (`scene` - not a launch's inactive-to-active), and on `changed()` - a managing write, an album noted, Look
  after the library given - while one is up. MainTabs' `initial: true` permission ask and its every-tab foreground ask
  are gone. **A departure from the web**, which asks as the page comes back from hidden and after every Edit panel
  change whatever shows: the phone draws the count in one place, and opening Settings asks it.
- **The page out of reach**: the list keeps under the editor's amber line (`.editOutOfReach`), its rows off, and a pull
  asks nothing (`pulled()` guards `online`); back in reach with no editor open on a session, the library is read again
  (`reach`). A session's editor reads on coming back itself - the same scan.
- **Each failure in its own place's words**: LibraryScanModel keeps the read's error (`failed`), `failure` says it in
  the editor's words (READ_FAILED's "Couldn't read the library.") and `failure(saying:)` in another's - the page's
  `failure` is READ_FAILED before anything is read and CHECK_FAILED over a list, so the page's status line never shows
  the editor's sentence after an editor's read fails. (The `failed:` parameter added in 4c67368 is gone.)
- **A mark follows the outcome rule** (RetagFlow.outcome): only a 4xx is a refusal, said under the buttons; no answer
  or a 5xx may have been kept - said as maybe finished (a 5xx's own words under the buttons when it has them), the
  folder read again and the session and the count told what that read shows, as an answered mark is.
- **Check 354 reworded** (Apply is on the pushed Release page, the bar on the root only: Apply, then back to the first
  page, the steps dimmed until it has been read again), **351 gains the full-screen cover** (opened and closed, the bar
  and "2 of N" still there), 349 the count asked as Settings opens after a change made on another tab, and 354 the
  page out of reach. Still 349-354: 355 is slice 7's.

Mutations, each applied alone and each failing a test now: in Core, a step dropping its note, an end always noting
nothing, the editor closing with no note, a session begun while an ending is held, a step ignoring the gate, the gate
ignoring the scan's read, a second close ending again, `QueueCount.failed()` dropping an ask queued meanwhile, and the
facets' tiebreak reversed (NeedsLookTests, CareVectorTests); in the App, the note dropped in `carry`, a step not carried
out, `editorClosed` not carrying the Run's end, each of the gate's five inputs left out, Discard stepping without the
gate, the sheet's content disappearing ending the session, the count asked at start-up on any tab, and a mark's 5xx said
as a refusal (tests/test_ios_needs_look.py - source pins, as the App target has no tests of its own).

Tests: NeedsLookTests 15 (7 more: the Run one session at a time, a step's note, a step to an album gone, ending once
however the editor goes, only the newest ending's read, no step through a shut gate, a failed count with one queued);
CareVectorTests 11 (the sessions through the Run); tests/test_ios_needs_look.py 14 (6 more: the count only while a page
that uses it shows, a mark judged as a write, the page's own words and its out-of-reach line, the gate's inputs and
`following`, the page carrying out the Run, the session ending at the sheet's dismissal); test_ios_edit.py and
test_ios_settings.py follow the onDismiss, Discard's gate and the pull's order.

Verified on the Mac: the unsigned generic-iOS Debug build (BUILD SUCCEEDED, no warning), `swift test` (1881 Core tests
in 198 suites, 158 Audio in 17, 12 more, all passing), the full pytest suite (4881 passed, 1 skipped) and all 94 sims
with Node 22 (ioscare's `--check` over the regenerated fixture). Not verified - only the phone can tell: that
`.sheet(item:onDismiss:)` fires once for every way the sheet goes (a swipe, Close, Discard, `albumEdit = nil`) and never
for a full-screen cover over it; that SwiftUI calls Settings' and Needs a look's onAppear/onDisappear as the count's
`showing` assumes (a push, a pop, another tab, Now Playing's full-screen cover); the steps coming back on as each
write's read lands; and checks 349-354 as reworded.

## Library care on the phone (Phase 8, slice 7 - 2026-11-16)

The spec's section 6 (notes/ios-specs/phase8-managing.md), with 12's change A (the rescan without its tracks, on main
since 2.1.28): Settings > Manage > **Library care** is the app's own page now - Rescan, the runs that fetch covers, CD
art and lyrics for every album without, and In nobody's library pushed from it. Built on the `ios` branch at 460f049
(Needs a look after its review). The app stays 0.13 (13); src/__init__.py untouched; no server or web change; the player
engine has no diff.

### Core (DeadwaxCore)

- **LibraryCare.swift** (new). `BulkTargets` is lib/bulkTargets.ts: the kinds, `hasOwnDiscArt`, `targets`, `Run`
  (`startRun`), `Outcome`, `adding` (`addOutcome`), `outcome(LyricsSummary)` and `failedAs` (useLibraryCare.ts's lyrics
  step and a step that threw), `step(kind, album, failure:)` - a cover's or CD art's 404 is `missing`, any other 4xx a
  failure answered, a 5xx, no answer or a timeout `unanswered` (counted as failed, as the web counts it, but it may
  have written), a cancellation nothing - and `summary` (`bulkSummary`). `LibraryCare` is lib/libraryCare.ts and the
  page's own: the words, `careLine`, `narrow` (`narrowAlbums`, TypedMatch), `scopeWords`, `scopeLine`, `planWords`,
  `real`, `busy`, `targets`, `note`, `scopeNote`, `scanTotals` (groupAlbums' key, JavaScript's lower case),
  `formatAge`, `scanAge`, `facts`, `startLabel`, `stopLabel` - and the phone's own sentences (`stopped`,
  `screenOnNote`, `waiting`). **CareRuns** is every decision the page makes: one run at a time; a ticket per read, so
  `real` is "a read landed that began since deadwax was last out of reach", and a kind whose run wrote (or may have) is
  `behind` until a read begun after the run ended lands; `readsNow` (shown, in reach, nothing out; the first read, after
  a gap, for a kind behind, and shown again); `rescan` / `rescanEnded` (landed: the count told when the scan lists
  albums, as the web announces it; unanswered: may have finished, read again, then told; refused or dropped: nothing);
  `start` (its own targets asked again, so Start carries on with only the albums still without); `next` - the only way
  an album is asked for, so every stop lands after the album out: Stop, the app going to the background (`suspended`),
  deadwax out of reach (`reach`), Edit albums gone (`allowed`), the session ending (`sessionEnded`); `finished(step)`
  counting it and saying whether the count is told (it wrote, or may have); `result` (the web's summary, then the
  phone's stop sentence); `keepsScreenOn(visible:)`. `Managing.careParts` and `heldShown` (permissions.ts careParts;
  LibraryCare.tsx's `sessionMe()?.auth === 'on' && parts.held`). `Held` is HeldByNobody.tsx and myLibrary.ts: the
  words, `line`, `listed`, `flagWords`, `flagName`, `albumName`, `saidName`, `added`, `dismissed`, `listedAlbums`,
  `showLabel`; `Answer`, `UnheldAlbum` (so named because `Album` is Models.swift's, and the contract tests find structs
  by name), `Flag`, `Added`, `Dismissed`, all read loosely; and `Held.Flow` - one write at a time, never out of reach
  nor before a read to trust. The client's `rescan()` (`POST /library/rescan?tracks=false`, answered as `libraryScan`
  is, its ETag kept), `heldByNobody()`, `addFlagged(_:)`, `dismissFlag(_:)`.
- **ScanAlbums.swift**: ScanAlbum's `total_size` (the facts' size); ScanAnswer's `scanSeconds` from X-Scan-Seconds.
- **Managing.swift**: `Tool.native` is Edit an album, Needs a look and Library care, so the footer names three.
- **Routes.swift**: `rescan` (POST, query `tracks`, 300 s), `held` (GET, 30 s), `heldAdd` and `heldDismiss` (POST,
  20 s) - 92 routes.

### The app (ios/App/Manage/)

- **CareRunModel** (new), held by the app: DeadwaxApp makes it and puts it in the environment, resets it with the rest
  when the person changes, and Reachability's `whenChanged` tells it of reach; RootView's scene phase tells it of the
  background (RootView, not MainTabs: the tabs may be under the sign-in). Its own LibraryScanModel (the scan with its
  ETag, as Edit album and Needs a look read it), CareRuns, and a generation per person. It carries out what CareRuns
  decides and nothing else: reads when `readsNow` says (as the page shows, comes back to the front, deadwax comes
  back, a run or a rescan ends); Rescan through LibraryScanModel's new `rescan` (ticketed with the reads, so only the
  newest lands), "deadwax may have finished this - looking again" announced and the library read again when it never
  answered, then `navigation.managed()`; and `drive`: `next` -> the album's Get through the very client call Edit
  album's Get makes (`getCover(path:)`, `getDiscArt(_:)`, `getLyrics(_:)`, each with its own wait), held through the
  background by a BackgroundHold -> `finished` -> `managed()` when told; at the end the result announced and the library
  read for the kind left behind. The screen: `isIdleTimerDisabled = runs.keepsScreenOn(visible:)` at every change of
  the page showing, the app's phase and a run starting or ending - the only place the app touches it.
- **LibraryCareScreen** (new): the care line by the parts; NO_PERMISSION with neither part; Managing needs deadwax when
  opened out of reach before a read; the ladder (the problem, Reading the library, a first read failed with Try again);
  Rescan's section (the facts in a TimelineView every 30 s so the age moves on, a read again that failed with Try again,
  the button, RESCAN_WORDS as its footer); Narrow to and the scope note; a section per kind (Stop with a spinner and the
  screen-on note while it runs; else Start with its count - none to take, no button - dimmed while another runs, with
  "One run at a time - …"; its note; its result). In nobody's library is a row pushing `AppRoute.heldByNobody`. Out of
  reach over a read scan: Edit album's amber line, nothing pressable. Kinds keyed by kind; Reduce Motion drops the
  list's animations.
- **HeldByNobodyScreen** and its page-held **HeldModel** (new): the line, the first 20 albums (name, then folder, read
  once), Show all / Show fewer, the flags with Add for them (the primary face) and Dismiss, refused or failed words in an
  ErrorNote under them; read on showing, back in reach, back in front, on a pull, and after every write. A write goes
  through `Held.Flow.begin` (one at a time) under a BackgroundHold, its words announced; a 4xx says deadwax's words
  (EditWords.said over the web's failure words); any other end may have gone through - `writeFailure`, "deadwax may
  have finished this - looking again", and the read shows. Nothing past a sign-out (AppNavigation's session).
- **ManageSection** pushes `AppRoute.libraryCare` for `.care`; **Shared/Routes.swift** has the two routes and their
  destinations.

### What the web's .tsx files hold, read by pattern

As in slices 2-6, the page's own rules stay in the web's .tsx and the exporter reads each out (hashed into made_from,
so ioscare fails when one changes): from **app/LibraryCare.tsx** who the page is for (`parts.shown`), a scan to trust
(`real`), Rescan busy (`scanBusy`), Rescan refused while busy, a rescan telling the library, Try again never twice, the
facts, the scope note, the albums in scope, a kind's albums (`targets`), a kind's note, the Stop label, Stop else Start
with albums to take, Start's words, Stop pressed once, a kind's result, In nobody's library shown when, the state
ladder, a first read failed, a read again failed, Rescan and the runs by their parts, the line by the parts, neither
part, read again on showing, and the page's words (the title, Reading the library, Try again, the headings, Rescan and
Rescanning…, Narrow to and its prompt, Checking the library…); from **app/useLibraryCare.ts** a picture's step written
and failed (404 missing), the lyrics step, a step that threw counted, one run of a kind and never of none, Stop once, a
run that wrote left behind, stopped asked before each album, a run that wrote telling the library; from
**app/HeldByNobody.tsx** HELD_SHOWN, a flag's and an album's name, an album's folder, a flag's words, the name said,
what a write says, Show all and Show fewer and when, the albums listed, one write at a time, read again after each
write, the flags when, what is said and what is shown, and its words; from **lib/appRoutes.ts** MANAGING_ADMINS_ONLY
being NO_PERMISSION. Moving them into lib/libraryCare.ts is a small no-change refactor on main whenever wanted.

### Decided here, and where the phone departs from the spec (or the web)

- **One run at a time** (the web runs the three kinds at once): writes go one at a time on the phone, and three runs
  in parallel would triple what a suspension cuts short. The others' Start is dimmed, saying why.
- **The phone's own stops**, each said after the web's summary and naming the button that carries on ("Got 14 covers.
  Stopped at 14 of 60. It stopped as the app went to the background - Get covers carries on."): the background,
  deadwax out of reach, Edit albums gone (the runs' sections go with it, so that one is only announced), the session
  ended. The spec's sentence ("Stopped at 14 of 60 when the app went
  to the background - Start carries on.") is reworded so the web's own "Stopped at" stays as the web says it.
- **The session ending stops a run** (the phone's own): every album after a 401 would be refused too; the same person
  signing in again keeps the result, and Start carries on.
- **An album that never answered** (no answer, a timeout, a 5xx) counts as failed, as the web's catch counts it, but
  leaves its kind behind and tells the count: it may have written.
- **Rescan tells the count only when the scan lists albums** (the web's `if (albums.length)`); one that never answered
  is read again first, then tells.
- **A read again that failed is said under the runs** for someone with Edit albums but not Look after the library: the
  web shows it only in Rescan's section, so says it nowhere for them.
- **In nobody's library is a page pushed from a row** (the spec's), where the web draws it inline under the runs; its
  words are the web's - "Add for them", "Dismiss", "In nobody's library" - not the spec's "Add to their libraries", "Put
  away" and "Held by nobody" (the web renamed them in 2.0.8). Its writes don't tell Needs a look's count (the web
  announces nothing for them: they change who holds an album, not its tags or files).
- **The facts' age moves on** every 30 s while the page shows (the web's is drawn when the page renders).
- **No saved scan first**: as in slices 1 and 6, the phone never draws the saved scan, so `stale` is always false.
