### Verified, and not

On the Mac: `swift test` (1912 Core tests in 200 suites, 158 Audio in 17, 12 more, all passing); the unsigned
generic-iOS Debug build, BUILD SUCCEEDED, no warning; the full pytest suite, 4893 passed and 1 skipped (the palette
rules caught two things first: Add for them drawn `.borderedProminent`, now PrimaryFace, and three section headers
without Noto Sans); all 94 sims with Node 22 (ioscare running both exporters' `--check`). tests/test_ios_library_care.py
runs a real rescan over real FLACs and the real In nobody's library routes with logins on. Assumed: that 300 s is
ample for a rescan of James's library (the route has no bound; a first scan of a big library takes a minute or more,
and one that runs past it says deadwax may have finished it, and reads the library again), and that a BackgroundHold's seconds cover the
album out when the phone locks (a lyrics album can wait up to its own EditWaits.lyrics; one cut short is unanswered,
counted failed and may have written).

Not verified - only the phone can tell (docs/ios.md checks 355-360): `isIdleTimerDisabled` keeping the screen on
through a run with the page in front, and letting it sleep on another page; what iOS does to a run when the phone
locks mid-album (the hold, the stop after it, the sentence, Start carrying on); the rescan's facts and its age moving
on; Narrow to's counts against the web's; In nobody's library's Add for them and Dismiss on a real flag; the parts by
permission; SwiftUI's onAppear/onDisappear and RootView's scene phase as CareRunModel's `visible` assumes (a push over
the page, another tab, Now Playing's full-screen cover, the sign-in over the tabs); VoiceOver hearing each run's result
and the largest text; Reduce Motion.

### After review (16 Nov)

The review of ea9f7af (code read only) found three real bugs and seven smaller things; each was traced before it was
changed. One - a rescan's refusal - turned out to match the web, and is left as it is.

- **The page could stay on "Checking the library…" with no Start.** A read already out as a run ended had a ticket no
  newer than the run's (`behind[kind]`), so landing it kept the kind behind; one out as deadwax came back into reach had
  a ticket no newer than the gap, so `real` stayed false. Nothing asked again - `readsNow` had said no while it was
  out. Now `CareRunModel.read()` asks `readIfNeeded(again: false)` after every read that lands (under the generation
  guard), and CareRuns says read again exactly when the one that landed began too early. LibraryCareTests:
  `aReadOutAsARunEndsIsFollowedByOneToTrust`, `aReadOutAsDeadwaxComesBackIsFollowedByOneToTrust`.
- **A 403 mid-run didn't stop the run** (the phone's own departure from the web, written down here): an admin taking
  Edit albums away left the run asking album after album, each refused and counted failed, until /me happened to be
  read again. Core's `BulkTargets.Step` has a `.forbidden(Outcome)` for a 403: counted as the web counts it (failed -
  every track for lyrics; the vectors' 403 row still gives the web's count), told to nobody (nothing written), and
  `CareRuns.finished` stops the run with `.notAllowed` (Stop pressed first keeps its own word). The web's runBulk counts
  any throw as `failedAs` and carries on, so its run goes on refused to the end; the phone stops after the first, says
  "It stopped: running it needs Edit albums, which an admin hasn't given you.", and asks /me again
  (`server.refreshMe()`) so the runs leave the page. Every other 4xx carries on, as the web's. LibraryCareTests:
  `a403StopsTheRunAfterItsAlbumAndEveryOther4xxCarriesOn` (a table: 403, 400, 404, 409, 422, 500).
- **Under the sign-in over the app the page still counted as shown** (a ZStack overlay fires no onDisappear), so a
  scene or reach change read the library, got a 401 and left "Couldn't read the library just now." under the sign-in,
  with nothing to read again after it. `readIfNeeded` is now gated on `server.signInOver == nil`, and
  LibraryCareScreen's `.onChange(of: server.signInOver == nil)` calls `care.sessionBack()` (a read as shown again) when
  it clears. In nobody's library had the same problem - its scene and reach reads under the overlay - and has the
  same fix: HeldModel's `read()` asks nothing under it, and the screen reads again when it clears while visible.
  tests/test_ios_library_care.py pins both gates and both onChanges.
- **In nobody's library's buttons came back before the read after a write** (`Held.Flow.ended()` cleared `acting`
  while the re-read was out, so the flag just dealt with could be pressed again). `open` and `begin` take `reading`
  now, and the buttons stay off while any read of the list is out.
- **The ladder's words are the web's.** A failed read with no albums to show says READ_FAILED ("Couldn't read the
  library."), as the web's `library.error && !library.albums.length` does - it said REREAD_FAILED for a library read
  empty. Tracing it found a worse one, in Needs a look too (slice 6): the phone passed `scan.loaded` (an answer in hand)
  as the ladder's `loaded`, where the web's means a read has ended (useLibrary sets it in its `finally`), so **a failed
  first read showed the spinner for good**, with no Try again. LibraryScanModel has `ended` (an answer or a failure),
  both pages pass it, and both say READ_FAILED whenever there are no albums (Needs a look's CHECK_FAILED, Library care's
  REREAD_FAILED, over albums on screen). tests/test_ios_needs_look.py's pin moved with it.
- **A rescan's refusal stays in the read-again slot, Try again reading again** (not changed): the web's Rescan is
  `library.reload(true)`, whose error lands in `library.error` - drawn as REREAD_FAILED in Rescan's section, its Try
  again `reload(false)`, a plain read. The phone's is the same.
- **No `.cancelled` step or stop.** Nothing in the app cancels a run's request (the drive's Task is never cancelled,
  the transport is never invalidated, BackgroundHold's expiry only ends the hold), so `Step.cancelled` and
  `Stop.cancelled` were unreachable. A cancellation, should one come, is counted as an album that never answered -
  failed, as the web counts any throw, and it may have written. A missing client is no longer a step either: before
  each album the drive checks `server.client` beside the sign-in, and either one stops the run as the session ending
  (`sessionEnded`); the album is then fetched with that same client.
- **The writes' waits are pinned to the server.** Each store call opens its own connection, which may wait out SQLite's
  busy timeout (store._connect's `timeout=10`) first: the list's two calls stay 30 s, Add for them's five (the open
  flags, the album followed, the flag closed, the grants, the job's row) are 60 s (from 20), Dismiss's two 30 s (from
  20). tests/test_ios_library_care.py counts `await store.` in each handler and holds each wait to calls x busy + 10.
  The rescan has no server bound to pin to, so its 300 s is pinned as a value, with a comment saying so.
- **LibraryCareTests' lyrics wait is the real number**: 40 tracks are 4500 s (20 rounds x 220 s + 60, to the minute),
  and one track the route's 600 floor - not `>=` the floor, which held for anything.
- **docs/ios.md** checks 358 (a reach blip during the read; a session ended mid-run by a password reset in People, the
  sign-in, nothing left over after) and 360 (Edit albums taken away: the run stops at the next album by itself, with
  the count) say what the phone does now; the section says the 403 and the sign-in.

Verified after review, on the Mac: `swift test` (1915 Core tests in 200 suites - the three new above, the
cancellation one rewritten - 158 Audio in 17, 12 more, all passing); the unsigned generic-iOS Debug build, BUILD
SUCCEEDED, no warning; the full pytest suite, 4892 passed and 1 skipped, with one failure that was timing under load:
test_coverart_relay's pending-cap test (it ran beside `swift test` and xcodebuild; no server file changed here, and
that file passed 125 of 125 three times on its own); all 94 sims with Node 22, ioscare's `--check` among them (the
vectors are unchanged: the 403 row's count is the web's). Not verified - only the phone can tell: checks 358 (the
read after a reach blip, the session ended mid-run and signed in again) and 360 (a run stopping at the next album when
Edit albums is taken away, and /me read again taking the runs from the page).

### Needs a look and its count under the sign-in (16 Nov, from slice 7's review)

Library care's review found the page still counted as shown under the sign-in over the app; traced on Needs a look
(slice 6) and its count, the same was true, and each could ask:

- **NeedsLookScreen's reach and scene reads.** The sign-in is a ZStack layer over MainTabs, so nothing under it gets
  onDisappear: `.onChange(of: reachability.online)` (`model.reach`) and the scene coming back to the front
  (`model.shows`) read the library under it, got a 401 and left "Couldn't check the library just now." (or a failed
  first read) with nothing reading again after the sign-in. So could the page coming back on screen as Now Playing
  closes under the sign-in (RootView closes it as the sign-in comes: the page's `.task` runs again).
- **The steps.** Edit album is a `.sheet` on MainTabs, and a presented sheet sits above the root's ZStack, so (as
  SwiftUI presents it - not seen on a phone) the editor stays up over the sign-in: ‹, Skip, Next album and Close still
  reach `carry` - `review` (`POST /library/queue/reviewed`) and a session's ending read.
- **The count** (QueueCountModel): Settings and Needs a look stay in `showing` under the sign-in, so the scene coming
  back (`scene` -> `changed`), a page coming on screen as Now Playing closes (`shows`), or a write from the editor over
  it (`managingWrites`) asked `/library/queue/summary` - a 401, the old number kept, and nothing asking again after.

Gated as Library care's are, in the App (there is no rule of Core's to move: each is the App's own guard):
NeedsLookModel's `read()` - every read of the page's goes through it: reach, shows, the pull, Try again, an ending - and
`review()` ask nothing while `server.signInOver` is set (a read skipped is a read failed, a note skipped an album left
new, as a 401 would leave them); NeedsLookScreen's `.onChange(of: server.signInOver == nil)` calls
`model.signedInAgain()` while the page is visible - a read, unless Edit album is open on a session, whose scan this is
(as `reach`). QueueCountModel's `ask()` passes `allowed` false under it (QueueCount.ask then changes nothing), its run
loop treats a sign-in that came meanwhile as a failure (the one asked again waits), and MainTabs'
`.onChange(of: server.signInOver == nil)` calls `queueCount.changed()` as it goes - asked only with a page up that
uses it. tests/test_ios_needs_look.py pins each gate and both onChanges, and that the page has one scan read and one
note to gate.

Not touched, for the coordinator: Edit album itself over the sign-in. Its sheet (like the EQ's and Add to a playlist's)
stays up over it, so its own reads and writes can still be asked and refused with a 401 - RootView closes only Now
Playing as the sign-in comes. Whether to close the editor (losing anything typed) or gate its writes is Edit album's
decision, not this page's.

Verified on the Mac: `swift test` (1915 Core tests in 200 suites, 158 Audio in 17, 12 more, all passing - nothing of
Core changed); the unsigned generic-iOS Debug build, BUILD SUCCEEDED, no warning; the full pytest suite run alone,
4893 passed and 1 skipped (the cover-art relay's timing test with it, unloaded); all 94 sims with Node 22. Not
verified - only the phone can tell (docs/ios.md check 354): the page and the count under the sign-in, and the read
and the count after signing in again; and whether Edit album's sheet really stays up over the sign-in.

## Server settings on the phone (Phase 8, slice 8 - 2026-11-16)

The spec's section 7 (notes/ios-specs/phase8-managing.md), with 12-18's rules: Settings > Manage > **Server settings**
is the app's own page now - the web app's Connections (its You's three rows) at the top, the organizing verdict, and
the web's three tabs as sections whose groups each push a page of their own, saved together from a bar at the foot of
every one of them; Lyrics' page carries Re-time saved lyrics, MusicBrainz's saved answers' carries their size and
Clear; and the Library's **Set up Navidrome** opens Connections' page as a sheet over the Library rather than the web
app in Safari. Part A was main's **2.1.33** (44224c5, nothing a user sees: tabForGroup, tabMarks, retypeSecretNote with
RETYPE_WITH_ADDRESS, and editedEnvDraft moved from components/SettingsView.tsx into lib/serverSettings.ts word for
word, so the exporter can run them - notes/app-desktop.md "Server settings' rules, moved into lib/ (2.1.33)"); the
slice is built on the `ios` branch with it merged ("Merge main 2.1.33 into ios"). The app stays 0.13 (13);
src/__init__.py untouched; no server change; the player engine has no diff.

### Core (DeadwaxCore)

- **ServerSettings.swift** (new). The answer (`ServerSettingsAnswer`: groups, settings, the organizing verdict) read
  loosely, each setting's `choices` put in the web's order: the body is read once more as ordered JSON and each choice
  map rebuilt as `JSON.parse` and `Object.entries` would leave it - a key written twice keeps its first place and its
  last value, and array-index keys ("0", "12") come first, ascending (`jsOrder`), whatever order deadwax wrote them in.
  `ServerSettings` is lib/serverSettings.ts and the pages' own: the tabs and their hints, `tab(forGroup:)`, `tabMarks`
  and the phone's `groupMarks` (the same rule taken per group - the Organizing group carries the verdict's attention),
  `sections`, the drafts (`Drafts`: typed values and reverts in the order made; `edited` - editedEnvDraft, a value typed
  back to what is saved is no draft - `reverted`, `afterSave`, the phone's `stillDiffering`), `saveWait`, the retype
  note (`retypeNote`, both of 2.0.0-player.65's cases), a setting's `Row` (SettingRow: its control, value, placeholder,
  source, badges, effect, lock, revert, note, detail), `pickerChoices`, `isAddress`, the words, `barText`, and each
  failure in its own words (`readFailure`, `saveFailure` - a 400's detail as it came, a 403 NO_PERMISSION -
  `unansweredWords`). `Parts` says who sees what (the page with Settings and the log, Connections for whoever runs
  deadwax, Re-time with Edit albums too). **SettingsFlow** is every decision the pages make: only the newest read
  lands; a read to trust is one begun since deadwax was last out of reach (`real`), and Save waits for one; `readsNow`
  (shown, in reach, allowed, nothing out - the first read, one not to trust, after a save that never answered, and shown
  again with no draft); the one save (`save` - every draft, in order, any read out called off; `saved`; `refused` - a
  4xx, nothing taken, every draft kept, its words in the bar; `unanswered` - no answer or a 5xx, said as "deadwax may
  have finished this - looking again", the settings read again and only the drafts that still differ from them kept;
  `saveDropped`); `discard`, `barText`, `barShown`, the marks. **SavedAnswers** is MusicBrainzAnswers.tsx: the line,
  Clear's label, hint and refusal (a path drafted, nothing saved, a Clear out, out of reach), read again when either
  setting changes as saved (`key`), and a Clear that never answered read again to see. **RetimeRun** is
  RetimeLyrics.tsx's run: the library read, then `next` - the only way an album is asked for, so every stop lands after
  the album out: Stop, the background (`suspended`), out of reach, the session ended, a 403 (`step(failure:)`
  -> `.notAllowed`), the lead drafted (`leadDrafted`) - `finished`, the web's note and the phone's own stop sentence,
  `keepsScreenOn`, `pageGone` (an ended run said once). **Connections** and **ConnectionChecks** are You.tsx's rows:
  `fromPing`, `fromNavidrome`, `unanswered`, `spoken`; checked the first time a page drawing them shows for this
  person, on Check again, and once more as such a page shows after a `want` - a save carrying a Connections-group key,
  deadwax back in reach, the sign-in over the app gone - only the newest check's answers landing.
  The client: `serverSettings()`, `saveServerSettings(_:)` (its wait grown by the batch), `savedAnswers()`,
  `clearSavedAnswers()`, `pingMusicBrainz()`, `pingSlskd()`, `retime(_:)` (the lyrics fetch with `retime`, waited
  for by EditWaits' new `retime(album)`).
- **Routes.swift**: `serverSettings` (GET), `saveServerSettings` (PUT), `savedAnswers` (GET), `clearSavedAnswers`
  (POST), `pingMusicBrainz`, `pingSlskd` (GET) - 98 routes - and their waits (30, 60 at least and 30 + 10 s a setting
  saved, 30, 120, 120, 30), each held to the handler by tests/test_ios_server_settings.py or pinned with why.
- **Managing.swift**: `Tool.native` takes in `.settings`, so the footer names four.
- **NavidromeGate.swift**: `setUpURL` gone - the button opens the app's own sheet.

### The app (ios/App/Manage/, and the Library's gate)

- **ServerSettingsModel** (new), held by the app as CareRunModel is: DeadwaxApp makes it and puts it in the
  environment, resets it with the rest when the person changes (the drafts with it), and Reachability's `whenChanged`
  tells it of reach; RootView's scene phase tells it of the background, and of the sign-in over the app going
  (`sessionBack`). Pages tell it as they show and go (`shows`, `hides`: counters for the pages, and for those drawing
  the saved answers, Re-time and Connections). It carries out what Core decides: reads when `readsNow` says, never
  while `server.signInOver` is set; a 403 asks /me again; the save under a BackgroundHold ("Server settings: save"), its
  ends announced; after a save carrying a NAVIDROME_ key, `library.checkNavidrome()` (the web's
  `onServerSettingsSaved`), so the gate opens by itself; the saved answers read and cleared; Connections' three asks,
  each landing on its own; Re-time driven album by album through the client's `retime(_:)` under a BackgroundHold,
  the library read with no ETag first. The drafts outlive the pages (the web keeps them in its module).
- **ScreenAwake** (new): the one place the app touches `isIdleTimerDisabled`, from a set of reasons - Library care's
  run and Re-time's - so one ending never lets the screen sleep under the other. CareRunModel goes through it now.
- **ServerSettingsScreen** (new): NO_PERMISSION without Settings and the log; Managing needs deadwax when opened out of
  reach before a read; the first read (Reading the settings, then its failure with Try again); then the page line,
  **ConnectionsSection** (each row a dot, the word and the sentence under it - selectable - read once; Check again,
  dimmed until a check began and out of reach), a read again that failed, the verdict, and the tabs' sections of group
  rows (`NavigationLink(value: AppRoute.serverSettingsGroup(id))`, marked). Every page carries
  `.serverSettingsPage(_:)`: the save bar as a bottom `safeAreaInset` (inside PlayerClearance, above the mini player
  and the tabs - a toolbar's bottom bar sits under the app's tab bar), `editOutOfReach` once something was read, and
  the shows/hides.
- **ServerSettingsGroupScreen** (new): the group's note, Connections' rows on the Connections group's page, then a
  section per setting headed by its key in mono: a menu (`pickerChoices`), a secure field or a field (the URL keyboard
  for an address, no capitals, no corrections, the placeholder as the web's), "Locked"; Revert to the environment; the
  footer's source and badges as one AttributedString, the effect, the lock, "Will revert…", the retype note in amber,
  the detail in red. **RetimeSection** under Lyrics, **SavedAnswersSection** under MusicBrainz's saved answers (Clear
  asked first by a confirmationDialog). `groupGone` when deadwax's answer has no such group.
- **SetUpNavidromeSheet**: Connections' group page in its own NavigationStack, Close (dimmed while saving), not swiped
  away while saving. **LibraryView** holds it (`settingUp`) and attaches it above the gate's switch; NavidromeGateView's
  Set up Navidrome only asks for it. It goes on Close, or once Navidrome answers (see "After review" below).
- **ManageSection** pushes `AppRoute.serverSettings` for `.settings`; **Shared/Routes.swift** has the two routes and
  their destinations; **Palette.greenIcon** (`--dw-green-icon`) for Connected's dot.

### What the web's .tsx files hold, read by pattern

As in slices 2-7, the pages' own rules stay in the .tsx and ios/scripts/export-server-vectors.cjs reads each out by a
pattern (hashed into made_from, so iosserver fails when one changes) and runs it compiled: from **app/ServerSettings.tsx**
the title, the spinner's words, Try again, Discard, Save and Saving…, the marks' titles, the bar's words, a save's
refusal and the ladder; from **components/SettingsView.tsx** a row's value, placeholder, source, badges, revert label
and lock, and the verdict; from **components/RetimeLyrics.tsx** the running label, the note, the hints and a run stepped
album by album as the module steps it; from **components/MusicBrainzAnswers.tsx** Clear's label, hint, refusal and
line; from **app/You.tsx** Connections' title, fromPing and fromNavidrome; from **app/App.tsx** and **app/access.ts** who
sees the page. Moving those into lib/ too is a small no-change refactor on main whenever wanted.

### Decided here, and where the phone departs from the spec (or the web)

- **Marks per group**: the web marks a tab; the phone's root lists groups, so each group row carries the mark the
  web's rule gives it (Organizing carrying the verdict's attention).
- **One save bar on every Server settings page**, a bottom inset rather than a toolbar (the app's tab bar would hide a
  bottom toolbar). Save is off from the moment deadwax goes out of reach until a read begun after it lands - a read out
  as it went may land too early.
- **A save that never answered** (no answer, a timeout, a 5xx) may have landed: the web says the failure and keeps
  every draft; the phone reads the settings again and keeps only the drafts that still differ (`stillDiffering`). A 403
  says a Managing page's NO_PERMISSION and asks /me again.
- **A menu keeps a value that isn't one of its choices** (unset, or one this deadwax doesn't know) as its first entry
  ("Not set" when empty), where the web's dropdown would show its first choice - which reads as a value that isn't
  there.
- **The page line names Settings, not You**: the phone's own choices are in its Settings, under Getting albums. (The
  web's line says Settings too since its 2.1.35, so the phone's is the web's word for word.)
- **Connections on the Connections group's page too**, so Set up Navidrome's sheet shows whether Navidrome answers
  after a save; and checked again (the phone's own) after a save carrying a Connections setting, back in reach, and
  after signing in again.
- **Clear asks first** (the web clears at once): a phone's tap lands more easily, and "only speed is lost" is still
  something lost.
- **Re-time needs Edit albums too**, as its route does, and says so; its stops are the phone's (the background, out of
  reach, the session ended, a 403, the lead drafted) with "running it again carries on", and an album that never
  answered "may have been re-timed all the same". The screen stays on while it runs and Lyrics' page is in front, as
  Library care's run - both through ScreenAwake.
- **The settings are read each time a page shows with no draft** (the web reads each time its page renders), never
  over a draft.
- **Set up Navidrome opens Connections over the Library** (the web's `showServerSettingsTab('connections')`), not the
  web app's Server settings at its first tab in Safari; the sheet goes once Navidrome answers, and Close keeps the
  drafts in the model for Settings > Manage > Server settings.
- **Fields stay editable offline and while a save goes** (as the web's); only Save, Clear and Re-time are writes.

### After review (16 Nov) - slice 8

The review of d9a1584 (code read only) found eight things; each was traced before it was changed, and all eight were
real.

- **A false "Saved." after a save that never answered.** `readLanded` said "Saved." when no draft was LEFT - so
  Discard while the look was out (drafts empty, `checking` still set), or a sent setting typed back to its saved value
  during it, made a read of the old settings say "Saved." of a batch that never landed. Now "Saved." is decided by
  what was SENT: `stillDiffering(sent, sent: sent, now:)` empty, and no draft left (as `saved` says it). **Discard
  while looking ends the look** with no word on how the save came out, and as what is shown may be from before the
  save, `real` goes false (`gap = max(gap, landed)`) so the settings are read again - a read already out began after
  the save, so it is the one that settles it. **The look never sticks**: its read failing is `checkStalled`, the bar
  says that failure (not "looking again") with **Try again** on every page, and the list's re-read line stays quiet so
  it isn't said twice; Discard ends it too. `readLanded` returns whether it settled such a save, and only then is the
  bar announced. ServerSettingsTests: `discardingWhileASaveIsLookedAtNeverSaysSavedOfABatchThatDidntLand` (Discard
  with a read out and without, typed back and not landed, typed back and landed, a secret sent),
  `aLookWhoseReadFailedSaysSoAndTryAgainOrDiscardEndsIt`.
- **Set up Navidrome's sheet went with any reach blip, even mid-save.** It was attached inside NavidromeGateView, and
  the gate turns `.open` whenever deadwax is out of reach (or the check failed for want of it) - so the view went and
  took the sheet, past `interactiveDismissDisabled(saving)`. Now LibraryView holds `settingUp` and attaches the sheet
  to a ZStack over the root's switch; the gate's button only asks for it. It is put away (`setUpDone`) only when
  Navidrome really answers - in reach, and the newest check (LibraryModel's checks are newest-only) one deadwax
  answered with `status.ok` - and never during a save (the save ending looks again). It can't fire on a stale answer:
  the sheet only opens over a closed gate, whose check said otherwise, so `navidromeAnswers` turns true only on a check
  that landed since; going out of reach makes it false, and coming back leaves the old check, still not ok. A new
  person closes it. docs/ios.md check 369 now has the sheet staying through Wi-Fi off, and a save cut off.
- **A read could begin during a save.** `readIfNeeded` and `retry` spawned `Task { await read() }`, and `readBegan` ran
  only as the Task started - two asks in one turn sent two GETs, and a Save pressed between let a GET out during the
  save, whose landing after the PUT could draw the old values over "Saved.". The ticket is taken before the Task now,
  as Library care takes its own; the saved answers' read too.
- **An extra GET on first open.** The page's frame was on a `Group { if … }`, so the spinner giving way to the list
  went as a hide and a show - and a show with no draft reads again. Both pages are a ZStack now.
- **Re-time's library-read hold spanned the run** (its `defer` ran when the Task ended, after `driveRetime`). It ends as
  the read does; each album keeps its own.
- **A ping called off stayed on "Checking…".** `ConnectionChecks.dropped` puts the row back to its last answer - or,
  never answered, `Connections.notChecked` ("Couldn't check", nothing more) - and wants a check the next time a page
  shows. A cancelled Re-time album counting as failed and "may have been re-timed" matches Library care, and stays.
  ServerSettingsTests: `aPingCalledOffGoesBackToItsLastAnswer`.
- **Clear's 403 said the generic failure.** It says a Managing page's NO_PERMISSION now, as Save's 403 does (the
  vectors hold no 403 for Clear: the phone's own).
- **VoiceOver read each setting's name twice** - the section header, then the control labelled with it. The header is
  hidden from VoiceOver; every control (the menu, the field, Locked) carries the name.

tests/test_ios_server_settings.py pins each: the tickets before their Tasks, Discard reading again, the ping's
`dropped`, the hold ended before the drive, the ZStacks, the bar's Try again, the hidden header, and the sheet in
LibraryView above the gate with its closing rule.

Verified: swift test - 1955 Core tests in 202 suites, 158 Audio in 17, 12 in 1; the unsigned device build with no new
warning (only the AppIntents metadata one); check_project.py; pytest on its own, 4909 passed and 1 skipped; all 95
sims. NOT verified, as before: any of it on a phone - the sheet through a real Wi-Fi drop, VoiceOver reading each
name once, and the ZStack sending one GET on first open (read from how SwiftUI applies modifiers, not watched).

## The event log on the phone (Phase 8, slice 9 - 2026-11-16)

The spec's section 8 (notes/ios-specs/phase8-managing.md), with 13-14's rules: Settings > Manage > **Event log** is the
app's own page now - what deadwax has said since it started, the last 500 lines, newest first, and each new line as
it's logged - rather than the web app's in Safari. The web's rules run as they are in the vectors; the stream is the
phone's first answer read as it comes. Built on the `ios` branch at b946439 (main 2.1.33 merged). The app stays 0.13
(13); src/__init__.py untouched; **no server change** - /interface_logs/recent and the stream are 2.0.0-player.33's,
as they are; the player engine has no diff.

### Core (DeadwaxCore)

- **EventLog.swift** (new). `LogLine` and `RecentLog` read loosely (a field of another type left out, never the line;
  a fractional `seq` read as none - deadwax's are whole, and the vectors leave that case out, where the web would key
  by it). `EventLog` is lib/eventLog.ts and the page's
  words: `kept` (LOG_KEPT, 500), `State` - `joining(_:)` (joinLine), `joining(history:)` (joinHistory, with fillGap's
  gap), `emptied()` (clearLog), `streamFrom` (EventLog.tsx's `logStreamUrl(boot ? last : null, boot)`: both or
  neither) - `streamQuery`, `level` (levelOf), `time` (lineTime: HH:MM:SS on the device's clock, TimeClip's whole
  milliseconds and "Invalid " past a Date's end, as `toTimeString().slice(0, 8)` gives), the title, the page's line,
  the list's label, EMPTY_WORDS, the history's failure (`historyFailure`: sayError's notice with "failed" and retry),
  STREAM_WORDS, `allowed` (App.tsx's `perms.has('server')`). Each held line is a `Line` with an `ID` of its run, its
  number and the phone's own count of lines taken - fixed as the line is taken, so a line coming above leaves every row
  below as it was; never its place.
- **EventStream.swift** (new). The stream, pure: `Lines` (bytes to lines - LF, CR and CRLF, a CR and its LF split
  across reads, a BOM dropped only at the very start, a line over 1 MB dropped whole and the next read, UTF-8 decoded
  with replacement) and `Frames` (the WHATWG EventSource parse: comments, `data` joined by newlines, `event`, `id`
  without NUL, `retry` digits only; a blank line dispatches only with data). `End` classes how an ask ended -
  cancelled, signed out (401), forbidden (403), refused (another 4xx), lost (everything else: no answer, a timeout, a
  5xx, an answer that isn't the stream, the stream ending). `isStream` is EventSource's content-type check, and
  `NotTheStream` what an answer failing it throws. `keepalive` 15, `silence` 45 (three keepalives: the stream's wait
  between bytes, so a WireGuard drop with no word is noticed), `retry` 5 (STREAM_RETRY_MS). **Feed** is every decision
  the page makes, each ask numbered as it's decided and an answer to any but the newest dropped: `update(wanted:online:)`
  (wanted and idle: the history; not wanted and something out: stop - the line "Lost…" out of reach, "Connecting…"
  for the next showing), `historyLanded` (joined, then the stream from where it ends), `historyFailed` (said, with Try
  again, and the stream opened all the same - a 401 halts for the sign-in, a 403 asks /me), `opened` (Live), `frame`
  (a message's line joined; anything that isn't a line left out, as JSON.parse failing leaves it), `streamEnded`
  (lost: "Lost the live feed - reconnecting…" and a wait; refused: "Not live" and its words, halted until Try again
  or until it's wanted again after it wasn't; cancelled by the system: asked again, never said), `retryDue` (the stream from the last
  line held - the history first when it's owed or the lines have a gap), `tryAgain`, `clear`, `reading` (the first
  read's spinner, which gives way to its failure), `tryAgainShown`, and `announcement(inReach:)` (what VoiceOver hears,
  one announcement at a time - see "After review" below). The client: `recentLog()`, and
  `logStream(after:boot:)` - the session's cookie by hand as every request's, `Accept: text/event-stream`, the route's
  wait between bytes; a status other than 200 through `failure()` (so a 401 tells the app, as anywhere), the content
  type checked, then the frames as an AsyncThrowingStream whose end calls the request off.
- **HTTP.swift**: `HTTPLines` and `HTTPLineTransport` (`lines(for:)`), beside `HTTPTransport.send`, which stays a
  whole answer for every other route.
- **Routes.swift**: `recentLog` (GET /interface_logs/recent) and `logStream` (GET /interface_logs/interface_logs,
  `after` and `boot`) - 100 routes; `logStream`'s wait is 45 s (`silence`), /recent keeps the transport's own.
- **Managing.swift**: `Tool.native` takes in `.log`, so the footer names five - and says nothing at all unless People
  is drawn (an admin with logins on).

### The app (ios/App/Manage/)

- **URLSessionTransport** answers `lines(for:)` on `URLSession.bytes(for:)`, from a URLSession of the streams' own
  (made once, cookies off and no cache as the other's, its wait between bytes `silence`, its wait over all URLSession's default - a stream
  holds its connection while it's open, so it never takes one of the other requests'). The answer's status and headers
  as they arrive; a non-200's body read up to 64 KB to say why; the body as `EventStream.Lines` until it ends, fails, or
  the reader stops - which cancels both the reading Task and the bytes' own task. A connection failing tells
  Reachability, as any request's does.
- **EventLogModel** (new), held by the app as ServerSettingsModel is: DeadwaxApp makes it, puts it in the environment
  and resets it when the person changes; Reachability's `whenChanged` re-checks it; RootView tells it the scene phase
  and the sign-in over the app going. `wanted` is the page showing (a counter), the app in front, deadwax in reach,
  Settings and the log, neither the sign-in nor (after review) Now Playing over the app, a client. It carries out Feed's actions - `read` (/recent), `open`
  (the stream, each frame handed on), `wait` (Task.sleep, then `retryDue`), `stop` (cancel what's out), `askMe`
  (`server.refreshMe()`) - in one `asking` Task at a time, each ask's number taken by Feed before the Task is made, and
  a generation dropping anything of the last person's. Nothing else: no rule of its own, **no BackgroundHold, no
  ScreenAwake** - the background stops it. The lines outlive the page, as the web keeps them in its module.
- **EventLogScreen** (new), its frame on a ZStack: NO_PERMISSION without Settings and the log; "Managing needs deadwax"
  when opened out of reach before anything was heard; else the list - the page's line, a problem (the history's
  failure, or a refused stream's words, in the danger red with Try again), then the lines (`ForEach` over the held
  lines, keyed by `Line.ID`), "Reading what deadwax kept…" or the empty words. The stream's line (`StreamLine`: a dot -
  grey, green-icon live, amber-icon lost - and the words, amber while lost) is a top `safeAreaInset`, under the bar.
  Clear in the bar, dimmed with no lines; `.editOutOfReach` once something was heard. `LogRow`: the time in the mono
  face, the level (semibold; red or amber), the part (one line, wrapping at accessibility sizes), over the words (red or amber with the level),
  stacked at accessibility sizes; one VoiceOver element (`EventLog.spoken`, words first) with Copy as an action; a
  context menu's Copy (`EventLog.copyText`, the line as drawn) to UIPasteboard. Reduce Motion: the list's transactions
  carry no animation and disable any an `.animation` would add.
- **ManageSection** pushes `AppRoute.eventLog` for `.log`; **Shared/Routes.swift** has the route.

### What the web's .tsx files hold, read by pattern

As in slices 2-8, ios/scripts/export-log-vectors.cjs runs lib/eventLog.ts, api/logs.ts, lib/errorWords.ts and
lib/permissions.ts compiled, and reads out of **app/EventLog.tsx** by pattern (each piece hashed into made_from, so
ioslog fails when one moves) a line's key, the empty words, the history's failure, the stream's address from what is
held, the page's line, the title, the list's label, and the two retries (a stream the browser gave up on - CLOSED -
asked again by hand, the history first); from **app/App.tsx** who opens the page, **app/access.ts** seesDetail and
**lib/appRoutes.ts** the not-allowed words. 37 runs of 1100 steps (13 worked, 24 seeded - EventSource's own reconnect
from the number it first asked from among them) replayed through `State` with the state compared after every step;
198 times in four zones (St John's and Kathmandu's half hours, London's changes, far values in UTC); 24 history
failures; 10 addresses; 65 permission sets.

**The real route's first frames** are ios/scripts/log_stream_answers.py's (Fixtures/log/stream.json): /recent and four
streams (from where the history ends, from a line held below the last, another run's number, from now) run through
the real src/routes/interface_logs.py over ASGI with a fixed run and fixed lines - status, the headers the phone
reads, the body as sent. tests/test_ios_event_log.py makes it again and compares, and EventStreamTests reads each
through Lines, Frames and Feed.

### Decided here, and where the phone departs from the spec (or the web)

- **A dropped connection asks again from the last line held**; EventSource asks again from the number it was first
  opened with, and joinLine drops what it had. The phone's ask is the smaller; the vectors replay EventSource's way
  too, so either joins the same.
- **An answer that isn't the stream** (a 5xx, a proxy's page, the wrong content type) is where EventSource gives up
  for good and EventLog.tsx asks again by hand after 5 s, the history first: the phone does the same. A connection that
  drops reopens the stream alone (EventSource's own reconnect), unless the history is owed or the lines have a gap.
- **A 4xx stops it** ("Not live", the phone's own state, with deadwax's words or "Couldn't open the live feed." and Try
  again): EventSource would also give up, and the web says only "Lost…" for ever. A 401 says nothing - the sign-in
  comes over the app - and a 403 says NO_PERMISSION and asks /me again, so the page turns into NO_PERMISSION.
- **The stream's state is a strip under the bar** (the spec's "under the bar"); the page's line is the list's first
  row. Neither is a line of the log.
- **Copy** is the phone's own (the spec's), on a long press and as a VoiceOver action; it copies the line as drawn.
- **"Reading what deadwax kept…"** while the first read is out with nothing held, rather than "Nothing logged yet." -
  which it isn't known to be. A failed first read shows its failure and Try again, never an endless spinner.
- **Out of reach** the stream is stopped, the line says "Lost the live feed - reconnecting…" and the amber line comes
  over the lines; back in reach, the history is read again and the stream rejoined.
- **The lines are the app's while it runs**, as the web's module keeps them: coming back to the page shows them at
  once and fills in the rest. A new person empties them.
- **VoiceOver reads a line once, its words first**, then its level, time and part; it hears the stream lost, refused
  (with why, in one announcement) and back, not every "Connecting…", and nothing over the app's own out-of-reach
  banner (the web's line is a live region, read every time).
- **Each line's identity is the phone's own** (run, number, and its count taken): the web keys by `boot:seq` or by
  place, which two lines can share (a number of the wrong type) and which moves as lines come above.
- **/recent keeps the transport's own wait** (8 s): its handler reads 500 lines from memory under a lock, with nothing
  to wait on.

- **EventLogVectorTests** (new, 9): the fixture and its sources, the words, levels, times in four zones and untimed

  failures, the addresses, who opens the page.
- **EventStreamTests** (new, 23): lines across every ending and a split CRLF, an over-long line dropped, frames as

- **tests/test_ios_event_log.py** (new, 8): the routes by method, path and permission (test_logins' ROUTES); the

- test_ios_contract.py (100 routes); test_ios_settings.py (five NavigationLinks), test_ios_library_care.py and

### Verified, and not

On the Mac: `swift test` (1985 Core tests in 204 suites, 158 Audio in 17, 12 more, all passing); the unsigned
generic-iOS Debug build, BUILD SUCCEEDED, with only the AppIntents metadata warning every build has; check_project.py;
the full pytest suite run alone on the rebased tip (on 5dc3d47), 4919 passed and 1 skipped; pyflakes over src
and tests, clean; all 96 sims with Node 22 (ioslog
running the exporter's `--check`). tests/test_ios_event_log.py runs the real /recent and the real stream route over
ASGI, and EventStreamTests reads what they sent through the phone's reader. Assumed: that URLSession's
`timeoutIntervalForRequest` on a `bytes(for:)` task is a wait between bytes, as it is documented to be for a data
task, so 45 s of silence ends a dropped stream; that `bytes(for:)` hands each frame on as it arrives rather than
buffering; and that cancelling the reading Task and the bytes' task closes the connection at once.

Not verified - only the phone can tell (docs/ios.md checks 370-373): the stream over WireGuard (the keepalives through
the tunnel, how soon a drop is noticed, "Lost the live feed - reconnecting…" then Live with no line missing); lines
arriving as a search runs, as promptly as the web's; the stream stopping as the app goes to the background and the
phone sleeping with the page open; Copy's context menu and the pasted text; the list under Reduce Motion (no slide-in)
and VoiceOver (each line once, the stream lost and back said); the largest text sizes; 500 rows scrolling.

### After review (16 Nov) - slice 9

The review of c485edd (code read only) found four plausible things and some minors. Each was traced before it was
changed, and all of them were real:

- **The List's VoiceOver label.** `.accessibilityLabel(EventLog.listLabel)` sat on the whole List, which isn't an
  accessibility element of its own - and on such a container SwiftUI can hand the label to every element inside it,
  over each line's own `EventLog.spoken`. Dropped, with `EventLog.listLabel` (the web's `aria-label`, no longer drawn;
  the fixture keeps the web's words): the title and the page's line - the list's first row, "…newest first" - say what
  it is. `.accessibilityElement(children: .contain)` before it was the other way, but a container element wrapped round
  a List is one more thing VoiceOver's list navigation would have to get through, for words the page says already.
- **`timeoutIntervalForResource = .infinity`** on the streams' session: a value CFNetwork may not take as meant. Gone -
  `configuration(waiting:)` sets only the wait between bytes, so the wait over all is URLSession's default, a week,
  which no stream held only while the page is in front comes near. tests/test_ios_event_log.py pins its absence from
  both the streams' session and the configuration it starts from.
- **The stream stayed open under Now Playing.** Now Playing is a full-screen cover, which leaves the page under it
  shown (no onDisappear), and the web's `managingLive` is `pageShown && nav.tab === tab && !visualizerShown &&
  !sheetOpen` - Now Playing being `sheetOpen`. EventLogModel takes AppNavigation now, `wanted` has
  `!navigation.nowPlayingShown`, and the screen re-checks on `.onChange(of: navigation.nowPlayingShown)`, so the stream
  is called off as Now Playing opens and rejoined from the last line held as it's put away (a refused stream asked
  again then too, as after any time it wasn't wanted). pytest holds the web's rule beside the phone's.
- **VoiceOver announcements collided.** A refused stream posted its words, then "Not live" at once - which cut them
  off - and going out of reach posted "Lost the live feed - reconnecting…" in the same turn as Reachability's banner
  line. What VoiceOver hears is Core's now: `Feed.announcement(inReach:)`, asked after each change is carried out,
  keeps what it last told and gives ONE announcement for what changed since: the history's failure when it's new (and
  live isn't said on top of it - "what happens from now still shows" covers it); lost; refused with why in the same
  breath ("Not live. Couldn't open the live feed."); live again only after lost or refused was said; and nothing at all
  out of reach, where the banner speaks at that moment and its "Back online" says the return (Reachability sets
  `reach` before telling its handlers, so `inReach` is already false when the banner is said). The model's two
  `announce` functions are one, posting only what Core says. EventStreamTests:
  `voiceOverHearsTheStreamLostAndBackNeverEveryConnecting` (lost, back, a refusal and a 403 each in one
  announcement) and `voiceOverHearsTheHistorysFailureOnceAndNothingOverTheBanner`.

Minors:

- **Reduce Motion** set `transaction.animation = nil`, which was nil already - nothing wraps the feed's changes in an
  animation - so it did nothing. Under Reduce Motion the List's transactions now also set `disablesAnimations` (as Up
  Next's instant scroll does), so no `.animation` above can add one. Whether a List animates a row in with no
  animation in its transaction at all is iOS's to say; not watched (check 371's region).
- **The part's `.lineLimit(1)`** cut a long `src` short at accessibility sizes, where it stands on a line of its own:
  there it wraps now (`lineLimit(nil)`, fixed vertically), so check 371's "nothing cut off" holds.
- **docs/ios.md** said a lost feed was asked again "every 5 seconds": only while deadwax answers with an error. When
  nothing answers, the transport's silence makes Reachability probe and find deadwax out of reach - usually before the
  5 s are up - which stops the asking until it's back in reach. A refused stream is asked again on return from the
  background, deadwax back in reach and Now Playing put away, not only on Try again and the page shown again. And Copy
  gives more than one line when the words hold newlines. All three said now; Feed's own doc too.
- **EventLogVectorTests' "every identity once"** couldn't fail: every identity carries a count taken, unique by
  construction. In its place, `identityMoved(from:to:)` after every step of every run: each held line keeps its
  identity and its order among the others, those that went are the oldest or all of them (Clear), never one from the
  middle, and each new line's identity was taken after every one held - which a port that took a held line again
  (rebuilding the list as it fills a gap, say) would break. `theIdentityCheckCatchesALineTakenAgain` shows it failing
  on each of those.

Verified: swift test - 1987 Core tests in 204 suites, 158 Audio in 17, 12 in 1; the unsigned device build with no new warning (only the AppIntents metadata one);
check_project.py; pyflakes over src and tests, clean; pytest on its own, 4919 passed and 1 skipped; all 96 sims. NOT verified, as
before: any of it on a phone - VoiceOver's announcements as they're actually spoken (one cutting another off is iOS's
behaviour, read, not heard), the List under Reduce Motion, Now Playing calling the stream off and the page rejoining as
it goes.

## Change password on the phone (Phase 8, slice 10 - 2026-11-16)

The spec's section 9 (notes/ios-specs/phase8-managing.md), with 13-14's rules: Settings > Account > **Change password**
is the app's own page now - your Navidrome password changed by deadwax as you (`POST /deadwax/me/password`,
src/routes/own_password.py, 2.0.2) - rather than the web app's You in Safari. Built on the `ios` branch at db6a4ff. The
app stays 0.13 (13); src/__init__.py untouched; **no server change** - the route, its strict body and its cookie are
2.0.2's (and review 3's re-key) as they are; the player engine has no diff.

### Core (DeadwaxCore)

- **OwnPassword.swift** (new). `OwnPassword` is lib/ownPassword.ts and people.ts' password rules: the title,
  SAME_PASSWORD, APPS_LINE, HTTP_NOTE (`httpNote(protocol:)`, and `httpNote(at:)` from the phone's address - nil only
  for https), PASSWORD_MIN/MAX, `passwordProblem` (lengths in UTF-16 units, people.ts' CONTROL class unit for unit, the
  name compared lowercased as JavaScript lowercases, `!==` as unit equality - Swift's `==` would call a composed and a
  decomposed é the same), `formProblem`, `formReady`, `doneWords`, `changeLine`, `changeOffered` (logins on, a name,
  never break-glass - Managing.changeOffered now hands on to it). The labels: Current password and New password the
  web's; **New password again** and **Change**/"Changing…" the phone's. `Outcome` is what a change came to:
  `changed(signedOut:warning:session:)` - a 200 WITH a new `deadwax_session` cookie, which is the proof; `notRenewed` - a
  200 with `changed: true` and no cookie (NOT_RENEWED: the session stands under its old id); `refused(words:kind:fix:)`
  - any 4xx but 401, deadwax's `detail` as it came (with its `why` for whoever runs deadwax); `signedOut(reason:)` - a
  401; `failed(words:fix:)` - a 5xx with deadwax's own words (TIMED_OUT, NOT_KEPT, DIDNT_TAKE, UNREACHABLE…);
  `unknown(words:)` - no answer, a timeout, a bare 5xx, a 200 that isn't deadwax's: "deadwax may have changed your
  password - its answer never came. If deadwax asks you to sign in again, it did: sign in with the new password. If it
  doesn't, try again." (the transport's words in brackets for whoever runs deadwax); `cancelled`. `Said` is what the
  page shows after, and its one announcement. `pagesKept` keeps the page through a tab tapped again while a change is
  out.
- **OwnPasswordForm** and **OwnPasswordBody** redact themselves: `description`, `debugDescription` and an empty
  `customMirror`, so `print`, `dump`, string interpolation and a debugger's summary never show a password. The body's
  keys are `current`, `password`, `password_again` - exactly the server's strict model (an extra key is its 422).
  `OwnPasswordAnswer` reads `changed`, `signed_out` and `warning` loosely.
- **OwnPasswordFlow**: the page's state. `begin` gives the body and a ticket synchronously (one change at a time; an
  answer to an older ticket is dropped); `ended` leaves the fields as the web does - emptied once changed (or the
  session ended), kept after a refusal, Current emptied and `focusCurrent` bumped for `not_your_password`, kept for an
  unknown outcome - and returns the one announcement; `typed` clears what was said; `hidden` empties everything said
  and typed but leaves a change out.
- **PasswordRekey**: ServerModel's hold on the sign-in while a change is out. deadwax moves this phone's session under
  a new id BEFORE it answers, so anything asked meanwhile under the old cookie is answered 401 PASSWORD_CHANGED - which
  says nothing about the session the answer brings. `holds(reason:)` keeps the first such 401 instead of bringing the
  sign-in; `ended(_:rekeyed:)` drops it when the new session was kept, brings the sign-in with the change's own 401's
  reason or the held one's otherwise, and asks /me when the outcome leaves it unsure whether the session in hand still
  stands (notRenewed, failed, unknown); `forgot` lets it go when the person, address or session changed meanwhile.
- **APIFailure**: `Answer.fix` and `APIFailure.fix` - People's and Change password's refusals are `{detail, kind,
  fix}`; ErrorBody reads `fix` as a string, as `kind`.
- **SessionCookie.value(fromCookie:)**: the session a request carried, from its own `Cookie:` header.
- **DeadwaxClient.changeOwnPassword(_:admin:)**: the POST through `answer()` (so a 401 tells the signed-out hook, as
  every route's does), never retried. **Routes**: `ownPassword` (101 routes), waited on for 240 s.

### The app

- **ChangePasswordScreen** (ios/App/You/, new): a pushed Form - `changeLine` at the top; the three SecureFields
  (`.password`, then `.newPassword` twice; no capitals, no autocorrection; Next, Next, Done) with the problem as typed
  under them in the footnote face; the footer's plain-http note (amber) and APPS_LINE; Change (a spinner and
  "Changing…" while out), on only when `flow.canChange` and the sign-in isn't over the app; then what was said - done
  in the held green with deadwax's warning in amber, a problem in the danger red with `fix` under it - as one VoiceOver
  element. Back is hidden (and so the swipe) while a change is out, and AppNavigation keeps the page through its tab
  tapped again (`passwordChanging`, `OwnPassword.pagesKept`). `.editOutOfReach` while deadwax can't be reached. The
  fields reach the form through bindings whose setter also calls `typed()`, so an answer emptying them doesn't clear
  what it said. Current takes the focus after a wrong current password, unless VoiceOver is running (it would cut off
  the announcement). The fields are emptied as the page disappears and as the sign-in comes over the app.
- **AccountSection**: Change password is a `NavigationLink(value: AppRoute.changePassword)`, under
  `OwnPassword.changeOffered`; no WebAppRow is left in Account.
- **ServerModel.changeOwnPassword**: refused (`.cancelled`) unless the launch is ready, no sign-in is over the app,
  there is a client and an address, and no change is out (`rekey.began()`); held through the background
  (`BackgroundHold`); after the await, `.cancelled` (nothing kept) if the person, address, session or launch changed.
  On `.changed`: **the Keychain first** (`SessionKeychain.save`), then `session`, then a **new client** with the new
  cookie - synchronously on the main actor, so nothing can ask under the old one between - and `asks += 1` so a /me
  still out under the old session is dropped. Then `rekey.ended` - nothing, the sign-in, or /me asked. Every path that
  used to bring the sign-in on a 401 (`askBehind`, `refreshMe`, `noteSignedOut`) goes through `sessionEnded`, which the
  hold can keep.
- **Downloads**: `DownloadSession.Event.finished` carries `sentUnder` - the session the task's own request carried,
  read from its `Cookie:` header - and `DownloadModel.signedOutHeard(sentUnder:)` holds nothing for a 401 to a task
  sent under a session since replaced. Without it, a download task queued under the old cookie and answered 401 after
  the re-key would have marked the NEW session refused: `refused(session)` true, the plan's `signedIn` false, every
  task out called off and nothing asked for 60 s. Now the record goes back to wanted (DownloadRules' `.signedOut`, as
  before) and the plan that follows asks for it under the new session. A task whose request can't be read is taken as
  the session in hand's, as before.

### What the web's .tsx files hold, read by pattern

ios/scripts/export-password-vectors.cjs runs lib/ownPassword.ts, lib/people.ts and lib/signIn.ts compiled, and reads
out of **app/ChangePassword.tsx** by pattern (each piece hashed into made_from, so iospassword fails when one moves):
the three labels, the button's words (Save, Saving…), the body sent (compiled and run as a function of the form), a
wrong current password's kind emptied and focused, one change at a time and only when ready, a done change's fields
emptied before what is said, a failure keeping the fields, the problem as typed, the plain-http note and the Amperfy
line; from **api/me.ts** the route and that a new session follows it. 293 passwords (lengths at and around 8 and 128 in
UTF-16 units, astral characters, every control range and its neighbours, the name in other cases and normalizations -
the Kelvin and Angstrom signs, a composed and a decomposed é - and 160 seeded), 140 forms (with what each sends), 10
counts for doneWords, 6 lines, 6 notes, 11 people offered or not.

### Decided here, and where the phone departs from the spec (or the web)

- **A 200 with no new cookie is not a re-key** (notRenewed): nothing goes to the Keychain, the session in hand stays,
  the fields are emptied and it says "Password changed, but deadwax sent this phone no new sign-in." with deadwax's
  warning (or "Sign out and sign in again here with the new password."), and /me is asked.
- **A 5xx with deadwax's own words is said as it came** (failed), as EditWords.writeFailure does; only a bare 5xx, a
  timeout or no answer is "may have changed". The spec said 5xx and no answer alike; deadwax's 5xx words already say
  whether anything changed (NOT_KEPT, TIMED_OUT…), so they are the better sentence.
- **A 403 is said as it came** (EDITING_OFF names what to do), not as NO_PERMISSION: the route is every user's, so a
  403 here is never a permission.
- **`fix` is shown** under a refusal; the web reads only `detail`.
- **APPS_LINE is under the form from the start** (check 374), where the web says it only once a change is done.
- **The labels**: "New password again" for the web's Again (read alone, as a Form row or by VoiceOver, Again says
  nothing); Change for Save. No Show toggle (iOS's SecureField has none to switch, and the password manager fills).
  No hidden user-name field (the web's is for a browser's password manager to save the right entry; iOS's AutoFill
  without associated domains doesn't use one).
- **The re-key hold closes a race the web has**: the web's api/http.ts drops a 401 sent under an older session, but
  one asked under the old cookie that answers BEFORE the change's 200 signs it out. The phone holds it until the
  change answers.
- **Downloads' 401 by the session sent under** - the spec assumed DownloadModel's wait "until the client changes" was
  enough; it wasn't, as above.
- **Never retried**: one POST per tap, and a tap can't go while one is out; an unknown outcome asks /me, never the
  route again.
- Assumed: `SessionKeychain.save` succeeds (it's delete-then-add with its status unread, as at sign-in) - if it
  didn't, the next launch would start from the old session, which deadwax has ended, and show the sign-in.

On the Mac: `swift test`; the unsigned generic-iOS Debug build, BUILD SUCCEEDED, with only the AppIntents metadata
warning every build has; check_project.py; the full pytest suite run alone; pyflakes over src and tests; every sim with
