test_ios_change_password.py posts the phone's body to the real route and reads its cookie as the phone does.

Not verified - only the phone can tell (docs/ios.md checks 374-378): the password manager's fill and suggestion on the
three fields; the re-key against a real deadwax and Navidrome - the music playing on and nothing asking to sign in
after a change, the other devices signed out; downloads across a change (a task in flight finishing, one queued
refused and asked again under the new session, nothing held for a minute); the new session surviving a kill and
reopen (the Keychain's save); VoiceOver's one announcement and Current's focus; the page under the largest text
sizes; Back and the swipe off while a change is out.

### After review (16 Nov) - slice 10

The review found nothing serious; each finding was traced before it was fixed, and each was real.

- **Resume could stop saving after a change.** ResumeController recorded `signedOutUnder = session()` when a save's 401
  ARRIVED: a save still out under the old cookie, answered 401 after the re-key, was recorded as the NEW generation,
  and saving stopped until the next launch. Now `send` captures `session()` as each save goes, passes it to `refused`,
  and Core's `Resume.heldAfter401(sentUnder:now:)` records it only while it is still the one in hand; otherwise the 401
  is a failure like any other (`saves.failedAt`), tried again under the new session at the next trigger. Tested by a
  table and by a ResumeController run (a 401 sent under generation 1 landing under 2 stops nothing).
- **A download's 401 landing before the change's 200 called off every download.** deadwax answers the old cookie 401
  from the moment it moves the session, before the change's answer brings the new one, and that 401 was under the
  session still in hand - so `refusedSession` was set and every running task cancelled (no resume data) for a minute.
  Now ServerModel exposes `changingPassword` (true from just before the POST to just after `rekey.ended`, and let go by
  `dropChange`), DownloadModel watches it, and Core's `DownloadRules.heard401(sentUnder:current:changing:)` decides:
  `replaced` (sent under a session since replaced: nothing, as before), `deferred` (under the session in hand while a
  change is out: only that song is held back - `heldForChange`, left out of the plan's tasks to make - and the session
  it came under kept in `deferredRefusal`), `refused` (the old body, now `refuseSession`). When the change ends
  (`serverChanged`, with `changingPassword` false) the held songs are planned again, and `afterChange(deferred:current:)`
  says whether the 401 was the session in hand's after all (no re-key: refused then) or the move's (re-keyed: nothing).
- **The hold wasn't tied to the session it began under.** `PasswordRekey.began(under:)` records the session;
  `holds(reason:session:)` holds only while the session in hand is still that one; `personChanged`, `use` and `signOut`
  let it go (`dropChange` - `rekey.forgot()` and `changingPassword` false). The guard after the await is Core's
  `PasswordRekey.answerStands(sent:now:)` over a `Context` of person, address, session and launch-ready.
- **Fields under Now Playing**: the page's `.onChange(of: navigation.nowPlayingShown)` empties them, as the user guide
  already said it did.
- **Two announcements**: `OwnPasswordFlow.ended(_:_:signInOver:)` returns nothing to announce when the sign-in came
  over the app as the change answered (the sign-in says what happened); the fields are left exactly as without it.
- **The event log's halt**: a halt for a 401 was let go only by the sign-in coming and going. Now `Feed.sessionMoved
  (wanted:online:)` - called from RootView's `.onChange(of: server.client?.session)` through `EventLogModel
  .sessionMoved()` - lets a 401's halt go and asks again under the new session whatever was out under the old one (the
  history first: nothing twice); a refusal or a 403 stays halted until Try again.
- **The held reason**: a 401 held through a change that then didn't re-key (notRenewed, failed, unknown, cancelled)
  brings the sign-in with the phone's own words, `OwnPassword.endedWhileChanging` ("This phone's sign-in ended while
  your password was being changed - sign in again, with the new password if the change went through."), never
  deadwax's PASSWORD_CHANGED, which names "another device". A refusal's held 401 keeps deadwax's reason (nothing
  changed, so the session ended for a reason of its own).
- **A cancelled POST** with nothing held asks /me (`.askMe`), as an unknown outcome does: a request called off on the
  phone may still have reached deadwax. The table's unreachable `(.changed, nil, .askMe)` row is gone - a change is
  re-keyed exactly when it is `changed` (ServerModel keeps the cookie before `ended` is asked), so `ended` takes the
  outcome alone and `.changed` is always `.nothing`.
- **Redirects**: Core's `Redirects.follows(from:to:)` - the same scheme, host and port (lowercased; a URL's own
  scheme's port when it names none) - is asked by every session that can be asked: URLSessionTransport's per-timeout
  sessions and its stream session take `SameOriginRedirects.shared` as their delegate, as does Reachability's probe;
  CappedRead (the cover viewer's full size) and the player's StreamFetch are their own delegates and implement
  `willPerformHTTPRedirection` with the same rule. A refused redirect's 3xx is the answer (a route's error; a song that
  fails). The downloads' background session can't be asked - iOS follows a background task's redirects itself and
  never calls the delegate - so DownloadSession takes an answer whose URL isn't the asked one's origin as status 0,
  never the song. Whether iOS carries the hand-set `Cookie:` on such a background redirect is iOS's, and not verified.
  This is a small diff in DeadwaxAudio (StreamFetch's import of DeadwaxCore and one delegate method), said here
  because the engine is otherwise left alone. The user guide's first-open step says to give the address deadwax
  answers at, since a proxy's http-to-https redirect is now refused.
- **App rules into Core**: the post-await guard (`answerStands`), the downloads' sent-under rule (`heard401`,
  `afterChange`) and the page's enabled rule (`OwnPasswordFlow.canChange(user:online:signInOver:)`, which `begin`
  shares) are pure and table-tested; the page asks `canChange` and `begin` with the sign-in's state.
- **Tests**: the order test also finds no `await` between the Keychain save and the new client; `bringSignIn(` is
  called from exactly two places (a 401 not held, the change's end); the no-password-logged search covers
  OwnPassword.swift, DeadwaxClient.swift and URLSessionTransport.swift too (DeadwaxClient's one URLQueryItem is the
  route's own query, which for this route is none); the Python `session_of` is now SessionCookie.value(fromSetCookie:)
  step for step - quote stripping and `.whitespaces` trimming included - with its own cases; a new test finds every
  URLSession the app and DeadwaxKit's sources make and holds each to the redirect rule.

Left as they are:

- **The engine's client box is updated a turn late**: the player's engine is handed the new client a turn after the
  re-key, so a gapless open in that window goes out under the old cookie, is refused, and heals itself after 1.5 s.
- **The orphaned server session**: when the guard after the await discards a changed outcome (the person, address or
  session moved while it was out), the new session deadwax made for this phone is never used and lives on the server
  until it times out. Nothing on the phone holds it.
- **The second-page case**: a second Change password page while a change is out (its own flow idle, so its Change is
  on) is refused by ServerModel's one-at-a-time `rekey.began` as `.cancelled`, which says nothing and keeps its
  fields.

## People on the phone (Phase 8, slice 11 - 2026-11-17)

The spec's section 10 (notes/ios-specs/phase8-managing.md), with 13-14's rules: Settings > Manage > **People** is the
app's own page now - Navidrome's accounts looked after by deadwax as the signed-in admin (src/routes/people.py, the
nine routes of 2.0.0-player.61 and after) - rather than the web app's People in Safari. With it nothing in Manage opens
Safari any more (WebAppRow and `OpenURLAction.webApp` are left, unused, for slice 12 to remove). Built on the `ios`
branch at 16ef56d. The app stays 0.13 (13); src/__init__.py untouched; **no server change** - the routes, their strict
bodies, the unlock and its idle timeout are the server's as they are; the player engine has no diff.

### Core (DeadwaxCore)

- **People.swift** (new). `People` is lib/people.ts and lib/permissions.ts' People part, and app/People.tsx's own
  words: the titles, UNLOCKED_LINE, HTTP_NOTE (`httpNote(at:)` from the phone's address), the name, display-name and
  password rules (`cleanName`, `nameProblem`, `displayProblem`, `passwordProblem`, `formProblem`, `formReady`,
  `resetProblem`, `resetReady` - lengths in UTF-16 units, the pattern's every edge, the name folded as JavaScript
  folds it), a row's `chips`, `signInWords` (with `ago`), `libraryWords` and `librariesWarning`; `actions(person)`
  (Reset password, Make admin or No longer admin, Remove - each offered or not from the server's `can`) and
  `refusals(person)` (why one isn't); `removeReady` (the typed name, exactly), `makeAdminWords`/`unmakeAdminWords`
  (the flip's question and what it loses), `removeLines`, `knownWords`, `madeWords` (what to tell the new person, with
  deadwax's address), `resetWords` (who was signed out), `savedWords`, `versionNote` (Navidrome older than People
  needs), `view` (which of the four faces the page draws: not allowed, locked, the list, not an admin in Navidrome),
  `checkboxes` (five, by category, locked for an admin and for a refused account), `lockedReason`, `changed`,
  `offered`/`allowed` (who is shown the row and who the page). `onPhone` turns the server's and the web's "You →
  Account → Change password" into the phone's place, "Settings → Account → Change password", wherever deadwax's words
  are said (a server before 2.1.35's: since it the server names Settings itself, which passes through unchanged).
  `clipped` keeps whole characters (never half a pair) up to a rule's most plus 8, so a field can't grow without end
  and its problem still shows. The models - PeopleState, PeoplePerson, PeopleKnownOnly, PeopleCan, PeopleTicks - read
  the GET's answer loosely (an unknown field ignored, a missing one its default), dedupe rows by id and drop a row
  with no id; the bodies - PeopleUnlockBody, PeopleCreateBody, PeopleResetBody, PeopleAdminBody, PeopleRemoveBody,
  PeopleForgetBody, PeoplePermissionsBody, PeopleLockBody - are each route's strict model key for key
  (PeoplePermissionsBody always sends all five). The three that carry a password, and PeopleAddForm and
  PeoplePasswords, redact themselves (`description`, `debugDescription`, an empty `customMirror`).
- **PeopleFlow.swift** (new). `PeopleFlow` is the page's state, as app/usePeople.ts holds it: the last answer (and
  when it was answered), the read's ticket (`readBegan`, `readEnded` - only the newest lands; a failed first read is
  said with Try again; a 403 asks /me again), the forms typed (Unlock's password, Add's four fields, Reset's two,
  Remove's typed name, each person's ticks), the sheet open, the one write out (`writing`) and what was said (`said`,
  placed: the list, Add, a person's Reset or their page). Each write is `beginX` - synchronously, in the tap: the
  ticket and the body, refused while another is out - and `ended(ticket, outcome, now:, signInOver:, origin:)`, which
  returns a `PeopleAfter`: the one announcement, whether to read the list again, to ask /me (after the flip, whatever
  came of it, and after a 403), to leave a person's page (after Remove), to arm the idle check. A refusal of kind
  `locked` (409) brings Unlock back at once: the answer and every password typed are dropped; Add's user and display
  names, the name typed into Remove and each person's unsaved ticks are kept (none secret), and a sheet still up says
  People.lockedNote. `hidden()` empties every password (the page going, Now Playing over it) - not the app going to
  the background, which leaves the fields as they are, so a password manager's fill or a paste from another app
  survives the trip; `signInCame()` does that, empties the typed name and puts a sheet away, unless a write is out -
  and `ended` does it once that write answers under the sign-in; `left()` forgets the answer once no page is left. `PeopleOutcome` and `PeopleRead` are what a
  write and a read came to: `refused(words:kind:fix:askMe:)` only for a 4xx (said as it came, with its `fix`; the 403 of
  require("people") has no kind), `failed` for a 5xx with deadwax's words, `unknown` ("deadwax may have finished - its
  answer never came", EditWords.mayHaveFinished, the transport's words in brackets for an admin) for a bare 5xx, a
  timeout or no answer, then a read again; `signedOut` for a 401 (through `sessionEnded`, never said here);
  `cancelled`, neither.
- **The unlock's timeout.** The server forgets an unlock after UNLOCK_IDLE_SECONDS (900) without a People request
  (`_unlock_for` keys it by the session's hash and refreshes it on each one). The web learns of it only from the next
  answer, a `locked` 409 or a read showing `unlocked: false`. The phone does the same, plus one read of its own:
  `People.idleCheckSeconds` (902) after the last answer, on a ContinuousClock (it counts through sleep), the model reads
  once - which, by then, the server answers locked, so Unlock shows without waiting for a tap to be refused. The read
  is a GET, and a GET refreshes the unlock only while it still stands - so the check never keeps it alive. It is the
  page's only timer; it runs while a People page shows and the app is active. **Once per answer**: a read sent while
  the check is due records the answer it was for (`idleAskedFor`, set by `readBegan(now:)`), and `idleWait` arms no
  other for that answer - so a check that fails (a 403, a proxy's 502, no answer) is said under the list and nothing
  more is asked by itself until a read or a write answers again.
- **PeopleWaits**: each route's wait worked out from the handlers' own worst cases - the store's busy timeout (10 s),
  a native call (20), a native write (60), Subsonic's getUser (20) - rounded up to the minute: the read 50 s plus 30 s
  an account (120 at least), Unlock 120, Make account, Reset, the flip and Remove 300, Forget and the permissions 240,
  Lock the transport's own (it forgets the unlock in memory). **DeadwaxClient**'s nine methods (`people(accounts:)` with
  the last answer's count, and one per write through `answer()`, never retried). **Routes**: nine endpoints (110
  routes).
- **Managing.swift**: People's row is native.

### The app

- **PeopleModel** (ios/App/Manage/, new): the app-held `@Observable` model, made in DeadwaxApp beside the event log's,
  reset in `whenPersonChanges`. It asks only while a People page shows, the app is active, deadwax can be reached, the
  sign-in isn't over the app, the person is allowed and there's a client (`mayAsk`); reads again on the page showing
  (after a second away, with nothing read, or with the idle check due), the app coming back, reach returning, the
  sign-in going, Now Playing closing and the session moving; and, after each answer, asks Navidrome's version and arms
  the idle check (`landed`) - only while `mayAsk` holds, so a read landing after the sign-in came or the page went is
  drawn and asks nothing more. A write takes its ticket in the tap, tells AppNavigation (`peopleWriting`), holds through
  the background (`BackgroundHold`), drops its answer if the person changed meanwhile (`generation`, bumped by `reset`
  from `whenPersonChanges`), and then announces, leaves the person's page, asks /me (not under the sign-in), reads again
  and arms the check - as `PeopleAfter` says. A session that moves while a write is out (Change password's re-key) lets
  the answer land: it is about the same person's accounts, and `sessionMoved()` only reads People again. Every binding to a field clips it and clears
  what was said (`typed(at:)`).
- **PeopleScreen** (new): one List. Not allowed: the permission's words. Then the status sections: deadwax's refusal
  with its fix (and Sharing's link where it names logins), **Unlock People** (`PeopleUnlockSection`: the SecureField,
  `.password` content, the focus unless VoiceOver runs, Unlock, the plain-http note under it), a failed read with Try
  again, deadwax out of reach with nothing read, or a spinner (`People.loading`). Unlocked: UNLOCKED_LINE, the version
  note, what was said, **Everyone in Navidrome** (you first; each row's name, user name, chips as one line, sign-in and
  library words, one VoiceOver element, a NavigationLink to the person's page by id) and **Known only to deadwax**
  (knownWords, and Forget… behind a confirmationDialog). The bar: **Lock**, and **+** (Add a person) - both only on the
  list. Back is hidden while a write is out.
- **PersonScreen** (new, pushed by `AppRoute.person(id)`): the person's facts and what was said; **Permissions** - the
  five Toggles (off for an admin, a refused account or while a write is out), lockedReason in the footer, **Save
  permissions** sending all five, on only when changed; then the actions `People.actions(person)` offers - Reset
  password… and Remove… open sheets, Make admin / No longer admin asks in a confirmationDialog (and flips only if the
  person is still what was asked about) - with `refusals(person)` in the footer.
- **PeopleSheets** (new): **AddPersonSheet** (user name, display name, Password and Password again as `.newPassword`,
  the problem as typed, the plain-http note, Make account; done, it says madeWords and the answer's warning, and Close
  becomes Done), **ResetPasswordSheet** (New password and New password again, the problem, the note, Reset password,
  then resetWords), **RemovePersonSheet** (removeLines - what goes, what stays, that there's no undo - the user name
  typed in mono, Remove in the danger red, on only by `removeReady`). Each is `.interactiveDismissDisabled` while a write
  is out, and keeps a snapshot of the person it opened for, so it still says who it was about when People locks again.
- **AppNavigation**: `.people` and `.person(id)`; `writingPeople`, so a tab tapped again keeps People's pages while a
  write is out (`People.pagesKept`); `leavePerson(id)` pops a removed person's page. **ManageSection**: People is a
  NavigationLink. **RootView**: scene, sign-in, session and Now Playing changes reach the model.

### What the web's .tsx files hold, read by pattern

ios/scripts/export-people-vectors.cjs runs lib/people.ts and lib/permissions.ts compiled, and reads out of
**app/People.tsx**, **app/UnlockPeople.tsx**, **app/AddPerson.tsx**, **app/ResetPassword.tsx**,
**app/RemovePerson.tsx**, **app/usePeople.ts** and **api/people.ts** by pattern (77 pieces hashed into made_from, so
iospeople fails when one moves): the labels and buttons, each body sent (compiled and run as a function of the form),
which actions are drawn, the flip's and Forget's words, what a `locked` refusal does, each route. 170 user names, 168
display names, 187 forms, 114 resets, 124 rows, 29 ages, 52 known-only rows, 12 typed names for Remove, 25 permission
changes, 20 things said after, 27 version strings and 6 views.

### Decided here, and where the phone departs from the spec (or the web)

- **The idle check** above: the web has no timer; the phone reads once 902 s after the last answer, on a clock that
  counts through sleep, and reads again on every return (scene, reach, the sign-in, Now Playing, the session).
- **Sheets, not inline forms**: Add, Reset and Remove are sheets; a person's page is pushed rather than opened in the
  list. A sheet stays up when People locks again, saying lockedNote ("People locked again - close this and unlock it
  with your Navidrome password. The passwords typed here are gone."); the sign-in coming over the app puts a sheet away
  unless a write is out.
- **What's kept through a lock**: Add's user and display names (also through Close), the name typed into Remove and
  each person's unsaved ticks - none secret, all annoying to type again; never a password.
- **The labels**: "Password again" / "New password again" for the web's Again; no Show passwords toggle (SecureField
  has none, and the password manager fills); Make account/Making…, Reset password/Resetting….
- **The phone's place** for Change password in every sentence deadwax or the web says (`People.onPhone`).
- **Each write's own fallback words** ("Couldn't make the account." and the rest) where the web has one for all; and
  "may have finished" with a read again for an unknown outcome, never a retry.
- **madeWords** names the user name sent when the answer names none.
- **Lock** shows Unlock People as soon as it answers, without waiting for the list read again.
- **What was said is placed** on the page it's about: Reset's in its sheet, the flip's and Save's on the person's page,
  the rest on the list.
- **Fields clipped** to the rule's most plus 8 whole characters (the unlock's password isn't: it's checked against
  Navidrome, not a rule).
- **`fix` is shown** under a refusal; the web reads only `detail`.
- **Chips as a joined line**, not capsules (the palette has none).
- **Rows** deduped by id and an empty id dropped (the list is keyed by identity); the name falls back to the user name.
- Assumed: no change of the admin's own password holds the sign-in throttle at the moment of an unlock (PeopleWaits'
  unlock wait counts one other unlock, not both).

### After review (17 Nov) - slice 11

One must-fix and four smaller findings, each traced in the code before it was fixed.

- **The idle check looped on a failed read** (the must-fix). `readEnded` returns non-nil for a failure, so the model
  ran `landed()` and `armIdle()` with `answeredAt` unmoved: once 902 s old the wait was 0, `idleDue` still true, and
  `read()` went again at once - and again on each failure. An admin demoted while away got People's 403 (`askMe`), so
  every turn also asked /me, each dropping the last /me still out; a proxy answering 502 while deadwax restarted kept
  Reachability online and looped until deadwax came back. Now Core decides: `readBegan(now:)` records the answer a read
  sent while the check is due was for (`idleAskedFor`), `idleDue` is false for that answer, and `idleWait(now:)` - the
  model's only way to arm it - is nil for it. Only a new answer (a read's list, a write's answer) arms another. Tested
  over a 403, a 502, a 5xx with words, no answer, a 401 and a cancellation, each sent while due: none arms a 0 s read,
  a read asked again by hand and failing arms none, an answer arms a full 902 s, and a read sent before the check is
  due leaves it armed as it was.
- **A sheet stayed over the sign-in after a write answered under it.** `signInCame()` keeps the sheet while a write is
  out (to say what came of it); when that write then answered (Add done, Reset or Remove refused or failed), `ended`
  only muted the announcement, and the sheet - with a refused Reset's passwords - stayed over the sign-in. Now `ended`,
  with `signInOver` and anything but `.signedOut`, does what `signInCame()` does once the outcome is recorded: the
  sheet goes, with every password and the typed name; what it said there goes with it (the list read once the sign-in
  goes says what came of it). Tested for Add, a refused Reset and a failed Remove, and that the same refusal with no
  sign-in keeps the sheet and its passwords.
- **Asks after a read landing under the sign-in or after the page left.** `landed()` asked Navidrome's version, armed
  the idle check, and the read's 403 spawned `refreshMe()` whatever the state - and `refreshMe()` clears `signInOver`
  when it succeeds. Now the read's /me, `landed()`'s version and idle check, and `askVersion` itself are each behind
  `mayAsk` (a page showing, the app active, in reach, no sign-in, allowed, a client), as ServerSettingsModel's
  `readIfNeeded` checks again; a write's /me isn't asked under the sign-in (signing in answers with /me's own answer, so the role is fresh once it
  goes).
  `shows()`, when it doesn't read, runs `landed()`, so a read that landed in the moment between two of People's pages
  still gets its version and its check.
- **The read after Unlock waited only the floor.** Its `accounts` came from the list in hand, which a lock empties, so
  the read that brings the list back - the one that matters - had the 120 s floor rather than 50 s plus 30 s an
  account. Now `accountsListed` keeps the last list's count through Lock, a `locked` refusal and People left (it
  changes only when a list is read); the model passes it. Tested: seven accounts kept through each (300 s), a shorter
  list read after taking its own count.
- **Two sentences here didn't match the code**, now corrected above: `hidden()` doesn't run as the app goes to the
  background (the fields are kept, so a password manager's fill survives the trip - the code is left so), and a write's
  answer is dropped only for another person (`generation`), not for a session that moved.

## No way out to the web app (Phase 8, slice 12 - 2026-11-17)

The spec's section 11 (notes/ios-specs/phase8-managing.md), with checks 388-391: James, 2026-11-16, "nothing in the
app should take you to the web app". Slices 1-11 each switched its own entry to the app's own page as it landed (the
album's ••• and Manage's Edit an album in 1, Needs a look in 6, Library care in 7, Server settings and Set up Navidrome
in 8, the event log in 9, Account's Change password in 10, People in 11), so by slice 11 nothing drew a way out to the
web app - but the pieces of Phase 7's were still there, unused. Slice 12 takes them out and adds a test that keeps any
new one out, by CI rather than by memory. Built on the `ios` branch at e879995. The app stays 0.13 (13);
src/__init__.py untouched; **no server change**; the player engine has no diff; the xcodeproj is unchanged.

### What went

- **Core, Managing.swift**: the web app's addresses - `appPath`, `fragment(_:)`, `albumFragment(id:)`, `youFragment`,
  `url(_:at:)`, `albumURL(id:at:)`, `youURL(at:)`, the internal `url(fragment:at:)` - and `notice(opened:)`, what a
  refused open said. `Tool.native`, true for every row since slice 11 and read only by the footer. **ManagingWords**:
  `changePasswordLine`, `opensInSafari`, `opens`, `othersOpen` (slice 1's constant and slice 6's function, with its
  `rest`), `signIn`, `offline`, `notOpened`, `footer(loginsOn:online:tools:)`, `outSymbol` and `safariSymbol`. What
  stays is every rule (`parts`, `albumEdit`, `artistManaging`, `asksQueueSummary`, `needsLook`, `tools`,
  `changeOffered`) and the words the fixture holds to the web's (`title`, `label`, `editAnAlbum`, `changePassword` -
  CHANGE_TITLE, read by ManagingVectorTests and OwnPasswordVectorTests).
- **AlbumInfoWords**' `opensInSafari` and `outSymbol` were aliases of Managing's two: they are Album info's own
  literals now, the same words ("Opens in Safari.", `arrow.up.forward`) - its MusicBrainz rows are one of the links
  out the app keeps.
- **The app**: `WebAppRow`, `extension OpenURLAction { webApp(_:player:) }`, and ManageSection's footer (drawn empty
  since slice 11), with the Reachability it read only for that. Comments that still said a thing opened in Safari
  (YouView, AccountSection, LibraryView's gate, NavidromeGate.swift) say what it opens now.
- **The vectors**: ios/scripts/export-managing-vectors.cjs no longer compiles lib/appRoutes.ts nor reads App.tsx's
  `openManagingPage`; the fixture's `addresses` and `albums` (14 album ids' web addresses) are gone, 36 KB to 33 KB,
  its `words`, `me` and `sets` byte for byte as they were. ui/test/iosmanaging.sim.cjs still runs it with `--check`.
- **Tests that held the gone**: ManagingTests' four (every tool at the web app's address on six kinds of base, none
  without one, the footer's words, a refused open's notice), ManagingVectorTests' address replay, ScreenYouTests'
  `changePasswordLine` line, PeopleFlowTests' `native` and `footer` lines; and in Python the five places that pinned
  `native`, `footer`, `WebAppRow` or `changePasswordLine` (test_ios_settings, test_ios_people,
  test_ios_server_settings, test_ios_library_care, test_ios_event_log) now pin that they're gone.

### What the spec named that was gone already, or never there

- `ManagingWords.editLine` and `editInWebApp` (and `line(_:)`) - slice 1 (see "Edit album on the phone").

### The test: tests/test_ios_no_web_app.py

It reads every Swift source of the app - ios/App and DeadwaxKit's Sources, 343 files - as the compiler lexes it, in
views of the same length and lines: comments blanked (nested block comments too); then string literals' contents and
`#/.../#` regex literals' blanked as well (raw, multi-line and escaped quotes; an interpolation's code kept, its own
strings blanked in turn; a regex on one line, or from a `#/` ending its line to its `/#`); and the string literals'
words alone. A use is looked for only in the second, so a word in a comment, a string or a regex is never one; every
file's brackets balance in it. A source with a string, comment or regex literal that never closes - where the reading
lost its place - is refused whole. Then:

- **Every `openURL(...)`, `Link(...)` and `ShareLink(...)`** - `Link` spelt `SwiftUI.Link`, `Link<Label>` or
  `Link.init` too - is found with what it opens or shares - openURL's first argument, Link's `destination:`,
  ShareLink's `item:` - and, when that is a bare name, what the name was last bound to before it (`guard let link =
  row.link else`, `if let address = URL(string: ...) {`, `if !state.on, let guide = ...`). Any other mention of `Link`
  or `ShareLink` (a typealias, `Link.init` handed on) is refused, so a spelling the test doesn't read fails rather
  than passing unread; NavigationLink, EQLink and creditLink are other names. Each call must be on its list, keyed by
  **file and what it opens or shares**, never a line number:

  | file (ios/App) | what it opens | the link |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | Album/AlbumInfoView.swift | `row.link` | Album info's This pressing / Every pressing on MusicBrainz |
  | EQ/EQProfileScreen.swift | `URL(string: EQWords.Profile.gitHubAddress)` | AutoEq on GitHub, at a correction's foot |
  | Manage/PeopleScreen.swift | `URL(string: People.sharingDoc)` | Sharing deadwax, when logins are turned off on deadwax with the app open |

  | file (ios/App) | what it shares | the share |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | EQ/EQExport.swift | `EQExportFile(... whole: true ...)` | Export... > The Whole Curve, a file |
  | EQ/EQExport.swift | `EQExportFile(... whole: false ...)` | Export... > The Correction Alone, a file |
  | You/DebugView.swift | `url` | the turntable recording's file |
  | You/DebugView.swift | `shown.text` | the engine log, as text |

  And each entry must still be found: an allowed link or share taken out fails until its entry goes too.
- **Where those three links go** is checked in Core: `gitHubAddress` and `sharingDoc` are each one literal, the whole
  address (AutoEq's project, and docs/sharing.md in deadwax's repository, both on GitHub); a row's `link` is made only
  by `AlbumInfo.page`, which answers `https://musicbrainz.org/<kind>/<id>` for a MusicBrainz id and nil for anything
  else; `self.link = link` in AlbumInfoRow's init is Core's only assignment, and an argument labelled `link:` anywhere
  but Core's AlbumInfo.swift is refused (an `AlbumInfoRow(..., link:)` or `.init(..., link:)` the app made).
- **deadwax's own address**: anything opened or shared whose destination names the phone's address (`ServerAddress`,
  `address`, `base`, `origin`, `absoluteString`, `/player`, `server.`) is refused, on a list or not. No Swift string
  literal is `"/player/"` or starts `"/player/#"`.
- **openURL itself**: the environment's `@Environment(\.openURL) var openURL` read once, under that name, only in a
  file whose own openURL call is allowed (Album info); a second read, one under another name, one in any other file, a
  `var`/`let openURL` of its own, `openURL` used any other way than called (Phase 7's `openURL.webApp(...)`, handed on
  as a value) and someone else's `.openURL(` (UIApplication's old one) are refused.
- **UIKit**: `UIApplication.shared` held under a name - but DownloadModel's `let application` - and `open`/`openURL`
  on `UIApplication`, `shared`, `application`, that name or a parameter typed `UIApplication` (the app delegate's);
  and any `open(..., options:)`, a scene's open or UIApplication's.
- **Never at all**: `OpenURLAction` (an extension, or a handler), the environment's openURL set
  (`.environment(\.openURL, ...)`), `SFSafariViewController` and `import SafariServices`, `WKWebView`, SwiftUI's
  `WebView`, `import WebKit`, `ASWebAuthenticationSession`, `UIActivityViewController`, markdown parsed at run time
  (an argument labelled `markdown:`), a `LocalizedStringKey(...)` or `Text(.init(...))` made at run time (its markdown
  links tap), and a link attribute (`LinkAttribute`, an `AttributeContainer`'s `.link`, `NSAttributedString.Key.link`,
  `dataDetectorTypes`; `.link(...)` called on something, `.link =` set, `.link:` as a key but in a `case`). A case's
  own `.link(...)` - after `case`, `return`, `(` or an operator - is no call on anything, and passes.
- **In a string literal's words** (each literal on its own, an interpolation's opening `\(` kept): a markdown link to
  an address (`](` then any scheme, `<scheme:` or an interpolation), a link's address given apart (`[1]: https:...`),
  an autolink (`<https:...>`, `<name@...>`, `<\(...)>`) - each of which SwiftUI's Text would draw as a link - and, in
  ios/App's literals, any address at all (`scheme://`, `www.`), since a Text may make a bare one tappable too and Core
  holds the app's addresses. The one kept is ServerAddressView's placeholder, `http://192.168.1.20:8090`.
- **The reading's own two facts**: ios/App is built in Swift 5 mode (SWIFT_VERSION 5.0 in ios/Config, nothing turning
  bare-slash regexes on), where `/.../` is no regex literal - so `#/.../#`, which it reads, is the only kind the app
  can have; and DeadwaxKit's Sources import no UI framework (SwiftUI, UIKit, SafariServices, WebKit,
  AuthenticationServices, AppKit), so Core - Swift 6 mode, where `/.../` is a regex this doesn't read - has no way out
  to write.
- **The gone stay gone**: none of Managing's removed names in Core, none of `WebAppRow`, `webApp(`, `webEdit` or
  `Managing.url(`/`albumURL(`/`youURL(`/`notice(` anywhere, no `addresses` or `albums` in the fixture and nothing made
  from appRoutes.ts or openManagingPage, and no appRoutes, formatRoute or parseHash in the exporter.

**The matcher is held to made-up sources first** (`test_the_matcher_refuses_a_planted_way_out`): 51 planted ways out,
each asserted refused *for its reason* - a bare openURL, a Link with and without a label, the web app's address built
from the server's base, `Managing.url` as Phase 7 called it, Phase 7's own WebAppRow and extension (cut down from
e879995's ManageSection.swift), `openURL.webApp` alone, UIApplication's two opens, openURL handed on, Safari's view,
WKWebView and SwiftUI's WebView, a markdown link, a ShareLink of deadwax's base, an openURL handler; and since the
review each bypass it found (below) - and nine more asserts: Phase 7's row read as ManageSection.swift (no link out
of its own there), an allowed destination or share in the wrong file, one
in its own file built from deadwax's address, a second or renamed environment read and an openURL of its own in
Album info's file, an Album info row's link made there, and DownloadModel's binding anywhere else. And to what isn't
one (`test_the_matcher_passes_what_isnt_a_way_out`): the words in line, block (nested), raw, multi-line and
interpolated strings, NavigationLink, EQLink, creditLink, updateLink, `.onOpenURL` (a file shared *to* the app),
`navigation.open(...)`, a case's `.link(...)` and `.link:`, UIKit as the app uses it (`UIApplication.shared.` this and
that, its notifications, the app delegate's `application(_:didFinishLaunchingWithOptions:)`), three regex literals -
and the three links, the four shares, DownloadModel's `application`, the placeholder and Core's row links, each in its
own file.

**And against the real files**: thirteen mutations planted into the sources themselves, the test run against each, the
file put back - a Link to the server's base in the Library, an OpenURLAction in Settings, Album info opening another
property, the EQ's Link pointed at another constant, People's Link taken away (the allowlist gone stale), the AutoEq
address changed to deadwax's `/player/`, a markdown link in a Text in Account; and after review a
`SwiftUI.Link<Text>.init` in the Library, a ShareLink of its own in Account, `UIApplication.shared` held as `ui` in
KeyWindow, a `#/a//b/#` hiding an openURL in Album info, a second environment read there, and a
`Text(LocalizedStringKey(words))` in Account: each failed the test, one test each.

### Decided here, and where the phone departs from the spec

- **Python, not Swift**: the Swift suite can't read the App's sources; pytest runs on every push and tag through
  tests.yml and docker-publish's call, beside the other test_ios_* readers of the App.
- **Keyed by file and destination after one binding**, so a line moving, a label renamed or a modifier added changes
  nothing, while what it opens changing - or the same expression in another file - fails.
- **`Tool.native` and `othersOpen` went too**, though the spec's list doesn't name them: the footer was their only
  reader, and both only said which rows opened Safari.
- **ShareLink has a list of its own** (since the review; at first it wasn't listed, only kept from deadwax's address):
  it hands a file or text to the share sheet rather than opening a page, but a new one could share deadwax's address
  under a name the address check can't see, so each is keyed as Link is. There are four: the EQ's two exports (a
  file), Debug's turntable recording (a file) and Debug's engine log (text).
- **No other link out was found.** `.onOpenURL` in RootView is the other way in (a file shared to deadwax). The test
  reads DeadwaxKit's Sources too, where there's no SwiftUI today, so one added there is refused all the same.
- **The docs**: docs/ios.md says in Manage that nothing in the app takes you to the web app and lists the three links
  out; the intro, "What it can't do yet" and two troubleshooting rows (Get lyrics, and Connections for slskd's refusal)
  no longer point at the web app for managing. The old checks (237-246) keep their words, with a line pointing at
  388-391.

### Tests

- **tests/test_ios_no_web_app.py** (new, 6): the matcher refuses 51 planted ways out, each for its reason, and passes
  what isn't one; nothing in the 343 sources opens the web app, the three links and four shares listed are all there
  are and each is there; the app is read as Swift reads it (Swift 5 mode, no UI framework in DeadwaxKit); each link
  goes to a site that isn't deadwax's; the web app's way out is gone from Core, the App and the vectors.
- **Swift**: ManagingTests (2 left: each reader's rows, Change password's offer), ManagingVectorTests (3: the
  fixture without addresses and not made from appRoutes.ts, the words and order, every set and /me answer),
  ScreenYouTests, PeopleFlowTests.
- **ui/test/iosmanaging.sim.cjs**: the exporter's `--check`, without the addresses (notes/sims.md).

On the Mac: `swift test` (2232 tests: 2062, 158 and 12, all passed - five fewer in Core than before, the address and
footer tests that went); the unsigned generic-iOS Debug build, BUILD SUCCEEDED, with only the AppIntents metadata

### After review (17 Nov) - slice 12

The review found no way out in the code, and two must-fixes and five gaps in the test, each fixed here and each
bypass it used planted in the matcher's made-up sources, refused for its own reason.

- **Check 389 sent James through a step he can't reach** (a must-fix). With logins off, Manage has no People row
  (`Managing.parts`: `people` needs `loginsOn`), and the checks are done signed in as an admin with logins on - so
  People's logins-off line, with **Sharing deadwax** under it, shows only if logins are turned off on deadwax while
  the app is open. 389 checks the two links a tap can reach and says why the third isn't a step; Manage's table says
  when Sharing deadwax shows, and that the test keeps it to the guide on GitHub. "Each opens in Safari" there and in
  389 is "your browser (Safari unless you've changed it)" now; Album info's own "Opens in Safari." stays.
- **Link spelt another way passed unread** (a must-fix): `SwiftUI.Link(...)`, `Link<Text>(...)` and `Link.init(...)`
  weren't calls to the matcher. Now they are, and any other mention of `Link` or `ShareLink` is refused.
- **UIKit's opens**: `let ui = UIApplication.shared; ui.open(url)` and `scene.open(url, options: nil)` passed. Now
  UIApplication.shared is held only as DownloadModel's `application`, open is refused on anything that holds it (the
  app delegate's parameter too), and so is any `open(..., options:)`.
- **Tappable text with no `](https:`**: an attribute container's link, a LocalizedStringKey made at run time, an
  autolink, and a markdown link to an interpolated address passed. Now each is refused, with the link attribute's
  other ways in (`.link =`, `NSAttributedString.Key.link`, `.link:`, `dataDetectorTypes`), a link's address given
  apart, any scheme after `](`, and in ios/App's literals any address at all - the one kept a TextField's placeholder.
  `.link(...)` is refused as a call on something rather than everywhere: Artists' credits use a `.link(id:)` case.
- **ShareLink** was kept from deadwax's address but not listed, so a new one sharing it under another name passed.
  Now it has its list of four, as Link has, and `UIActivityViewController` is refused. The docstring claims only what
  the test does.
- **Inside an allowed file**, any number of environment reads under any name passed, and so did the environment's
  openURL set and an Album info row given a `link:` by the app. Now Album info's one read, as `openURL`, is all; the
  environment's openURL set is refused anywhere; and a `link:` argument outside Core's AlbumInfo.swift is refused.
- **A regex literal hid the rest of its line**: `#/a//b/#` read as a comment from its `//`. Now `#/.../#` (any number
  of `#`, on one line or over lines) is read as the literal it is, the first `/#` closing it (an escaped one closing
  it early only shows more as code). And the reading refuses a source it lost its place in - a string, comment or
  regex that never closes - rather than trusting what follows. The bare `/.../` regex isn't read; the test holds the
  app to Swift 5 mode, where it isn't one, and DeadwaxKit - Core is Swift 6 - to importing no UI framework.

Verified after review, on the Mac: `swift test` (2232: 2062, 158 and 12, all passed); the unsigned generic-iOS Debug
build, BUILD SUCCEEDED with only the AppIntents warning; check_project.py; pyflakes over src and tests;
tests/test_ios_*.py, test_source_bytes.py and test_logins.py (609 passed, 1 skipped - the new reading test the one
more); all 98 sims with Node 22; and the thirteen mutations above, against the real files. Nothing in the app changed.

## The Mac app, slice 1: it runs and plays (2026-11-17)

The Mac app's plan (~/Desktop/Code/deadwax-plans/mac-app.md), slice 1 - sections 0, 1.1, 1.4, 3, 4, 5 and 11, with
James's answers of 17 Nov: the Mac idiom (TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY 6); no provisioning profile, the sign-in kept in a
file in the sandbox container, made 0600, never the Keychain; closing the window may quit the app for now (the music
playing on with it closed is slice 2's, and nothing here makes it harder); downloads as on the phone; macOS 14. The
iPhone app built for the Mac through Mac Catalyst from the same files - one target, one scheme, one MARKETING_VERSION
(0.13 (13)). Built on `mac1`, from the `ios` branch at 4bee7e9. src/__init__.py untouched; **no server change**;
**ios/Deadwax.xcodeproj untouched** - every setting is in the xcconfigs, as the trial found; PlaybackEngine has no
diff, and DeadwaxAudio's one change is DeckVoiceHost's import.

### The trial's three fixes

- `SUPPORTS_MACCATALYST = YES` (Base.xcconfig; it was NO in the device-only block).
- `import CoreAudio` in DeadwaxAudio's DeckVoiceHost.swift: on Catalyst, `UnsafeMutableAudioBufferListPointer` comes
  from CoreAudio, which AVFAudio doesn't re-export there as it does on the iPhone.
- `INFOPLIST_FILE[sdk=macosx*] = Config/Info-Mac.plist`: macOS refuses `LSSupportsOpeningDocumentsInPlace = NO`
  ("not supported on macOS. Either remove the entry or set it to YES"), which the phone's plist needs.

### Core (DeadwaxCore)

- **Device.swift** (new): `Device` - `.iPhone`, `.mac`. Core never asks the platform; what differs takes the device
  as a value (section 3.3), handed in by the App's `Platform.device`.
- **Resume.swift**: `Resume.label(for:)` - "iPhone" (the old `label`, kept) or "Mac", the web's `deviceLabel` for
  Safari on a Mac (resume.ts), so the other device's notice says "Picked up from your Mac". Inside play_queue.py's
  LABEL_PATTERN.
- **SessionFile.swift** (new): the Mac's sign-in, the same three calls SessionKeychain has.
  - **Where**: `<Application Support>/deadwax/sessions/<name>` - in the container,
    `~/Library/Containers/net.lizardlounge.deadwax/Data/Library/Application Support/deadwax/sessions/`. One file a
    server, its account in the Keychain's terms.
  - **The name** is the server's, escaped as KeptAlbumIndex.safeName escapes the kept /me's folder (`%` and two hex
    digits for every byte but an ASCII letter or digit; never a `/` or `.`). Past 200 bytes it is a 183-character
    prefix, `-`, and FNV-1a 64 of the whole server in 16 hex digits, so two long servers stay apart, every name fits
    APFS's 255 with the temporary file's `.` and `.new`, and a capped name (the one with a bare `-`) can't be an
    uncapped one.
  - **Kept for this user alone**: the folder made 0700 (and tightened if it was looser), the file 0600 - made so
    before a byte is written: `.<name>.new` created empty with `posixPermissions` 0600, its mode checked, the value
    written and synchronized, then put in place - over an old file in one step since the review (`place`, below). A
    replaced file takes the new one's mode, so a 0644 left by anything else becomes 0600 at the next save.
  - **A failed save keeps nothing**: the temporary file is removed and the server's old file deleted too, as the
    Keychain's delete-then-add leaves nothing when the add fails - a stale session never outlives a failed save. The
    App ignores the Bool, as it ignores the Keychain's.
  - **Read** takes a regular file only, decoded as UTF-8; a `.new` left by a stop mid-save is never read as the
    session. **Delete** (sign-out) removes the file and any `.new` beside it.
  - Nothing is logged, and nothing but the cookie's value is in the file.

### The app

- **Shared/Platform.swift** (new) - **the one switch**: `#if targetEnvironment(macCatalyst)`, said once, in this file
  alone (tests/test_ios_mac.py holds it). `Platform.mac`, `Platform.device`; on the Mac `Platform.launching()`,
  `Scene.macWindow()` and a no-op `View.pullToRefresh`; on the iPhone `launching()` does nothing, `macWindow()` is
  `self` and `pullToRefresh` is SwiftUI's `refreshable(action:)`.
- **The window** (1.1): `macWindow()` - `.defaultSize(430 x 860)` and `.commands` replacing `.newItem` (no New
  Window) and `.help` (no help book) with nothing. `launching()`, from the app delegate's didFinishLaunching, observes
  `UIScene.willConnectNotification` and `didActivateNotification` and sets each window scene's
  `sizeRestrictions` (390 x 640 at least, 600 wide at most) and `titlebar` (no title, the unified toolbar) - again at
  each activation, in case the first came too soon for macOS to take them.
- **SessionStore.swift** (new): read, save, delete - `SessionFile` on the Mac, `SessionKeychain` on the iPhone,
  exactly as before. ServerModel's five calls (two reads, two saves, the one delete in `signOut()`, the only sign-out
  path that cleared the Keychain) go through it.
- **NowPlayingController**: on the Mac, `MPNowPlayingInfoCenter.playbackState` beside `nowPlayingInfo` (1.4) -
  playing or paused in `show`, paused in `republishPaused`, stopped in `clear`. iOS works it out from the audio
  session, so the phone doesn't set it.
- **PlayerModel**: the ResumeController's label is `Resume.label(for: Platform.device)`.
- **Pull to refresh** (section 11): the 17 `.refreshable` in 15 files are `.pullToRefresh` - one helper, not 17
  `#if`s. The helper's closure is `@MainActor @Sendable`: SwiftUI's own takes `@_inheritActorContext`, which a
  wrapper can't, and without the `@MainActor` every call site warned that main-actor work ran outside the actor.

### The build, the icon and the scripts

- **Base.xcconfig**: the Mac block - `SUPPORTS_MACCATALYST = YES`, `DERIVE_MACCATALYST_PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER =
  NO` (already the default; said, so the Mac's id can't become `maccatalyst.…`), and `[sdk=macosx*]` for the rest:
  TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY 6, INFOPLIST_FILE Config/Info-Mac.plist, ENABLE_APP_SANDBOX YES,
  ENABLE_OUTGOING_NETWORK_CONNECTIONS YES, and since the review ENABLE_USER_SELECTED_FILES readonly (the EQ's Import
  from Files…). No MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET: it follows IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET 17.0 to
  macOS 14.0 (the built plist's LSMinimumSystemVersion; the binary's LC_BUILD_VERSION is platform 6, minos 17.0). The
  entitlements come from the three ENABLE_ settings - no .entitlements file, so nothing that needs a profile.
  **The block must come after every setting it qualifies**: the first Mac build read Info.plist and failed, because
  `INFOPLIST_FILE[sdk=macosx*]` stood above `INFOPLIST_FILE = Config/Info.plist`, and a later plain assignment hides
  an earlier conditional one. check_project.py refuses that order now.
- **Config/Info-Mac.plist** (new): Info.plist less LSSupportsOpeningDocumentsInPlace, plus CFBundleName `deadwax`
  (the menu bar's About, Hide and Quit deadwax - the phone's stays $(PRODUCT_NAME), which its home screen never
  shows), CFBundleIconFile `AppIcon`, LSApplicationCategoryType `public.app-category.music`, and
  NSSupportsAutomaticTermination and NSSupportsSuddenTermination both NO (a music player must not be quit by macOS
  while it plays with no window in front). UIApplicationSupportsMultipleScenes stays NO: slice 2's.
- **The icon**: make-icon.py draws the Mac's too - the record on macOS's rounded square (824 px of 1024, 100 px in
  from each edge, corner radius 185), RGBA with the corners transparent, supersampled - and writes
  `App/Icon/AppIcon.icns` (icp4, ic11, icp5, ic12, ic07, ic13, ic08, ic14, ic09, ic10: 16 to 1024 px, 243,476 bytes).
  The phone's PNGs come out byte for byte as before. No asset catalog, as before (actool needs a Simulator runtime).
  The iPhone's .app carries the icns too, unused there - the one byte-level difference in its bundle.
- **check_project.py**: the xcconfig reader keeps a conditional `KEY[cond]` as a key of its own, so the iPhone's
  `KEY` reads as it did. New rules: each Mac setting as MAC_SETTINGS has it; any other conditional setting refused
  (nothing changes the iPhone build by the back door); the phone's TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY still 1; no
  MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET in any xcconfig; no plain `KEY =` after a `KEY[...]` in Base.xcconfig, nor any in
  Debug/Release.xcconfig; **Info-Mac.plist is Info.plist** less the one key and plus the five, value for value - a key
  added to either alone, or a value changed, is "the two have drifted"; the icns's types and sizes, its 1024 present,
  opaque at its centre and transparent at its corners (an unfiltered 8-bit RGBA PNG, as make-icon.py writes).
- **install_helper.py**: `plist <file> <key>` (a top-level value as text) and `entitlements <file>` - "ok" when the
  signed entitlements hold app-sandbox, network.client and (since the review) files.user-selected.read-only, and no
  keychain-access-groups or application-groups.
- **ios/scripts/install-mac.sh** (new; bash 3.2, `set -euo pipefail`, install.sh's say/step/stop/confirm):
  1. Xcode (DEVELOPER_DIR defaulting to /Applications/Xcode.app; 16 or later) and Xcode's python3 for the helper.
  2. The free space said (`df -h`), and a stop below 4 GB (`df -k`).
  3. The team from ios/Config/Local.xcconfig (`helper setting`); none, or the example's XXXXXXXXXX, stops, naming
     install.sh and the example.
  4. install.sh's project guard (Xcode's edits to the .xcodeproj stop the pull), then `git pull --ff-only` unless
     `--no-pull`.
  5. GitHub asked whether ios.yml passed on the commit (`helper ci`); a failure or a run still going is asked about
     (`--yes` answers it - since the review, this question and no other); out of reach builds anyway.
  6. `xcodebuild … -configuration Release -destination 'generic/platform=macOS,variant=Mac Catalyst' ARCHS=arm64
     -derivedDataPath ~/Library/Caches/deadwax-build-mac -allowProvisioningUpdates build` (Debug with `--debug`), its
     log in last-build.log there; a failure shows its errors and last lines and names the Apple Development
     certificate. The build time is said.
  7. What it made: `codesign --verify --strict`; `codesign -d --entitlements - --xml` through `helper entitlements`;
     the bundle id through `helper plist`; and, should Xcode have embedded a profile after all, its expiry said
     (`security cms -D`, `helper expiry`) - since the review, as a stop installing nothing (its UUID and how to be rid
     of it), unless `--allow-profile`.
  8. deadwax open (`osascript -e 'application id "net.lizardlounge.deadwax" is running'`, which neither opens nor
     asks it anything): "deadwax is open - quit it to install the new one? (If it's playing, the music stops.)" - asked
     only after the build, so the music stops only once the new build is ready. No stops with nothing changed; yes
     (or Enter) sends `tell application id … to quit` and waits up to 20 s; an Automation refusal or a deadwax that
     won't go stops, saying so - never kill. `--quit` (since the review) sends it without asking; `--yes` never does.
  9. `--dry-run` stops here, having said each "would" (the pull, the build line, the checks, the quit, the copy and
     the open) and done none of it.
  10. Into place: `mkdir -p ~/Applications`; a `.deadwax.app.old` left by a stopped run put back first; `ditto` to
      `.deadwax.app.new`; the old app moved aside, the new one moved in (the old one back if that fails), the old
      removed. Never /Applications, never sudo.
  11. `open ~/Applications/deadwax.app`, then the version and build (Base.xcconfig), the time, and the space before
      and after.
- **ios.yml**, the macOS job: "The Mac app, an unsigned Catalyst build" (Release, arm64, `build-mac`, signing off)
  after the iPhone's, and "What the Mac build made", one test a line: arm64 alone, the icns, the bundle id, 0.13,
  CFBundleName deadwax, CFBundleIconFile, UIDeviceFamily 6, LSMinimumSystemVersion 14.0, the category, both
  termination keys false, UIBackgroundModes' audio, and no LSSupportsOpeningDocumentsInPlace. The project job's
  `bash -n` over ios/scripts/*.sh takes install-mac.sh by itself.

### Decided here, and where it departs from the plan

- **The session file fails closed**: a save that can't complete deletes the server's file rather than leave an older
  session in it; the Keychain's own save (delete, then add) behaves the same.
- **No Keychain probe on Debug** (section 11 suggested one, to say for certain what the Keychain answers without a
  profile). Nothing in slice 1 reads the Keychain on the Mac, so it would answer a question nothing asks; TN3137 says
  the data-protection keychain needs the entitlement a profile gives. Left for a slice that needs it.
- **The window is shaped from the scene notifications**, not a scene delegate: the app is SwiftUI's
  `WindowGroup` with an app delegate and no scene delegate of its own, and a notification observer needs no change
  to the project.
- **install-mac.sh `--dry-run`**, beyond the plan: it says each step's command and does nothing, so the script can
  be read against the Mac before it touches anything.
- **Hardened runtime**: Xcode 27 turns ENABLE_HARDENED_RUNTIME on for a macOS build by itself; nothing here needs an
  exception from it (no JIT, no unsigned libraries), so it stays as Xcode has it.

### After review (17 Nov) - Mac slice 1

The review of ff9fb2b found one must-fix and six gaps, each fixed here.

- **AppIcon.icns failed tests/test_source_bytes.py** (the must-fix): the slice's own run passed only because the icns
  was still untracked then, and the test reads git's files. `.icns` is in BINARY_IN now, allowed in `ios/App/Icon/`
  alone, with the .ttf's kind of comment, and the test of the rule says it's checked anywhere else. Run again on the
  commit itself.
- **Import from Files… on the Mac**: the EQ's `.fileImporter` opens the Mac's Open panel, and under the App Sandbox a
  file chosen there is readable only with `com.apple.security.files.user-selected.read-only`.
  `ENABLE_USER_SELECTED_FILES[sdk=macosx*] = readonly` gives it from a build setting, as the other two - no
  .entitlements file, no profile. It's one of check_project's MAC_SETTINGS and one of install_helper's
  MAC_ENTITLEMENTS (read-write is refused: it isn't read-only). Export… is a ShareLink and needs nothing. ios.yml's
  Mac build is unsigned, so it reads no entitlements and has nothing to add.
- **The session file and Time Machine**: the phone's Keychain item is `AfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly`, so no backup
  carries the sign-in elsewhere; ~/Library/Containers is backed up. SessionStore marks the sessions folder
  `isExcludedFromBackup` after every save - so a folder made again is marked again - App-side, as the flag is a
  Foundation resource value Core needn't know of. The folder holds sessions alone. test_ios_mac pins the order
  (save, then the flag) and the Keychain's ThisDeviceOnly it matches.
- **SessionFile.save over an old file** now puts the new one in place in one step: `place(_:at:)` -
  `replaceItemAt(final, withItemAt: temporary, backupItemName: nil, options: .usingNewMetadataOnly)` when what's
  there is a regular file (the new file's metadata, so its 0600, rather than the old one's merged in), else whatever
  has the name (a symlink, a folder) removed - never followed or written through - and the temporary moved in. What's
  in place is then checked regular (lstat) and held to 0600 (`ensure`), or the save fails closed as before.
- **An empty server** would have been `url("")` - the sessions folder itself - and a failed save's `delete("")`
  every session. read, save and delete each refuse an empty server first.
- **A profile Xcode embedded after all** is the 7-day app James decided against, so install-mac.sh stops there,
  before deadwax is asked to quit and before anything is copied: when it runs out, the profile's UUID file name in
  ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/UserData/Provisioning Profiles, check_project.py to name a setting that needs one, and
  the build folder to delete. `--allow-profile` installs it anyway, with the old note; `--yes` isn't enough. The dry
  run says which.
- **`--yes` stopped the music**: it answered every question, the quit included. It answers GitHub's checks alone now;
  `--quit` quits a running deadwax without asking. Without `--quit`, the question is asked as before - Enter is
  yes, and no answer at all (not a terminal) is no, so `--yes` from a script leaves deadwax playing and installs
  nothing. The help, the docs' table and checks 404, 407, 412 and 414 say so.
- **The docs**: check 407's `ls -l` and the "sign in every time" row reach into another app's container, so macOS
  may ask whether "Terminal" would like to access data from other apps - Allow is right, said in both and in "Where
  the Mac keeps your sign-in" (with Time Machine). The differences list gains Import from Files… (the Open panel)
  and Export… (the Mac's Share menu); its other lines held as they were. Rows for the profile stop and for an
  import that can't be read.

Tests: SessionFileTests three more (the in-place replace over a 0644 file; a symlink and a folder of the name
replaced, never written through; the empty server); test_ios_mac's session tests pinning the guards, `place` and
the backup flag; test_ios_install_mac - `--yes` asks about the quit and, unanswered, stops; `--quit`; Enter is yes;
the profile stop with and without `--yes`, `--allow-profile` installing; the dry run with both new flags; the new
entitlement missing or read-write; ENABLE_USER_SELECTED_FILES changed; the help's flags (55 cases now).

## On James's Mac: every sheet carries the app's models (2026-11-17)

**What James saw** (Mac app 0.13 at 64e3e9c, slice 1): "the Mac app opened fine, Local Network allowed" (404 in part:
nothing asked before it opened, so no Gatekeeper or Open Anyway for a build made on this Mac; 406: the Local Network
prompt came, he chose Allow - whether it asked again for the IP versus the name, not said). Then: "I tried to open the
play screen and the mac app has become completely non-functional".

**What the Mac said.** Three runs. The first crashed as the click presented Now Playing - its crash report and its log:
`SwiftUICore/Environment+Objects.swift:34: Fatal error: No Observable object of type PlayerModel found`, raised in
`PresentationHostingController.init` under `SheetBridge.present`, with none of the app's own frames between: the page
presented had NO environment at all, not one model missing. The next two hung on the same click (12 s and 24 s, two
`.hang` reports in /Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports - the main thread in layout under a UINavigationController's
transition, with `<OnScrollGeometryChange Modifier> tried to update multiple times per frame` logged as it began) until
he quit. Each click's log shows the Mac making a scene of its own for the presentation ("Creating foregrounded scene
(persistentID: UINSSceneHostingViewController-…)").

**Reproduced here, without a click.** A scratch build (never committed) with a hook - an environment variable opening
Now Playing, or the EQ import sheet, 6 s after launch - run through `open --env … --stdout …` (run straight from the
shell, the app waits for ever in `AVAudioSession sharedInstance`'s XPC: macOS's audio service won't answer a process
LaunchServices didn't start). Both crashed the same way: Now Playing on `PlayerModel`, the plain `.sheet` on
`AppNavigation`, its first. So every sheet and cover on the Mac, not Now Playing's alone - slice 1 shipped with none of
them ever opened (nothing here can click, and its checks hadn't been run).

**Why.** On the iPhone a presented page inherits its presenter's environment, so the 23 models DeadwaxApp puts on its
root reach every sheet. On the Mac (macOS 27.2's Catalyst, the Mac idiom) the presentation is hosted in that scene of
its own and its page starts from an empty environment. Putting the models on the WindowGroup scene instead
(`Scene.environment`) was tried in the scratch build: the same two crashes - the presentation's scene isn't the
WindowGroup's.

**What changed.**
- **Shared/Presenting.swift (new)**: `appSheet` and `appCover`, the `isPresented` and the `item` forms of SwiftUI's
  `.sheet` and `.fullScreenCover`, each a modifier that reads, on the presenter's side, `\.appModels` (AppModels, one
  field for each of DeadwaxApp's 23 models) and the two layout values a page's sheets inherit on the iPhone
  (`\.tabBarRoom`, `\.playerClearance`), and puts them on the page it presents through `carryingApp`. `CarriesApp` puts
  each model back, `\.appModels` itself (so a sheet over a sheet carries them on), the two values, and the root's tint
  and font.
- **Platform.swift**: `carryingApp` is `modifier(CarriesApp(carried:))` on the Mac and `self` on the iPhone - so on the
  iPhone every presentation is SwiftUI's own exactly as before, inheriting as it always has.
- **DeadwaxApp.swift**: `.environment(\.appModels, AppModels(…))` beside the 23 `.environment(model)`.
- **All 23 presentations** (13 files, CoverViewer's `coverViewer` among them) call `appSheet` / `appCover`.
- **tests/test_ios_mac.py**: no `sheet(`, `fullScreenCover(`, `popover(` or `inspector(` in the App outside
  Presenting.swift (whose four are each followed by `.carryingApp(carried)`); AppModels' fields, the `AppModels(…)`
  DeadwaxApp makes and CarriesApp's `.environment(m.…)` are DeadwaxApp's `.environment(…)` models, in its order; Platform
  says `carryingApp` as above on each side. Both new tests were seen failing: on a bare `.sheet(` put back in AlbumView,
  and on `people` left out of CarriesApp.

**Not carried, on purpose**: values set beside a presentation rather than above it - EQSheet's `\.eqDone` and
`EQSheetStack`, `\.editMode` - which its sheets don't inherit on the iPhone either (each is put on inside the modifier
that presents).

**Verified here**: the scratch build with this change and the hook - Now Playing opened and stayed up, and the EQ
import sheet too, each still running 20 s later at 0% CPU, no crash report, no "multiple times per frame" fault;
test_ios_mac.py and test_ios_install_mac.py; the builds and checks listed in the commit. **Not verified**: whether the
hang James saw was this same fault seen another way (it never came back in the scratch runs, but no click was made in
them) - check 408's Now Playing step and 413's every-page pass say; `Menu` and `.contextMenu` contents, which aren't
presentations here, were never opened on the Mac either.

## The Mac app, slice 2: menus, keys, right-click and the window (2026-11-17)

The Mac app's plan (~/Desktop/Code/deadwax-plans/mac-app.md), slice 2 - sections 1.1 (closing the window, decision 4)
and 1.3, item 2 of section 6, checks 416-423 of section 7. Built on `mac-s2`, from the `ios` branch at 64e3e9c (slice
1 and main's 2.1.35). src/__init__.py untouched, the app still 0.13 (13); **no server change**;
**ios/Deadwax.xcodeproj untouched** (the App folder is synchronized, so the two new App files needed nothing); the
engine files and DeadwaxAudio have no diff. **Nothing an iPhone user sees or does changes**: every new helper is
Platform.swift's, and is the view itself (or EmptyView) on the iPhone.

### Core (DeadwaxCore)

- **MacMenu.swift** (new): what deadwax adds to the menu bar - each item's words, key, whether it can be used and
  whether it's ticked, from a `State` the App reads each time the menus are drawn (queued, playing, shuffle, a
  library's shuffle (`paged`), Repeat, the song's length, whether it names an album, a text field with the cursor,
  the tabs shown, the page's Refresh (none, ready, on its way), Now Playing open).
  - **The commands and keys** (the plan's 1.3): Settings… ⌘, - Find ⌘F - Refresh ⌘R - Play/Pause Space - Next ⌘→ -
    Previous ⌘← - Forward 10 Seconds ⌥⌘→ - Back 10 Seconds ⌥⌘← - Shuffle - Repeat off, Repeat all, Repeat one (a
    submenu, Up Next's order) - Go to Current Song ⌘L. No two share a key, none is the system's (⌘Q, ⌘W, ⌘H, ⌘M, ⌃⌘F).
  - **The words** are the app's where it has them, never retyped: Play/Pause and Next the player's (PlayerWords),
    Previous Now Playing's, Shuffle `shuffleLabel(paged)`, Repeat's submenu `repeatLabel(.off)` and its three
    `UpNextWords.repeatSaid`, Refresh the Library's ••• (LibrarySwitchWords.refresh), Settings… the tab's own name
    (YouWords.title) with the Mac's ellipsis. Controls, Forward/Back 10 Seconds, Go to Current Song and Find are the
    Mac's own, as Music names them. (After review: the dialogs' Cancel the Mac draws is QueuePickWords.cancel, the
    app's own word - MacMenu's retyped `Words.cancel` went.)
  - **Enabled**: every Controls item needs something queued; Forward and Back a known length; Shuffle not a library's
    shuffle (on and dimmed then, as Now Playing's); Go to Current Song an album and the tabs; Settings… and Find the
    tabs (signed in, the sign-in not over them); Refresh the tabs, a page with one, none on its way and Now Playing
    closed (the page under it isn't refreshed unseen). **Ticked**: Shuffle while on, the Repeat that's set - nothing
    with nothing queued.
  - **A text field with the cursor** (`typing`): Space, ⌘→ and ⌘← are the field's (a space, the line's end and
    start), so they come off Play/Pause, Next and Previous meanwhile (`yieldsToTyping`); the items still work from
    the menu. ⌘→/⌘← yielding is a decision beyond the plan's (it names only Space): a field moves on them.
  - `skip(_:from:length:)`: Forward and Back 10 s, within the song (Scrub.clamp), nil with no length.
- **MacMenuTests** (Swift Testing, 10): nothing queued; playing and paused; Repeat's three each ticked alone; Shuffle
  and a library's; a text field keeping its keys; the keys as the plan has them; the words the app's own; the skips;
  Go to Current Song; Refresh (where there is one, one at a time, not under Now Playing).

### The app

- **Shared/MacCommands.swift** (new) - `MacCommands: Commands`, handed to `Scene.macWindow(_:)` by DeadwaxApp:
  `CommandGroup(replacing: .appSettings)` Settings…, `(replacing: .textEditing)` Find, `(replacing: .textFormatting)`
  nothing, `(after: .toolbar)` Refresh, and `CommandMenu("Controls")` - MacMenu's sections with dividers, Shuffle and
  Repeat's three as Toggles (ticks), Repeat's in a Menu. No words or keys of its own (test_ios_mac reads the file for
  a literal); each click is the player's own call (`toggle`, `next`, `previous`, `seek(to:)` with MacMenu.skip from
  `shownPosition`, `toggleShuffle`, `setRepeat`, `navigation.openAlbum(PlayedAlbum.route(...))`), MacMenu read again
  as it lands. Also here:
  - **TextEditing** - whether a text field has the cursor, from UIKit's begin/end notices for UITextField and
    UITextView (SwiftUI's fields, a search bar's, the editors' text views), a weak table of fields, `typing` true
    while one of them is first responder. Started in `Platform.launching()` on the Mac only.
  - **MacRefresh** and **MacRefreshing** - ⌘R's page: each page's refresh registers as it appears and leaves as it
    goes; the page shown is the latest still there (a page pushed over another, a tab). Since the review, a sheet's
    root registers too (`.macSheet()`) and everything carries how many sheets deep it's drawn - see "After review".
    One at a time: `running` while its action is out. `Page` is a MainActor class holding the action as its view last drew it
    (a Sendable closure stored in the modifier warned; a MainActor class doesn't).
  - **FindFocus** - Search's field takes the cursor (`searchFocused`, iOS 18 / macOS 15) 150 ms after Find asks,
    the tab's switch drawn; on macOS 14 Find opens Search and the field waits for a click.
- **Shared/MacRightClick.swift** (new) - AlbumRightClick and PlaylistRightClick: a tile or row has no songs, so they
  are asked for each time the pointer rests on it a quarter second (`onHover`, then a fetch not called off by the
  pointer leaving - a menu opening over the tile takes it), the answer kept with a download drawn meanwhile, as the
  pages do. Since the review: an answer is kept only for what it was asked for - the person, the album's id now
  (`AppNavigation.albumId`, an apply's new one) and its Edit album writes (`albumWrites`), a playlist's changes here
  (`PlaylistsModel.lastChange`) - so a retag or a moved album is asked again before the menu queues it; an album
  deadwax calls gone with songs of it here carries the page's `goneButHere` (Add to Queue and Album info alone); with
  no answer yet the menu says Loading whenever one can come (online, signed in), not only after the rest (the menu
  doesn't redraw while open: right-click again); out of reach with nothing kept, or deadwax having said there is
  nothing, no menu. The album's Album info opens its sheet from the tile.
- **Player/QueueMenu.swift**: the •••'s items are `QueueMenuItems` - the very list, drawn by `QueueMenu` (the •••)
  and by every right-click, so the two can't differ. `QueueMenuRequest.album(...)` and `.playlist(...)` build an
  album's and a playlist's own ••• in one place: the album and playlist pages call them (adding their Refresh), and
  so do the right-clicks (without it). AlbumModel's `albumPick` went with it (nothing else read it).
- **Shared/Platform.swift**: the Mac's `macWindow(_ menus:)` adds `menus` to the commands; `pullToRefresh` is
  `refreshCommand(action)` on the Mac (⌘R where the phone pulls); and the new helpers, each `self` (or EmptyView) on
  the iPhone: `refreshCommand` (MacRefreshing), `macContextMenu` (`contextMenu(menuItems:)`), `albumRightClick`,
  `playlistRightClick`, `escapeCloses(_ on:)` (`keyboardShortcut(.cancelAction)`), `returnCancels`
  (`.defaultAction`), `findField`, `oneWindow` (`handlesExternalEvents(preferring: ["*"], allowing: ["*"])`) and
  `Platform.dialogCancel()`.
- **Right-click, where**: a song's row - TrackRow, PlaylistSongRow, SongRow, Search's song row - its own •••'s
  request; an album's tile or row - LibraryTile, LibraryRow, Search's album row, the artist page's ArtistAlbumRow -
  the album page's •••; a playlist's row (PlaylistRow, the Library's Playlists and Downloaded playlists) the playlist
  page's •••, nothing while that page's Edit is open. The EQ's correction row and the event log's line keep their
  phone long presses, as they were (a right-click on the Mac).
- **⌘R, where**: every `pullToRefresh` (17 in 15 files, through the helper) and `refreshCommand { refresh() }` on the
  three pages whose pull shuffles - the Library's pager, an album's page, a playlist's - their •••'s Refresh.
- **Escape**: `.escapeCloses()` on every sheet's Close, Cancel or Done (Add to a playlist, Sources, Up Next, Info,
  Album info, the EQ's Done, Pressings, Edit order, the EQ import's two, Edit album, Set up Navidrome, People's three,
  Artist images, Move albums' three), Now Playing's chevron, the cover viewer's ✕, a full-size cover's Close, and a
  playlist's Edit Cancel - so where Close asks, Escape asks. New playlist's form only on its own sheet
  (`NewPlaylistFields(escapes: true)`), as inside Add to a playlist the picker's own Cancel has Escape.
- **Return**: `.returnCancels()` on every confirmation dialog's role-cancel button (Keep editing, Keep it, Keep as it
  is, Cancel - 11 dialogs); Downloads' four dialogs, which leave Cancel to the system, draw `Platform.dialogCancel()`
  on the Mac - a Cancel with Return on it - and nothing on the iPhone. The EQ's name alert (a field, Save, Cancel) is
  left as it is: Return there is the field's.
- **The window**: `UIApplicationSupportsMultipleScenes` YES in Info-Mac.plist (NO on the iPhone, as before), so
  closing it doesn't quit (decision 4). Every model is DeadwaxApp's, so the tab and every pushed page come back with
  a new window; `server.start()` guards itself, so a new window doesn't relaunch anything. The Library's page is the
  pager's @State, lost with the window - so on the Mac LibraryView writes it to `AppNavigation.macLibraryPage` and
  opens on it (nil, the first page as before, on the iPhone). `oneWindow()` sends a file or a link to the window
  that's open. File > New Window is gone since slice 1.
- **AppNavigation** (Routes.swift): `find()` (Now Playing closed, Search at its root - popped as the tab tapped again
  pops - and `findWanted`), `findTaken()`, `showSettings()` (Now Playing closed, the Settings tab), `macLibraryPage`;
  `reset()` clears the last two.
- **check_project.py**: MAC_PLIST's `within` - a value set inside a dictionary both plists have, the rest of that
  dictionary still the phone's, key for key - holds the scene manifest's one difference, and `PHONE_WITHIN` holds the
  iPhone's NO, so the parity rule names the difference rather than loosening.

### Decided here (beyond the plan's words)

- **The iPhone had no long press on any of these rows** (songs, albums, playlists, artists): so the right-click is
  the Mac's alone, and the iPhone gets none.
- **Album tiles and rows** take the album page's ••• (the tile has none of its own), less Refresh; **playlists** the
  playlist page's. **Artists get no right-click**: an artist's row has no •••, and the artist page's ••• is an
  admin's managing (Artist images…, Move albums…), drawn from the page's own facts.
- **The ••• has no Go to album** (and no Play Next or Play Last since 16 Nov's Add to Queue): check 420 lists what the
  menus really offer - Add to Queue, Add to a playlist…, the download items, Album info, Edit album.
- **⌘R on the Library, an album and a playlist** is their •••'s Refresh, as the phone's pull there shuffles; and
  dimmed under Now Playing.
- **Find** replaces Edit's text-editing group (Find, Spelling and Grammar, Substitutions...); **Format** is emptied.
- **Return in a field** stays the phone's (New playlist's name creates it, Change password's last field changes it,
  the sign-in's signs in): only dialogs are held to Cancel, as the plan's 1.3 says ("the dialogs' default stays
  Cancel"). If James wants a field's Return held too on the Mac, it's a line per field through Platform.

### Tests

test_ios_mac.py: Platform's helpers on the iPhone (`self`, EmptyView, no key, menu or command) and on the Mac; the
scene wired with MacCommands and oneWindow; ⌘R on every pull and on the three pages, the same `refresh()` as their
•••; MacCommands drawing MacMenu alone (no literal, Button/Toggle/Menu/CommandMenu words MacMenu's, two keys both
`Self.shortcut(item.shortcut)`, each click the player's call, every MacMenu command handled, no volume); TextEditing's
four notices; Find (SearchScreen's one `.findField()` after `.searchable`, AppNavigation's find/showSettings/reset,
FindFocus); the Library page kept on the Mac only; right-click only through the helpers, each with QueueMenuItems,
the rows and tiles counted, the two builders used by the pages and the right-clicks, no Refresh offered; Escape
counted per file and on every toolbar Cancel/Close, every dialog's Cancel with Return and nothing else.
test_ios_install_mac.py's parity case: the Mac's scenes NO, a key added inside either's manifest, the manifest
removed, the phone's set YES (refused, not loosened), a manifest that isn't a dictionary. test_ios_edit.py reads the
album builder.
