## Manual search, slice A2: the Done row opens its album (2026-11-24)

James, 24 Nov, to "Go on with manual search's slice A2?": "Yes". The last piece of the spec's table
(~/Desktop/Code/deadwax-plans/manual-search.md 3.1's "From A2", 3.2-3.3's A2 parts). A manual search's download is
filed by its own tags with the sharer's ids dropped, so its Done row had no release to open by: A1 drew it without a
tap. Its server half is main's 2.1.40 (notes/downloads.md "The Done row's album (2.1.40)"): /jobs' `filed_as` and the
id bridge by `job_id`, merged here.

### What changed

- **Core, `Requests.swift`**: `FiledAs` (top level: tests/test_ios_contract.py reads DownloadJob's whole body, so a
  struct nested in it would be counted as its fields) and `DownloadJob.filedAs`, read leniently - a name of another
  shape is "", a `filed_as` of another shape none. **`DoneAlbum`** - `.release(id)` or `.job(id)` - and its `key`, the
  release or "job-<id>" (no MusicBrainz id can be that). **`RequestRow.opens: DoneAlbum?`** is now what a Done row
  opens; `release` is computed from it (`.release`'s id, else nil), so the web's vectors, which compare `release`, hold
  as they were.
- `jobRow`: a manual row with a `filed_as` naming an album (`ManualSearch.filedAs`: trimmed, nil for a blank album) is
  titled by it - "<its album> · manual search" - with its artist (the typed one when it names none), under every
  heading it reaches. In Done, in the library (filed, partly_filed, already_there): `.release` when the job has a
  release id, else `.job` **only when `filed_as` is there**; `plays` as before, for filed and partly_filed.
- **Why `filed_as` gates `.job`**: it is sent only by a 2.1.40 server, and only for an album the store still has
  live. A 2.1.38/2.1.39 server answers `job_id` with a 422 (exactly one of its two keys), so without the gate a tap
  would say "Can't find this album…" for every manual row; with it the row is as A1 drew it, and docs/ios.md says to
  find it in the Library.
- `Routes.storeAlbum` gains `job_id`; `DeadwaxClient.storeAlbum(jobId:)` and `storeAlbum(_: DoneAlbum)`.
- **App, `Models/RequestsModel.swift`**: every Done-row state - `albumIds`, `ready`, `misses`, `notes`, `inFlight`,
  the look tasks - is keyed by `DoneAlbum.key` where it was keyed by the release; `DoneLooks` is untouched (it keeps
  its rows by a string it never reads, and stays the web's to the vector). `runLooks` keeps a key -> DoneAlbum map of
  the drawn rows and asks each due one of the bridge by what it is; `open` the same; `plays` by the key.
  `RequestCards`' DoneRowView and RequestsScreen's note read `opens`.
- No `#if`; nothing Mac-only. No new words (the row's note is the Done rows' own).
- docs/ios.md: the Requests paragraph (the title from the tags, the tap and ▶, 2.1.40) and check **475**; the
  Last.fm plan's checks move to 476-504.

### Tests, and the faults they were seen failing on

- ManualSearchTests.swift (+4, 17): `aFiledManualDownloadIsTitledAsItsTagsNameItAndOpensByItsJob` (filed, partly
  filed, already there with no ▶, interrupted opening nothing, a release id by now opening `.release`, a blank album
  keeping the typed words and opening nothing, a blank artist keeping the typed one, a non-manual row ignoring it, the
  title under Downloading too), `aDoneRowsAlbumIsKeptByItsReleaseOrItsJob`, `filedAsIsReadAsJobsSendsIt` (odd shapes
  read leniently) and `aManualDoneRowsAlbumIsAskedOfTheIdBridgeByItsJob` (FakeTransport: `job_id=12`, and a release
  still `release_mbid=`). A1's `aManualDownloadIsMarkedUnderEveryHeading` now also holds that a row without
  `filed_as` opens nothing. Five faults, each applied alone and the suite run, then restored - every one caught: no
  `filed_as` gate (three tests), the title not from `filed_as`, a job asked of the bridge by release, a blank album
  believed, the job's key as the bare id.
- tests/test_ios_contract.py: `filed_as` among what /jobs can send (its source line asserted), and the jobs route
  through the real app with the manual row filed into a live store row - `filed_as` on it alone; the route test
  now holds `job_id` among the bridge's declared parameters (it failed here before main's 2.1.40 was merged: "the app
  sends ['job_id'], which the server ignores"). The bridge's shape test reads the route's two halves since 2.1.40
  (`_by_release`, `_by_job`) and holds a job's answer to the same keys.

### The review (one, of S3 and A2 together)

- **Important, fixed on main before 2.1.40 was committed**: the by-name lookup took an older id-less copy of the album
  (another folder, already listed) for a download Navidrome hadn't scanned yet - title and artist only - and the app
  would have kept that id in `albumIds["job-N"]` while its songs kept loading. Now the year and the song count must
  agree wherever both sides say them (notes/downloads.md).
- Nits fixed there too: a common title past the first 20 answers (a second search3 by artist and title), and
  `filed_as` sent with no LIBRARY_PATH.
- **Kept, known**: after Edit album > Release on such an album - what its Done row's line suggests - Navidrome
  probably gives it a new id (its album identity moves to the release id), and the app's kept `albumIds`/`ready` for
  "job-N" are then stale: a tap opens a dead id, ▶ plays song ids Navidrome no longer has, until the next songs ask
  fails and forgets them (DoneLooks' own refresh). A release row has the same shape but far less exposure. Not
  fixed: it heals itself, and the usual path after a match is the album page, not Requests' ▶.
- Looked at and found sound: access (`_job_for`, the same rule as cancel and retry, before Navidrome is asked); a
  `.job` row can't turn into `.release` (jobs.release_mbid is never updated after the job is made - the server answers
  a match made since); every keyed map in RequestsModel; an older server never asked by job; `filed_as` and the bridge
  agreeing on "live" (pins.album_state); the poller's order (set_job_album, grant_job, the status).

### Not verified - only James's phone and Mac can say (475)

- Everything on a device: the title from the tags, the tap, ▶ from the first song, a "You already had it" row opening
  with no ▶, the Mac's Requests.
- Navidrome's real search3 answer for an album with no MusicBrainz id, its `year` and `songCount` for one, and whether
  it lists an id-less copy and an "[unmatched]" one of the same name as one album or two (M9, 467) - "exactly one"
  answers null when it's two, and the row says "Not ready to play yet…".

## Last.fm, slice A1 (2026-11-24)

James, 24 Nov: the 10 most popular songs on an artist's page, from Last.fm, all time. The design is
~/Desktop/Code/deadwax-plans/lastfm.md; this is its app slice **A1** (2.4, 2.5, 2.7, 3.1, 3.2, 3.3's listeners, 3.6-3.8,
section 4's A1): the listeners line and Top Songs, on the iPhone and the Mac alike. Not in it: the Albums order menu
and Most played, Similar Artists (A2), Start Radio and Autoplay (A3 - Start Radio is left out of a top song's •••), About
(A4). The server's half is `GET /deadwax/lastfm/artist`, main's **2.1.41** (S2, notes/lastfm.md), built beside this
slice against 2.5's shape and merged into `ios` at 825e099f before the slice was done; its real answers are
Fixtures/lastfm/answers/artist.json. What it leaves alone:
- src/ and ui/ are untouched; the app is still 0.13 (13). **ios/Deadwax.xcodeproj is untouched** (the three new App files
  are in the synchronized folder, the Core files and tests in the package, found by folder).
- **The engine files have no diff**, nor does anything of DeadwaxAudio's; a top song plays through
  `PlayerModel.play(playlist:at:)`, as an album's song does.
- No `#if` in any App file; no word differs between the iPhone and the Mac.

### What was built

**Core (pure, tested on Linux and macOS):**
- `Lastfm.swift`: `LastfmState` (/me's `lastfm`: on, off, refused - and **absent**, see below); `LastfmTrack` and
  `LastfmArtist`, the route's answer, read loosely (`looseField`/`looseList`: a part absent or malformed is nil; a
  track with no title, or a blank one, is dropped; an answer that doesn't say it's enabled is not, one that doesn't
  say it's whole is unavailable); `LastfmLink` - lastfm.py `lastfm_url`'s rule exactly: https, printable ASCII with no
  space, `\` or `@`, at most 2048 letters, host last.fm or under it; `LastfmMatch.key` - lastfm.py `match_key`, a feature
  aside, a feature tail and a dash take dropped (`strip`), then `SongTitle.key`. `strip` is Python's regexes ported by
  hand onto unicode scalars: `PyText` holds `str.isspace`'s 29 characters, `\w` as `re` reads it (a letter of any L
  category, anything with a numeric value, `_`) and the IGNORECASE folds `re` makes (ſ for s, İ/ı for i, K for k).
- `TopSongs.swift`: `rows(_:albums:)` - each top song met with a song of the page's albums by `LastfmMatch.key`, the
  candidates ordered earliest first (the album's year, undated last; the page's play order; disc; track; the album's
  own order), each library song used once, greedily in Last.fm's order; with the albums' songs not all in (`nil`)
  every row waits. `play(_:from:playable:)` - the playable top songs you have, in Last.fm's order, from this one.
  `album(_:title:mbid:name:)` - the album a song you don't have opens: the first song of MusicBrainz's search that is
  this one (`LastfmMatch.key`) and theirs (their id among its artists when the page knows it, else its credit their
  `Fold.key`), its first album as `sortAlbums` has them. `trouble(_:admin:)` - MusicBrainz's 503 in the spec's words,
  anything else through ErrorWords.
- `LastfmPage.swift`: `waitMs` 800, `kept` 64, `unsureKeptMs` 60 s; `placeOf` (judged once, as describe.ts);
  `Arrival` - a page waits only with Last.fm on, deadwax in reach and nothing kept, until an answer or the wait
  releases it, and an answer that lands after the albums were drawn is placed after them for the page's life;
  `shown(state:online:answer:seesDetail:)` - the hero line (kept whenever Last.fm is on and the page is online, or an
  answer is in hand), the listeners, whether Top Songs draws, the foot line; `state(me:answer:)`; `present`; `Ask` -
  what the route takes (an id that is one, a name trimmed, 1-200 letters); `Kept` - the session's answers by artist,
  the last 64, an unsure one (unavailable, not enabled, or a failure) a minute.
- `LastfmWords.swift`: every word of the slice, the spec's exactly; `listeners(_:)` rounded down at every boundary
  (integer tenths: "9.9K" for 9,999, "999K" for 999,999, "2.3M" for 2,399,999, never ".0"); 0 or none is no line.
- `Me.lastfm` (read loosely in a hand-written `init(from:)`, the other fields exactly as strictly as before) and
  `Access.lastfm`; `Routes.lastfmArtist` (the route count 110 -> **111**, no timeout of its own: the route answers
  within 4 s); `DeadwaxClient.lastfmArtist(mbid:name:)`, sending only the parts the route takes - never one empty (the
  route answers a 422 for `mbid=` or `name=`), nothing at all with neither.

**App:**
- `Artist/ArtistView.swift`: the hero's line under the name ("2.3M listeners", footnote, quiet; there from the first
  frame whenever `shown.heroLine`, blank until the answer says, hidden from VoiceOver while blank); Top Songs between
  Play and Albums, or after the albums for a late answer; everything below Play waiting on the arrival; the foot line
  for `seesDetail` with **Server settings**, which pushes Server settings > Connections. Last.fm is asked once the
  artist's answer is in hand (`.task(id:)` on who they are, /me's word and reachability), again on a pull.
- `Artist/TopSongsSection.swift`: the heading with See All (more than five), five `TopSongRow`s, `LastfmCredit`
  ("From Last.fm", a `Link` to the answer's page, the words alone without one). `TopSongRow`, shared with the page: a
  song you have plays in the tap (`TopSongs.play` -> `player.play(playlist:at:)`), dimmed and inert offline when it
  isn't on the device, swiped right to add it, its ••• QueueMenu's song items (`QueuePick.song(song, of: album)`), a
  right-click on the Mac the same; a song you don't have spins while `TopSongOpener` asks, says its trouble for the
  visit, does nothing offline; a waiting row is drawn and nothing more.
- `Artist/TopSongsScreen.swift`: See All's page, `.topSongs(ArtistRoute)`, at the readable width on the Mac.
- `Models/TopSongOpener.swift`: a song you don't have's album - MusicBrainz's song search with
  `SongSearch.fieldedQuery`, read with `SongSearch.group`, picked by `TopSongs.album`, opened as
  `GroupRoute(SongAlbum)` with the song marked - only where it was tapped (the same tab, the same pages, Now Playing
  away), let go on a tab change, Now Playing and leaving, as a MusicBrainz artist's row's bridge is. An album found is
  kept for the session.
- `Models/ArtistPageModel.swift`: `lastfm`, the arrival, the opener, `askLastfm`, the 800 ms wait, `topRows` (the
  answer's songs met with `asks.answers` once every album's songs are in or failed and in the page's play order;
  offline, with what is in hand of each album, the page's or this phone's), and `albums(online:downloads:)` moved here
  from the view. `Models/ArtistsModel.swift`: the session's `LastfmPage.Kept`, and which artist page is showing for an
  artist (weakly), for the Top Songs page.

### Decisions, and where this departs from the spec

- **`absent` is not `off`** (the spec, 2.7: "absent as off"). An older deadwax has no `lastfm` in /me and no
  LASTFM_API_KEY to point anyone at, so the page draws nothing of Last.fm's and no foot line either. A word this app
  doesn't know is absent too.
- **An answer saying Last.fm isn't enabled is believed over an older /me** (`LastfmPage.state`): refused if it's also
  unavailable, else off - so a key Last.fm starts refusing mid-session draws the foot line at once, not at the next
  /me (check 485 still says to leave the app and come back, for the case of a kept answer, which the server answers
  while refused).
- **The foot line's button pushes Server settings > Connections on the tab you're on**, not the You tab: switching tabs
  under someone reading an artist's page is the bigger surprise, and Server settings is a page any tab can push.
- **The session's answers are kept by artist id**, with what they were asked as, so the first frame knows there's an
  answer before the artist's own answer (and so their MusicBrainz id) is in hand. A failure is kept a minute only while
  nothing is drawn: one that fails after an answer was drawn keeps that answer.
- **Last.fm's ask and the wait are unstructured tasks**, as the albums' songs are: a page covered by another (See All)
  keeps its ask, and only the newest answer for the page lands (a counter, and the page's key).
- **The Top Songs page reads the artist page's own model** (the `ArtistsModel` registry, weak): its rows are the very
  rows of the page under it, nothing asked again, a song's album asked through the same opener. With that page gone
  it is its own, asking as the page asks.
- **The client's signature is `lastfmArtist(mbid:name:)`**, both optional, each sent only when the route takes it.
- **A song you don't have's album is the first matching song's** in MusicBrainz's order (`SongSearch.group`), its
  first album as `sortAlbums` has them. A "Borderline (Live)" has the same key as "Borderline" (SongTitle.key drops a
  bracketed aside), so if MusicBrainz lists the live take's song first, its live album is the one opened - the spec's
  rule, kept; 480 asks whether it's the studio album in practice.
- **The check numbers are the spec's 476-487**, adjusted to what was built: 478 compares with Last.fm's own page; 482
  opens an artist not opened this week (deadwax keeps Last.fm's answers a week, so a restart doesn't make one cold);
  485 leaves and comes back; 486 has no Start Radio.

### After review (2026-11-24)

One review of A1; every finding below fixed in the slice, before any commit.
- **Important: a song you have could read "Not in your library".** `topRows` met the top songs with only the albums
  whose songs were in hand. Offline that was the page's asks or `downloads.keptAlbum` (downloaded albums only), so
  Tame Impala opened online, then again offline (a new page, no asks, Last.fm's answer the session's), drew "The Less I
  Know the Better" on an un-downloaded Currents as missing - a note cover, and a tap that would open MusicBrainz's page
  for an album you have. Online, an album whose songs failed (`unsent`) did the same. Now **`TopSongs.library`** says
  which albums are in hand - online the asks' answers once every album has answered or failed; offline the asks' or
  this device's - and whether any of theirs isn't (`unknown`). With one not in hand, a song no album in hand has is
  **`.unknown`**: drawn as a waiting row, dimmed, inert, never "Not in your library". Matched songs stay matched with
  the albums in hand (an earlier take on an album not in hand can't be seen: the row may show a later album's take
  until it is).
- A song you don't have is searched for by **`TopSongs.searchQuery`**: `LastfmMatch.strip`'s title ("Let It Happen -
  2015 Remaster" asks for "Let It Happen"), the title as written when that strips to nothing.
- **The hero's line keeps its height once drawn for the page** (`LastfmPage.drawsLine`, and `shown`'s `reserved`):
  the model notes the page (`keepLine`) as each ask begins and as each answer lands. Before, an answer saying Last.fm
  isn't enabled after /me said on, or the page going offline before any answer, dropped the line and moved Play.
- **The Top Songs page on its own** (no artist page under it registered - after `ArtistsModel.reset()`, a new person, say) spun
  for ever when its ask failed. It now says the artist's failure as their page does (ErrorNote, `ErrorWords.artistGone`,
  Try again: load again and the missing albums' songs) and Last.fm's the same way (the model's `lastfmFailure`, Try
  again asking again), and its own ask asks a failure the session keeps again at once (`retryFailed`) rather than
  waiting out its minute.
- **`LastfmLink` reads the host as written** (`percentEncodedHost`, any `%` refused): `URLComponents.host` decodes, so
  `https://evil.com%2elast.fm/` and `https://%6Cast.fm/x` passed, which Python's `urlparse` - and `lastfm_url` - refuse.
  test_ios_contract.py now holds both rules to the same links.
- The session's kept answers are timed by **`Monotonic`**, not `Date()`, as SearchModel's are.
- LastfmMatchTests compared Strings with `==` (canonical equivalence: "é" equals "e" and a combining acute); they now
  compare unicode scalars, and a check proves a decomposed letter is a difference.
- docs/ios.md: an older deadwax said exactly - 2.1.36-2.1.40 draw a blank line under the name and no Top Songs, before
  2.1.36 nothing; the rows that may be yours, the search's title, the line keeping its place, check 484's re-open.
- **Known, not fixed**: on a split album (another performer's song beside theirs), a top song can match the other
  performer's song of the same title - the candidates are every song of the page's albums, by title alone.
- **The server's, not the app's**: Python's `re.IGNORECASE` folds ı and İ in a take aside where the app's port doesn't
  (the review's finding 2); it's being fixed on main. The app follows `match-vectors.json`, as the server will.

Tests: TopSongsTests +4 (an album not in hand never "not in your library"; offline, the page's or this device's albums,
any other unknown; online, an album that didn't load; the search's title), LastfmPageTests +1 (the line kept),
LastfmDecodeTests (the two percent-encoded hosts, a path's percents, a port), test_ios_lastfm.py +1 (the page's
troubles, `retryFailed`, Monotonic) and the rules above pinned. Faults, each applied alone, run, restored - every one
caught: an unknown row said missing (three TopSongsTests); an album not in hand ignored (two); offline, this device's
albums not read; online, rows met before every album settled; the raw title searched (Core and the opener); the
reservation ignored (Core, the view not passing it, the model not keeping it); a percent-encoded host decoded; strip's
result normalised (the scalar comparison); an unknown row not dimmed; topRows not passing `unknown`; the page's
Last.fm failure unsaid; a kept failure waited out; the wall clock.

## The Mac redesign, slice R1: the frame and the shared pieces (2026-11-25)

James, 24 Nov: the whole Mac app redrawn on the design canvas (the web's look, more vintage), built a slice at a time.
The plan is ~/Desktop/Code/deadwax-plans/mac-redesign-build.md - its section 7, "James's answers (24 Nov)", binding over
the rest - and the drawings mac-redesign.md, dw.css, Main.dc.html and Albums.dc.html. This is **R1**: the frame and every
piece the later slices build their pages from; the pages themselves are still the phone's. What it leaves alone:
- **The iPhone looks and works exactly as before.** The gate is `git status --porcelain -- ios ':!ios/App/Mac'` - a
  `git diff --stat` misses the untracked files and reads nothing of ios/Config unless told to. It names:
  - App: DesktopFrame.swift and MacSidebarView.swift (drawn only on the Mac); Platform.swift (its Mac half, and an
    iPhone half of `self` and `{}`); Typeface.swift (additive: the `Mac` namespace); RootView.swift (one Platform
    helper, `.namesWindow(gateName)`, whose iPhone half is `self` - the review's finding 6); and the three
    `App/Fonts/NotoSansMono-*.ttf`.
  - Config: Info.plist and Info-Mac.plist, each with the three mono files added to UIAppFonts.
  - Core: MacLook, MacTable and MacInFront with their tests (pure, new), and MacSidebar's `Words.brand` (additive).
  - ios/scripts/make-fonts.py (the mono family) and ios/design/dw.css (never bundled).
  MainTabs, TabStack and `appRoutes()` have no diff; nor do the engine files, DeadwaxAudio,
  `Fixtures/words/iphone.json`, DeadwaxClient or Core's Routes.
- **The mono faces ship in the phone's bundle too** - one target, one bundle: three TTFs, 440,592 bytes in all (about
  440 KB), registered in Info.plist as in Info-Mac.plist. James chose it ("Bundle Noto Sans Mono", 24 Nov); the phone
  never draws them (Typeface.Mac alone reads them, and the reach test keeps Typeface.Mac off the phone's files).
- **ios/Deadwax.xcodeproj is untouched**: App/Mac and the fonts are in the synchronized folder; the Core files and
  tests in the package. src/ and ui/ are untouched; the app is still 0.13 (13).

### What was built

**The look, as tokens** (each held to dw.css by tests/test_ios_mac_look.py):
- `ios/design/dw.css`: the canvas's stylesheet, copied outside App/ so it is never bundled - the tests' source of truth.
- `App/Mac/Look/MacPalette.swift`: dw.css's colours under their own names (`bg`, `side`, `panel` ... `acc`, `selt`,
  `selbg`, `well`), each line commented `// --name`; and the parts' faces, edges, sheens and drops, each commented
  `// dw: <selector> <property>`, gradients stop for stop. `off` is app.css's `--app-pin-off`, 0.45.
- `App/Mac/Look/MacCorners.swift`: buttons 4, boxes 5, chips 3 (James's answer 1: rounded on the Mac only - the phone's
  `Corners` stay 0, and test_ios_palette's square-corners test skips this one file).
- Core `MacLook.swift`: every size the drawings give (sidebar 220, panel 400, bar 66, title 28, toolbar 40, status 24,
  rows 30/26, buttons 26/22, field 24, label 84, segments 20/24, chip 19, count 17, tabs 35/26/29, keys 34/46...).
  MacFrame's web-held 232/470/72 and their vectors stay as they were, unread by the new frame except its 1280 and its
  880 x 600 (the panel is still MacFrame's 470 until its slice).
- Type: `Typeface.Mac.text(_:)` and `.mono(_:)` at fixed sizes (`Size`: h1 28, h2 20, brand 19, h3 18, lcd 14, base 13,
  control 12.5, small 12, label 11.5, count 11). **Noto Sans Mono** is bundled (James's answer 3): Regular, Medium and
  SemiBold TTFs made by ios/scripts/make-fonts.py from interface/styles/font/noto-sans-mono/*.woff2 - the web's own
  subset, the same characters - with fonttools from the venv already here; registered in both plists' UIAppFonts and
  read only through `Typeface.Mac`.

**Components** (`App/Mac/Components/`): MacRaised (a face, a sheen on the inset shape, a 1 pt edge, a drop; pressed
turns the gradient over and drops the sheen) and MacRule; MacButtonStyle (normal, primary, red, on; small); MacTitleStrip;
MacToolbar and MacGroove; MacWell, MacField and MacFieldRow; MacSegmented (dw.css's .seg exactly: a well, flat
segments, the chosen one the selection's fill and edge - nothing raised); MacCheckbox; MacPopUp and MacCaret;
MacFolderTabs; MacGroupBox; MacStatusBar; MacKeyStyle, MacToggleStyle and MacDisplay (the lcd); MacChip and MacCount;
MacOutput (AirPlayButton with the EQ's route name). Only MacTitleStrip, MacWell, MacSegmented and MacCount are drawn
yet (the frame and the sidebar); the rest wait for their pages.

**The frame** (`App/Mac/Frame/`):
- **MacTabStack** - TabStack's copy with `.macRoutes()`; **MacRoutes** - the one switch over all 30 `AppRoute` cases,
  each sent to its area's `Mac<Area>.page(for:)` (Library, Album, Artist, Search, Requests, Settings, Edit, Manage),
  which returns the phone's page exactly as appRoutes draws it until that area's slice swaps it.
- **MacPage** - a toolbar over a page on `bg`, for the slices; **MacTitle** - the strip's and the Window menu's name:
  the sidebar's lit row (`MacSidebar.at`, so the two can't disagree), or the page on top's own name (an album, an
  artist, a playlist, a search group).
- **MacStatusItems** and **MacSelection** - what the page in front says in the status bar, and what it has selected
  (an album or an artist), for the panels and the later toolbars. Both keep their pages through Core's **MacInFront**:
  the pages on screen, the last to come on in front; a page changes what it says where it is, and a page off the
  screen changes nothing.

**DesktopFrame**: the title strip on top, laid under the title bar (`.ignoresSafeArea(.container, edges: .top)`), as
tall as the bar's inset and 28 at least; the sidebar at MacLook's 220; the status bar under the page and the panel
while the page in front has said something (nothing does yet); the four stacks MacTabStacks over the area roots; and
`Platform.nameWindow(title)` on every change of title - the scene's title, kept in Platform's Mac half for the windows
`shape()` meets later, while `titleVisibility` stays hidden. **MacSidebarView** restyled as drawn: `deadwax` at 19 bold,
the search field in a MacWell (its edge `acc` while it has the cursor), headings at 11.5 semibold in `label`, rows 26 tall
of words alone at 13 (the lit one `selt`, semibold, on `selbg` with `selbd`'s edge), playlists indented 20 in `t2`,
counts as MacCount, Yours | All a MacSegmented, on `side` with `frame`'s rule at its right. Every MacSidebar call
(rows, lit, fold, counts, the switch's moves) is as it was.

**Platform** (Mac half; the iPhone half `self` or `{}`): `nameWindow(_:)`; `returnPresses()` (`.keyboardShortcut
(.defaultAction)`); `arrowKeys(_:)` (`onKeyPress` for ← and →, Platform being the one file the tests let hold it).

### Decisions, and where this departs from the plan

- **Observed stores, not preferences**, for the status items and the selection: the pages are inside the frame's TabView
  and NavigationStacks, each a UIKit controller on Catalyst, and a preference isn't carried up out of them. Each page
  registers under its own UUID; the one that appeared last is in front. Read from an optional environment, so a sheet
  (none there) says nothing.
- **The type sizes are named h2, h3 and base**, not the CSS's title/body: test_ios_palette bans iOS text-style names
  (`.body`, `.title`...) inside `.font(...)`. **count is 11** (dw.css .count's 600 11px), a size the plan's list left out.
- **The purple primary takes Return only where asked** (`.returnPresses()`), not by being primary: a toolbar's Play over
  a list must leave Return to the list's selection (MacTable.returned).
- **`MacButtonStyle(kind:small:)` by name**, with no `.mac` static: test_the_app_hands_core_the_device_for_its_words bans
  `.mac` as a value. Its kinds are `.normal`, `.pri` (.btn.pri), `.danger` (.btn.red) and `.on`, and MacChip's tones
  `.plain`, `.caution`, `.good`, `.marked` and `.bad` (.chip, .amber, .green, .purple, .red): named for what they do,
  since the colour matcher reads a bare `.red` or `.primary` as SwiftUI's own colour (the review's finding 1).
- **Focus is drawn as `acc`'s edge**, the web's `:focus-visible` outline, on the well and the segmented control.
- **The folding headings keep a small chevron** (Playlists, Manage): without it nothing says they fold. Drawn in `label`.
- **Words.brand ("deadwax") is in Core's MacSidebar**, beside the sidebar's other words. MacSidebar.symbol is now read by
  nothing in the app (rows have no glyphs; test_ios_mac holds that the sidebar doesn't) - kept, with MacSidebarTests'
  checks of it, rather than removed from Core in a slice whose rule is MacSidebar's rows unchanged.
- **The panel's hairline is unchanged** (Palette's, its slice restyles the panel); the sidebar's rule is now its own.
- **MacPopUp is SwiftUI's Menu** with our face; if Catalyst draws its own pop-up over it, that is accepted (section 2).

### After review (2026-11-25)

One review, no important bugs, nine nits - all fixed, none committed. James has since decided the iPhone takes the new
look too ("Both together"); the re-plan is being written apart, and none of it is here.

1. **Colours in every form.** test_ios_mac_look's matcher missed `return .red`, `.foregroundStyle(.secondary)` and
   `.tint(.purple)`. It now refuses Color's own (`Color.x`, Color.clear aside), any colour or SwiftUI style by its bare
   name where a ShapeStyle goes (the hierarchy, the accent, `.tint`, `.foreground`, `.background`, separators,
   selection, links, placeholders, `.multicolor`, `.bar`) - a modifier of the same name (`.tint(`, `.background {`)
   aside - the system's (`.systemRed`), materials and the style types; its self-test plants each and the clean forms
   the views write. MacCaret takes its colour (MacPalette.buttonText) rather than `.fill(.foreground)`, and the kinds
   and tones were renamed (above).
2. **A part held to its layer.** A part from a property with more than one colour says which, counting from 1
   (`dw: .btn box-shadow 2`), and is held to that one alone; one-colour properties name none. A box-shadow's part says
   what it is by its name, and the layer must be that: a Sheen white, a Drop dark and outside, a Shade dark and inset, a
   Ring a spread ring (`0 0 0 Npx`).
3. **MacPalette is dw.css's colours and nothing else.** Every line of the enum before its makings is a comment or a
   colour line with its source, made only as `hex(0x...)`, `rgba(...)` or `vertical(...)` of those (the one Double,
   `off`, the web's); after the makings, only the four private makings; no file extends MacPalette. Its self-test
   plants `Color.purple` with and without a comment, a `.opacity` on a dw.css colour, a bare Double, a `static var`,
   and a colour or a func after the makings.
4. **The reach** covers what the redesign declares outside App/Mac: `Typeface.Mac`, and Core's MacLook, MacTable and
   MacInFront. Planted in Player/NowPlayingView.swift, `Typeface.Mac.text(.base)` and `MacLook.rowHeight` are caught.
5. **The selection's owner.** `select(Y, by: A)` from a list off the screen (under a pushed page B) made A the owner.
   Both stores are now Core's MacInFront (MacInFrontTests: the reviewer's sequence step by step), and the reach test
   holds that `select` and `change` go through its `changed`.
6. **Stale titles.** A playlist's page is named from PlaylistsModel's list as it is now (asked again after every
   write), its route's preview only until the list has it - a rename in Edit renames the strip and the Window menu.
   And RootView names the window for a launch screen in place of the app (`.namesWindow(gateName)`, Platform's: Sign
   in after a sign-out, deadwax for the address, checking and can't-reach screens; none while the app is up, the frame
   naming it - a sign-in over the app keeps the page's name).
7. **Check 521** said the switch was glossy and pressed. It isn't, and neither is dw.css's .seg: a well with the line's
   edge, flat segments, the chosen one `selbg` inside a `selbd` edge. MacSegmented already drew that; a test now holds
   it to .seg rule by rule, and the check says what's drawn.
8. **The gate** is stated as `git status --porcelain` over ios/ outside App/Mac (above), and the mono TTFs' place in
   the phone's bundle is recorded.
9. **dw.css recopied** from the canvas (~/Desktop/Code/deadwax-plans/mac-redesign/dw.css): it gained the phone's own
   `.dw.ph` blocks (every corner 0; Now Playing's and the mini player's transport as bare glyphs). The test drops every
   `.dw.ph` selector before reading a rule, and holds that the copy has them and that none of the Mac's values moved
   (the chip still 19 tall though the phone's is 22).

Tests after review: test_ios_mac_look 12, test_ios_mac_reach 8, MacInFrontTests 4 (Swift's run 2217 tests, from
2213). The first seven faults were run again, each still caught, and one more for each fix, each applied alone, run and
restored byte for byte - every one caught:
- a bare `.red` in MacChip's switch, and a `.tint(.purple)` on MacPopUp: `test_nothing_in_the_macs_views_draws_a_value_of_its_own`;
- buttonSheen given the drop's colour (layer 1 named), the same with layer 2 named (the Sheen must be white), and
  keyRing given the drop's colour: `test_every_colour_in_the_palette_is_one_dw_css_names`;
- `static let extra = Color.purple` with no comment: `test_macpalette_is_dw_css_colours_and_nothing_else`;
- `Typeface.Mac.text(.base)`, and `MacLook.rowHeight`, planted in NowPlayingView.swift:
  `test_app_mac_is_named_only_from_the_macs_frame`;
- MacInFront's `changed` putting a page off the screen in front: MacInFrontTests `aPageOffTheScreenIsNeverPutInFront`;
  MacSelection's `select` through `appeared`: `test_the_frames_stores_keep_the_page_in_front_by_core`;
- a playlist named by its preview, and RootView without `.namesWindow(gateName)`: `test_the_window_is_named_for_what_is_up`;
- the segments given MacButtonStyle: `test_the_segmented_control_is_dw_css_seg`;
- dw.css cut back to before the phone's blocks: `test_dw_css_is_the_canvas_copy_read_without_the_phones_rules`.

Still not seen on a screen: James's own deadwax was running again, so no smoke run - the list above stands, with the
renamed window on a sign-out and after a playlist's rename added to it.

## The redesign, slice R1b: the shared look, and the phone's pieces (2026-11-25)

James decided on 25 Nov that the iPhone takes the new look too ("Both together"). The plan was re-written for both
devices: ~/Desktop/Code/deadwax-plans/mac-redesign-build.md, section 3. Its sections 3.8 and 7 are binding:
- the word is "Queue", not Up Next;
- Lyrics stays in the cover's place and is not a sheet tab;
- the phone is square;
- Play and skip stay sharp glyphs.

R1 made the shared parts Mac-only. **R1b** moves them to `App/Look/` under DW names, and each one takes its device's
sizes, corners and type. It also makes the phone's own pieces in `App/Phone/`. **No screen the phone draws today
changes.** The App/Look parts are still drawn only from the Mac's frame. The App/Phone pieces are drawn nowhere until
their slices.

The gate is `git status --porcelain -- ios ':!ios/App/Mac' ':!ios/App/Look' ':!ios/App/Phone'`. It names:
- the three frame-side files:
  - Platform.swift (two comments);
  - Typeface.swift (additive);
  - MacSidebarView.swift (renames);
- Core's DWLook.swift and DWLookTests.swift (both new);
- DeviceWordsTests.swift (its comment).

The following have no diff:
- ios/Deadwax.xcodeproj (App/ is a synchronized folder);
- ios/Config and `Fixtures/words/iphone.json`;
- the engine files, DeadwaxClient and Core's Routes;
- the turntable, src/ and ui/.

The app is still 0.13 (13).

### What moved

These moved from App/Mac to App/Look. Nothing in R1's drawing changed except the names.

| R1's (App/Mac) | now (App/Look) |
| --- | --- |
| MacPalette's tokens, and the faces of its buttons, wells, fields, chips and counts | DWPalette (the phone's parts added) |
| Mac/Look/MacCorners | DWCorners: `Mac` (4/5/3) and `Phone` (Corners', 0), chosen by `Platform.mac` |
| MacRaised, MacRule | DWRaised, DWRule (`drop` optional, for the strip's flat buttons) |
| MacButtonStyle | DWButtonStyle (`.large` added: .btn.lg; `fills` for .btn.lg.grow) |
| MacWell, MacField, MacFieldRow | DWWell, DWField, DWFieldRow (the label trails on the Mac, as R1's did; it leads on the phone, 88 at least, over a hairline) |
| MacChip, MacCount | DWChip, DWCount |
| MacSegmented | DWSegmented (`large`: .seg.lg; it fills the row on the phone; the focus and the arrow keys are Mac-only) |
| MacPopUp, MacCaret | DWPopUp, DWCaret |
| MacToggleStyle (it was in MacKeys.swift) | DWToggleStyle (its dot is Mac-only: the phone's .tog.sm is a square) |

What stays in App/Mac:
- MacPalette keeps the title strip, toolbar, groove, checkbox fill, folder tabs, status bar, keys and the lcd;
- MacKeys keeps MacKeyStyle and MacDisplay (the phone has no key and no lcd, because its glyphs are sharp);
- so do the strip, toolbar, group box, status bar, output, frame and checkbox.

App/Mac's files and MacSidebarView were renamed by script, with no other change.

**Sizes.** Core `DWLook` holds each shared part's sizes per device, and `DWLook.of(device)` picks one:
- `onMac` is MacLook's values exactly (DWLookTests holds this).
- `onPhone` is `.dw.ph`'s: buttons 36/32/48, field 36, rows 44, label 88, chip 22, segments 28 and 38. A finger's
  target is 44, and every height is a minimum (`grows`).

Core `PhoneLook` holds the phone pieces' sizes. Each one is commented with its `// dw.ph:` rule. Five of them come from
the drawings' own inline styles and are commented `// drawn:` instead (the Library's titled top: 50, 16, -0.5, and its
title of 28).

**Type.** `Typeface.Look.text(role)` and `.mono(role)` take the Mac's fixed size or the phone's `.dw.ph` size. The phone's
size is scaled `relativeTo:` the nearest text style, the smaller on a tie. `Typeface.Phone` holds the phone pieces' sizes,
scaled in the same way.

### What was made (App/Phone, drawn nowhere yet)

- **PhoneStrip** (`.chips`): a one-tap strip.
  - The shown button is in the selection's fill and edge, with no drop.
  - It starts at the leading edge. It scrolls sideways when it won't fit (`ViewThatFits`) and never wraps; the shown
    button is brought into view whenever it changes (after review, below).
  - It is `.isTabBar`, and each button is selected when shown.
- **PhoneTop** (`.topbar`): 44 tall, or 50 with a title.
  - It carries a leading part, a trailing part and the page's name centred clear of both.
  - **PhoneBack** is the purple "‹ Back" link, read as "Library, Back" (Core's `PhonePieceWords.back(to:)`).
  - **PhoneBigTitle** (`.big`) is 34 and a header.
- **PhoneTabItem** and **PhoneLitLine**: an item of the tab bar or of Now Playing's bottom row.
  - The lit line is 24 x 2 on the top edge, in `acc`.
  - The item has the Large Content Viewer.
- **PhoneMiniGround** and **PhoneSeekLine** are the restyled mini player's parts. The restyle itself is R4's.
- **PhoneCard**, **PhoneGroup** (its legend is a header), **PhoneKV** (one element), **PhoneGo** and **PhoneChevron**.
- **PhoneSwitchStyle** (`.phoneSwitch`): a ToggleStyle.
  - It is drawn as `.sw`, square, with the purple from PrimaryButton.
  - VoiceOver reads it as a switch and its value, through `accessibilityRepresentation`.
  - It fades while it can't be used (`DWPalette.off`).
- **PhoneFoot** and `.phoneFoot { }` (`.foot2`): 68 tall at least.
  - It sits above the home indicator, with its ground run into it.
  - It stays under the keyboard and doesn't ride up on it. The page keeps its room above the foot, and has none while
    the keyboard is up.
- **PhoneMeta** and **PhoneMetaLink** (`.meta`).

Every bar caps at xxxLarge, as the tab bar does. Everything else grows.

### Decisions, and where this departs from the plan

- **No NowPlayingSheet.** The sheet's tabs (Queue, Info, EQ) need R3's Core work, so the sheet waits for R3. R1b
  gives it PhoneStrip.
- **No ••• piece.** It is iOS's own Menu (plan 3.2).
- **The phone's purple is Core PrimaryButton's.** It is read through `deck(PrimaryButton.x)`, never retyped. Pressed,
  it is PrimaryFace's reviewed press (after review, below), not DWRaised's turned-over gradient.
- **DWPalette holds colours later slices draw**: the tab bar, the row rule, the mini player, and (after review) the
  checkbox's fill and the meter's. App/Look gains only new files after R1b (plan 3.5).
- **The phone's field label (88) and the KV label (116) are minimums**, so they grow with the text size. The Mac's
  label stays R1's exact 84.
- **The reach test is stricter than the plan.** App/Look may name neither the Mac zone nor the phone zone, so a shared
  part never depends on one device's pieces.
- test_ios_mac.py is not in R1b's Touches list. It was touched for the renames only.
- dw.css was "copied again", and the copy is byte-identical to the canvas's.

### Tests, and the faults they were seen failing on

**tests/test_ios_phone_look.py** (19 tests) reads dw.css by the cascade.
- The cascade works like this:
  - it takes the `.dw.ph` rules a piece's element matches, right to left;
  - specificity decides first, then order, with `!important` above both;
  - shorthands are expanded and `var()` is substituted.
- Its self-tests: a later phone rule wins, specificity beats order, and the Mac reads as R1's reader did.
- It holds these to that cascade:
  - DWLook's phone sizes, PhoneLook, `Typeface.Look`'s phone half and `Typeface.Phone`;
  - the phone's colours, with every shared part the phone draws differently having its twin;
  - the purple, as PrimaryButton's, and DWCorners' phone half, as Corners' 0.
- It also holds these rules:
  - no colour, radius or font of their own in App/Look or App/Phone;
  - every fixed frame is on an allowlist, and every other height is `lookHeight`;
  - every button's target is DWTarget (44 at least);
  - VoiceOver, the text size cap and the keyboard;
  - the pieces are drawn nowhere yet.

**test_ios_mac_look.py** now reads the Mac's values from App/Look. It reads both palettes, with each colour's layer and
direction, and checks that DWLook's Mac half and Typeface.Look's Mac half are R1's.

**test_ios_mac_reach.py** has the three zones:
- **Mac:** App/Mac's names, MacLook, MacTable, MacInFront, `Typeface.Mac` and `DWCorners.Mac`. Named only from App/Mac,
  the four frame files and Platform's Mac half.
- **Phone:** App/Phone's names, PhoneLook, `Typeface.Phone` and `DWCorners.Phone`. Never named from App/Mac, the frame
  files, Platform's Mac half or App/Look.
- **Look:** named from anywhere.

**test_ios_palette.py**: DWCorners is the corner test's one Look exemption, and only PhoneSwitch takes `roundShape`.

**Core DWLookTests** (4 tests).

R1b's six faults and R1's seven were each applied alone, run, and restored byte for byte. Every one was caught:
- a phone value from an overridden `.dw.ph` rule (DWLook's phone `rowHeight` 44, the earlier `.row`):
  `test_dwlooks_phone_sizes_are_the_phones_rules`;
- a phone corner of 4 (DWCorners.Phone.button): `test_the_phones_corners_are_corners_square` and test_ios_palette's
  `test_the_looks_phone_corners_are_corners`;
- `PhoneChevron()` in MacToolbar: `test_the_phones_pieces_are_drawn_nowhere_yet`, and the reach's
  `test_app_mac_is_named_only_from_the_macs_frame` and `test_the_reach_catches_each_zone_out_of_place`;
- `MacPalette.titleEdge` in DWChip: `test_nothing_in_app_look_or_app_phone_draws_a_value_of_its_own` and the same two
  reach tests;
- the phone's primary edge as `hex(0x7c3aed)`, PrimaryButton's own value retyped: `test_the_phones_purple_is_primarybuttons`;
- `.frame(height:)` in place of PhoneGo's `lookHeight`: `test_every_height_on_the_phone_is_a_minimum`;
- R1's, adapted to the new homes:
  - `acc` 0xc084fd: `test_every_colour_in_the_palette_is_one_dw_css_names`;
  - `Color.red` in DWChip: both no-value-of-its-own tests (the Mac's and the phone's);
  - MacTabStack's `.appRoutes()`: `test_the_frame_stacks_are_the_macs_with_its_own_routes`;
  - MacPalette named from Typeface.swift: `test_app_mac_is_named_only_from_the_macs_frame`;
  - the iPhone half's `returnPresses()` given `keyboardShortcut(.defaultAction)`:
    `test_platforms_iphone_half_does_nothing_new` and test_ios_mac's
    `test_platform_is_the_iphones_exactly_as_before_on_the_iphone`;
  - the stripes not starting again under a heading: MacTableTests `theStripesStartAgainUnderEveryHeading`;
  - a vanished row's selection kept: MacTableTests `aVanishedRowsSelectionBecomesNone` and
    `aClickSelectsAndADoubleClickOrReturnOpens` (MacTable itself is unchanged in R1b).

### Not verified - checks 524 and 525

- No App/Look part or App/Phone piece has been seen on a screen.
- R1's Mac (524) is as R1 left it only by the builds and the tests.
- That the phones are unchanged (525) is only the iPhone build's word and the gate's.
- PhoneFoot's keyboard handling is untried on a device: whether the layer taking the keyboard's room keeps the foot at
  the foot of the screen under the keyboard is only how SwiftUI's safe areas are documented to work.
- PhoneStrip's sideways scroll and its scroll into view, and whether the field's well takes a tap just outside it, are
  untried until a slice draws them.

### After review (2026-11-25)

One review found nothing broken today: the Mac draws what R1 drew, and the phone draws nothing new. It found one
problem that would have forced R2 to rework a piece, plus test gaps and nits. All of them are fixed; nothing is
committed.

1. **The strip brings the shown button into view.**
   - The Library's five buttons measure 450 pt at the default text size, so the strip scrolls on every iPhone (375-430
     wide). Before the fix, after a swipe to Downloaded its lit button stayed off the screen.
   - The scrolling half is now in a ScrollViewReader. It scrolls the shown button to the centre as it opens, and
     whenever the button changes, by a tap or by the page's own swipe. It moves as the Library's swipe does
     (LibrarySwitchControl's `.snappy`, none with Reduce Motion).
   - **The targets were clipped.** A scroll view takes no touch outside itself, so the 44 pt targets were cut to its
     32 pt height. The row is now padded by the target's reach (6) above and below, so the scroll view holds the whole
     targets. The strip is then drawn as tall as its faces again (`.padding(.vertical, -reach)`), so its layout doesn't
     change.
   - Where the strip fits, it now starts at the leading edge, as `.chips` does, rather than being centred by its parent.
2. **Each device's half of every shared piece is held by a test.**
   - Before the fix, `if !Platform.mac` in DWFieldRow and `fixedSize(horizontal: false…)` in DWButtonStyle both passed
     every test.
   - `test_each_shared_piece_parts_by_device_only_where_said` holds every `Platform.` line in App/Look, line by line.
     App/Phone has none.
   - `test_each_device_half_of_the_shared_pieces_draws_its_own` holds what each half draws: DWFieldRow (R1's trailing
     label on the Mac, the card's row on the phone), DWButtonStyle's `fixedSize`/`fills`, DWSegmented's halves, and
     DWToggleStyle's dot.
3. **The self-tests now hold something.**
   - `.count`'s font check had read as `(A and B) or C`. It now asserts 11px, weight 600 and the substituted
     `"Noto Sans Mono"` family. A synthetic `font` shorthand with `var()` is checked too.
   - Core DWLook has `reach(_ height:)`: half what a face lacks of the target, and DWTarget draws it. DWLookTests now
     asserts each piece's real target (36→44, 32→44, 48→48, 28→44, 38→44) and the Mac's reach of 0, in place of the
     always-true `max(face, target) >= 44`.
   - DWField had no target, so a phone field's real target was its 36 pt well. Its well now takes a 44 target, and a
     tap there focuses the field. The well sits under the field, which takes taps on itself first.
4. **DWTarget reaches up and down only** (`rect.insetBy(dx: 0, dy: -reach)`), as SegmentReach does. Grid and List (28
   wide, 6 apart) no longer get overlapping targets. The test refuses any width or x change.
5. **The phone's primary pressed is PrimaryFace's.**
   - It uses `phonePrimaryPressedFace` and `phonePrimaryPressedEdge`, made from PrimaryButton's
     `pressedTop/Bottom/Edge` (brightness 0.92, held to theme.css by test_ios_palette).
   - The highlight is kept and nothing is turned over, so an album's Play keeps its press when it moves to DWButtonStyle.
   - The two pressed lines are sourced `web: --dw-primary-pressed`. The palette reader accepts that source only for
     these colours, only in DWPalette, and refuses it in four other forms.
6. **DWPalette has everything ahead of its slices.**
   - New: the checkbox's fill (moved from MacPalette, for R11's DWCheckbox) and the meter's shade and three fills
     (`meterFill`, `meterMarked`, `meterGood`; `.meter`, `.pur`, `.grn`, for R8's DWMeter). All are held to dw.css.
   - `test_the_palette_holds_what_later_slices_draw` checks that they are there.
7. **Nits.**
   - PhoneBack reads "Library, Back" (Core `PhonePieceWords.back(to:)`, in the phone's reach zone).
   - PhoneSwitch fades by `DWPalette.off` while disabled; it reads `isEnabled` in a view of its own.
   - PhoneFoot's `.ignoresSafeArea(.keyboard)` is now on the layer the foot sits in (a VStack the page's height, with
     a Spacer over the foot), not on the 68 pt foot. That keeps the plan's "under the keyboard", but it is **untried
     on a device**.

**Mutations.** 23 more faults were each applied alone, run, and restored byte for byte. Every one was caught:
- **The strip:**
  - no scroll on a change, the reach padding dropped, the leading frame dropped: all three caught by
    `test_the_phones_pieces_read_and_grow_as_the_plan_says`.
- **The device halves:**
  - DWField's and DWSegmented's `if !Platform.mac`: both branch tests (DWSegmented also `test_the_segmented_control_is_dw_css_seg`);
  - `fixedSize(horizontal: false)`: `test_each_device_half_of_the_shared_pieces_draws_its_own`;
  - the toggle's dot on the phone: both branch tests and the read-and-grow test;
  - the large weight on the Mac: the parts-by-device test;
  - the purple's words swapped, and its face's condition inverted: the parts-by-device test and
    `test_the_phones_purple_is_primarybuttons`.
- **The self-tests and targets:**
  - the cascade reading no `var()`: `test_the_cascade_is_specificity_then_order`;
  - DWField without its target, and DWTarget grown sideways: `test_a_fingers_target_is_44_at_least`;
  - Core's reach a quarter of what a face lacks: DWLookTests `thePhonesGrowAndTakeAFinger`.
- **The pressed primary:**
  - turned over, or not darkened: `test_the_phones_purple_is_primarybuttons`;
  - its edge retyped as `hex`: that test and three palette tests.
- **The palette:**
  - the meter fill off dw.css: `test_every_colour_in_the_palette_is_one_dw_css_names`;
  - checkFill back in MacPalette: that test and `test_the_palette_holds_what_later_slices_draw`.
- **The nits:**
  - the back link read as the page alone, the switch not faded, the keyboard ignored by the foot alone: each caught by
    `test_the_phones_pieces_read_and_grow_as_the_plan_says`;
  - the Core back words without "Back": DWLookTests `theBackLinkIsReadAsIOSsOwn`.

Tests after review: test_ios_phone_look 22 (from 19), DWLookTests 5 (from 4).

## The redesign, slice R3b: the Queue, Info and the EQ inside (2026-11-25)

The build plan's 3.4 "R3b" (~/Desktop/Code/deadwax-plans/mac-redesign-build.md): Now Playing's sheet's three pages
redrawn on the phone as iQueue, iInfo and iEQ, and on the Mac the dock's Queue and Info tabs given the same time left
and Played. "Queue" on both. No server data, no engine diff (DeadwaxAudio, AudioSessionController, Core's UpNext and
QueueController are untouched), and the EQ's settings, curve and processing are as they were: its controls are redrawn,
each making the same EQModel call it made. The app is still 0.13 (13); `__version__` is untouched.

### What was built

**The sheet's top is each page's (NowPlayingSheet.swift).** R3's sheet drew PhoneTop and the strip over every page. Now
`SheetTop` (the strip's tab binding and the sheet's own dismiss, read outside every page's stack) is handed to each page,
and `sheetTop(top) { trailing }` puts `‹ Now Playing` and the page's own buttons in the page's NavigationStack bar
(iOS 26's glass behind them hidden), with the strip as the root page's first row. A page pushed on a stack (Album info,
the EQ's pages) has the system's bar and Back as before; the strip is on root pages only. The sheet keeps Info's
About/Debug choice (`infoTab`), so the strip's taps keep it (R3's review, 9). `.presentationBackground(DWPalette.panel)`.

**The Queue (UpNextScreen.swift; Core QueueTimeLeft.swift).** On the phone (`sheet != nil`) still a List - Edit's
moves and removals are the List's - in the plain style with the look's rows:
- The top: History (scrolls the song playing's row to the view's foot, what was played over it) and Clear (Playing
  Next out), then Edit/Done, each DWButtonStyle small. From xLarge (`folds`: `size > .large`) History and Clear go in
  a •••. Worked out for 375 points at 0.55 em a letter: about 362 at Large unfolded, 395 at xLarge unfolded (so it
  folds there), about 323 at xxxLarge folded, where the top stops growing.
- The song playing as the selected row (selbg/selbd/selt, tallRowHeight), first - (R3b's review) with no heading over
  it, nor over Playing Next's songs after it, each saying its artist and album; `QueuePageWords.heading` turns "From
  X" into "Next from X", the one heading; under an album's heading of one album and one artist the rows are their
  titles alone (`showsLines`). Rows are rowHeight (48 on the phone), Edit's rows too (`QueueRowHeight`, a modifier,
  never a frame of 0 on the Mac - lookHeight is an exact height there).
- The foot: Shuffle and Repeat (lit while on, VoiceOver's "selected"), and the time left. ViewThatFits: one line, or
  the time on its own line under the two. Capped at xxxLarge.
- `QueueTimeLeft.words(view, position:speed:)`: "8 songs · 33 min left" from UpNextView's rows - Playing Next's, the
  list's and its `more` - plus what is left of the song playing (its length less the position, never below none),
  divided by the speed. History never counts. Rounded up to the minute (`span`: "1 hr 12 min"); (R3b's review)
  `left`: under a minute "under 1 min left", none left no time at all. "over …" with a song of unknown length or
  `more`, rounded DOWN so it never says more than is known, and under a whole minute known no time ("2 songs") -
  never "over 0 min left". Repeat One says the songs alone; Repeat All counts the one round the list draws (the rest
  of the round playing, or at its last song the next round, "again"), never the rounds after - the `then` line's;
  nothing playing, or nothing to say, nil. Read in `QueueTimeLeftLine`, a small view of its own - the only one
  reading `player.shownPosition` and `player.speed`.
- The plays are unchanged: a row's tap is `player.jump(to: row.key)`, History's `guard player.jump(to: row.key)`, an
  older row's `player.rollBack(handed.rows, floor:)`, each in the tap with nothing awaited before it.
- The Mac keeps its insetGrouped List, its headers with Clear, its toolbar Edit and Done with Escape; it gains the time
  left along the panel's foot (`macFoot`), (R3b's review) in the status bar's 11.5 in its own type (Typeface.Look's
  chip, not mono), at the foot's left.

**Info (InfoView.swift; Core About.swift, additive).** `InfoView(sheet:picked:)`. In the sheet, a ScrollView of:
- the song's row (cover 64, title, artist in the accent, `facts.line` "Wilco (The Album) · 2009"), one element;
- DWSegmented About/Debug for an admin, bound to the sheet's `infoTab`;
- **This song** (PhoneGroup): Sound's Format first, then `facts.song` - Track, Disc, Length, Size, Played, Written
  by - then the rest of Sound, Plays from, and the EQ's row (InfoEQRow, its own view, reading `eq.infoSound`);
- **The album**: `facts.album` - Released, Label, Songs, This pressing (logins on), Folder (an admin) - and Album

  921 kbps", either alone, no row for neither (nil, or 0) - from the song as the player has it (`player.song(for:

  that date: Info's ask decodes getSong as the relay passes it on (`played` among it), while the album's songs come
  from the routes' Song through `SongDetails(song:)`, which has no `played` - so the fallback is the count alone

  moves at midnight.
- The Mac's dock: the song section's lines become `facts.song`'s rows (LabeledContent), Played among them. The rest of
  the Mac's Info is as it was; Go to artist is the phone's only.

### What else is lost when the sheet's page goes (R3's review asked)

- **A page pushed on a tab's stack** (the EQ's presets, correction or a filter; Info's Album info) is gone when the
  strip moves to another tab: one tab's page is drawn at a time, so its stack goes with it. Keeping it would mean
  keeping each tab's view alive (or its path in the sheet) - not cheap or safe for the EQ, whose page follows the route
  on appear; left as it is. The filter editor's typed value, the one thing that was lost unsaid, is now applied.
- **Info's About/Debug choice**: kept, in the sheet (`infoTab`).
- **The Queue's scroll place**: it opens at the song playing each time, as it always did.

- iInfo's **On this iPhone 281 MB**: no such data for a song (and not asked for). (Its **Size** is built, R3b's review.)
- iEQ's **Flat** button and **Find yours…**: new behaviour, not a redraw - Find yours is reachable through Correction.
- The album's **Format** row (the song's says it whole).
- **PasteButton** (Advanced's Paste) stays the system's: it can't be restyled.

## The redesign, slice R2: Albums and Artists, and the Library's top (2026-11-25)

R2 of ~/Desktop/Code/deadwax-plans/mac-redesign-build.md (section 3.4, "#### R2"), built to wave-b-common.md and to
James's answer 1, which binds the phone: **"Today's behaviour, new look"**. So the phone's Library does what it did, in
iLibrary's, iArtists' and iPlaylists' look:
- Find is kept, its square magnifying glass before the •••;
- the strip is the pages in the order kept, then Downloaded (pushed, as the •••'s Downloaded was);
- Songs is a page only where it was one - never beside your own albums;
- Yours | All shows only with a library of your own, in place of the •••'s All music;
- the meta line holds the count, the sort (out of the •••), and Grid and List on Albums;
- the pager's swipe, Find's field, the pull to shuffle, the letter index and TopClearance work as before.

The Mac's Albums and Artists become its own pages: column lists (or tiles) under a toolbar. R3 and R8 were built at the
same time in their own worktrees; none of their files is touched here. The app is still 0.13 (13), `__version__` is
untouched, and the word fixtures are unchanged (no key changed).

The gate, `git diff 5123bab3 --stat -- ios ':!ios/App/Mac' ':!ios/App/Look' ':!ios/App/Phone'`, names:
- App/Library's six (LibraryTop, LibraryView, LibraryTiles, AlbumsScreen, ArtistsScreen, SongsScreen) and
  App/Playlists/PlaylistsScreen - the slice's Touches;
- App/Shared/Platform.swift: `listKeys`, a Mac half and a phone half that does nothing (the Mac's list hears its keys
  in one place, as `returnPresses` does);
- Core's LibrarySwitch.swift (added to - and, since the review, the old •••'s `LibraryMenu.sections` taken out) and
  LibrarySwitchTests, ArtistTotals.swift and ArtistTotalsTests (new);
- since the review, three that only named the old •••: a comment each in App/Models/LibraryModel.swift and Core's
  MacSidebar.swift, and ShuffleVectorTests' All music check (After review, 9).

The following have no diff: ios/Deadwax.xcodeproj (App/ is a synchronized folder), ios/Config, the words fixtures, the
engine files (DeadwaxAudio, AudioSessionController, Core's QueueController and UpNext), DeadwaxClient and Core's Routes,
App/Look, src/ and ui/ - and App/Phone, but for PhoneStrip's `pushes` since the review (After review, 9).

### What was built

**Core.**
- **ArtistTotals.swift** (new). `ArtistTotals.of(albums)` adds up each artist's songs, plays and last played
  from the album index the app already has - keyed by the album's `artistId`, never its name, so two artists of one
  name stay two; an album with no id counts for nobody; a negative count counts as none. `playedAt` is nil for an album
  never played, for Navidrome's zero time and for a value that isn't a date. `lastPlayedWords` is Artists.dc.html's
  column: "today", "yesterday", "3 days ago", "last week", then "12 Nov" (with its year when it isn't this one), by the
  calendar's days in the device's zone; a time after now (a clock set wrong) is today; nil is "" - never a date. The
  counts' words ("1,612 songs", "1 artist", `number`, `plays`, "1 selected"), the phone's artist row line ("6 albums ·
  59 songs", the old words while no songs are in hand) and LibraryColumnWords, the Mac's column heads.
- **LibrarySwitch.swift**, added to:
  - `LibrarySide` (Yours, All) and its scope; `LibraryPages.allMusic`, `shown(_:personal:side:)` (All's pages are
    Albums, Artists and Songs in the order kept), `sides` (Yours | All shows with a library of your own, the Library on
    your albums, deadwax reachable - just where All music was offered) and `side`;
  - `LibraryStripItem` and `LibraryStrip.items`: the pages, then Downloaded - none while the Albums page is Downloaded
    (offline), which is already it;
  - `LibraryMenu.topSections`: the top's ••• - Shuffle, the way back to the albums while the Albums page is
    Downloaded, then Refresh and Edit order;
  - LibrarySwitchWords' yours, all, sidesLabel, grid, list and playlistsCount.

**The phone.**
- **LibraryTop** is iLibrary's top: PhoneTop's "Library", and at its trailing end Yours | All (DWSegmented, when
  `sides`), the magnifying glass and the ••• (DWButtonStyle small, square). Find's field comes up under it. The
  clearance (TopClearance), the fill behind the status bar (Palette.page, black) and the TopProbe are as they were. The
  old switch (LibrarySwitchControl, its segment reach and its hairline) is gone.
- **LibraryView** draws the strip (PhoneStrip) under the top. A chip runs the switch's old tap - `show(chosen)` under
  `.snappy`, none with Reduce Motion - so the pager moves to the page; a swipe settling lights the page's chip; the
  Downloaded chip pushes `.downloaded` on the tab's path. On All the pages are the collection's (AlbumList
  `.scope(.store)`, ArtistsScreen's scope), the pull and the ••• shuffle All songs, and Refresh refreshes that side.
  LibraryView is now generic over a `Desk`, so the Mac can pass its own pages in (below); the phone's is `EmptyView`.
- **Each page's meta line** (PhoneMeta) under the strip: Albums' count, its sort as a purple link opening the sort's
  menu, and Grid and List (DWToggleStyle) at the end; Artists' count and order; Playlists' count ("3 of 9 playlists"
  while Find finds) and New playlist… (only while deadwax can be reached); Songs' count. The pushed lists (All albums
  from See All music, Downloaded) keep their navigation bar, its sort and their counts in the list, as before.
- **LibraryTiles**: LibraryLook holds dw.css's sizes (tiles 14 and 16 apart, 12 from the top, 7 over the title; tall
  rows 60 with 44 covers, 16 at the sides, 10 between). The tile, the rows (iArtists' tall row, LibraryListRow, with
  LibraryChevron), the New mark and the headers are drawn from it and from DWPalette, square.
- **ArtistsScreen**'s row says the artist's songs once the scope's albums have come (`ArtistTotals.rowLine`), made once
  per answer (`ArtistTotalsKey`: the scope and the shelf's serial).
- **SongsScreen** and **PlaylistsScreen**' rows are the same tall rows.

**The Mac.**
- **MacColumnList** (App/Mac/Components): the header strip (.cols), 30-point rows striped by MacTable.stripes, the
  selected row in the selection's fill and edge; widths from MacTable.widths; click selects, double-click or Return
  opens, ↑ ↓ Home End move (MacTable.moved/returned/kept); one VoiceOver element per row.
- **MacAlbumsPage**: the toolbar - Play (primary, a SharpSymbol play), Shuffle, the groove, Sort and its pop-up
  (LibraryModel.sort), Grid | List (LibraryModel.layout, kept on this Mac as the phone keeps its own), Find in albums
  (230) - over the list (Album with its 20-point cover, Artist 150, Year 54, Songs 58) or MacFrame.tileMin tiles. The
  status bar: albums and songs listed, "1 selected"; the selection is Info's (MacSelection).
- **MacArtistsPage**: the same toolbar over Artist, Albums 76, Songs 76, Plays 70, Last played 124. Albums is
  Navidrome's albumCount; Songs, Plays and Last played are ArtistTotals over the scope's album index. Status: artists
  and albums listed.
- **Play** on either plays only once the songs are in hand. They are asked as the row is selected (an AlbumModel or an
  ArtistPageModel, as the pages ask), and Play is dimmed until they come. The tap calls `player.play(songs:album:at:)`
  or `player.play(artist:shuffle:)` with nothing awaited. Shuffle is the Library's (ShuffleModel, All songs' for the
  collection's pages with a library of your own).
- **MacLibraryDesk** chooses the page. `MacLibrary.root()` passes it to LibraryView as its desk: at the root, with
  Albums or Artists showing, the desk is drawn in the top's, the strip's and the pager's place. `MacLibrary.page(for:)`
  sends the sidebar's All Albums and All Artists to the Mac's pages too.
- **MacPalette**: columnsFace, columnsRule, rowStripe and coverEdge, each from dw.css - since the review, R8's
  block byte for byte (groupRowFace with them, which R2 doesn't draw).

### Decisions, and where this departs from the plan

- **A desk closure, not a Mac page named from the Library.** App/Library may not name App/Mac
  (test_ios_mac_reach.py), so LibraryView takes the Mac's pages as a generic closure from MacLibrary.
- **Yours | All is the phone's alone.** The Mac's sidebar has its own (slice 3); on the Mac the top's is never shown.
- **The Mac pages' Find has no ⌘F.** test_ios_mac counts `.findField(` once app-wide, and ⌘F stays the sidebar's
  search, as slice 3 settled.
- **Edit order edits Yours' pages.** All shows Albums, Artists and Songs in the kept order; there is no order of its
  own.
- **Left out, as no data the app has can draw it:** the Albums list's Format column, the library's size and
  "Navidrome up to date" in the status bar - the album index carries none of them, and a route would be new server
  data.
- **Left out for now:** the header's sort caret (Sort is the toolbar's pop-up, the order the phone shares - a header
  that sorts would be a second way); group headings in the Mac's lists; Play on the Mac's Artists while offline (an artist's songs come
  from deadwax); the phone cover's 1-point edge. The Mac's Playlists, Songs and Downloaded are still the phone's pages, under the strip,
  and a swipe from Playlists onto Albums there brings the desk in.

### Tests, and the faults they were seen failing on

- **Core ArtistTotalsTests** (8 tests, new) and **LibrarySwitchTests** (5 added: songs never beside your own albums,
  Yours | All where All music was, the strip, the top's •••, Playlists' count).
- **tests/test_ios_library_look.py** (12, new): the tiles and rows against dw.css; the phone's Library square; tokens
  only in the redrawn files; the top as iLibrary's with Find kept; the top clearing the island; a chip moving the pager
  and Downloaded pushed; Songs never beside your own albums; the meta lines; the layout kept per device and bound on
  both; every play in the tap with the songs in hand; the Mac's column lists; the totals made once per answer.
- **Edited:** test_ios_palette.py's Library-top test (the new pager order, the fill, dw.css's top), and three lines of
  its bars test that held the switch's constants (now a note that the switch's pages are the strip's);
  test_ios_phone_look.py (the seven R2 files may draw the phone's and the Look's pieces; the animation is the chip's);
  test_ios_mac_reach.py (the Library's root passes the desk; Albums and Artists are no longer the phone's pages on the
  Mac).

Each fault was applied alone, run, and restored byte for byte. Every one was caught:
- the totals keyed by the artist's name, not its id: ArtistTotalsTests `eachAlbumCountsUnderItsOwnArtistAlone` (and

## The redesign, slice R3: the side panel's tabs; the Now Playing sheet (2026-11-25)

The build plan's 3.4 "R3" (~/Desktop/Code/deadwax-plans/mac-redesign-build.md), with James's answers 2 and 3 in its 3.8
binding:
- **"The cover's place"**: the lyrics stay where the cover is. The bottom row's Lyrics turns them on and off. The phone's
  sheet has no Lyrics tab; the Mac's dock has one.
- **"Queue on both"**: every word the app shows that said "Up Next" says Queue, on the phone and the Mac. The types and
  files keep Up Next's name (UpNextScreen, UpNextWords, `upNext` cases), and the web keeps its word.

Each tab's page is still today's: R3b redraws them. The app is still 0.13 (13); `__version__` is untouched.

### What was built

**Core `MacDock`** (MacDock.swift) - the side panel's rules:
- `Tab`: Sources, Queue (`upNext`), Lyrics, Info, EQ. `tabs(getOpen:)` puts Sources first only while a Get page is
  open. Nothing opens a Get page yet (R7's), so `AppNavigation.macGetOpen` stays false and the dock draws an empty page
  for Sources.
- `toggled`: a tab's key or bar button closes the panel when its tab shows, and switches to it otherwise. `shown`: a
  folder tab clicked, the •••'s Info or EQ, Settings > Playback's EQ row - that tab, whatever showed. `kept`: Sources
  goes when its Get page does.
- `afterQueueEnds`: the Queue closes, and Info unless something is selected; Lyrics stays.
- `makesRoom` / `liesOver`: beside the page from 1280 wide, over it below (MacFrame's rule, for a tab).
- `escape(typing:shown:)`, and `MacFrame.escape(typing:panel:)` over a tab, so the call sites that read it
  (UpNextScreen, InfoView, PlaylistView) are unchanged.
- `infoSubject(selected:playing:)`: the selection, else the song playing, else nothing - and `Words.heading`:
  "Selected album", "Selected artist", "Playing".

**Core `NowPlayingTabs`** (NowPlayingTabs.swift) - the phone's sheet and row:
- `strip`: Queue, Info, EQ. `row`: Queue, Lyrics, the output, Info, EQ.
- `opens(_:)`: Queue, Info and EQ open the sheet on their tab (`.tab`); Lyrics is `.lyrics`, never the sheet; the
  output is AirPlay's own.
- `chipBetween`: the output and Info.
- `shared(sheet:coverUp:)`: a shared EQ file always shows EQ - the sheet up on any tab moves to it in place, and with
  the cover full screen up it waits for the cover to close (eq.md 3.9's wait, as before).
- `symbol(_:on:)` and `Words`: "Now Playing" (the back link), "Now Playing's pages" (the strip, for VoiceOver),
  `eq(setting:)` ("EQ, Bass Boost").

**Core `MacMenu`**: View > EQ (⌥⌘E, `.eq`), after Info. `State.panel` is a `MacDock.Tab?`, and `State.selected` lets
Info be used with a row selected and nothing queued. The Queue item is dimmed with nothing queued unless its tab shows.

**The Mac (MacPanels.swift)**: `MacPanel(tab:)` is the dock: MacFolderTabs over `MacDock.tabs`, then one tab's page in
a `switch` - UpNextScreen, LyricsPanel, DockInfo, DockEQ - 400 wide (`MacLook.panelWidth`; MacFrame's 470 is the web's
and is no longer read here). `DockDone` is the dock's one Done and its one Escape (through `MacFrame.escape`).
- **DockInfo**: the heading from MacDock, then for an album selected `AlbumInfoList` on a stub of the row's album (it
  asks for the rest itself), for an artist selected their name, album count and Go to artist, else InfoView.
- **DockEQ**: EQScreen(opened: .now) on its own EQSheetStack. EQScreen reads `inSidePanel` for one thing, its inline
  title. EQLink pushes on that stack in the dock; on the Mac anywhere else (Settings > Playback's EQ row) it shows the
  EQ tab. EQDoneButton puts the panel away in the dock.
- **AppNavigation** (App/Shared/Routes.swift): `macPanel` is a `MacDock.Tab?`, set only through MacDock's rules
  (`togglePanel`, `showPanel`, `closePanel`, `queueEnded`); `macSelected` mirrors MacSelection (DesktopFrame) for the
  menus; `macGetOpen` for Sources.
- **DesktopFrame** draws `MacPanel(tab:)` once, beside or over the page by MacDock. **PlayerBar**'s ••• EQ shows the EQ
  tab. A shared or opened EQ file shows the dock's EQ tab, its preview over it (since the review - see "After review";
  as first built it opened the frame's EQ sheet over the window).

**The phone (NowPlayingSheet.swift, NowPlayingView.swift)**:
- **NowPlayingSheet**: PhoneTop with PhoneBack ("‹ Now Playing", the sheet's own dismiss), PhoneStrip over
  `NowPlayingTabs.strip`, then the tab's page - UpNextScreen, InfoView or EQSheet (its own stack, Done and the preview's
  wait), one at a time.
- **NowPlayingView**: one `appSheet(isPresented: $sheetUp)` in place of the three; `open(_:)` sets the tab and puts the
  sheet up, so a button tapped or a shared file moves the sheet already up in place. `sheetOver` (the scrubber's) is
  the sheet, Add to a playlist or the cover viewer.
- **The bottom row** in the footer's place: PhoneTabItem for Queue (spoken `upNextLabel`), Lyrics (lit while on,
  spoken `LyricsWords.label`, dimmed as before), Info and EQ (spoken "EQ, <setting>"); the output is AirPlay's glyph and
  the route's name (EQ's `shownName`) in `DWPalette.acc`, over AirPlayButton (as first built, the picker in the icon's
  place with a 44 target; since the review, under the whole column - "After review").
- **The speed chip** sits over the gap between the output and Info - since the review in a band of its own above the
  row (as first built, level with the icons, placed by anchors on them).
- **The •••** moved up beside the look button; its EQ left it (`onEQ: nil`). The Mac's bar keeps its EQ.
- The grip, the drag down and the cover viewer are untouched.
- PhoneTabItem gained `spoken` (VoiceOver's name where it says more than the words) - additive.

### Decisions, and where this departs from the plan

  `case .sheet(let tab):` read as one.

  (one EQ). Import… on the dock's EQ page is still a sheet over the window (check 535).

  song playing's (check 534 says so).

  R3b's Info redraws it.

  the selection mirrored), PlayerBar (the ••• EQ), EQRoute (the dock's stack and Done), DebugView (the word),
  PhoneTabItem (`spoken`, additive), Core UpNextView, DownloadWords and QueuePick (the words), four comment-only files,
  and MacSidebarTests (`MacFrame.Panel.none` spelled out once the overload made `.none` ambiguous).
- **EQScreen's header comment** still says Now Playing's •••; it is left for R3b, which redraws the page, so EQScreen
  changes only where it reads `inSidePanel`.

  (3/5 across, worked out from `row` and `chipBetween`). FooterGap, its key and SpeedChipPlace are gone.
