## The redesign, slice R4: the player bar, the mini player and the tab bar (2026-11-25)

The build plan's 3.4 "#### R4" (~/Desktop/Code/deadwax-plans/mac-redesign-build.md), the phone's pieces as its 3.2
draws them, and James's corrections in mac-redesign.md: the bar 66 tall; the display the bar's whole height, the cover
flush, three lines; shuffle, previous, play, next and repeat one row of drawn glyphs; less dead space; Queue, Lyrics
and Info one joined strip, then the EQ and the output. **No new server data**: DeadwaxClient and Core's Routes have no
diff, and neither do the engine files (DeadwaxAudio, AudioSessionController, Core's QueueController and UpNext). The
app is still 0.13 (13); `__version__` is untouched. No words fixture changed: the bar's new words ("Next", "3 of 11",
"Next: Roads") are Core's BarDisplay.Words, the same on both devices, so iphone.json and mac.json have no diff.

### What was built

**Core `BarDisplay`** (BarDisplay.swift) - what the Mac's display says, from the queue the player holds:
- `next(_:repeat:)`: the song that plays after this one - the queue's own `nextIndex`, so under Shuffle it is the
  shuffled order's. At the end: nothing with Repeat off; the list's first song with Repeat all (a shuffled list's
  next round isn't made until it is topped up, a moment before it plays, so it names nothing until then); nothing
  under Repeat one, or on Repeat One's copy of this song (Repeat just turned off), or during a library's shuffle
  past what is fetched.
- `place(_:)`: "3 of 11" - the song's place in its list this time round, out of the round's songs less those taken
  out (`left`), by one of two rules (after the review - see "After the review" below):
  - **in the list's own order** (Shuffle off, not a library's shuffle): its index in the list less the songs taken
    out before it. The list (`source`) and `left` survive a reload whole, so this holds however much of the queue
    Resume brought back - a 2,100-song playlist reloaded is still "1 of 2,100", and "300 of 2,099" with one taken out.
  - **shuffled, or a library's shuffle**: counted back from the round's songs still to come, and only while the queue
    holds every song the round has had (a library's shuffle: has fetched) or has it in `left` - else nil. Resume's
    window (windowOf: 50 before the song playing, 2,000 in all) can trim a round's front or cut its end, and a
    library's shuffle comes back without `left` (savedList keeps only the window's places): either way which songs
    were played can't be told, so there's no number until a round the queue holds whole - never a wrong one.

  So an album from its third song is 3 of 11 as Shuffle's third song is; Repeat all's next round counts afresh; a
  Repeat One copy is its song's place; a song taken out leaves the others' places as they were; a library's shuffle
  counts its whole order (Paged's total, "3 of 1,612"), an earlier round its own (`pagedRounds`). A song added with
  Play Next or Play Last has none. What follows from the rules: a shuffled list or a library's shuffle reloaded more
  than 50 songs in, or a shuffled list longer than 2,000, shows no number until its next round; under Shuffle a played
  song taken out (withoutKey records no `left` for one) leaves no number either; and Previous back into a stretch
  played shuffled, after Shuffle went off, reads that song's place in the list.
- `format(_:)`: "FLAC 16/44.1" from the song in hand alone (its suffix and type, bit depth and sample rate); with no
  depth "FLAC 44.1 kHz", with no rate "FLAC 16-bit", with neither "FLAC"; a lossy file its name alone (the queue keeps
  no bitrate). `formatSpoken` says it for VoiceOver ("FLAC, 16-bit, 44.1 kHz").
- `readout(_:)`: the two joined by the dot ("3 of 11 · FLAC 16/44.1"), either alone, nil with neither.

**`PlayerBar`** rewritten, as dw.css's `.player` (every size beside it named `// dw:` and held to it): 66 tall
(MacLook.barHeight), 14 apart and 14 in, on its own face (MacPalette's new `playerFace`, `playerEdge`, `playerSheen` -
dw.css's `.player` background, border-top and its inset sheen), its edge along the top.
- **The keys** (`.keys`, 11 apart): Shuffle and Repeat as toggles (DWToggleStyle, 30), Previous and Next as round keys
  (MacKeyStyle, 34), Play/Pause the big purple one (46), each glyph drawn (SharpSymbol, PlayPauseGlyph). Each key's
  action is PlayerModel's own call, the first thing in the click, as before.
- **The display** (`.lcd`, MacDisplay): the bar's height under its 1 pt edge. The cover flush at its left (65, its rule
  at its right; a click opens it full size); then the title with **Next** and its song at the right; "Artist — Album"
  (a button to the album) with the readout at the right in the mono face; the clocks either side of the scrubber
  (BarScrubber, `.meter`'s well, 6 tall, 8 while held). Narrow, each line gives way on its own - the first line's
  ViewThatFits drops Next, the second's the readout, each when its own line has no room, so which goes first depends on
  the words, not on an order; each line truncates with its whole words in its tooltip and VoiceOver ("Roads", value
  "Next: Mysterons").
- **The tools** (`.tools`, 6 apart): Queue, Lyrics and Info one strip (the new MacStripButtonStyle, App/Mac/Components/
  MacStrip.swift: .btn's faces, each overlapping the one before by its edge, the corners at the strip's ends alone -
  MacStripShape - the lit one drawn over its neighbours); a groove; the EQ (a button lit while its tab shows, named
  with the setting playing); the output (MacOutput, AirPlay's button and the output's name); the •••. Each of the four
  toggles its tab of the dock (AppNavigation.togglePanel); the •••'s Info and EQ still show theirs (R3).
- **Nothing queued**: the keys dimmed, "Nothing playing" in the display, the tools still open their tabs.
- **Space** is the Controls menu's, as it was (MacMenu: `Shortcut(.space)`, never while typing): the bar adds no key.

**`MiniPlayerView`**, as `.dw.ph .mini`: 60 tall (PhoneLook.mini, growing with the text) on PhoneMiniGround (#1c1b22
under its edge); the cover flush left, the bar's height under the edge (59), its rule at its right; the title in the
text's white, the artist in t2 (Typeface.Phone's small); Play/Pause bare - the sharp glyph in white, no face or edge -
in its 48 target with 12 past it; the seek line 2 tall along the top, `.prog`'s track and the purple gradient
(DWPalette.seekTrack, seekFill). Still no skip button; VoiceOver's Next song and Previous song on the title. **The drag
is byte for byte as it was** (its code's digest is held, from b6f8dcfa).

**`AppTabBar`**, as `.dw.ph .tabbar`: on DWPalette.tabBarFace (#121117) under its edge (tabBarEdge), the tabs 6 under
it, each 49 tall, its icon's box 24 and its words 11, medium; the shown tab in `acc`, the others #8a8a9c, and the lit
line (PhoneLitLine, 24 x 2, square) 7 over the shown tab alone, which is the bar's top edge. Requests' badge is the
look's count (DWCount) laid over the bar's colour, 9 right of the tab's centre and 1 over its top. The glyphs stay the
app's (the Library's squared stack), and so do `.isTabBar`, the Large Content Viewer, TabBarFoot's room and the cap at
xxxLarge.

### Decisions, and where this departs from the plan

- **Next is the app's queue's next** (UpNext's `nextIndex`, which Next on the keys plays), not computed from the web's
  PlayQueue: they agree everywhere but a shuffled list's end under Repeat all, where the app shuffles the next round
  only as it tops the queue up; until then it names nothing rather than a guess.
- **A lossy file's format is its name alone** ("MP3"): QueueTrack carries no bitrate. An MP4 file reads "ALAC" only
  when its content type says alac, else its suffix's name - "M4A", not "AAC": one song can't tell the two apart
  (AlbumInfo weighs a whole album's bitrates to). Navidrome's content type comes from the file's suffix, not from the
  codec, so an ALAC song will most likely always read "M4A" - unverified against a real Navidrome.
- **The output is R1's MacOutput** (AirPlay's own button and the name), not the drawing's `.btn` with a caret: the
  picker is macOS's, and can't be opened from a button of ours. Its name is capped at 150 with the button, and **left
  out below a bar 1000 wide** (MacOutput's new `named`), its tooltip kept: at the smallest window (880) the display
  then keeps 218 for its text, against 90 with the name - and the third line needs about 160 for an hour-long song's
  clocks (in test_ios_bar_look's arithmetic: the keys 218, the tools 421 named and 293 without).
- **The ••• stays**, after the output: it holds Add to a playlist… and Go to album, which the drawing has nowhere else.
- **Space was already the Controls menu's** (never while typing), so the bar draws no key of its own for it.
- **The lit strip button's zIndex is set by the bar**, not inside the style: a ButtonStyle's own can't reach the
  strip's stack.
- **The mini player's room past Play is 12** (`.mini`'s padding-right), not 14: the drag code is unchanged, but where
  it reads "on the title" (`width - (button + edge)`) moves 2 pt right with it.
- **The mini player keeps its own seek line**, not R1b's PhoneSeekLine: it grows to 8 under a finger and draws its
  part played every frame from the timeline; the colours are PhoneSeekLine's. PhoneSeekLine stays drawn nowhere.
- **The tab bar is 1 + 6 + 49 + TabBarFoot's room** (76 on a Face ID phone, 1 + 6 + 49 + 6 with none), not the
  drawing's fixed 83: TabBarFoot's room under the tabs was set with James on the phones (15 Nov) and stays.
- **The title stays iOS's subheadline** (15, growing with the text): Typeface.Phone has no 15.
- **The mini player's Play glyph stays at `.title2`** (Typeface.symbol), as it was: about two-thirds of the 32 pt box
  dw.css draws it in (`.dw.ph .mini .key.big svg`, in the 48 target). Left for James to decide on the phone.
- **Gone after the review, read by nothing**: MacFrame's web bar sizes (barHeight 72, barCover, barSideNarrow and
  barSideWide, barPad, barGap, barSide(width:), barMiddleMin) - frame-vectors.json keeps them, the web's record - and
  Palette's `tabBar`, `tabInactive` and `playerBar` (DWPalette's tabBarFace and tabItemText and MacPalette's
  playerFace draw those bars now).

### Tests, and the faults they were seen failing on

**Core BarDisplayTests** (30): Next is the queue's next; at the last song nothing (Repeat off) or the first (Repeat
all, and once topped up); Repeat one and its copies name nothing; under Shuffle the shuffled order at every place; a
shuffled round's end; a song added is next; nothing playing; 3 of 11; Shuffle's places, and Shuffle turned on midway;
a song taken out; Repeat all's next round; a Repeat One copy; a song added has none; a trimmed front; a library's
shuffle (1 of 1,612, and after more is fetched); a plain queue; the formats (an MP4 "M4A", "ALAC" only by its type);
the readout. After the review, nine more: a list of one under Shuffle and Repeat all; an earlier round of a library's
shuffle; a song taken out before this one in the list's order; reloads (a 2,100-song list, a shuffled one and a
60-song shuffled album, a library's shuffle with a song taken out); and the reviewer's three probes made tests,
seeded - Next names what plays and the place steps by one (3,000 runs of natural ends, Play Next and Last, removals,
Shuffle and Repeat changes), a library's shuffle fed a page at a time counts every song (500 runs), and Previous and
History's taps never name a wrong song or place (2,000 runs).

**tests/test_ios_bar_look.py** (16): the bar's sizes are dw.css's `.player`; the keys one row in the drawing's order;
every key acts in the click (no Task, nothing awaited); the display fills the bar with its three lines; Next and the
readout are Core's; the strip joined as dw.css joins it, then the groove, EQ and output (its width capped); Space
plays and pauses except in a field; the bar fits 880 and 1280 (added up from the sizes and the words; MacFrame's web
bar sizes gone); the mini player is `.mini`; Play bare and no skip button; the title's tap ends where the drag reads
the title (after the review); the drag as it was (its digest, PlayBar's reach and threshold); the lit line square and
over the shown tab alone; the tab bar's glyphs, badge and cap kept; no value of their own; "Queue".

**Shared test files edited** (the functions the brief named, and what follows from them): test_ios_palette's
`test_the_apps_own_bars_are_the_webs`, `test_the_requests_badge_is_the_webs` and `test_the_play_bar_is_the_tab_bars_top`
(now held to dw.css's `.tabbar`, `.count` and `.mini`, with a `_phone_look()` helper), and one line of
`test_the_bars_run_smooth_only_while_the_song_plays` (the seek line's fill is DWPalette.seekFill); test_ios_mac's
`test_the_bars_actions_are_the_players_own`; test_ios_phone_look's drawn-in sets (`R4_BARS`), as that file asks.

The brief's seven mutations, and three more, were each applied alone, run and restored byte for byte. Every one was
caught:
- "N of M" off by one (`place`'s number + 1): BarDisplayTests `theAlbumsThirdSongIsThreeOfEleven` and nine more of
  the place and readout tests;
- Next from the unshuffled order (the source's song after this one): `underShuffleNextIsTheShuffledOrder`,
  `aSongAddedIsNext`, `atAShuffledRoundsEndOnlyTheQueueKnowsWhatPlays`;
- Next at the last song (the first named with Repeat off): `atTheLastSongRepeatOffNamesNothing`;
- a key's action in a Task (Next's): `test_every_key_acts_in_the_click`;
- a skip button on the mini player: `test_play_is_bare_and_there_is_no_skip_button`;
- the drag's seek reach changed - PlayBar.seekReach 14 to 20, and the drag's start read 6 lower:
  `test_the_mini_players_drag_is_as_it_was`, each;
- the lit line rounded - PhoneLitLine a Capsule, and clipped to one in the tab: `test_the_lit_line_is_square_and_over_
  the_shown_tab_alone` and test_ios_palette's `test_every_corner_in_the_app_is_a_token` (the second also
  `test_the_bars_draw_no_value_of_their_own`); drawn on a tab not shown (`shown || tab == .library`): the lit line's
  test.

### After the review (2026-11-25)

The review found "3 of 11" could be wrong after a reload, four mutations that passed everything, a stale guide and
leftovers. Each fix, and what catches it (every mutation applied alone, run and restored byte for byte):
- **"N of M" after a reload.** Resume's windowOf cuts at Resume.maxEntries (2,000) as well as 50 before the song, so a
  2,100-song playlist read "101 of 2,100" after a reload (the old rule counted back from songs still to come, and the
  queue had lost its end); and a library's shuffle with a song taken out read "4 of 1,612" for "3 of 1,611", as
  savedList keeps no `left` for a paged queue. place() now has the two rules above: the list's own order counted from
  the front, which survives a reload; a shuffled round counted only while the queue holds it whole, else nil. Caught:
  the in-order rule turned off (`&& false`, every list counted back) - `aLongListReloadedKeepsItsPlace`,
  `aTrimmedFrontKeepsThePlace`; the whole-round guard dropped - `aShuffledListReloadedWithoutAllOfItsRoundHasNoPlace`,
  `aLibrarysShuffleReloadedWithASongTakenOutHasNoPlace`; the songs taken out before this one not subtracted -
  `inTheListsOrderASongTakenOutBeforeThisOneMovesItUp`, `nextNamesWhatPlaysAndThePlaceStepsByOne`; each rule's
  number + 1 - twelve tests (in order) and seven (counted back).
- **The four that passed everything:** `|| state.source.count == 1` dropped from next() -
  `aListOfOneUnderShuffleAndRepeatAllNamesItself`; an earlier round of a library's shuffle sized by the current
  round's `paged.total` - `anEarlierRoundOfALibrarysShuffleCountsItsOwnOrder`; MiniPlayerView's
  `.padding(.trailing, Self.end)` (BarTitle) removed - `test_the_titles_tap_ends_where_the_drag_reads_the_title`;
  PlayerBar's `.frame(maxWidth: Self.outputMost)` removed -
  `test_the_strip_is_three_joined_buttons_then_the_groove_eq_and_output`.
- **The guide** (docs/ios.md): the Mac's player bar as it is now (the keys in one row; the display with Next and "3 of
  11 · FLAC 16/44.1"; Queue | Lyrics | Info, then the EQ, the output and the •••); the side panel opened from the
  bar's Queue, Lyrics, Info and EQ (and check 533's sentence too); the mini player on its own ground; the tab bar's
  lit line and the badge's corner; 543's narrow window (each line on its own) and 544's "3 of 11" after a reload.
- **The leftovers**, removed (above): a MacFrame bar size put back - `test_the_bar_fits_the_smallest_window_and_the_
  one_it_opens_at`; Palette's `tabBar` put back - test_ios_palette's `test_the_apps_own_bars_are_the_webs`.
- **The notes**: M4A as the code has it, and Play's glyph left at `.title2` for James.

### Not verified - checks 543 to 549

- Neither device has seen it: only the builds and the tests. **Mac smoke run: not done** (James's installed app was
  running).
- On the Mac: the display's three lines at 1280 and 880, Next and the readout each giving way on its own line; the strip's
  joins and the lit button's edge; the output's name and AirPlay's picker from the bar; Space from the Controls menu
  with a key focused under full keyboard access; the bar's face and sheen beside the canvas.
- On the phones: the mini player as drawn (its ground, the cover's rule, the seek line over the edge); the drag's
  "on the title" boundary 2 pt further right; the lit line on the bar's edge and the badge at the largest text sizes;
  Ethan's phone for 547-548.
- "3 of 11" after a real quit and reopen (a long playlist, a shuffle partway in, a library's shuffle with a song taken
  out): BarDisplayTests round-trip Resume's own toSave and fromSnapshot, not the app's restore.

## The redesign, slice R8: Requests (2026-11-25)

Requests in the new look on both devices: mac-redesign-build.md "#### R8 - Requests", drawn in Requests.dc.html (the
Mac) and iRequests.dc.html (the phone). **No new server data**: DeadwaxClient and Core's Routes have no diff, and
neither do RequestsModel, its polling, the overlays or the engine files. The app is still 0.13 (13), and no words
fixture key changed (iphone.json and mac.json have no diff).

### The Mac: a table of its own (`App/Mac/Requests/MacRequestsPage.swift`)

`MacRequests.root()` draws MacRequestsPage now, not the phone's RequestsScreen. It is a MacPage:
- **The toolbar**, with Get albums: "Search Soulseek", the Artist and Album fields (Tab between them; Return in Artist
  moves to Album, Return in Album searches), Search, a groove; then **All | Active | Done** (DWSegmented, large), and
  **Clear done** at the right. It folds to fit its page (below, "After review"). Search opens Choose a
  source (SourcesSheet) over the page for a `GetRelease.manual` - the phone's ManualSearchSheet's own request, its
  `ManualSearch.canSearch` and subtitle - so a Get from it is a manual search's download as on the phone.
- **The table** (MacTable's rules): the header strip in the columns' face, then each heading (a group line, read as a
  header) and its rows, striped again under every heading. Columns Album (22 pt cover), Artist, From, Progress, Speed
  and the row's buttons. A click selects; a double click opens a done row (MacTable.clicked), and so does Return (MacTable.returned);
  ↑ ↓ Home End move the selection (MacTable.moved); the selection is kept by key and lets go when its row goes, or when
  the filter hides it (MacTable.kept). It scrolls sideways under 1002 pt and not otherwise.
- **Progress**: a download's DWMeter and its line ("3 of 11 files", or going / organizing's words); a waiting row's
  place, in amber when it warns; why one needs attention, in red, the detail as its help; a done row's chip (good, or
  caution - a few words, `RequestRow.chip`) and when it ended. Every word in it is one line, cut short in the cell, its
  whole the cell's help and in what VoiceOver hears.
- **Speed**: the rate measured here (`RequestWords.speed`, "244 KB/s"), a dash for none.
- **The buttons**: Cancel / Leave (Confirm before cancelling on asks first, in a dialog whose Keep it takes Return, so
  Return never cancels a download); Another source, or Same source again when there's no other (with Get albums), and
  the rest in a ••• beside it; a done row's Play and Open. Every action of a row is in its right-click and its
  VoiceOver actions too (Core's `RequestAction`). Play is `player.play(songs:album:at: 0)` in the click with nothing
  awaited, when `requests.plays(row)` has its songs, else Open's `requests.open(row)` - the phone's ▶ exactly.
- **The status bar**: "1 downloading", "2 waiting", "1 needs attention", "3 done" (each only when it is not 0) and the
  speed summed, while deadwax is reachable. "3 done" is a departure: the drawing counts the other three only.
- The edges as the phone has them: out of reach, a look that failed (the last rows still under it), downloads not
  kept track of, a spinner until the first answer, nothing yet.

**Core `RequestFilter.swift`** holds the rules, pure and tested on Linux:
- `RequestFilter` (all | active | done): each one's headings (Active is Downloading, Waiting and Needs attention -
  never Done), `shown(board)` (only the headings with rows), `lines(board)` (MacTable's lines), `count`, its empty
  words, and the status bar's words.
- `RequestFilter.rate(row)` is a row's speed only while it is downloading and not being cancelled; `speed(board)` sums
  those, so a finished job's last speed is never counted.
- `RequestCounts`, and `RequestColumns` (the drawing's widths, the album's least, the meter's least, the row and
  cover sizes, the buttons' words).
- (R8's review) `cancellable(key, in:)`, `RequestAction` (a row's actions: offered, its buttons, the •••'s rest),
  `RequestSpoken` (a row's and a card's words for VoiceOver, and the Mac's help), and `RequestTools` (the toolbar's
  three fits).

**Core `Requests.swift`**: RequestRow gains `from` (the peer, from the job's or the pending row's username), `speed`
(the measured rate, nil for 0), `progressWords` (what the Progress column says for a row that has no meter line of its
own) and `when` (a done row's age); and since the review `tries` ("2nd try") and `chip` (a done row's few words).
They come from what jobRow and pendingRow already read; nothing new is asked of deadwax. The phone draws none of them
(VoiceOver reads `tries`).

**MacPalette** gains the column list's four (`columnsFace`, `columnsRule`, `rowStripe`, `groupRowFace`), and since
the review the cover's edge (`coverEdge`, dw.css's `.cover` border), each with its `// dw:` rule.

### The phone: the drawing's cards (`RequestsScreen`, `RequestCards`)

- iOS's own bar, with Clear done in it over the large title "Requests" - not the app's PhoneTop (below).
- Search Soulseek… (A1's row) first, in the accent's colour on its hairline, only with Get albums and dimmed while
  deadwax is out of reach.
- The headings (.row.grp: 38 tall at least, the words at the foot, semibold, a header for VoiceOver), each only over
  rows (`RequestFilter.all.shown`).
- Downloading and Waiting are PhoneCards: cover, title, line, the **DWMeter** and the progress line in mono ("3 of 11
  files · 244 KB/s", the row's own `data`), beside the round ✕ (DWRaised on a Circle, 32 pt face in a 44 pt target).
  The ✕ asks first in its card with Confirm before cancelling on, as before.
- Needs attention's cards keep their two ways (Another source · N left, Same source again), as DWButtonStyle buttons
  that fill the card, and the reason in red with its detail folded under it. A pair of buttons stands side by side
  while both fit, and one over the other otherwise, each then across the card on up to 3 lines at the accessibility
  sizes (`ButtonWords`).
- Done rows: cover, title, line and chip, the round ▶ (`SharpSymbol(.play)` on the purple circle) and the row's tap
  opening the album, on the row rule. The ▶ plays in the tap as before; a manual search's Done row still opens its
  album (A2).
- Everything else is square (DWCorners' phone half is Corners' 0, the meter's included); the ✕ and the ▶ are the only
  round things.

### DWMeter (`App/Look/DWMeter.swift`)

dw.css's `.meter`, on both devices: a sunken track (the well, its inner shade, a 1 pt line) with the fill inside its
1 pt edge, in plain, marked (the default, the accent) or good. Its fill is `DWLook.meterShare(fraction)` of the track -
0 to 1, 0 for NaN - so it never passes it. Its height is DWLook's `meterHeight` (6 on the Mac, 8 on the phone), grown
with the text size on the phone. Its corners are `DWCorners.meter` / `meterFill`: 2 and 1 on the Mac, Corners' track
and fill (0) on the phone. It animates only without Reduce Motion, and VoiceOver skips it (the line beside it is read).

### Decisions, and where this departs from the plan

- **DWCorners gained `meter` and `meterFill`** (and their shapes), though plan 3.5 says App/Look gains only new files
  after R1b: the meter's Mac corners (2, 1) aren't any of the three R1 made, and the phone's must be Corners' like the
  rest. The edit is additive; test_ios_mac_look, test_ios_phone_look and test_ios_palette's
  `test_the_looks_phone_corners_are_corners` count five now.
- **The phone keeps iOS's navigation bar.** The drawing's large title is PhoneTop/PhoneBigTitle's, which needs iOS's
  bar hidden, and test_ios_palette's `test_the_librarys_top_sits_under_the_status_bar` (R2's) allows that only on the
  Library. The title and Clear done are iOS's large title and bar button for now.
- **The app's words, not the drawing's**: "Another source · N left" and "Same source again" (the web's, held by
  RequestsVectorTests) rather than "Next peer · 2 left" and "Ask again". The buttons column is the drawn 240 since the
  review, holding one of them and a ••• (below).
- **The phone's manual search is A1's row**, as the plan says, not the drawing's inline Artist and Album fields.
- **The ▶ stays purple** (phonePrimaryFace): the drawing's grey `.key` would need the key colours, which only
  MacPalette has.
- The phone's heading is `Typeface.subheadline` (15), since `Typeface.Phone` has no 15; a done row's title is 16, not
  the drawing's inherited 17.
- "Up Next" was in no string literal of RequestCards or RequestsScreen (a comment only), so nothing changed for the
  Queue rule.
- The "Requests bar test" the brief named isn't in test_ios_palette.py: the old card drew the Downloads screen's
  `DownloadBar`, which no palette test covered, and which Downloads still draws (R9's). The palette function edited
  is the look's phone corners test, for the two new corners.
- test_ios_mac.py's `SHEET_ROOTS` (a constant, not a function) names MacRequestsPage's one sheet, and
  test_ios_manual_search's builds name its one `GetRelease.manual`.

### Left out

- Other sources on a downloading row (James: "just leave it out").
- The drawing's Files, Other sources and Log tabs: no route gives what they show.
- "slskd connected" in the status bar: nothing tells the app.
- A done row's speed: deadwax keeps none once a job ends.

### Tests, and the faults they were seen failing on

**Core RequestFilterTests** (12): the filters' headings, a heading only over rows, the table's lines and stripes, the
counts, the speed (downloading rows alone), a row's speed words, the status bar, From / progress / when, the columns,
the buttons' words, the meter's share and its heights.

**tests/test_ios_requests_look.py** (12): DWMeter is dw.css's `.meter` (track, fill, edge, heights, corners per
device); its fill never passes its track; round stays round (two Circles: the ✕ and the ▶) and the rest is square; the
cards say what the drawing says; every heading has rows; every play is in the tap; the Mac's table, toolbar and status
bar are the drawing's; what no route gives is left out; no value of Requests' own; "Up Next" is the Queue.

Also touched: test_ios_phone_look (DWMeter among the look's parts, its fixed frames, the corners, Requests as the
first screens drawing the look's and the phone's pieces), test_ios_mac_look (the corners and DWLook's field count),
test_ios_mac_reach (the Requests root), test_ios_manual_search, test_ios_mac's SHEET_ROOTS, test_ios_palette's corners.

The plan's five mutations, and two more, were each applied alone, run and restored byte for byte. Every one was caught:
- Active including Done: RequestFilterTests `allShowsEveryHeadingActiveNeverDoneAndDoneAlone`,
  `theCountsAreEachHeadingsAndEachFiltersRows`, `theTablesLinesAreEachHeadingThenItsRows`;
- a finished job's speed counted: `theSpeedIsTheDownloadingRowsAloneNeverAFinishedOnes`,
  `aRowsSpeedIsTheDataLinesRateOrADash`, `theStatusBarSaysEachHeadingsCountThenTheSpeed`;
- a heading over an empty group (Core's `shown`): `aHeadingIsShownOnlyOverRows`; and the phone's list drawn from
  `sections` instead: `test_every_heading_has_rows_under_it`;
- a fill past its track (DWMeter's share unclamped): `test_a_meters_fill_never_passes_its_track`; and Core's
  `meterShare` with no ceiling: `aMetersFillNeverPassesItsTrack`;
- the ✕ squared (its DWRaised on a Rectangle): `test_round_stays_round_and_the_rest_is_square`.

### Not verified - checks 570 to 573

- Neither half has been seen on a screen: only the builds and the tests.
- Whether the meters, the files and the speeds match slskd's own as a download runs.
- On the Mac: the table's sideways scroll on a narrow window, a double click on a done row, the Cancel dialog's Return keeping the download,
  and Choose a source opening from the toolbar.
- On the phone: the large title and Clear done over the new cards, the meter growing with the text size, and
  Needs attention's and the cancel question's buttons stacking and wrapping at AX5. The page's ground is the dark
  system background, as on the other tabs, not the drawing's `--bg`.
- On the Mac (the review's): the toolbar's three fits at 1280, 880 and with a side panel open; the table with no
  sideways scroll at 1280; ↑ ↓ and Return in the table; the right-click and the •••; VoiceOver reading a row as one,
  with its actions; the cut words' help.

### After review (2026-11-25)

The review found seven things; each is fixed, with a test or a mutation that was seen to catch it.

1. **The Mac's Cancel dialog acted on a stale row.** The dialog kept the row it asked over and cancelled that, after
   the download might have moved on to being filed. Now the confirm passes the row's key, `confirmed(key)` looks the
   live row up with Core's `RequestFilter.cancellable(key, in: board)` (a job downloading or waiting whose cancel is
   `.ready`, else nil) and cancels only that. `onChange(of: board)` lets the question go once its row isn't ready. The
   phone's `cancelNow` does the same. deadwax's route takes any job, so the guard is the app's; the server's own is
   being fixed on main separately.
2. **The phone at the accessibility sizes.** DWButtonStyle's `.lineLimit(1)` cut "Another source · 2 left" at AX5,
   and the cancel question's small buttons, not filling, ran past the card. Card buttons now take their words through
   `ButtonWords`, whose own limit is `isAccessibilitySize ? 3 : 1` (the innermost limit wins over the style's).
   `ButtonPair` draws its buttons as `buttons(stacked)`, so stacked ones fill (`fills: stacked`, or `fills: true` for
   Needs attention as before). DWButtonStyle is unchanged.
3. **The Progress column spilled** past its 206 (226 less the cell's 10 either side): "12 of 12 files · adding to your
   library…" (a meter's line had `.fixedSize()`) and a done row's whole sentence in a chip. Every word there is
   `.lineLimit(1)`, giving way before the meter (which keeps `RequestColumns.meterLeast`, 48) or the chip. Each kind of
   row's whole words are the cell's `.help` and in its VoiceOver label. A done row's chip is Core's
   `RequestWords.chipWords`: "In your library", "Added to their library", "Partly in your library", "Not added", "You
   already had it", "Stopped" and the like, the longest about 159 pt.
4. **The page didn't fit.** At 320 the buttons column made the table's least 1082, wider than 1060 (a 1280 window, less
   the sidebar's 220), and the toolbar's 862 or so overran an 880 window's 660.
   - **The buttons column is the drawn 240**: the row's main action alone (Cancel / Leave; Another source, else Same
     source again; Play and Open), and a ••• pop-up with the rest (Same source again beside Another source). The
     table's least is 1002, so it fits 1060.
     - This was chosen over narrower words because the app's words stay: "Another source · 99 left" with the ••• is
       about 236 by the test's estimate.
     - It was chosen over dropping the second way on because both stay a click away, in the ••• and the right-click.
   - **The toolbar is a `ViewThatFits` of three** (Core's `RequestTools.Fit`):
     - **full** (about 862): the label, 170 and 210 fields;
     - **compact** (about 637, inside 880's 660): no label, 120 and 140 fields;
     - **folded** (about 448, inside the 589 a 1280 window leaves beside the side panel's column): the filter and Clear
       done in one pop-up named "Show" for VoiceOver, its value the filter.
     - Every control is in each. Under 1280 the side panel is a drawer lying over the page (DesktopFrame's, not
       changed here), so the page keeps its width and its toolbar.
5. **A row wasn't one VoiceOver element.** Each Mac row, and each phone card (a download's, a refused one's, a done
   row), is `.accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)` now.
   - Its label is Core's `RequestSpoken` (everything it shows: title, artist, from, progress, speed or the reason, who
     asked, which try). For whoever runs deadwax the error's own words are in it, and "tell whoever runs deadwax" for
     everyone else.
   - Its actions are its buttons', named in the app's words (Cancel or Leave, Another source, Same source again, Play,
     Open). They use `.accessibilityActions { ForEach }`, the looping form of `accessibilityAction(named:)`.
   - A done row's default action opens it. The phone's cancel question, while it asks, stays its own group under the
     card.
6. **The nits.**
   - The Mac's table takes ↑ ↓ Home End and Return through Platform's new `listKeys` (the Mac's half
     `onKeyPress(keys:)`, the iPhone's `self`), into R1's `MacTable.moved` and `MacTable.returned`. Return opens a done
     row, as a double click does.
   - A filter that hides the selected row lets it go.
   - Who asked and which try are the album cell's help (and VoiceOver's). Leave's help is its label and who asked ("Asked by you
     and Ethan"), the reason it leaves rather than cancels.
   - The cover has `.cover`'s 1 px border (`MacPalette.coverEdge`, on a chip's 3 pt corners).
   - The toolbar's fields have an order (`.tabs($focused, in: Self.order)`), and Return in Artist moves to Album.
   - "N done" in the status bar is named a departure (above).
7. **For R9, left as is:** You > Getting albums' `RequestWords.confirmCancelNote`, "The ✕ on a download in Requests
   asks first", is wrong on the Mac now, where the table's button says Cancel. Its words are R9's Settings'.

**New words, none in the fixtures:**
- the chip's, listed in 3;
- `RequestRow.tries` (Core's existing `tryText`);
- the spoken joins.

They're Core's and reach no words fixture (DeviceWordsTests lists its keys), so iphone.json and mac.json still have no
diff.

**Platform** gained `listKeys` and `ListKey` (the gate's one file outside App/Mac besides the Requests ones).

**Two shared test functions were edited:**
- test_ios_mac's `test_platform_is_the_iphones_exactly_as_before_on_the_iphone` lists the new helper.
- `test_tab_moves_between_the_fields_and_return_in_one_never_applies`'s TABS names the page.

`test_a_right_click_is_the_menus_own_items` gained `REQUEST_ROWS`: the Requests row's right-click is RequestAction's
list, the one its buttons and ••• partition, not QueueMenuItems.

**Tests since the review:**
- **Core RequestFilterTests** (19) adds:
  - the table fits the window as it opens;
  - the toolbar's fits;
  - a cancel that asked acts on the row as it is now;
  - each row offers what its buttons do, in the app's words;
  - a row is read as one;
  - a refusal's "tell whoever runs deadwax" only for everyone else;
  - the done chip's few words.
- **test_ios_requests_look.py** (19) adds:
  - a card's buttons at the accessibility sizes;
  - a cancel that asked acts on the live row;
  - nothing in the Progress column draws past it;
  - the table and the toolbar's widths, added up from Core's numbers and the words' lengths at 0.55 em, an
    estimate from above;
  - the fields' Tab and Return;
  - the table's keys;
  - a row is one element.

## The redesign, slice R5: an album, Playlists, a playlist (2026-11-25)

An album's page, Playlists and a playlist's page in the new look on both devices: mac-redesign-build.md "#### R5", drawn
in Album.dc.html, Playlists.dc.html and Playlist.dc.html (the Mac) and iAlbum.dc.html and iPlaylist.dc.html (the
phone). **No new server data**: DeadwaxClient and Core's Routes have no diff, and neither do the album's and the
playlist's models, their asks, the engine files or R3b's and R4's files. The app is still 0.13 (13), and no words
fixture key changed (iphone.json and mac.json have no diff).

### The Mac: three pages of its own

The Mac pages are the phone's pages' desks (R2's pattern): `AlbumView<Desk>` and `PlaylistView<Desk>` keep their
model, their asks, their writes and their leaving, and on the Mac draw `desk(...)` in their List's place; on the iPhone
there is no desk (`init(route:)`, `Desk == EmptyView`), so the phone's page is the one it was, restyled. MacAlbum's
`page(for:)` hands `MacAlbumPage.init(desk:)` and `MacPlaylistPage.init(desk:)`, and MacLibraryDesk gains `.playlists`
(LibraryView hands the desk to Playlists whatever the side, playlists being no scope's).

- **`App/Mac/Album/MacAlbumPage.swift`**, given `AlbumDesk` (AlbumView's model, the download, what plays, the offline
  and gone flags, the note, the library line, its ••• request, Edit, Play, Shuffle, play-from-a-song, a row's request,
  the mine block's change, Refresh and the download's "asked" for VoiceOver's end word):
  - **The toolbar** (MacToolbar, `ViewThatFits`): Play (pri, the sharp glyph) and Shuffle, a groove, Add to Queue, Add to
    a playlist…, Download, then Edit at the right for someone Managing.albumEdit shows it to. It fits every page down
    to the one beside the side panel's column (R5's review: the first write-up said it folded there - it doesn't);
    folded, should a long download state in the pop-up ever make it too wide, everything after Shuffle is the album's
    ••• - QueueMenu on the album's request, the right-click's own items (Download and Edit album among them).
  - **Download**: the arrow state's `DownloadWords.controlLabel` as a button (`downloads.download(album:)`, then
    `asked()`); once asked for, a DWPopUp whose section is headed `AlbumDownloadMenu.title` with its items - the
    phone's control's states in words.
  - **The hero**: the cover (132), the title (h1), the artist at the Mac's h3 in `acc` (a link while there is one to go
    to), the meta line, `MacAlbumFacts.played` ("Played yesterday · 12 times", against a `now` re-read at a day's
    change), the badge and the download chip ("On this Mac" or the album line), the mine block, and the quiet lines.
    A right-click on it is the album's menu (`.macContextMenu { QueueMenuItems(request: menu) }`).
  - **The songs**: R2's MacColumnList, columns # 46, Title, Plays 70, Length 66 and ••• 44; the box as tall as its rows
    while there is room (`.frame(minHeight: least, maxHeight: tall)`, `least` three rows clamped to `tall`,
    `.layoutPriority(1)`), scrolling inside it after. # is the song's own number (`AlbumPageLines.number`), a ▶ for the
    song the player has; **a disc's heading row** (`MacTable.Line.group`, MacColumnList's `lines:`, drawn as R2's group
    rows) above each disc's first song wherever the phone draws one - more than one disc, or a disc with a title -
    carrying the phone's words ("Disc 2 · Live at the Roundhouse", AlbumModel's `headings`, `MacAlbumFacts.songLines`).
    Plays is `MacAlbumFacts.plays` (blank for a nil, never 0). Return, a double-click or VoiceOver's action plays from
    the row (`desk.playFrom`), a right-click is the song's menu (`SongRightClick`).
  - **Properties** (MacGroupBox on `bg`, two columns): `MacAlbumFacts.properties` - Released, Added, Format, Size (only
    when every song says its own), and Album info's own folder row - "Folder" or "Folders", by `AlbumInfo.server`'s
    rule (`folders: server.access.isAdmin`), from the model's bridge answer or, when the model has none (logins off,
    break-glass: AlbumModel asks the bridge only for a personal library), the same `client.storeAlbum` the page asks
    itself for an admin.
  - **The status bar**: `MacAlbumFacts.status` - the songs, the length, the size.
  - The waiting states as the phone's: nothing yet, a failure with Try again, the note, a spinner.
- **`App/Mac/Album/MacPlaylistPage.swift`**, given `PlaylistDesk` (now with `canEdit`): the toolbar (Play, Shuffle, the
  groove, Add to Queue, Add to a playlist…, Download - `PlaylistDownloadMenuSection(titled: true)` in a DWPopUp once
  asked for, else a button for a playlist that isn't smart - and Edit, dimmed without `canEdit`; folded, the
  playlist's •••); the hero (the mosaic at 96, the name, `MacAlbumFacts.playlistLine` - whose and when it changed - the
  read-only words, the comment, chips for the songs, the length and On this Mac, the hero line); the songs edge to edge
  under a rule, columns # 46, Title, Album 190, Length 66, a row's open being `desk.playRow(index)`. Every waiting
  state is the phone page's (OpenFailedNote and RefreshFailedNote are internal now for it).
- **`App/Mac/Library/MacPlaylistsPage.swift`**: columns Playlist, Songs 64, Length 84, Whose 110, Changed 110 and On this
  Mac 110 (Core's `MacAlbumFacts.playlistColumns` - narrower than the drawing's 80/110/130/140/150, see "After
  review"), Whose and Changed left out on a page too narrow for Playlist's 160 beside them all; rows yours, then
  shared, then files (`PlaylistRules.groups` of `found`), offline with no list the downloaded shelf. A selection that
  rests 200 ms has its playlist asked for as its page asks (a PlaylistPageModel with `stored` and `heard`), so the
  toolbar's Play and Shuffle play it in the click with its songs in hand (`player.play(playlist:at:shuffle:)`) - only
  the playlist selected now, and only while its row is listed (the selection let go at the page when it isn't). The toolbar: New playlist… (pri; the phone's sheet in `.macSheet()`, its
  `PlaylistEdit.made`), the groove, Play, Shuffle, and Find in playlists (230). A row's right-click is
  `PlaylistRightClick`. The list's failure is said inline (`PlaylistWords.listFailed` - the phone's ListFailedNote is
  private to PlaylistsScreen). The status bar is `MacAlbumFacts.playlistsStatus` of the rows listed (Find's), nothing
  while none is.

**Core `MacAlbumFacts.swift`** holds the rules, pure and tested on Linux: `lineID`/`songLines`, `plays`,
`playedWords`/`played`/`playedRow`, `size`, `properties`, `added`, `status`, `whose`, `changed`, `playlistLine`,
`playlistsStatus`, `PlaylistColumn`/`playlistWidth`/`playlistLeast`/`playlistDropped`/`playlistColumns`/`fixedWidth`/
`playlistTitle`, `length`, and the pages' words. The day's words are R2's `ArtistTotals.lastPlayedWords`, never a
second set. **Album info** gains the Played row on the Mac only: `AlbumInfo.local(..., played:)` puts it last, and
AlbumInfoView passes `MacAlbumFacts.playedRow` with its own midnight `now` (check 555: the page and Info never
disagree). On the iPhone Album info is as it was.

**The brief's seven mutations** (eight runs - Download was taken off the phone's ••• and the Mac's toolbar apart) were
each applied alone, run and restored byte for byte. Every one was caught:
- a nil play count shown as "0": `aNilPlayCountIsABlankNeverNought`;
- the size ignoring a song without one (a disc missing from it): `theSizeIsEveryDiscsOrNone`, and Properties' and the
  status bar's tests;
- "yesterday" by elapsed hours, not the calendar: `playedIsTheCalendarsDayAcrossMidnight`, and the Played line's and
  Album info's row's tests;
- Play inside a `Task { await … }`: `test_every_play_is_an_existing_call_in_the_tap`;
- `offersDownload = false` on the album's •••, and Download taken off the Mac's toolbar:

## The Mac's Row Size (2026-11-25)

James, after R5 left the Mac's rows at R2's 30 with a 20 cover ("For James: left as they are" above): "I need
something on mac to resize the row height". Still app 0.13 (13); no server change, no new route, nothing on the phone.

**His two choices.**

1. **Where: View > Row Size**, as Music and Finder do it - a submenu of **Small**, **Medium** and **Large**, the one in
   use ticked, and **⌘+** / **⌘−** a size at a time, stopping at the ends with the item that can't step dimmed. ⌘+ is
   drawn as Finder draws Make Bigger, and works typed as ⌘⇧= or ⌘= on a US keyboard. Kept on this Mac alone, as the
   Mac keeps its sidebar's side and Grid or List.
2. **The sizes**: Small 30 with a 20 cover (today's, and the default), Medium 40 with 28 (the drawings'), Large 52 with
   40. The words keep their size, centred in the row; the header strip (24) and a heading's row (26) never change.
   Requests: Small its drawing's 34 (a cover and a meter in it), Medium 40, Large 52; its cover 22, 28, 40.

### Core: `MacRowSize` (`DeadwaxCore/MacRowSize.swift`, beside MacLook)

- `small`, `medium`, `large`; `standard` (Small) and `init(saved:)` - an unknown or missing saved value reads as Small;
  `storageKey` `deadwax-mac-row-size`.
- `rowHeight` (Small is `MacLook.rowHeight`, never a copy of it; 40, 52) and `cover` (20, 28, 40);
  `requestRowHeight` and `requestCover` (Small is `RequestColumns.rowHeight` 34 and `.cover` 22, Medium and Large
  every list's own).
- `bigger` and `smaller`, nil at their ends.
- `boxHeight(rows:headings:)` and `boxLeast(rows:headings:)`: the album page's songs box as R5 added it up - the header,
  each row at this size, each heading at its own 26, the edge's 2; at least the header and three rows, or the whole
  box when that is shorter. (After review) `boxLeast(rows:headings:room:)` holds that least to the room the page has
  left (never below 0; nil, unmeasured, leaves it as it is), and `boxRoom(page:around:)` is that room - the page's
  height less what's around the box, nil while the page is unmeasured (0).
- `coverGrowth` and `requestCoverGrowth`: how much wider the cover is than Small's. Playlists' Playlist and Requests'
  Album keep that on top of their least (`MacAlbumFacts.playlistLeast(_:)` 160/168/180,
  `RequestColumns.albumLeast(_:)` 160/166/178), so the name keeps the room it has at Small.
  `MacAlbumFacts.playlistColumns(width:size:)` and `RequestColumns.width/widths(_:size:)` take the size, defaulting to
  Small, so R5's and R8's callers and tests read as before.
- **The menu, in MacMenu**: `Command`'s `smallRows`, `mediumRows`, `largeRows`, `biggerRows` and `smallerRows`;
  `Command.rowSizes` and `Command.rowSize`; `State.rowSize`; `MacMenu.rowSize(_:)`, the submenu's two sections;
  `MacMenu.rowSize(after:from:)`, the size an item leaves the rows at; `Words.rowSize` "Row Size", "Small", "Medium",
  "Large", "Make Bigger", "Make Smaller"; `key` ⌘+ (`.character("+")`) and ⌘- (`.character("-")`), the three sizes
  none; `alternateKey`, ⌘= for Make Bigger alone. A size is always enabled and ticked while it's the size; a step is
  enabled while there is a size to step to. **The menu's items are never dimmed for a sheet, the sign-in or Now
  Playing**: they change only how tall rows are, and act on nothing under a sheet. (After review) `MacMenu.choose(_:saved:)`:
  an item's click from what's kept - the size it leaves the rows at and the value to keep, nil for a step with no
  further to go or another menu's command; a garbage kept value steps from Small.

### The App

- **`App/Mac/Components/MacRowSizing.swift`**: the environment's `macRowSize` (default Small). **DesktopFrame** hands
  the kept choice down once, `.environment(\.macRowSize, MacRowSizeStore.shared.size)`, so every list under the frame
  changes together. A sheet is a window of its own on the Mac, outside the frame, so it reads the key's default,
  Small (no sheet draws a Mac list today, so nothing shows it).
- **`MacRowSizeStore`** (after review; at MacCommands' end, beside TextEditing and MacRefresh): the one place the size is
  read and changed - `@MainActor @Observable`, `shared`, `size`, reading UserDefaults under `MacRowSize.storageKey` as
  it opens (`MacRowSize(saved:)`: unknown reads as Small) and keeping each choice as it is made
  (`perform(_:)`, through `MacMenu.choose`). The frame, the menus' state and `perform`, and the hidden ⌘= key all read
  it, so a change by any of them redraws the menu's tick and every list at once. It replaced three `@AppStorage`s
  (the frame's, the Commands', the key's): a `Commands` reading `@AppStorage` was the one menu state not observed the
  way the others are, and the review asked whether the tick would follow a change made by ⌘+ or ⌘=.
- **The readers**: MacColumnList's row (`.frame(height: CGFloat(rowSize.rowHeight))`) - Albums and Artists in List, an
  album's songs, Playlists, a playlist's songs; MacAlbumsPage's cover, MacArtistsPage's round picture and
  MacPlaylistsPage's cover (`rowSize.cover`); MacPlaylistsPage's columns (`playlistColumns(width:size:)`); MacAlbumPage's
  songs box (`rowSize.boxHeight` / `boxLeast`); MacRequestsPage's row, cover and table width
  (`requestRowHeight`, `requestCover`, `width/widths(_:size:)`). Requests' meter keeps its 6 and its words, centred
  in the taller row. MacPlaylistPage needed no change: its songs are MacColumnList's. The headings' rows, the header
  strip and the phone's `DWLook.here.rowHeight` are untouched.
- **(After review) The album page in a short window.** At 600 tall the page is 442 (600 less the title bar 28, the
  player bar 66, the toolbar 40 and the status bar 24); with its edges (20 + 16 + 18), the hero (132) and Properties
  (about 100-112), Large's least of 180 overflowed by 24 to 36, pushing Properties off the page. The least now shrinks
  to what's left: the page, the hero and Properties are measured (`onGeometryChange`, the page through the same
  `frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity, alignment: .topLeading)` MacPage already gives it, so nothing
  moves) and `boxLeast(..., room: boxRoom)` holds the least to the room. None of the three depends on the box, so
  there's no loop. At normal heights (the opening window's 820, a 662 page) the room is above every least and the
  page is as drawn. Shrinking the least was chosen over letting the page scroll: inside a page's scroll the box would
  be offered all the height it asks for, so a long album would scroll the whole page, not its box, at every height.
  MacRowSizeTests adds it up.
- **No Page Up/Down to add up**: MacColumnList and `Platform.listKeys` move by row (↑ ↓ Home End, ⌘↑ ⌘↓) and bring the
  selected row into view by its id, so nothing else counted rows. (After review) A size change moves the selected
  row too, so MacColumnList and Requests' table each bring it back (`onChange(of: rowSize)` beside their
  `onChange(of: selected)`, `proxy.scrollTo` by the same ids).
- **The menu** (`App/Shared/MacCommands.swift`): `CommandGroup(after: .toolbar)` - under Refresh, a Divider, then
  `Menu(MacMenu.Words.rowSize)`: the three as ticks (`tick`), a Divider, the two steps as buttons (`button`), all
  through MacMenu's items as every other item is. `perform` hands the click to `MacRowSizeStore.shared.perform` (the
  case sits before Save changes, which slice 7's test holds last). The menus' state reads `MacRowSizeStore.shared.size`.
- **⌘= (`RowSizeAlternateKey`, at MacCommands' end)**: a Mac menu item has one key, and the menu draws ⌘+, so ⌘= -
  the same key without ⇧ - is a hidden button on DesktopFrame: `keyboardShortcut(MacCommands.shortcut(MacMenu.alternateKey(.biggerRows)))`,
  dimmed at Large as the item is, (after review) `focusable(false)` so it's never a Tab stop with keyboard navigation
  on, 0 by 0, `opacity(0)` and `accessibilityHidden(true)` (VoiceOver reads the menu's item, never this). It's
  MacCommands' third key, the one file besides Platform allowed `keyboardShortcut`. **What answers where**: ⌘+ (⌘⇧=)
  and ⌘− are the menu's, and answer wherever the menu does; ⌘= is the main window's button, so it answers while that
  window is key. Whether ⌘= answers with a sheet up or before sign-in is unseen.
- **The keys were free.** No MacMenu item and nothing in Platform has +, - or =. The system's own ⌘+ and ⌘- are
  Format > Font > Bigger and Smaller (UIKitMacHelper's MainMenu.nib, read with `strings`), gone with Format's
  `CommandGroup(replacing: .textFormatting) {}` - the same evidence that let Info take Italic's ⌘I (slice 3). Catalyst's
  View has no zoom of its own. ⌘= is in no menu.
- **The words fixtures** (Fixtures/words, iphone.json and mac.json) are unchanged: DeviceWordsTests holds only words
  that say phone or iPhone and the words made from them, and MacMenu.Words has none.

## The redesign, slice R2b: the Library's top, one row again (2026-11-25)

James, the same day R2 landed: **"The top of the library on iOS is actually kinda a mess, can we streamline it a
bit?"** The design session redrew iLibrary, iArtists and iPlaylists (~/Desktop/Code/deadwax-plans/iphone-redesign.md,
"Changed 25 Nov: the Library's top is one row again", and a new block at the end of dw.css: `.ltop`, `.circ`, and
`.meta`'s `.views`, `.v` and `.scope`), James asked for one change to it - **"lets put the grid/list next to
yours/all"** - and approved it ("Send it").

What is his and what is the design session's:
- **His**: streamlining it; Grid and List beside Yours | All; and the row itself, which is his of 14 Nov ("let's put a
  magnifying glass button on the left side of the slider", "but the search button and options button at the top can
  be circles" - "The squared look").
- **The design session's**: no "Library" title and no strip of chips; Yours | All as two words with a hairline between
  them rather than a segmented control; keeping one quiet line under the row rather than putting everything in it;
  "white is where you are, purple is what a tap goes to"; Downloaded back in the •••.

Built on the ios branch's tip of the day, 8d1e841b (R2 b6f8dcfa, R4 e1e34d79, R5 8d1e841b); the worktree began at main
(7e26b69d), which has none of the redesign's phone slices. R3b has come onto the ios branch since (b57ded0f), after this
slice's base, and this slice was not rebased onto it: R3b changes test_ios_phone_look.py's PHONE_PIECES_DRAWN_IN block
(its R3B_PAGES) beside R2_LIBRARY's line, which this slice adds LibraryLine.swift to, so the merge conflicts there and
only there - the block wants the union of the two. The app is still 0.13 (13), `__version__` untouched, the word
fixtures unchanged.

### What was built

**The row** (LibraryTop.swift, iLibrary's `.ltop`): Find's circle 16 in from the leading edge, the •••'s 16 in from the
trailing one, and between them, 12 from each, the switch of the pages - DWSegmented `large`, one square sunken well of
equal segments, the page shown lit (`.seg.lg`), the pages in the order kept (Albums, Playlists, Artists on Yours;
Albums, Artists, Songs on All; all four with logins off). 52 tall at least, capped at xxxLarge as the bars are. Laid out
by a Layout of its own, `LibraryTopRow`, which measures its four views and places each where Core puts it
(`LibraryTopFit.row` and `.place`, held frame by frame in LibrarySwitchTests - since R2b's review; `lookPlace`, in
DWRaised.swift, places a view in Core's box): each circle centred where its 34 pt face is drawn (its 44 pt target
reaching 5 pt past it, into the 12 between it and the switch - never to it), the switch offered the room between.
Where the switch's equal segments need more than that room (`LibraryTopFit.folds` - each segment as wide as the widest
page's words), it goes onto a row of its own under the circles, as far in from each edge as they are: what it needs is
measured from a hidden `DWSegmentedNeed` of the same words in the same face, weight and room (DWSegmented.swift), placed
in the layout but never seen, touched or heard. VoiceOver reads the row as it is drawn (`LibraryTopFit.reading`): Find,
the switch, the •••; folded, Find and the ••• on the row before the switch under them - `accessibilitySortPriority` in a
container of the row's own, the fold read back from the need's and the row's widths as last laid out.

**The circles** (PhoneTop.swift's `PhoneCircleStyle`, for the Button and for the ••• Menu, whose label takes the
button style with `.menuStyle(.button)`): the look's raised face - `.btn`'s gradient, edge, sheen and label colour,
which `.circ`'s are, without `.btn`'s drop - drawn round with DWRaised, 34 pt in a 44 pt target, pressed turned over,
faded when it can't be used. Its face is a mark drawn at its size (FIXED in test_ios_phone_look.py, R1b's switch's
kind), its glyph Typeface.symbol(.body), growing to the row's cap.

**The line** (PhoneMeta, under the row on each page, as R2's was under the strip): 32 tall, 16 in at either side
(iLibrary's, iArtists' and iPlaylists' inline style - PhoneLook's `meta` and `metaTrail` are `drawn:` now), 13 pt, words
and bare glyphs. Albums: the count, then the order as a purple link with its caret; Artists the same; Playlists the count,
then New playlist… (it was at the line's end in R2); Songs its count. At its trailing end `LibraryLineEnd`
(LibraryLine.swift): Grid and List on Albums alone (Core's `LibraryLine.layouts`), two bare glyphs 28 square, 2 apart,
10 before Yours | All; then Yours | All where it shows - "Yours", a 1 pt hairline 12 tall (grown with the words,
@ScaledMetric), "All", 10 either side of it, the room inside each word's target.

Where all of it doesn't fit across, the line gives way inside itself first (R2b's review - Core's `MetaLine`): the
count's noun dropped (`MetaLine.short`: "2318 albums" "2318", "12 of 140 albums" "12 of 140"), VoiceOver still hearing
it in full (the short Text's label is the full words). Only where even that doesn't fit does its end fold onto a line of
its own under the words, at the trailing edge, the count in full again - the words wrapping there only should even the
short count need more than the line. The order's words and New playlist… are never shortened. PhoneMeta is a
`ViewThatFits(in: .horizontal)` of `MetaLine.Fit`'s four ways in their order (`full`, `short`, `folded`,
`foldedShort`), each a `PhoneMetaLine` Layout whose ideal width is `MetaLine.width` and whose two ends go where
`MetaLine.place` puts them: the choice is measured as drawn, in whatever face and size the line is in - Libre Franklin,
when it comes, moves where the line gives way, never whether it cuts a word. (`PhoneLook.metaFolds` and `PhoneMetaFold`,
R2b's first fold, went with it.)

**White and purple** - one rule, dw.css's (`.v` the accent, `.v.on` white; `.scope > b` white and semibold, the other
word a `.link`): the layout shown and the side shown are DWPalette.text (#fff), the other of each DWPalette.acc; the
side shown is semibold. The count keeps the line's third colour. Both read as selected to VoiceOver.

**The •••**: Shuffle, Downloaded, Refresh, Edit order (Core's `LibraryMenu.topSections`, `LibraryMenuItem.downloaded`).

### What moved, and what went

- The titled top: PhoneTop's `title`, PhoneLook's `titledTop`, `titledTopSide` and `titledTopTracking`, Typeface.Phone's
  `topTitle` (28, iLibrary's old inline style) - gone; PhoneTop's other users (Now Playing's sheet) never had a title.
- The strip: `LibraryStrip` and `LibraryStripItem` (Core) gone, and PhoneStrip back to R1b's (5123bab3's) - its
  `pushes`, R2's review's, was for Downloaded alone; Now Playing's sheet, its one user, never passed it.
- Downloaded: from the strip's last chip to the •••, where it was before R2 - with, while the Albums page is Downloaded
  itself, the way back to the albums in its place.
- Yours | All: from the top's DWSegmented to the end of each page's line, as two words (`LibrarySideChoice`, handed to
  each page by LibraryView only where `sides` is true).
- Grid and List: from DWToggleStyle's boxes (`.tog.sm`) to bare glyphs; DWToggleStyle's phone half is drawn nowhere
  now (the Mac's Shuffle and Repeat keep the style).

**Downloaded, the chip against the old •••.** They behaved the same, so the ••• item is the old one again: each
`navigation.open(.downloaded)`, pushed on the tab's path; each gone while the Albums page is Downloaded, where the old
••• (5123bab3's "places" section, `albumsPage == .downloaded ? .albums(scope) : .downloaded`) had the way back to the
albums and R2's ••• kept that way back. The only differences were the drawing: the old •••'s item had the download
symbol (DownloadWords.downloadSymbol) and the chip none, and the chip was a button VoiceOver heard after the strip's tab
bar. The item has the symbol again.

### Kept (today's behaviour)

The pager's swipe and `show`/`scrolled`; a segment's tap moving the pager as the chip's did (`.snappy`, none under
Reduce Motion); Find's circle opening its field under the row, with Cancel, each page keeping its own words; the pull to
shuffle; the letter index; TopClearance and its probe, byte for byte; each page's order menu and the layout, kept per
device; Yours | All's `choose` (the side kept, and on All the collection's Shuffle asked ahead), `LibraryPages.sides`
with R2's review's offline fix (a chosen All stays All while deadwax is out of reach); Edit order; VoiceOver's words
("Library pages", "More for the Library", "Your library or all music", Grid, List), and the Large Content Viewer on the
two circles.

### Fitting, by arithmetic (test_ios_library_look.py)

Measured in the bundled faces' own advances (the test reads the TTFs' hmtx), at Apple's footnote and body sizes, on 375
pt (an SE, a 13 mini) - the row and the line are capped at xxxLarge, so the accessibility sizes draw as it does. R2b
measured in Noto Sans; **re-measured in Libre Franklin** when the fonts commit was rebased onto R2b (25 Nov, through
tests/ios_fonts.py, the one place every fit test takes a width from): the numbers below are Libre Franklin's, Noto
Sans's beside them where they moved, and two ways in the tables changed, marked.
- **The row** leaves the switch 251 pt (375 - 2 x (16 + 34 + 12)). Three pages need 3 x the widest + 2: 172.2 at the
  standard size (Noto Sans 169.5), 250.8 at xxxLarge (246.9) - never folded, but with 0.2 pt left at xxxLarge by the
  advances' sum (CoreText's kerning draws "Playlists" 0.6% narrower: 1.8 pt). Four pages (logins off, the break-glass
  sign-in) need 229.0 at the standard size (225.4) and fold from xLarge, as before (263.9; 259.8); folded they have
  343, and need 333.7 at xxxLarge (328.5).
- **The line** has 343 pt on 375, 361 on 393 (a 16), 370 on James's 402 (a 17 Pro). Songs', Artists' and Playlists'
  hold one line at the standard size and at xLarge on 375, a four-figure find dropping its noun at xLarge. Albums' with
  Yours | All is the fullest: "140 albums · Artist" (the default order) is one line on all three; the review's "140
  albums · Recently added" is 352 of 343 on 375 (Noto Sans 351), so it is drawn "140 · Recently added" (305.2; 302.7).
  At the standard size - F one line, S the count's noun dropped, f folded, on 375 / 393 / 402:

  | count | Artist | Recently added | Year, newest first |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | 140 albums | F F F | S F F | S S F |
  | 2318 albums | F F F | S F F | S S S |
  | 12 of 140 albums | F F F | S S S | f S S |
  | 12 of 2318 albums | F F F | f S S | f S S |
  | 1234 of 2318 albums | S F F | **f f S** (Noto Sans f S S) | f f f |

  and at xLarge:

  | count | Artist | Recently added | Year, newest first |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | 140 albums | F F F | S S S | **f S S** (Noto Sans S S S) |
  | 2318 albums | F F F | S S S | f S S |
  | 12 of 140 albums | S F F | f f S | f f f |
  | 12 of 2318 albums | S S F | f f f | f f f |
  | 1234 of 2318 albums | S S S | f f f | f f f |

  So at the standard size a library's count never folds the line on any of the three, under any order; on 402 Find's
  first keystroke folds it only for a four-figure find under the longest order, and on 393 for a four-figure find under
  "Recently added" and "Year, oldest first" too (Libre Franklin's "Recently added"; "Year, oldest first" folded there in
  Noto Sans as well - this paragraph said only the longest order before); on 375 it still folds it for a find under
  "Year, newest first", and in a four-figure library under "Recently added" or "Year, oldest first" (never under
  "Artist" or "Title") - the 32 pt drop the review saw, left there
  (dropping Find's "of 2318" too would say less than Find means: James's to choose). Counts are Core's own, without a
  thousands separator ("2318", not "2,318"). R2b's first write-up said "on James's 402 pt iPhone 17 Pro it fits, 370 of
  room": it had checked "Recently added" alone - "1,234 albums · Year, newest first" was 374 of 370 - and the line
  folded at the standard size on all three phones.
- At xxxLarge every page but Songs folds; folded, each end fits its own line (Albums' 175.6; Noto Sans 173.7) and no
  word of the line is wider than it, so a wrap never cuts one.
- In Libre Franklin every piece measured here (the pages' names and Yours | All in SemiBold and Regular, the orders,
  the counts in full and short, New playlist…, the dot) was laid out by CoreText with the bundled faces at or under its
  sum of advances, so the arithmetic is the wider of the two.

### Departures from the drawing

- **List is `list.bullet`**, not the drawing's three bare lines: the app's own List glyph everywhere else
  (LibraryModel.switchSymbol, R2's toggle, the old •••'s Show as list), and the three lines are Edit order's
  (`line.3.horizontal`) in the same Library's •••.
- **No `.circ.on`**: SwiftUI's Menu gives its label no state while its menu is open, and iOS's own menu presentation
  marks the button it came from.
- **The folds** - the switch under the circles, a line's end under its words - and the count without its noun are
  nowhere in the drawing, which is drawn at one width and one text size; they are what "fit 375 pt at every size
  without clipping" asks.
- **The circles' face stays 34 pt** at every text size (James's 14 Nov circles were 36 and fixed too); their glyph grows
  to the row's cap. Grown, three pages would fold under them at xxxLarge.
- **The side shown is a button** that does nothing (the drawing's `<b>`): so VoiceOver reads the pair as one choice
  with the side shown selected, as R2's segmented control read.
- **`.views`' 10 pt margin only before Yours | All**: the drawing always has Yours | All after Grid and List; without a
  library of your own nothing follows them.
- The switch's lit segment doesn't slide between pages (James's 14 Nov switch's did, R2's strip didn't).

### Targets

The circles' and the switch's targets end 4 pt above the row's foot. The line's reach 6 pt above it, but the line is at
the top of the pager, a scroll view, which takes no touch above itself - so nothing meets, and above the line its
targets are cut to the line's edge, as R2's were under the strip (assumed from UIScrollView's hit-testing; not tried on
a phone).

### After review (25 Nov)

The review found the line folding at the standard size in ordinary use ("Fitting, by arithmetic"), twelve mutations the
whole suite passed, VoiceOver's order wrong under a folded row, and two errors in this write-up (the 402 pt claim; R3b
"unmerged"). James had meanwhile approved a newer design (iphone-redesign.md, "Changed 25 Nov: the phone is flat": the
circles bare glyphs, the well words over a line), slice R1c, which starts from this one - so the fix touches only what
survives it: behaviour, layout and tests. The circles' and the well's faces are as R2b drew them.
- The line gives way inside itself first (`MetaLine`, "What was built").
- Where each view goes is Core's, not the Layouts': `LibraryTopFit.row`/`.place` and `MetaLine.place`, held frame by
  frame in LibrarySwitchTests (`theRowPutsFindLeadingTheMoreTrailingAndTheSwitchBetween`) and DWLookTests
  (`aQuietLinesEndsAreWhereTheyAreDrawn`); the two Layouts measure, ask and place, their bodies held exactly by
  test_ios_library_look.py. Each guards its count of views with an `assertionFailure` in Debug.
- VoiceOver's order under a folded row ("What was built"; `voiceOverReadsTheRowAsItIsDrawn`).
- The other mutations were of behaviour the Python tests held only by a substring: each is held exactly now - the
  action of each tap on the line, the one line `let sides = sideChoice`, openFind's body, DWSegmentedNeed's whole body,
  the Artists order Picker's binding - and nothing at the line's end may be `.disabled` or untouchable.

### For R1c

Left for the flat restyle, from the review:
- The switch's segments have no room inside them: `largeSegmentPadding` is 0 on the phone (dw.ph's `.seg.lg`), so at

- No Large Content Viewer on the segments; James's 14 Nov switch had one.
- No open state on the •••: the flat design draws it in the accent while its menu is open, and SwiftUI's Menu tells its

- The Mac's borrowed Songs page now draws DWSegmented's focusable Mac path.

Each mutated on its own, run, and put back byte for byte (sha256 checked). R2b's own:
