## The redesign, slice R7: Search, Get and Sources (2026-11-25)

The plan is ~/Desktop/Code/deadwax-plans/mac-redesign-build.md 3.4, "R7 - Search, Get and Sources", and the drawings
Search, Get (the Mac), iSearch, iGet and iSources in ~/Desktop/Code/deadwax-plans/mac-redesign/. Built on 31cab12d (R1c,
the phone flat), then - after its review - rebased onto 5f2f6065 (R6), whose MacListKeys.pressed, MacTable.opens and
MacTable.stripes it now uses in place of its own. The app is still 0.13 (13); `__version__`, the word fixtures
(iphone.json, mac.json), Core's DeadwaxClient and Routes, and the engine files untouched.

### What each page became

**Search** (SearchScreen.swift, Mac/Search/MacSearchPage.swift). SearchScreen keeps every ask, stand-down and resume
it made (the field, `shown`, `standDown`, `resumed`, the tab's and the stack's and Now Playing's moves) and draws its
list as `SearchContent` - the hint, the gate words, the All view or a kind view, as before. It is generic over a
`desk` (AlbumView's way): MacSearch.root() hands it `MacSearchPage`, which draws the toolbar, the table's header and
the status bar round that very SearchContent; the phone (and every caller without a desk) draws `phone`.
- The phone, iSearch.dc.html: flat on the page's black (`DWPalette.page`) under iOS's large title. **The field** (R7's
  review) is the look's, iSearch's `.well.sfield`, where `.searchable`'s rounded box was: a `safeAreaInset` at the
  list's top (so it stays as the list scrolls, on the page's black), 40 tall, 12 in and 16 from the page's edges, 10
  above the strip (`SearchLook.field`, `fieldInside`, `side`, `fieldFoot` - dw `.sfield`'s height, padding and margin),
  square, DWWell under it (its edge the accent while it has the keyboard - `DWWell(focused:)`, R1c's typing rule's
  WELL), the magnifying glass in t3 (`fieldGap` 8), the words Typeface.Look.text(.field) in `fieldText` with the prompt
  in t3, and a ✕ (Clear text, `SearchWords.clear`) while there are words, its target 44 tall (DWTarget). It is a plain
  TextField bound as `.searchable`'s was - get `search.text`, set `search.type(typed)` - so every typed character takes
  the very path it took (the cadence, the stand-down, the resume and the asks untouched); ✕ is `search.type("")`, as
  `.searchable`'s own clear sets the text to ""; the keyboard's key is Search (`.submitLabel(.search)`), and its
  `.onSubmit` is `search.submitted()` - what `.onSubmit(of: .search)` called - then the keyboard put away
  (`@FocusState`), as iOS's field does; a scroll still puts the keyboard away (`.scrollDismissesKeyboard
  (.interactively)`, kept); autocorrection and capitals off, as before. What `.searchable` drew that this doesn't: its
  Cancel beside the field while typing (✕ empties it, the Search key or a scroll puts the keyboard away) and its
  tucking up under the title as the list scrolls (iSearch draws the field fixed). Scroll-to-top is the
  ScrollViewReader's, as before. The Mac's field is unchanged (the sidebar's, slice 3), and PressingPickerSheet's
  filter keeps iOS's `.searchable` (a sheet's own list, a filter not a search).
  The kinds are a **PhoneStrip** (All, Artists, Albums, Songs), its binding `search.state.view` read and
  `search.choose(view)` written - the query narrowed, never the results (CLAUDE.md's decision), the kind in use always
  shown; drawn out to the list's edges (the strip pads its own 16). Top results and each section's heading are
  `.row.grp` rows (SearchHeading: 38 tall, the words at the foot 6 up, 15 semibold - subheadline, as R8's - in the
  heading's colour), a section's **See all** at its end in the accent, still `search.choose(SearchView(kind))` - its
  target (R7's review) DWTarget's 44 reaching past the 38-tall heading, the heading drawn over the row under it
  (`.zIndex(1)`) so the reach is See all's, never that row's. Every
  row is `.row.tall` - 60, its cover 44 (square: `Rectangle()`; round for an artist), 12 from its title (body) and line
  (Phone.text(.small) in t2) - on a `rowRule` hairline drawn out to the list's edges (an overlay, so a song's swipe
  keeps its 16 inset), ending in what its tap does, from Core's `SearchTable.actions(row).first`: a song that plays,
  the bare ▶ (`.key.bare`: 28, its glyph 14 - footnote's, t3); the album you don't have, **Get** in the accent (the
  look's small button's words; the row's tap is the Get's page); a page, PhoneChevron. A song's ••• and its swipe are
  as they were. The slots, asking lines, failures, Mores and notes are the old ones on the look's colours and buttons.
- The Mac, Search.dc.html: MacPage's toolbar - "Results for “…”" (SearchTable.heading), the groove, the kinds as
  DWSegmented (the same binding as the phone's strip) and, where the toolbar doesn't fit, one DWPopUp named for the
  kind in use (ViewThatFits) - then **Search Soulseek by hand…** at its end for whoever may get albums. Under it one
  grouped table: the columns' strip (Name, Kind, Artist, Year, In your library, the buttons - SearchTable.columns,
  which drops the year, then the kind, then the artist where the page is narrow, the name keeping its least), then
  SearchContent inside it, each row a **MacSearchRow** (its cells SearchTable.cells: the kind and the artist in t2,
  the year in mono, the place a green chip when held, "not in your library" in t3 for what the library answered for and
  holds none of; its buttons SearchTable.actions - **Play** (`.normal`), **Open** (`.normal`), **Get** (`.on`)), each
  heading a **MacSearchGroupLine** (the table's `.row.grp`). A row's cells sit on one first text baseline, as
  MacColumnList's and Requests' (the year's Courier Prime would sit high centred), the cover centred on its title in
  the name cell. The rows are View > Row Size's (`requestRowHeight`,
  `requestCover` - Requests' 34 at Small), striped (R7's review) as one table: `SearchTable.striped` runs
  MacTable.stripes over the lines drawn - Top results' heading and rows, then each section's heading and rows - so the
  stripes run on unbroken down the table and start again under each heading (Search.dc.html's `k = 0` at each
  group, MacColumnList's way), a song's albums under its triangle taking the song's stripe (`stripedAs`); the
  selection's colours; a click selecting and a double-click doing the first button's - R6's `SpatialTapGesture(count:
  2)` kept off the buttons' column by `MacTable.opens(at:widths:controls:)`, so a double-click on Play is Play's alone -
  and the keys R6's `MacListKeys.pressed` (↑ ↓ Home End through `SearchTable.order` - Top results' rows, then each
  section's, each once, Top results' ids prefixed `top|`, so a row drawn twice is two lines - and Return opening the
  selected). Back to the top (R7's review), as the phone: a zero-height `ShelfAnchor.top` above the table, scrolled to
  on `searchScrollToTop` (Search chosen again, animated) and, at once, on another kind or other words drawn
  (`state.view`, `state.drawn?.text`). A right-click is the row's ••• (a song's
  QueueMenuItems, an album's albumRightClick - still one of each in the file). The status bar is SearchTable.status:
  the rows drawn by kind, and how many are in your library. The table is the page's width whenever that is at least
  its least (`.scrollDisabled(width <= total)`), so nothing scrolls sideways at 1280, at 880 or beside the panel.
- Each row's actions are the very calls the phone's tap makes, written once in SearchRowView: a song's Play is
  `tapped(song)` (`player.play(songs:album:at:)`, nothing awaited), its Open its album's page; an album's or an
  artist's `navigation.open(route)`; the album you don't have `search.open(group)`; a MusicBrainz artist
  `search.openArtist`; a song's album `search.openSongAlbum`. A MusicBrainz song in a section is a row whose name cell
  has the disclosure's triangle (its albums open under it, by `MacSearchLook.indent`), its button its named album's;
  the triangle's toggle is VoiceOver's action on the row too, and (R7's review) the row's default action - VoiceOver's
  double-tap - is `main()`, its first button's, as the double-click.
- **How the Mac draws SearchScreen's rows without SearchScreen naming the Mac** (test_ios_mac_reach's zones: a shared
  file names nothing declared under App/Mac, nor Typeface.Mac, MacPalette or the Mac's row size). SearchScreen.swift
  declares **SearchTableRow** - a row as values (its id, title, SearchTable.Cells, actions, VoiceOver's words, its
  picture: a library cover, round or not, or the Archive's front; striped, dimmed, busy, disabled, indented, the
  disclosure's state and toggle) and one closure, `act`, carrying out each action - and **SearchTableDesk** (`row`,
  `heading`, the row's height for Top results' empty place, a song's albums' indent), handed down as
  `EnvironmentValues.searchTable`. MacSearchPage sets it round SearchContent: each row a **MacSearchTableRow** (the
  name cell - the row size's cover on a chip's corners and 1 pt edge, the triangle, the indent - inside MacSearchRow),
  each heading a MacSearchGroupLine. Every row, heading and Top results' place reads `table` and draws the phone's when
  it is nil, so the phone, and the Mac anywhere outside that table, are unchanged.
- Left out: the drawing's **Yours first | Only yours** (the list has no such choice - your library's rows lead each
  section already, and there is no filter to only yours); See all on the Mac (the toolbar's kinds are it); and Get.dc's
  and iSources' pieces listed under Sources below.

**Search Soulseek by hand…** (the Mac): `AppNavigation.manualSearch()` - Now Playing closed, Requests at its root,
`manualSearchWanted` set - and MacRequestsPage takes it as it shows (R7's review: no timer): its Artist field's own
`.onChange(of: navigation.manualSearchWanted, initial: true)` - so a field drawn after the ask still sees it, and one
already drawn sees it change - puts the cursor there and, in a `defer`, `manualSearchTaken()`, so the ask is taken
whatever happens: "the way it already opens there", Requests' toolbar fields. The phone's is Requests' own **Search
Soulseek…** row, untouched.

**Get** (GroupView.swift, Mac/Search/MacGetPage.swift). GroupView is generic over a desk too: its model, every task,
the picker's sheet, the phone's Sources sheet and the store line stay its own, and on the Mac it hands MacGetPage a
**GroupDesk** - the page, the pressings' count, whether Get can be asked and is allowed, online, whether there is a
usual tracklist, and `get`, `pick`, the artist's page, GET_OFF and the store line (`GroupStoreLine`).
- The phone, iGet.dc.html: the hero - the cover 184, square; the title; the artist in the accent when they are a link;
  the meta line plain in small t2 type ("1997 · Album · not in your library" - iGet's `.meta`), only a "maybe in your
  library" in a dashed square edge (a mark, not a face); then **Get the album** (the primary button, large, across the
  page, no chevron) and **Pressing** in t2 with the chosen pressing's label and DWCaret in the accent (iGet's flat
  `.btn` row: a flat button's words are the accent, dw.css; 44 tall on its hairline: today's PressingPickerSheet as it
  opens; its VoiceOver hint the facts line, the pressings' count in it), the facts line in mono
  (`GetPageWords.factsLine`: the pressing's facts and "7 pressings" - two lines held whatever it says, so another
  pressing chosen moves nothing under it; at the accessibility sizes, `lineLimit(2...)` - at least two lines' room, as
  many as the words take), GET_OFF,
  the store line (StoreLineView, flat), and the maybe note; then the **Tracklist** heading (`.row.grp`, the count beside
  it - GetPageWords.songsLine, "11 songs · 49 min" when every track has a length) and its rows: the number in mono, the
  title (a song searched for in the accent, semibold, a 3 pt bar in the accent at its left edge, "the song you searched
  for" to VoiceOver), the mark's note and its caution chip, the length - 48 tall on a hairline. The disc headings and
  Not on this pressing as before.
- The Mac, Get.dc.html: the toolbar - **Get the album** (`.pri`), the groove and "Pressing", the chosen pressing as a
  pop-up button (today's picker as a sheet - Pressing ▾), "N pressings" as a chip, **Open artist** at its end - folded
  to Get, the pressing and Open artist where it doesn't fit; the hero (the cover 132 beside the title at h1, the
  artist, the meta line, the facts); the store line at most 520 wide; and the tracklist as a **MacColumnList** - #,
  Title, Against the usual tracklist (the mark's caution chip and note, or "the same" where there is a usual tracklist
  to compare with - `GetPageWords.against`), Length - its disc headings and Not on this pressing group rows, its box
  added up from the row size (`boxHeight`, `boxLeast`), the song searched for selected as the page draws. The status
  bar: the songs line and the pressing (`GetPageWords.status`).
- `get(page)`: on the Mac `navigation.getSources(request, from: route)`, on the phone `getting = request` (the sheet,
  as it was). The request's id is `GetRequest.numbered()` (R7's review): one count for the whole app, so two pages'
  Gets never share an id (each page had counted its own from 1, and the sheet and the dock key on it). ManualSearchSheet
  and MacRequestsPage still count their own: theirs are sheets of their own, never the dock.
- **Another pressing chosen while the dock's Get is open** (R7's review): the Get ends - `.onChange(of:
  page.chosenId)` calls `AppNavigation.pressingChosen(_:on:)`, which ends the dock's Get (its search let go, the tab
  gone) when it was asked from this page and `MacDock.getStands(asked:chosen:)` says it was asked for another pressing
  than the one now chosen. Ending it rather than asking again can never enqueue the pressing no longer chosen (a card
  from the old search could otherwise be tapped as the new one began); Get the album then asks for the one chosen.

**Sources** (SourcesSheet.swift's SourcesPage, SourceCardView.swift, Mac/Search/MacSourcesTab.swift, Routes.swift,
Player/MacPanels.swift, Core's MacDock.getLasts).
- The phone, iSources.dc.html: **Close** where it said Cancel (SourcesLook.close), the subtitle at the left, the chips
  as a strip of words (FilterStrip - each its own toggle, the pressed ones white over the accent's line, on the strip's
  hairline), **Sort** and its pop-up with how many were found at the right ("14 found" - SourcesLook.found, once
  something was), and the cards on the page's black: each a **PhoneCard** (no face, a hairline under it), its top line
  the score chip, the folder and its peer and Get (the best match's the primary, the rest the look's flat button), its
  facts three columns of a label over a mono readout, its missing line in amber, its Why behind the score. The query's
  field keeps its own box (R1c's typing rule, pinned inside its block). No speed bar: neither drawing has one.
- (R7's review) **Sample rate ▾**, beside Sort on both: any, or 44.1, 48, 88.2 or 96 kHz or more (`SourcesLook
  .sampleRates`, the web's floors) - `CandidateFilters.quality.minSampleRate`, judged by Core's QualityFilters (a
  folder's worst file; a folder saying no rate never passes a floor). It is kept in SourcesChoices with the chips, so
  the dock's tab finds it as left; `chosenFilters` (`SourcesLook.filters(chips, minSampleRate:)`) is what the cards
  are judged by and what the next peer's search picks with; it counts as a pressed filter, and Clear filters clears it.
- (R7's review) **"N found"**: "14 found" when every card is shown, "3 of 14" while the filters hide some
  (`SourcesLook.found(_:shown:)`, the shown count the cards passing). The sort line is capped at xxxLarge, and where
  Sort, Sample rate and the count don't fit on one line the count folds under the pop-ups (ViewThatFits). The phone's
  strip, scrolled at the largest sizes, pads its row by the 44 target's reach inside the scroll and takes it back
  outside, so a chip's target isn't clipped (PhoneStrip's way).
- (R7's review) **The speeds**, the Mac's panel foot under the cards (Get.dc.html's; iSources has none): "Speeds are
  each peer's own average." as drawn - but a card shows deadwax's own measured speed for a peer it has downloaded from
  (Sources.speedFact `.measured`), and then the drawing's words would be untrue, so it says "Speeds are what you got
  from a peer before, else its own average." (`SourcesLook.speeds(shown)`).
- Left out of Get.dc's and iSources' drawings, each for its reason: **Pin** (the app has no pins client, and Core's
  DeadwaxClient is not this slice's); **Show all 14** (what it does isn't drawn, and Clear filters shows them all);
  **the signal chips on every card** (each card's Why behind the score lists every signal already, scored); **the
  speed bar** (neither drawing has one - R7 removed SpeedBar, so Core's SpeedFact.percent has no reader on the
  cards).
- Both files are shared, so their Mac sizes come through the look's roles, never Typeface.Mac (test_ios_mac_reach):
  `Typeface.Look.text(.smallButton)` is the Mac's `.small`, `.field` its `.base`, `.chip` its `.label`, and
  `Typeface.Look.mono(.smallButton)` its small mono - each beside the phone's own size in one ternary.
- The Mac: Get the album opens the side panel's **Sources** tab (MacDock.tabs puts it first while a Get is open), never
  the sheet. `AppNavigation.macSources` is a **MacSourcesGet** - the page it was asked from, the GetRequest, and its
  own **SourcesChoices** (the chips, whether one was tapped, the sort) - and MacSourcesTab draws SourcesPage over it
  with `kept: get.choices`, so the tab switched away from and back finds it as it was. Docked, the page begins its
  search once and never lets it go itself (`.onDisappear { if !docked { model.close() } }`); its Close is
  `closeDock()` - the Get over (`endSources`, its search let go) and the panel put away. A download asked for from it
  is `sourcesQueued` - the Get ended, Requests at its root, as the sheet's.
- The tab goes when its Get page is left: every move of the front - `tab`, and each tab's stack - calls `frontMoved`,
  which ends the Get unless `MacDock.getLasts(.group(page), front: shownStack.last)` (the page it was asked from is
  still the one in front). Back, another page pushed over it, another sidebar row, the person changing (`reset`) all
  end it, its search let go before the panel goes (MacDock.kept closes the panel on Sources).

**The pressing picker** (PressingPickerSheet.swift): the look's colours, its fold's button the look's (flat accent words
on the phone); its filter iOS's own `.searchable`, as the brief says.

**The store line** (StoreLineView.swift - another slice's in name, edited because every page it stands on is R7's):
flat on the phone - its title (green when held), lines and notes in the look's colours on the page's black, no box,
Join and Add the look's flat buttons. The Mac's box (Palette.card, Corners.cardShape, Palette.border) and SecondaryPill
are as they were, behind `if Platform.mac` (test_ios_palette.py's pins kept).

R1c's **Not flat yet** (above, and docs/ios.md over checks 612-614) named "Search's rows, the pressing picker, an
album's Get and Choose a source's cards (R7)": docs/ios.md's list no longer does, and 612 names Search, an album you
don't have and Choose a source among the pages to look at.

### Core

- **SearchTable.swift** (new): the Mac table's columns and their widths by the page and the row size, the cells of a
  row, its actions (play, open, get - and their words and VoiceOver names), the line ids and the order ↑ ↓ move
  through (All's and a kind's), the stripes (`striped`, MacTable.stripes over the lines drawn), the status bar, the
  toolbar's heading and "Search Soulseek by hand…", `SearchWords.clear`; **GetPageWords** (the pressings' count, the
  facts line, the songs line, the Mac's columns and their widths, `against`, the status); **SourcesLook** (Close,
  "14 found" and "3 of 14", Sort, the sample-rate floors, `filters` and `pressed` with the floor, the speeds' words).
  SearchTableTests holds each - `theTablesLinesAreInTheOrderDrawn` the order, `theStripesRunOnUnderEachHeading`,
  `theSampleRateFloor`, `theSpeedsNoteSaysWhatTheSpeedsAre`.
- **MacDock.getLasts** and **MacDock.getStands** (and their tests): the dock's Get lasts while its page is the one in
  front, and stands only for the pressing it was asked for.

  ViewThatFits decides, and a heading row spanning the table (it is drawn out by `-SearchLook.side`).

  on a button being only the button's; Requests' Artist field taking the cursor after Search's by hand (its onChange,
  `initial: true`); VoiceOver's double-tap on a row doing its first button's.

  the keyboard away, the cursor's colour, the list scrolling under it, and typing feeling exactly as `.searchable` did.

### After James's look: the field raised (26 Nov)

James, on the phone: "the search bar is a bit low on mobile". iOS's large title stands under an empty 44 pt row of its
bar (the row a pushed page's Back would use), and the field's `safeAreaInset` sat under the large title, so the field
was that row lower than iSearch draws it: `.big` "Search" 10 under the status bar, the field 10 under the title.

- **What changed:** the phone's page takes `.toolbarTitleDisplayMode(.inlineLarge)` (iOS 17, the app's floor): the
  large title - still the bar appearance's Libre Franklin 34 bold (Typeface) - drawn in the bar's own row at its left,
  so the field comes up by the row. The field, its inset, its 10 over the strip and everything it does are as they were.
  The title no longer folds as the list scrolls; the row it would have folded into is the one it's drawn in.

  over the list, as LibraryView's pager does - matching iSearch to the point. It was taken back before it was
  committed: the Library is the one page that hides the bar (test_ios_palette's
  `test_the_librarys_top_sits_under_the_status_bar` holds that), and its top took three fixes and a UIKit probe to keep
  clear of the Dynamic Island on James's iPhone, the last after a return from Now Playing. With iOS's bar kept, UIKit
  keeps the safe area.

### After the review (2026-11-25)

The review held the RootView branches, the rows, the cancel words, SettingsCards and the two shared-test exceptions,
and the reading of Gapless and the Quality floor (James is told one line about the Quality floor; it is unchanged).
What it found, and what was done - each pinned by a test and its mutation shown failing (below):

1. **The Mac drew the phone's pieces in its own exact frames.** The pages the Mac pushes under Settings are the
   phone's own - Settings > Downloads (and through it Download your library, the other accounts' downloads, what
   didn't download, each album's Remove), Change address, Debug, Change password - and `lookHeight` is exact on the
   Mac: an album's and a playlist's row were 30 tall holding a 44 cover and three lines, `settingsRow()` 46, and a
   switch's row (PhoneSwitchRow, DWLook's target tall) 0 - its hit shape zero tall, so Download your library and Only
   while charging took no click. Now each is Platform-aware: `settingsRow()` is its content's height on the Mac with
   `SettingsLook.macRowRoom` (8) above and below (the phone's 46 at least unchanged); `settingsSwitch()` is the purple
   switch on the phone and the Mac's own - a plain `Toggle` `.toggleStyle(.switch)` tinted the accent - on the Mac;
   DownloadsScreen's `tallRow(macRoom:)` is the phone's 60 at least and the Mac's content height (AlbumLine's own 4
   above and below, a playlist's and the library's row 4). A row's Remove stays its swipe (a trackpad's on the Mac): a
   right-click of its own was tried and taken out, test_ios_mac's rule being that a right-click is only ever the •••
   menus' own items - the Mac's Downloaded page's right-click is the album's •••, Remove Download among them. The
   words keep the phone's faces on these pages, as before R9. Held by
   `test_the_pages_the_mac_pushes_under_settings_draw_at_the_macs_sizes`: `mac_path()` - test_ios_phone_look's
   phone_path turned round - over those pages and the pieces they draw finds no `.phoneSwitch`, PhoneSwitchRow,
   `lookHeight(DWLook.here.target)` or `tallRowHeight`, and no settingsRow 46 or PhoneGo/PhoneKV; and the phone's
   Getting albums, Playback, Account, This phone and About pages are opened from the phone's root alone (the Mac has
   its boxes).
2. **Two columns started too narrow.** At 1280 (a page of 1060) This Mac's two buttons wanted ~478 of a 475 column; at
   1100 (a page of 880) ~93 past a 385 one; and Normalization's line beside its four segments had ~98 at 1280, 8 at
   1100. Worked out from the bundled faces (tests/ios_fonts.py, semibold from above): a row is the label's 124 and 8,
   then its control - This Mac's Show Downloaded and Downloading and downloaded… (12.5, 11 either side, 6 apart) the
   widest at ~478 (481 semibold) - so a column needs it plus its box's 12 either side, and two columns 2 × (478 + 24)
   + 18 + 44 = ~1066 (1071 semibold): **`twoColumns` is 1072**. So the window's opening 1280 (1060) shows one column,
   as do the side panel's (1280 - 220 - 401 = 659) and the smallest window's (660); two from a 1292 window, or 1693
   with the side panel open. Every row's line - a choice's, a fact's, the EQ's, Confirm before cancelling's - is
   **under its control**, lined up with it (MacSettingsNote's 132 in), never beside it. Held by
   `test_the_macs_settings_take_two_columns_only_where_they_fit` (the sum, from the Core words and the faces; one
   column wherever it falls back; the notes' place).
3. **The account card at the largest sizes.** At AX5 its row wanted ~487 of the phone's 343; at xxxLarge the name had
   ~83 (39 while "Signing out…"). From xxxLarge and every accessibility size (`typeSize.isAccessibilitySize ||
   typeSize == .xxxLarge` - from xxxLarge, where the name was already cramped) the Admin chip and Sign out go **under
   the name**, Sign out across the card on up to three lines; the card on top, `.top`-aligned. Held by

4. **Labels cut at AX5**: Remove All Downloads, Try All Again, Keep Them and Remove, Change password, "Signing in…".

5. **The Mac's Downloaded lost more than was said.** The first ask (FirstAskCard) was only in AlbumsScreen's

## The redesign, slice R10: Edit album, the folder list and Release (2026-11-25)

The Mac redesign's build plan (~/Desktop/Code/deadwax-plans/mac-redesign-build.md), 3.4's R10: Edit album on the Mac
as one page - the library's folders at its left, the album's editor at its right - and the phone's sheet's root as
iEdit draws it. The drawings are Main.dc.html (the Mac's) and iEdit.dc.html (the phone's), in
~/Desktop/Code/deadwax-plans/mac-redesign/. Built on ed819e69 (R9). The app is still 0.13 (13); `__version__`
untouched; no server data new (no diff to Core's DeadwaxClient or Routes); no engine file touched. Tags, Artwork,
Lyrics and Delete are still today's pages: R11 draws each as a tab (below, "Where R11 plugs in").

### The Mac: one page (ios/App/Mac/Edit/)

- **Every Edit album on the Mac opens this page, never the sheet.** `AppNavigation.editAlbum` (App/Shared/Routes.swift)
  sends the Mac to `macEditPage(_:)` first: Now Playing closed, the You stack shown with Settings' Edit an album
  (`.chooseFolder`) on top, `macEdit` set to the opening. `albumEdit` - the sheet's - is never set on the Mac, so
  DesktopFrame's sheet is unreachable there now (its owner may take it out; it isn't R10's file). One page of it,
  ever: on top already it stays, with its list and its place; further down it is taken out and put on top, as
  Manage's row puts it - or over Needs a look when opened from there, so Back is the queue's page again. The
  sidebar's Edit an album (`macMove`'s `.manage(.edit, _)`) goes back to it while it is on the stack.
  MacEdit.swift's `.chooseFolder` draws `MacEditWindow()` (its doc already named R10; the phone's Choose the folder is
  as it was).
- **MacEditWindow** is the page. The editor is the sheet's own model (EditAlbumModel), made afresh for each opening as
  the sheet makes it - Needs a look's folder and scan in queue mode, otherwise the list's own scan - and opened
  (`.task(id: Opening(id:step:online:))`). A folder picked in the list is an opening of its own, 200 ms after the pick
  rests (R2's rest).
- **MacFolderList** (its left, 398 wide from a page of 1000, 280 under it with no Artist column): MacToolbar's Find
  field and the **All | Needs a look** switch (DWSegmented large), then MacColumnList's rows - Album, Artist (112),
  Year (50) and the amber count of the issues still to look at (42) - each row read cell by cell, as every list but an
  artist's and an album's (MacColumnList's `voice` is theirs alone, test_ios_artist_look), the album's words saying
  the artist where there is no Artist column, and `EditAlbumPage.Words.folderRow` the row's help. Every folder
  (AlbumEdit.folderChoices' match with no limit: the list is lazy) in the Library's order, and Needs a look counted
  by the queue's own function - both since the review (below, "After review"). The status bar says how many folders
  the list shows and how many need a look.
- **MacEditHeader**: the cover (72), the album, its byline, the facts and the size in the readout face, the folder's
  path (selectable, truncated in the middle, the whole path its help), **Matched to MusicBrainz** or **Not matched**
  as a chip, and **Open album** (the album's page, pushed over this one, which is kept). Several folders for one
  album: a pop-up of their paths. The chip and Open album sit beside the words from an editor of 560, under them
  below that.
- **The tabs** are MacFolderTabs over `EditAlbumPage.tabs` (the person's permissions: Release, Tags, Artwork and
  Lyrics with Edit albums, Delete with Look after the library). The tab is the editor's own `@State` (MacAlbumEditor's
  since the review), above the model, so changing it never touches typed work.
- **MacReleaseTab** (Release): Needs a look's issues and marks, when there are any; **Pressing** - the MusicBrainz
  search field (Return finds releases, never applies), **Find releases**, and the pressings as rows, the chosen one
  lit; **Fields** - Artist, Album, Year and Original year side by side, Edition, the hint; **Cover** - the folder's
  and the pressing's covers, the cover's switch and **Compare full size…** (Compare covers, in a sheet); **What Apply
  does** - the preview, with **Show every change**. Two columns from an editor of 620, one under it. Tab goes
  through the search field and the five fields in the order drawn (`.tabs`, test_ios_mac.py's TABS).
- **MacEditFooter**: 48 tall under the tab, what the tab's action does at its left and, under Release, **Revert** and
  **Apply** (the purple one, saying what it waits for while it runs). Under a part still today's page, its **Open
  Tags…** (etc.) opens that page over this one in a sheet, as the phone pushes it - with Done (Escape) to close it.
- **Apply is the sheet's own** on both devices: `EditAlbumModel.apply()`, which posts RetagModel's body - the folder,
  the release chosen, the fields and the cover's switch - and the server works the plan out again from it. No plan is
  sent; no file of this slice calls EditClient.
- **Never left mid-apply, nor with typed work** (EditAlbumModel.holdsWork - typed work, a write including an apply,
  a mark): the window can't be closed (`keepsWindowOpen`), Back isn't drawn, and AppNavigation's `kept()` keeps the
  page under anything opened over it (`macEditHolds`, told by the page as it changes) - a tab's button doesn't pop
  it, a sidebar row opens over it. Another folder picked, a step through the queue, or an opening from elsewhere
  (`macEditAsked`: the page brought to the front, nothing let go) each ask **Discard changes?** first - Discard the
  destructive one, Keep editing Return's - and none is asked while an apply runs: it waits for the apply to end.
- **The page goes** when it is on no stack any more (`editPageGone`, from `frontMoved`): its opening over, and its
  Needs a look session told, as the sheet's dismissal tells it. The album deleted: the page stays with nothing in its
  editor until a folder is picked (`macEditEnded`); in queue mode it stays saying so, as the sheet does. A sign-out
  lets it go first (`reset()`).
- **Revert** (both devices): Release made afresh on the folder as the scan last read it - its fields the folder's, the
  cover's switch as it opens, the pressing it is tagged with chosen again - as the editor opens on it
  (`EditAlbumModel.revertRelease()`, the model's own since the review - its `retag` setter private again). Nothing
  is written. Only with typed work to put back, deadwax in reach, no write or mark under way, and the folder not
  waiting to be read again (`EditAlbumPage.canRevert`).

### After review (2026-11-26)

The coordinator's review of 7ea076f8: two Mac bugs, a counting rule broken, holding rules with almost no tests, and the
seam R11 and R12 build on. All of it amended into the one commit, still on ed819e69.

#### The bugs

- **The page left while it loads.** `open()` set `opened` before its read; a tab switched or a page pushed over the
  page cancelled the `.task`, the read came back `.dropped`, nothing landed - and on return `open()` returned at once,
  so the page said it was finding the folder for good, its list empty and no Look again. Now EditAlbumModel keeps
  `answered` (set where the opening's read lands or fails, never where it drops), and the Mac's page calls
  `reopen()`: `open()` the first time, then `lookUp()` again while nothing has come back. The phone's sheet still
  calls `open()` alone (its task goes with the sheet, and the model with it) - nothing it does changed.
- **A delete on the Mac left the album's page behind.** `leaveAlbum` popped the shown tab's top only - on the Mac
  that is Settings, with Edit an album on top. On the Mac it now takes every page of the album off every stack, as
  `albumMoved` follows one on every stack (`isAlbum(_:_:)`); the phone's rule is as it was. (Delete is R11's; R10's
  routing broke it.)
- **Two "need a look" counts on one window.** The switch, the status bar and the rows counted
  `MetadataQueue.outstanding` alone; the queue and the sidebar's badge count `needsAttention || isNewImport`. Now
  `EditAlbumPage.waiting` asks the queue's own function (`MetadataQueue.queueAlbums([album], nil)`), the status bar's
  count is `NeedsLook.summaryTotal`, and a row's mark is `EditAlbumPage.mark`: its issues, amber, or **New** (the
  queue's chip, `.marked` as the Library's New mark) for a clean new import, VoiceOver's "Newly added". Nothing for a
  folder the queue doesn't list - an issue the server doesn't call needing attention included.
- **Every keystroke ran the page's body.** `body` read `model?.holdsWork` (→ `retag.unsaved` → `retag.fields`), so a
  letter typed in Album filtered, sorted and diffed ~1,400 folders again. The holding reads (`keepsWindowOpen`, Back,
  `macEditHolding`) are MacEditHolding's, a modifier of their own; the list works out its rows and the status bar's
  counts itself (MacFolderList's body, from the scan, Find and the switch); the queue's bar is a view of its own
  (MacEditQueueBar), its step gate read there. The page's body reads no field.
- **The seam for R12.** The editor - header, waits, tabs, scroll, foot, part sheet, and what it says in place of an
  album - is **MacAlbumEditor** (App/Mac/Edit/MacAlbumEditor.swift), below.
- **A spurious "Discard changes?" after an apply.** An opening asked for during an apply was asked about once
  `applying` turned false - before the follow-up read landed, while `retag.unsaved` still compared against the album
  as it was before the write. askAboutOpening and a pick now wait for `following == 0` too (an apply counts in
  `following` until its read is done), and `following` changing asks again.
- **The Mac's foot ignored permissions.** MacEditFooter is drawn under Release only with Edit albums, as the tab and
  the phone's foot are; under a part still today's page it keeps its Open… (Delete's, for Look after the library).

#### The seam: MacAlbumEditor (R11, R12)

`MacAlbumEditor<Bar: View>(model: EditAlbumModel, layout: EditAlbumPage.Layout) { bar }` - and without the slot,
`MacAlbumEditor(model:layout:)`.

- **The host owns** the model (made for each opening, as the sheet makes it), its opening and its questions (Discard,
  the steps), the folder list if it has one, the holding modifier, and the page's width (`EditAlbumPage.Layout`).
- **The editor owns** the tab (`@State`, above the model, kept across a new model), the part sheet and its stack (put
  away when the model changes or the folder is deleted), Release's Compare covers sheet, and the out-of-reach,
  which-folder and status states with Look again.
- **`bar`** is drawn over the header: MacEditWindow passes MacEditQueueBar in queue mode, nothing otherwise. R12's
  MacNeedsALook hosts the same view beside its own list, passing its own bar.
- **R11** adds Tags, Artwork, Lyrics and Delete as tabs inside it - in place of `partCard` and `MacEditSheet.part` -
  and their actions to MacEditFooter; nothing in MacEditWindow changes for it.
- Its reads of the model are none of them a field's (no `holdsWork`, `unsaved` or `.fields`): a keystroke re-draws
  MacReleaseTab and MacEditFooter, never the editor or its host.

#### The tests that held nothing

Each of these mutations passed every test after the first pass; each is now pinned in test_ios_edit_look's
`test_the_macs_holding_rules_are_each_pinned`: the 200 ms rest (test_ios_library_look pins it for the Library's three
pages, not here); `editPageGone` acting with Edit an album still on a stack; `frontMoved` not calling it (and each
stack's `didSet` calling `frontMoved`); `macMove`'s back-to-page case for the sidebar's Edit an album, before the
Manage row's own; Discard on a folder pick letting the hold go before it opens the folder; Keep editing ending the
asked opening's Needs a look session; a delete outside queue mode ending the opening; the `macEdit?.queue != nil`
guard; `reset()` letting `macEdit` go first (the worst: the next person's Edit an album opening on the last one's
folder), its sessions ended once the session has moved on; MacFolderList's `.disabled(writing)`.

And one more found on the way: **Discard said to a folder pick** while another opening waited to be asked about let
that opening go (`macEditAsked = nil` in macEditPage) without ending its Needs a look session. macEditPage now ends
it, as Keep editing does.

#### The phone's flat rule, widened (test_ios_phone_look.py's `drawn()`, the coordinator's one shared change)

`DRAWS` matched `.background(` and `.fill(` with the bracket straight after, so a face laid any other way passed every
flat test. It now also sees: `.background { … }` and `.background(alignment:) { … }` (trailing closures); `.overlay(…)`
and `.overlay { … }`; `.listRowBackground(…)`; `.backgroundStyle(…)`; and a colour standing as a view of its own in a
`ZStack { … }`. A closure reports the colours that stand in it as views (`bare_colours`: a statement of the block, or
of an `if` in it, that is a colour - never a colour an argument names); a call's own colours are counted without the
draw calls inside it (`own_text`), which are found on their own. Colours now include the old palette, SwiftUI's
(`Color.x`, not `.clear`), a bar's and a material. PhoneFoot's own ground, `.background { DWPalette.footFace }` (the
page's black under the foot, run into the home indicator's room), is in FLAT_DRAWS with its reason.

Run over the whole tree, it catches in files that aren't R10's - left as they are, for the merge:

## The redesign, slice R11: Tags, Artwork, Lyrics and Delete (2026-11-26)

The Mac redesign's build plan (~/Desktop/Code/deadwax-plans/mac-redesign-build.md), 3.4's R11, with
wave-e-common.md: Edit album's other four parts as tabs on both devices - the Mac's inside R10's MacAlbumEditor, the
phone's under the root's strip - each tab's action in its foot. The drawings are Main.dc.html (the Mac's) and
iEditTags, iEditArtwork, iEditLyrics and iEditDelete (the phone's), in ~/Desktop/Code/deadwax-plans/mac-redesign/.
Built on b017851a (R10 and its tests), rebased onto R14 (0eda8964) before the last checks. The app is still 0.13
(13); `__version__` untouched; no server data new (no diff to Core's DeadwaxClient or Routes); no engine file touched.
Every write is the one it was: TagsModel has no diff, and EditAlbumModel's only one is the review's - which album
pages a delete from a folder opening closes ("After review", finding 11); every write's call, guard and plan as R10
left them.

### Both devices

- **Every part a tab** (`EditAlbumPage.strip` - `Strip { tabs }`, `pushes` gone): Release, Tags, Artwork and Lyrics
  with Edit albums, Delete with Look after the library, as before. Nothing pushes a part any more; EditPage keeps only
  what the tabs push (Choose a release, Compare covers, Changes, Choose the folder, a track's page, Edit tags).
- **Tags edits the tracks ticked, every track with none ticked** (`EditAlbumPage.tagTargets`, `ticked`, `allTicked`):
  a tick left on a file gone since (a release applied renames them) counts for nothing. The editor is TagsModel as it
  was: `edit(_:)` starts a new set from what its files say, so a tick that would change the set while typed work waits
  asks **Discard changes?** first - the phone's Edit N tracks…, the Mac's checkbox. Apply is `EditAlbumModel.applyTags()`:
  the fields typed over, for the server to plan again - no plan sent. The preview and the write share TagsModel's one
  computation, as they did.
- **Artwork**: Get cover and Get CD art are GetButton and `EditAlbumModel.get` as they were - getting a cover saves
  what the Cover Art Archive has for the release the folder is tagged with, applies no release and chooses nothing.
  Compare covers (the folder's beside the pressing's) is Release's own page or sheet. With no release, each box's
  pointer and **Go to Release** (`EditAlbumPage.Words.openRelease`), which shows the Release tab - a tab now on both
  devices, so the web's "in the Release tab" is both devices' words.
- **Lyrics**: "8 of 12 tracks have lyrics saved beside them, as a .lrc." (GetResults.lyricsLine), Get lyrics beside
  "Nothing saved is replaced." while any track has none. The count is the album's as the editor holds it
  (`EditAlbumModel.album`, handed down each draw, never kept by the view): Get lyrics reads the folder again once it has
  written (`get`'s `lookUp()`, after `guard run.wrote`), and the line says the new count. **No Each track group**: which
  track has lyrics is no fact the app can have - the scan counts them, and a list would need a route.
- **Delete**: read live each time the tab shows (`.task(id: "\(album.path)|\(model.online)") { await
  model.readDeletion() }`); **Delete permanently** is DeleteButton on both devices, off until this folder's summary is
  in hand (`canDelete`), asking once more in the device's own question ("Delete Dummy?" / "There is no undo.", Cancel
  the default and Return's), the question tied to the folder and summary it was asked over, put away if the page is
  followed to another folder, refused by `DeleteFlow.beginDelete` if either has changed. Only the question's Delete
  deletes. After a delete on the Mac, R10's `leaveAlbum` takes every page of the album off every stack, unchanged.
- **DWCheckbox** (App/Look/DWCheckbox.swift, new - R1's MacCheckbox made for both; MacCheckbox stays, as its users -
  MacSettingsRoot, and R14's MacPeoplePage - aren't R11's): dw.css's `input[type=checkbox]`, the Mac's 13 in a well, the phone's square 20 that
  grows with the text (`@ScaledMetric`), flat - its edge alone while off, the purple with a white tick while on - in a
  finger's target of 44 (DWTarget). One element to VoiceOver, a toggle. `showsWords: false` where the row says what it
  ticks. MacReleaseTab's cover switch is one now, in place of the system's Toggle.

### The Mac (ios/App/Mac/Edit/)

- **MacAlbumEditor** draws the five tabs (`tabContent`): MacReleaseTab, MacTagsTab, MacArtworkTab, MacLyricsTab,

### Core (pure, tested on Linux)

EditAlbumPage: the strip (every part a tab), Tags' targets and counts, Delete's rows, and the words - the Mac's foots,
Select all and Deselect all, the Tags line and the editor's legend, Apply to N tracks, See a file's every tag…, a Tags
row's VoiceOver words, the table's columns, Artwork's lines and Compare with this pressing…, Go to Release, Nothing
saved is replaced, Delete's rows and who holds it - and, since the review, `selectAll`, `asksFirst`, `afterRead`,
`deleteFoot`, `folderPages`, `bridgeRelease` and `coverPointer` ("After review"). EditAlbumPageTests: the strip's case
and the new `onlyTheTickedRowsAreEdited`, `tagsWords`, `artworkAndLyricsWords` and `whatADeleteTakesIsSaidInRows` (and
the review's four). The app's verb is **Select** (TagEditWords.select): the drawings' "Tick" is in no word.

**The words fixtures** (by hand, never DEADWAX_WORDS_WRITE): iphone.json and mac.json gain
`EditAlbumPage.Words.tagsNote` and `EditAlbumPage.Words.seeFullSize` (new words, device-aware from birth - added as the
fixture's rule says), and DeviceWordsTests lists them; tagsNote is in `theMacsWordsDiffer`'s own words (the phone's
names its ›, which the Mac's rows haven't), seeFullSize swaps Tap for Click. **One phone word changed on purpose:** the
Tags line was `TagEditWords.selectNote` ("…Tap a track's name to see everything in its file.") and is now
`EditAlbumPage.Words.tagsNote` ("…Tap › to see everything in a track's file."): a tap on the row ticks it now, and the
› opens the file. `TagEditWords.selectNote` (TagEdit.swift, not R11's) is drawn by nothing now; its fixture keys are
as they were.

**The phone's Artwork pointers changed on purpose** (no fixture holds them: they aren't device-aware): the phone said
GetResults.coverPointer and discArtPointer, the web's words with "in the Release tab" made "on the Release page" -
Release was a page of its own. It is a tab now, so the phone says the web's words (`webCoverPointer`,
`webDiscArtPointer`), but for the button. (After review) The replace pointer shows only where Artwork offers no
Compare - Release's own condition, the pressing chosen having a cover - so it never names Release's button: "To
replace it, compare it with the release's in the Release tab." on both devices (`EditAlbumPage.coverPointer(album,
compare:)`, the button's word passed only while Release shows it; R11's first `phoneCoverPointer` named "(Compare)"
where no Compare was). With no release, "To get a cover, first match the album to a release in the Release tab." with
Go to Release. GetResults.coverPointer and discArtPointer (GetResults.swift, not R11's) are drawn by nothing now;
EditPartsVectorTests still holds them.

### Left out, and why

- **The cover's file name and pixel size, and CD art's pixels and bytes** (Main.dc.html's Cover and CD art boxes): the
  scan has the file names alone, and no route answers a picture's size - no server data new.
- **Lyrics' Each track group** (iEditLyrics, Main.dc.html): which track has lyrics isn't in the scan (it counts them).
- **"Tick"**: the drawings' verb; the app's is Select (2.0.8's), so the words say Select.
- **The drawing's 1.2 : 1 columns** on the Mac's Tags: the two boxes share the width equally (an HStack of two
  `maxWidth: .infinity` frames).
- **The track table's own scroll**: the table is as tall as its rows inside the editor's scroll, so a long album
  scrolls the page, not a box inside it.

### After review (2026-11-26)

The review found Delete itself sound - the call, the guards, the dialog with Return on Cancel, `canDelete` - and these:

1. **Delete no longer said how many other files go.** The drawing's "Also in there" row kept DeleteWords.others' names
   and dropped its lead, and the server names twelve files at most while counting every one (`other_file_count`). Both
   devices now say deadwax's words, not the drawing's "10 .lrc": "and 40 other files:" in the caution's colour
   (`DWPalette.amberText`) over the names, ", …" past the twelve - the phone under Tracks as a row of the group, the
   Mac in the well under "10 tracks · 290 MB" (DeleteWords.counts). `EditAlbumPage.alsoInThere`, `deleteFacts` and
   `Words.alsoInThere` are gone (drawn by nothing; no fixture held them). The `Text(others.lead)` pin is back in
   test_ios_edit_parts, with the lead's colour; EditAlbumPageTests has 40 files, 12 named.
2. **Who holds it, on the Mac,** was only the foot's two lines. MacDeleteTab draws the whole sentence
   (DeleteWords.holders) in the caution's colour under the well; the foot says it short, "In a library: Ann's"
   (`EditAlbumPage.deleteFoot`, `held`'s words).
3. **The Mac's every-tag sheet could lose "Discard changes?"**: Edit this track… put the sheet away and raised the
   question in one transaction, and SwiftUI drops a question raised over a sheet on its way down. It now sets `picked`
   and puts the sheet away; the sheet's `onDismiss` chooses it (`choose`, through Core's `EditAlbumPage.asksFirst`), so
   the question shows once the sheet has gone - and `choose` itself never raises it with a sheet up (it waits in
   `picked`). `discarding` is held only while the question can show: the dialog's own dismissal, a sheet coming up
   (`onChange(of: everyTag?.id)`) and the tab's model held anew (with `picked`) each clear it. The names a question is
   answered with are read when it's answered (`fileNames`), never the body's from before.
4. **The Mac's Tags editor could be left empty** after a release applied renamed files under a tag draft: TagsModel's
   read keeps of the ticks and the tracks edited only the names the folder holds, and the editor re-edited only with
   nothing typed - every edited file renamed left it with nothing to show, and a partial rename left "Apply to all 10
   tracks" over the 9 it would write. Fixed in MacTagsTab, by Core's `EditAlbumPage.afterRead` (TagsModel needs no
   change: its filtering is right - Apply never sends a name the folder no longer holds): nothing typed, the editor
   takes the ticks; typed over with some edited tracks left, those are ticked (`.tick`) - the legend and Apply to N say
   what Apply writes, the typed work kept; none left (`.stranded`), the editor says so ("The tracks these changes were
   for have been renamed since, so they can't be written. Discard them to edit the tracks as they are now.",
   `Words.editedGone`) with **Discard** - never an empty box, never typed work put away unasked. It runs as the files
   are read and as typed work is put back (`onChange(of: tags.unsaved)`: Revert, every Undo).
5. **The phone's Tags row was two VoiceOver elements** (the toggle and the ›). The row is one now: the outer HStack
   `.accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)`, its label and length, the toggle traits, the tick its default action
   (`.accessibilityAction { toggle() }`), See a file's every tag… a named action.
6. **TagsFoot at the largest size the foot gives** (PhoneFoot stops at xxxLarge): "Deselect all" and "Edit 10 tracks…"
   came to about 350 against 343. The foot is a `ViewThatFits`: side by side while they fit, one over the other (and
   10 more room above and below) once they don't. DeleteButton's, TagsFoot's and Edit tags' Apply's
   `lineLimit(typeSize.isAccessibilitySize ? 3 : 1)` never applied inside PhoneFoot and are gone. (ReleaseFoot has the
   same dead line limit - R10's, and test_ios_edit_look holds it; left.)
7. **The cover pointer named a button not on the page** ("(Compare)", "(Compare full size…)"): it shows exactly where
   Release shows no Compare. `EditAlbumPage.coverPointer(album, compare:)` names the device's button only when passed
   one, each device passing it only while `ArtworkLooks.releaseCompares` (Release's own condition, `coverRelease`) -
   so today the words alone: "To replace it, compare it with the release's in the Release tab."
   `phoneCoverPointer` is gone.
8. **Mac VoiceOver said "selected" twice** of a ticked row that is also the list's selected one: the label's ",
   selected to edit" and MacColumnList's `.isSelected` (the row selected, the one See a file's every tag… opens). The
   label now says a checkbox's own word, ", checked" (`Words.tagRow`); "selected" is VoiceOver's alone.
9. **Words drawn nowhere, still pinned**: `TagEditWords.selectNote` (its fixture keys, DeviceWordsTests, the vectors'
   `selectNote`, MacPowerTests) is in TagEdit.swift, and `GetResults.coverPointer` and `discArtPointer`
   (EditPartsVectorTests, GetResultsTests) in GetResults.swift - neither file R11's, so all are left as they were and
   no fixture key changed. (selectNote and the vectors are the web's words, held to the web's panel.)
10. **The notes said the phone's CD art is 112 with its hole**, but each picture sat unframed in an adaptive grid's
    cell (112 at least, growing to the row's width over two). The drawing is true now: each disc framed at 112, the
    cell no wider (`.adaptive(minimum: 112, maximum: 112)`); and "with its hole" said as it is - the hole is the empty
    disc's, drawn while a picture comes or when it couldn't (the Mac's at 150, said the same).
11. **(R10's, mine now) A delete from a folder opening left the album's page standing**: `gone` closed pages only by
    the subject's id, and Choose the folder, the Mac's folder list and Needs a look open `.folder(path)`, with none.
    Now, opened by its folder, the album's pages are found by the album the folder holds (Core's
    `EditAlbumPage.folderPages`): each album page open, on every stack, as it was opened, is the folder's album when the
    folders its own Edit album would find (AlbumEdit.folders - by the release the page knew, else by its name) hold the
    folder, or when it's the album the id bridge names for the folder's release - asked as Delete's summary is read
    (`askFolderBridge`, `storeAlbum(releaseMbid:)`, an existing call: no server data new), kept with the folder it was

    (`leaveAlbum` - every stack's on the Mac, the tab shown's top on the phone, as R10 left it), one with folders left
    is asked again now and after the settle. An album opening's own page is as before. (Not changed: an album opening
    that picked another album's folder in Choose the folder still treats the subject's page as that folder's.)

**Words changed** (none device-aware, so no fixture key moved): `EditAlbumPage.Words.tagRow`'s ticked ", selected to
edit" is ", checked"; `Words.editedGone` is new; `Words.alsoInThere` is gone; the replace pointer drops its button's

## The redesign, slice R12: Needs a look (2026-11-26)

The Mac redesign's build plan (~/Desktop/Code/deadwax-plans/mac-redesign-build.md), 3.4's R12, checks 590-593 - the
last slice of wave E. The drawings are NeedsALook.dc.html (the Mac's) and iNeedsALook.dc.html (the phone's, flat).
Built on d18c45a2 (R10, R11, R13 and R14 in). The app is still 0.13 (13); `__version__` untouched; no server data new
(no diff to Core's DeadwaxClient or its endpoints); no engine file touched. Nothing that is sent changed: It's fine
posts the album's own folder and its outstanding issues (EditAlbumModel.markFine, as before), an apply is planned
again on the server, the queue stores only what was ignored. There is still no bulk apply.

### The phone (iNeedsALook)

- **NeedsLookScreen** is a ScrollView of a LazyVStack, no List: the large title (`NeedsLook.title`), **Marked fine ·
  N** at the top's right (a toolbar button while any album has every issue marked fine - its count the facet's, bold
  while it shows, All again when pressed then: `NeedsLookPage.markedFineTapped`), the notes, the web's ladder (the
  library's problem, Reading the library, a first read failed with Try again), then **the strip** (PhoneStrip over
  `NeedsLookPage.strip` - every facet but Marked fine, each "All 3", All's count summaryTotal's), the status line, the
  cards and what takes an album off the list. The old `listRowBackground: Palette.accent` (the shaded open row R10's
  `drawn()` found) is gone with the List; the one open is said to VoiceOver ("Open"), never shaded.
- **A card** (NeedsLookCard): a PhoneCard - the cover at 48 (`Corners.artShape`), the album, its artist and edition,
  its folder in the readout face cut in its middle, PhoneChevron - and its chips under them, each DWChip's flat dot and
  words in its tone (issue amber, New purple, Fixed green, Marked fine and Deleted plain), wrapping onto more lines
  (NeedsLookChipRows, a Layout). At the accessibility sizes each chip is a line of its words in the colour DWChip gives
  that tone (`ChipKind.colour`, pinned equal to DWChip's private mapping). Faded once the session has said what became
  of it. One VoiceOver element, the phone's words as before.
- **Queue mode's bar** (EditQueueBar, EditAlbumSheet.swift) is no longer the system's bottom toolbar: ‹, "2 of 9" in
  the readout face and Skip › (Next album › once a write was told of the album), the accent's flat words, a finger's
  target tall, on one text baseline - drawn **in the foot's own layer**, over each tab's actions (`EditQueueBar.above`:
  Release's Revert and Apply, Tags', Delete's), and as the foot alone where a tab has none (Artwork, Lyrics) or no
  album is drawn (`barred`). PhoneFoot is App/Phone's and untouched, so the bar is inside its content, the actions'
  row (PhoneLook.foot, 68) under it; the foot stays at the screen's foot under the keyboard, as before.
- **Apply moves on.** ReleaseFoot takes the bar: once a release was applied (`RetagModel.applied`, cleared by any
  field changed or pressing picked), in queue mode and not on the last album (`NeedsLookPage.movesOn`), the purple
  button is **Next album** - the bar's `take(1)`, so through the gate and "Discard changes?" like Skip.

### One editor, one page: macEditHost

R10's Mac Edit album had one page, Edit an album's (`.chooseFolder`). AppNavigation now says which page draws it,
`macEditHost`: Needs a look's for a row of its queue opened with it in front (`macEditHost(queue:front:)`), else Edit an
album's (an album page's Edit, a folder picked, and R10's case of a queue's opening asked for over another page's work).
`macEdit(on:)` gives each page only its own opening, so the editor is never drawn twice; everything R10 does for its
page is the host's - the work it holds kept (`kept`), the page brought back to ask "Discard changes?" (`backTo`),
the opening over once the page is on no stack (`editPageGone`), Needs a look's sidebar row going back to it
(`macMove`'s `.manage(.queue)`), reset. MacEditHolding is shared and says nothing while its page draws no editor, so
one page never says "no work" over the other's.

**R10's note, fixed.** R10 read queue mode's end from `queue.nav` going nil on its page. The end is said now where the
Run decides it: NeedsLookModel.closeEditor ends the Mac's opening (`macEditEnded`) as it closes the phone's sheet,
whichever page draws the editor.

### Typed work, on both devices

Every step weighs it first - ‹, Skip ›, Next album (the bar's or Apply's), a row picked, a facet chosen (Show or Marked
fine, which ends the session; refused outright mid-apply and while the folder is read after it), an opening asked for
from elsewhere (asked here only when this page is the host). Over typed work, "Discard changes?" (Discard through the
gate as it is then; Keep editing leaves the album open selected). The phone's sheet's `take` is R10's, unchanged; the
bar and ReleaseFoot's Next album are that `take`. The Mac page's body reads no typed work - `holdsWork` is read only in
its three actions and MacEditHolding.

### Decisions and departures

- **Inline chips under Row Size.** The drawing's rows are two lines, 56 tall; MacColumnList's rows are View > Row
  Size's height, so the chips sit beside the title, folding (`NeedsLookPage.more`), the whole in the help.
- **The phone's lead line** ("Albums whose tags, folder or cover need fixing…") is left out, as iNeedsALook has it; the
  Edit albums note stays.
- **The AX chips' colours** duplicate DWChip's private mapping (App/Look, not this slice's to open), pinned equal by
  test_ios_needs_look_look; NeedsLookChipRows duplicates SourceCardView's private Wrap for the same reason.
- **"Library read N ago"** in the Mac's status bar: the model keeps no time of its read.
- **‹ as words** (`NeedsLookPage.back`, U+2039) on both bars, not a chevron image, so the three sit on one text
  baseline with the readout (test_ios_readout_rows).
- **The bar inside the foot's content**, not a layer of its own: PhoneFoot is App/Phone's and gains only new files.

### Mutations

Each applied alone to the worktree, the named checks run (test_ios_needs_look_look unless named; Core's under `swift
test --filter NeedsLookPageTests`), the file put back. All 16 caught:
- **Apply not moving on**: Core's `movesOn` never true (`applyMovesOnToTheNextAlbumButTheLast`,
  `test_apply_moves_on_and_its_fine_marks_this_album_alone_on_the_mac`); ReleaseFoot never told of the apply
  (`applied: false` - `test_stepping_in_the_sheet_never_loses_typed_work`); the Mac's Next album applying again in place
  of stepping (`test_apply_moves_on_and_its_fine_marks_this_album_alone_on_the_mac`).
- **It's fine clearing other albums' issues**: markFine posting the scan's first album's folder
  (`test_apply_moves_on_and_its_fine_marks_this_album_alone_on_the_mac`); a mark told of one album marking every row of
  the session (Core's `rowChanged` - `itsFineMarksOnlyTheAlbumItIsFor`).
- **The strip's count and the tab badge counting different things**: All counting every album scanned (Core's
  `facets` - `theStripAndTheBadgeCountTheSameAlbums`, `test_the_strip_and_the_badge_count_the_same_albums`); the Mac's
  status bar counting `albums.count` (the same two, and `itsFineMarksOnlyTheAlbumItIsFor`).
- **The flat rule**: a card given a face (`.background(DWPalette.card)`) and the open row shaded again
  (`listRowBackground(Palette.accent)`) - `test_the_phones_page_is_flat_and_drawn_as_iNeedsALook` (R1c's `drawn()`
  over the page's phone path; test_ios_phone_look's own flat test reads only App/Look and App/Phone, so R10's table row
  for this file - "none yet" - is held now).
- **The holding rules**: the Mac's step over typed work unasked, a facet over typed work unasked, a facet mid-apply
  (`test_stepping_on_the_mac_never_loses_typed_work`); the sheet's step over typed work unasked
  (`test_stepping_in_the_sheet_never_loses_typed_work`); the phone's Skip past the gate
  (`test_the_sheets_queue_bar_is_above_the_foot`).
- **The host**: both pages drawing the editor (`macEdit(on:)` ignoring its host), and the Mac's opening outliving the
  Run (closeEditor's `macEditEnded` dropped) - `test_the_mac_edit_is_drawn_on_one_page_its_host`.
- **The typing rule**: none - this slice draws no field.

### After review

The review's findings, each fixed in this one commit with its test and the mutation that undoes it (each applied alone
to the worktree, the named check run, the file put back - every one caught; test_ios_needs_look_look unless named, Core's
under `swift test --filter`):

1. **⌘R stranded the editor.** The page's ⌘R (`pulled()`) read the library whenever it was online, so a read of the
   page's begun while the editor's was out - its first, just after a row was picked, or the one after an Apply - took
   over: the editor's came back `.dropped`, its look-up did nothing and it waited for good (Apply off, the steps dimmed,
   no Look again). Two parts, both in Core so `swift test` drives them. **⌘R asks nothing while a session lasts or a
   read is out** (`NeedsLookPage.pullReads`, as Try again and a sign-in again were already held): the editor reads the
   queue's scan and says its own Look again, and the list is read again as the run ends. And **a look-up carries its read
   to an answer** (`ScanReads`, the scan's tickets now - LibraryScanModel's `reads`; `readShared` is the editor's
   look-up's read, EditAlbumModel.lookUp): a read a newer one took over waits for that one's end, and one that came to
   nothing (a read cancelled with its page) is asked again, once (`ScanReads.tries`); a look-up called off with its own
   page stays dropped, as before, and `reopen()` asks as the page comes back. The page's own reads and rescans take
   their tickets from the same ScanReads, so only the newest lands, as before. ScanReadsTests drives ⌘R mid-read and
   ⌘R just after a row is picked over a network whose every answer the test gives; NeedsLookPageTests'
   `aPullIsHeldWhileAReadIsOutOrASessionLasts` the rule; `test_a_refresh_never_strands_the_editor` the wiring.
   Mutations: pullReads' `!session` dropped (`aPullIsHeld…`, `aRefreshJustAfterPickingARowNeverStrandsTheEditor`)
   and its `!reading` dropped (`aPullIsHeld…`, `aRefreshMidReadNeverStrandsTheEditor`); the model's pull passing
   either as false (the source test); `answer` not waiting - returning its own `.dropped` (three of ScanReadsTests) -
   and the ask-again removed (`aRefreshJustAfterPicking…`); `end(after:)` answering nil for an ended newer read in place
   of its end (`aReadThatTookOverAndLandedFirstIsTheEditorsAnswer`); lookUp back on `scan.read()` (the source test).
2. **It's fine needs Edit albums too**, on the Mac as on the phone: the phone offers it in the Release tab's Needs a
   look section, drawn only with Edit albums (`edit.editors`), and with Look after the library (`AlbumEdit.marksFine`);
   the Mac's foot asked marksFine alone, so a person with Look after the library and not Edit albums had It's fine on
   every tab. Now both read `NeedsLookPage.offersFine` (`Managing.albumEdit(...).editors && AlbumEdit.marksFine(...)`),
   NeedsLookPageTests' `itsFineNeedsEditAlbumsToo` over every set of permissions. Mutation: offersFine's `.editors`
   dropped (that test); the foot asking marksFine alone again
   (`test_its_fine_needs_edit_albums_on_the_mac_as_on_the_phone`).
3. **A refused mark was said only on the Release tab** - and never for a person without Edit albums, who has no Release
   tab. In queue mode the foot says `markFailure` over its buttons, on every tab; the Release tab's own says it only
   outside queue mode (the one note drawn, never two). Mutation: the foot's failure removed
   (`test_a_refused_mark_is_said_on_every_tab_in_queue_mode`).
4. **The window's counts disagreed after It's fine.** The status bar read the live scan; the pop-up's counts and Marked
   fine · N were the session's, held as it began - so after It's fine the status bar said one more marked fine and the
   pop-up and Marked fine did not, until the run ended. `NeedsLookPage.counted` keeps the facets the session draws
   (its albums stay its own) and gives each the live scan's count, Marked fine last, a facet whose albums have all gone
   dropped unless it is All or the pressed one. The model's `chips` and `pressedChip` are those, so the phone's strip
   and Marked fine follow the same way. NeedsLookPageTests' `afterItsFineTheStatusBarThePopUpAndMarkedFineAgree` and
   `theFacetsDrawnAreTheSessionsCountedLive`; mutations: `counted` returning what the session holds (both), the model's
   `chips` the session's again (`test_every_count_the_window_shows_reads_the_live_scan`).
5. **The queue foot was cut at the narrowest editors.** One HStack of It's fine, the line and the tab's actions did not
   fit an editor of 378 (1280 with the side panel open) - the line went first. The foot now takes the first of three
   ways that fits (`ViewThatFits`, MacEditFooter's `queued`): the line whole beside It's fine and the actions; the line
   over It's fine and the actions; the line, It's fine and the actions each a line of their own. The line is never
   given a line limit: whole on one line in the first way (`fixedSize()`), wrapping in the others (measured as nothing
   wide - `idealWidth: 0` - so the way chosen is the one whose buttons fit), its whole on the pointer (`.help`) and to
   VoiceOver. The widths are worked out with the bundled faces (tests/ios_fonts.py) in
   `test_the_queue_foot_fits_every_editor`: the editor 661 at the window's opening, 379 at its smallest, 378 with the
   panel open; It's fine 116 (Marking it fine… no wider), Revert 62, Next album › 96, Apply to all 1,234 tracks 165,
   Delete permanently 140; Release on one line needs 566 (so the opening's 661 draws it as before), the line over the
   buttons 339, every tab's last way 275 at most. The foot is 48 with one line of buttons (11 over and under the 26),
   taller only when it wraps. Mutations: the last way removed, and the line given `lineLimit(1)` (that test).
6. **EditAlbumSheet's docs**: EditQueueBar's and ReadAgainFailed's back on their own structs, the long line wrapped
   (`test_each_struct_keeps_its_own_doc`).
7. **R10's `.onChange(of: navigation.macEdit?.queue?.nav == nil)` in MacEditWindow is removed**: closeEditor covers
   every path. Every session end with the editor up - a step to an album gone, a facet chosen - goes through `carry`
   with `close`, and closeEditor ends the Mac's opening whenever it is this queue's, whichever page hosts it (a queue
   opening asked over another page's work included); every other end (macEditEnded, another opening, a sign-out's
   reset) lets the opening go before it tells the page (`editorClosed`), so the handler's own guard could never hold -
   it was dead. `test_the_queues_end_is_said_where_the_run_decides_it` and test_ios_edit_look's pin read it gone, and
   closeEditor's call; R10's mutation (closeEditor's `macEditEnded` dropped) is still caught by
   `test_the_mac_edit_is_drawn_on_one_page_its_host`.
8. **Mutations that survived, now caught**: the status bar's marked-fine count counting any album with an ignore (the
   fixture gains an album with one issue ignored and one not - NeedsLookPageTests' `theStripAndTheBadgeCountTheSame
   Albums`, `itsFineMarksOnlyTheAlbumItIsFor` and `afterItsFine…`); `step(to:)` cut to its sign (steps of 2, 3 and -3
   now - `aRowPickedDuringASessionIsAStepToIt`); the Mac bar's ‹ and Skip
   › no longer dimmed by `canStep` (`test_the_macs_queue_bar_waits_for_the_step_gate`); the selection not cleared as
   the session ends, nor after an open refused, nor following a step (`test_the_macs_page_keeps_its_selection_on_the_
   session`); the rows not off during a write (the same); and Needs a look's album cell now among the Mac's tables'
   covers in test_ios_readout_rows (FolderCover in its COVERS, the page's `cell(` in its CELL_BUILDERS) - a cover moved
   out of its title's HStack is caught there.

Older pins moved with the code: test_ios_edit's cancellation (a read's is `fetch`'s now, both readers through it),
test_ios_library_care's rescan (ticketed by the one ScanReads) and test_ios_needs_look's pull (its guard Core's
`pullReads`). The words: no fixture changed; docs/ios.md's 590 and 591 say ⌘R with an album open, the foot at the
narrowest window, the counts agreeing at once and It's fine needing Edit albums.

## The redesign, slice R13: Library care and the Event log (2026-11-25)

The Mac redesign's build plan (~/Desktop/Code/deadwax-plans/mac-redesign-build.md), 3.4's R13: Library care and the
event log, each in its own look on each device - the Mac's toolbar and boxes (LibraryCare.dc.html, EventLog.dc.html),
the phone's flat pages (iLibraryCare, iEventLog), in ~/Desktop/Code/deadwax-plans/mac-redesign/. Built on ed819e69
(R9). The app is still 0.13 (13); `__version__` untouched; no server data new (no diff to Core's DeadwaxClient or
Routes, nor App/Shared/Routes.swift - R10's in this wave); no engine file touched. **The runs are unchanged**: still
CareRunModel's, driven from the client one album at a time, Stop ending a run after the album under way (CareRuns'
`stop` and `next`, not touched), and a Get fetches what the album's own Get in Edit album does - it applies, retags
or chooses nothing.

### The phone (iLibraryCare, iEventLog)

- **Library care** (LibraryCareScreen) is a SettingsPage - flat groups on the page's black, the large title. Its
  **Rescan** group: Rescan's words (Core's `rescanWords`, as before), then **Rescan the library** - a flat button - with
  the scan's facts beside it on its first baseline, in the readout face and t3, their age moving on (TimelineView), and
  a read again that failed under them. (After review: the drawing's short facts, "140 albums · 2 min ago" - Core's
  `shortFacts` - the whole line VoiceOver's; and Try again under its words at the accessibility sizes.) Its **Covers, CD art and lyrics** group: **Narrow to** (DWFieldRow with a
  DWField - a box: anywhere you type keeps its face), what the runs act on, and one row per kind (iLibraryCare's
  `.go`): its name (62 wide at least), what its Get would take, short ("14 albums without a cover", "Every matched
  album has its cover", Checking the library… while the scan isn't one to trust - Core's `rowLine`), and **Get · 14**;
  while its run goes, a meter (DWMeter, the sunken track) and "4 of 14 · Post · Björk" in the readout face (`runLine`:
  the album being fetched, as Stop says it, and that album; the count alone between two albums), and **Stop**, then
  **Stopping…** (dimmed) once pressed. The waiting line ("One run at a time - …") and the run's result stay under the
  row. Under the group, `runsNote`: "One album at a time, and nothing else about an album changes. The screen stays on
  while a run is under way and this page shows." VoiceOver reads a row once - its name, its line or where its run is
  (`spokenRow`), the waiting line and the result - with the long words (`note`) its hint and Get's or Stop's whole
  words (`startLabel`, `stopLabel`) its actions. **The collection** (with logins on, for Look after the library):
  **In nobody's library** and **Flagged downloads**, each with its count (DWCount), both opening In nobody's library's
  page - Flagged downloads has no page of its own (that would be a route, and App/Shared/Routes.swift is R10's).
- **In nobody's library** (HeldByNobodyScreen) is a SettingsPage too: its group (the line, the albums on the
  hairlines, Show all) and **Flagged downloads** (each flag its name, who asked, why; **Add for them** the purple one,
  small, and **Dismiss** flat). The model (HeldModel, Held.Flow's one write at a time) is unchanged.
- **The event log** (EventLogScreen): the bar holds the **chip** (Connecting…, Live, Reconnecting…, Not live - Core's
  `chipWords`; Live green, Reconnecting… amber, VoiceOver its whole words), **Copy** (every line shown, "Copied 6
  lines" said) and **Clear** (its hint `clearHint`: "Empties this view only - deadwax keeps its lines, and new ones
  still come."). Under it the **level strip** (PhoneStrip): Everything, Warnings 2, Errors 1 - each with the count of
  the lines it would show (`stripWords`, Core's `count`); **Warnings shows the errors too** (`shows`: any level but
  info). Then the problem in red with Try again, as before, and the lines: time, level and part each in the readout
  face on one first baseline, the words under them in the body face (red for an error, amber for a warning), the row's
  hairline (iEventLog's 9 over, 10 under). "Nothing logged yet." / "No warnings or errors in this view." when none
  shows. A line's long press still has Copy, VoiceOver's actions too. **The old line under the bar is gone** (the

  chip says where the feed stands and Clear's hint what Clear does. The model (EventLogModel, EventStream) is

The review's ten findings, each fixed in the same commit, each with its test and the mutation that undoes it (scratchpad
r13-review-mutate.py on a copy, r13-core-review-mutate.py in Core; every one caught - tests/test_ios_care_look.py unless
named):

   `test_the_chip_in_the_bar_stops_growing_at_xxxlarge` (the widths from ios_fonts: fits at xLarge, not at xxLarge,
   fits the page capped, what the cap stops); mutations: the cap removed, the chip in the bar at every size, in the bar
   to xxxLarge, none under the bar.

   its_own_kind` compares every `care.stop`/`care.start` argument per view - the row's `kind`, the toolbar's

## The redesign, slice R14: People and Server settings (2026-11-25)

The Mac redesign's build plan (~/Desktop/Code/deadwax-plans/mac-redesign-build.md), 3.4's R14, checks 598-602. The
drawings are People.dc.html and ServerSettings.dc.html (the Mac's), iPerson.dc.html and iServerSettings.dc.html (the
phone's, flat), with iArtists.dc.html's rows for People's list. Built on ed819e69 (wave D merged). The app is still
0.13 (13); `__version__` untouched; no server data new (no diff to Core at all, nor to App/Shared/Routes.swift); no
engine file touched. Nothing that is sent changed: the ticks as the boxes show them (all five, the flow's draft), a
revert as an explicit `null` (Core's SettingUpdate), People unlocked with the admin's own Navidrome password, a secret's
field a SecureField showing its placeholder and never its value.

### The phone (iPerson, iServerSettings)

- **People** (PeopleScreen) is a ScrollView, no List: PeopleStatus (the first read's spinner, why People can't work
  here, Unlock People), then the unlocked line, the version note, what the list's last write said, **Everyone in
  Navidrome** as a PhoneGroup of iArtists' rows (PersonRow: LibraryListRow with the person's initial on a round 44,
  their name, PeopleFacts.line - the user name and chips - under it, LibraryChevron; one VoiceOver element of the name,
  that line, their sign-ins, their library and the no-library warning), and Known only to deadwax (each name on the row
  hairline with Forget…). Lock and + stay in the bar.

  admin or No longer admin beside it, under it from xxxLarge), what was said, **Permissions** as the purple switches
  (`Toggle(isOn: people.ticked(...))` and `settingsSwitch()`) with **no lines under them** - each line is the switch's
  VoiceOver hint; a tick's warning stays in amber - then the locked reason and the admins' line, **Account** as PhoneGo
  rows (Reset password…, Remove… in red) and the refusals. **Revert** and **Save permissions** are PhoneFoot's
  (PersonFoot), only for an ordinary person People saves permissions for. Revert (PeopleRevert) puts each switch back as

  (each tab's mark in its words: "Library · Needs attention") over the chosen tab's **group rows** (PhoneGo, a chip for a

- **A group's page**: a **SettingCard** per setting on the page's black - its name in the readout face (hidden from
  VoiceOver: the control says it), its control (SettingControl: Locked, a menu Picker, or a field), its chips
  (SettingChips: the source - Set here in purple, From the container environment plain - Unsaved, Needs attention; a dot

### Why the phone's cards stay on the group pages

iServerSettings draws the cards on the root under the strip. They stay on each group's own page instead: the model
counts its pages (`shows(.group(id))`) to read the saved answers while their page is shown and to keep the screen awake
for Re-time, and Set up Navidrome is the Connections group page itself. Drawing every card on the root would need the
model's accounting changed - a ServerSettingsModel diff, not in this slice. The Mac's page tells the model the same way
for the groups it draws (below).

### The Mac (People.dc.html, ServerSettings.dc.html)

- **People** (MacPeoplePage, for `.people` and `.person(id)`): the toolbar's **Add a person…** (purple) and **Lock**, only

  People with the admin's own password - PeopleField, the Mac's own field there). Unlocked, a MacColumnList at the left (398 at most,
