The review found nothing wrong in what is sent (the ticks, Revert's null, secrets, the unlock, Remove's guard, Add and
Reset), but two layout bugs, a broken rule and tests that let most of the slice's own choices change unseen. Each fix,
then what was left as it was:

  Playlists page leaves Whose and Changed out). At 1060 all three at every size; at 660 and 659 Person and Role; at 589
  Person and Role at Small, Person alone at Medium and Large. The Person cell's help says it all - display name, user
  name, role, sign-ins - and the name holds its line before the user name (`layoutPriority`), which is cut in its middle.
- **Buttons that don't fill never wrap.** DWButtonStyle (App/Look's, untouched) holds a button that doesn't fill to one
  line, so a line limit on its words does nothing. ManageWrapButton (ServerSettingsGroupScreen) draws a button as it was
  while it fits, else across its row (`fills`), its words (ManageButtonWords) as many lines as they take on the phone -
  the innermost line limit holds - and on the Mac one line cut at its end, the whole in its help (a Mac button is 26
  tall). Re-time's running button (some 354 at the default size), Re-time saved lyrics (351 at AX3), Clear MusicBrainz's
  saved answers (373 at xxxLarge) and Revert to the environment with what it brings back (337 at the default size, 487 at

## Last.fm, slice A2 (2026-11-26)

Last.fm's second app slice, **A2** of ~/Desktop/Code/deadwax-plans/lastfm.md (2.5's `similar` and `top_albums`, 3.1,
3.3's order menu, 3.4, 3.6-3.8, section 4's A2, checks 490-493): **Similar Artists** under an artist's albums and the
albums' **Most played** order, on the iPhone and the Mac alike. The server's half is S4, main's **2.1.43** (notes/lastfm.md
"S4"), already on this branch: the same `GET /deadwax/lastfm/artist`, its answer carrying both, so nothing new is asked.
Not in it: Start Radio and Autoplay (A3), About (A4). What it leaves alone:
- src/ and ui/ are untouched; the app is still 0.13 (13); **ios/Deadwax.xcodeproj is untouched** (the three new App files
  in the synchronized folder, the Core files and tests found by folder). Core's `DeadwaxClient` and `Routes` are
  untouched too: the answer decodes from the route A1 calls (the route count stays 111).
- **The engine files have no diff**, nor does anything of DeadwaxAudio's. Nothing plays differently.
- Of Routes.swift only the one case and its line in `appRoutes`; nothing of Edit album's, Needs a look's or Manage's
  (R11's).

### James's decision (26 Nov): "Your most played"

The Mac artist page's songs section under the discography (MostPlayedSongs - the songs of theirs YOU have played most,
by Navidrome's counts) was "Most played"; A2's menu brings an albums order called "Most played" (Last.fm's plays,
everyone's). Two "Most played"s on one page, meaning different things, is the confusion James ruled out: the songs
section is **"Your most played"** everywhere it is shown or spoken (`ArtistPageFacts.Words.yourMostPlayed`, replacing
`.mostPlayed`; docs/ios.md's mentions, check 560 included), and the menu keeps the plan's words - **"Sort albums"** its
label, **"Newest first" | "Most played"** its orders (`LastfmWords.sortAlbums`, `.newestFirst`, `.mostPlayed`). Each
lives once, in Core's words.

### What was built

**Core (pure, tested on Linux and macOS):**
- `Lastfm.swift`: `LastfmArtist.similar` and `.topAlbums`, read as loosely as the rest (`looseList`: absent, null or
  not a list is nil, `[]` none listed). `LastfmSimilarArtist` (src/lastfm.py `_similar_entry`): a name needed (one
  missing or blank is dropped), the `mbid` only of MusicBrainz's shape (`MBID.of`, so trimmed and lowercased), `match`
  only 0-1 (lastfm.py `similarity`), `url` only Last.fm's (`LastfmLink`). `LastfmAlbum` (lastfm.py `top_albums`): a
  title, a count (never negative - `LastfmArtist.count`) and its kind, `Counted` - `plays` or `listeners`, lastfm.py
  COUNTED's two; an album missing any, or of a kind this app doesn't know, is dropped.
- `AlbumPlays.swift` (new): `AlbumOrder` (`newest`, `played`; UserDefaults `deadwax-artist-album-order`, read with care -
  anything but `played` is newest); `counted` (the answer's albums of the FIRST album's kind - plays are never set beside
  listeners - nil for none); `offered`; `of` (each row's plays by its key: an album of yours by Last.fm's `mbid` equal to
  the album's `musicBrainzId`, a release's, else by `Fold.key` of its title; one of theirs by its group's folded title,
  since Last.fm's ids are releases', not groups'; several on one row give the LARGEST, never a sum; 0 is none);
  `ordered` (the rows with plays first, most first, ties and the rest in the order given - newest first - none added,

  again as each album's songs land); `Visit` (which albums the visit orders by: `drawn` judges once, `reopen` for a

### Decisions, and where this departs from the plan

- **The order is judged once per visit** (`AlbumPlays.Visit`): an answer later than the page's 0.8 s wait leaves the
  albums newest first for the visit - Most played stored or not - and the menu ticks what is drawn (Newest first); the
  stored choice isn't changed. Choosing Most played then orders them at once (the person asked them to move); a pull
  judges the next answer. The plan's rule was only "never re-sort under a finger"; this is its reading.
- **The menu's room is held** (hidden, inert) while Most played isn't offered but the hero's line is drawn - an answer
  may yet bring albums by plays - so the heading's end doesn't change as it comes. With Last.fm off there's no menu and
  no room.
- **The phone's menu is the glyph**, a flat small button; **the Mac's is a pop-up showing the order** ("Newest first"),
  as a Mac pop-up shows its value. The same items (`AlbumOrderItems`) in both.
- **Plays never sum, and never mix**: "Currents" and "Currents (B-Sides)" (one row, `Fold.key` dropping the aside) give
  the larger; a list's kind is its first album's, and an album of the other kind is left out.
- **Theirs (MusicBrainz's rows) match by title only**: Last.fm's ids are releases', a MusicBrainz row is a release group.
- **A similar artist with two library artists of their folded name is no match** ("Low" and "LOW"): drawn as theirs
  (if Last.fm has an id), never guessed at. **One without an id who isn't yours is left out**: it has nowhere to open.
- **Theirs get no picture looked up**: the person glyph, as the plan says - no Wikidata or TheAudioDB ask per tile.
- **The tiles wait for the library's artists** (asked if not in hand) for 1.5 s at most - from the ask, since the
  review - the row's room held blank, so
  a tile of yours isn't drawn as theirs only to change; a failed list draws every tile as theirs.
- **On the Mac, Similar Artists is the page's last section**, after Your most played: that list is about these albums,
  Similar Artists leads away from the artist - as on the phone, where it is last too.
- **On the Mac the plays sit in the In your library cell**, not a column of their own (a column only Most played order
  fills would be empty most of the time). They fit at 660; at the narrowest page (589, beside the side panel) the cell's
  format gives way first, the plays carried in full by `.help` and VoiceOver.
- **Tile sizes**: the phone's a ScaledMetric of 112 relative to footnote ("Not in your library" measures 106.9 at 13 pt -
  it fits), so it grows with the text - never past the page (since the review); the Mac's a fixed 112 (the Mac's faces are the drawings' fixed sizes,
  Typeface.Mac), which puts four in view at the 589 page.
- **No right-click on a tile**: a tile has no •••, and on the Mac right-click is exactly the ••• items.

`LastfmWords.newestFirst` "Newest first", `LastfmWords.mostPlayed` "Most played", `LastfmWords.plays(1)` "1 play",
`LastfmWords.plays(4123456)` "4.1M plays", `LastfmWords.plays(4123456, listeners)` "4.1M listeners",
`ArtistPageFacts.yourMostPlayed` "Your most played". `ArtistPageFacts.Words.mostPlayed` is gone from the code (it had no
key in either snapshot). DeviceWordsTests adds the eight.

### After review (2026-11-26)

A2's review found eight faults and five nits. Each fix is in the same one commit (still on d18c45a2, as before).

1. **On the phone, Most played's plays were cut off the end of the row.** A row's line is one line
   (LibraryListRow's `.lineLimit(lines)`), and a 375-point phone leaves it about 271 points at the default size: 375,
   less the page's 2 x 16, the 44 cover, the text's 2 x 10 and the chevron. With the plays last, "2012 · in the
   collection · 2 pressings · 65M plays" outgrew that at the default size, and nearly every row did at xxxLarge.
   **The plays now lead the line** ("4.1M plays · 2015 · in your library", `Shown.line`), so only a line's tail is
   ever cut. **At the accessibility sizes a row with plays takes two lines** (`Shown.lines(_:accessibility:)`, through
   LibraryListRow's own `lines`; LibraryTiles is untouched): at AX5 even "9.9M listeners" outgrows a line.
   `test_most_played_plays_are_never_the_part_cut` measures with ios_fonts' Libre Franklin at footnote's 13, 19, 33
   and 44 points, using the reviewed worst lines and the widest words `LastfmWords.plays` makes:
   - at 13 and 19 the plays and an ellipsis fit one line;
   - at AX3 the plays fit the first of the two lines whole;
   - at AX5 each word and an ellipsis fits a line;
   - in the old order, the worst lines' plays fall past the room at all three of the first sizes.
   The widest words are "999M listeners" and its kin: `short` gives a decimal only under 10 of a unit, so 65.3M is
   "65M", never "65.3M". On the Mac the plays stay at the end of In your library, kept whole by `layoutPriority`.
2. **The name fallback ignored a conflicting id.** A similar artist Last.fm has one MusicBrainz id for, and an artist
   of yours with another id and the same name, were matched by name. Now **a name matches only where one side has no
   id**: two ids that differ are two artists, whatever their names (`Library.match`). This corrects lastfm.md 3.4's
   wording ("by MusicBrainz id, else by folded name"), which read as though the name settles it whenever the ids
   don't agree. Tests: `idsThatDifferAreTwoArtistsWhateverTheName` (Nirvana, the US band and the UK one) and
   `byNameOnlyWhereOneSideHasNoId` (theirs without an id, and yours without one).
3. **Similar Artists' 1.5 s wait began when the page opened** (R6's `ownedWaited`, which counts from `.task`'s start).
   So a list Last.fm brought late found the wait long over, and tiles of yours could be drawn as theirs and then
   change. Now the tiles have **their own wait (`similarWaited`), begun in the same task that asks for the library's
   artists**: an `async let` ask, the 1.5 s from that moment, and the task waits for the ask too. With nothing to ask
   (the list in hand, or deadwax out of reach) there is no wait. See All's page does the same in one task (its
   separate timer is gone).
4. **`AlbumPlays.Made` compares the visit's albums**: `theListIsMadeAgainForTheVisitsAlbums` (the same rows and choice,
   new albums, a new order).
5. **`Visit.reopen` keeps the albums in hand** until the pull's answer judges them: `aPullKeepsTheAlbumsInHandUntilItsAnswer`.
6. **Whether Most played was offered and which order was drawn read different answers.** Offered read the model's
   answer, while the order drawn read the visit's albums. A later answer missing `top_albums` hid the menu while the
   rows stayed in Most played order. Two fixes:
   - **An answer is kept part by part** (`LastfmArtist.keeping(_:)`): a later answer's missing part never replaces one
     in hand. The model keeps the merged answer, and so does the session's Kept.
   - **Offered reads what the order reads**: `Visit.offers` (the visit's albums, else the answer in hand's), through
     `ArtistPageModel.albumsOffered(page:kept:)`. Before the page is begun it reads the session's kept answer, as
     `visitAlbums` does.
   Tests: `mostPlayedIsOfferedWhileTheRowsAreInItsOrder`, `aLaterAnswersMissingPartsNeverTakeAwayWhatIsDrawn` and
   `anAnswerIsKeptPartByPart`.
7. **At AX5 a tile was wider than the page**: the ScaledMetric of 112 grows to about 379, and the phone's page is 343.
   Each place a tile is drawn measures its width (`onGeometryChange`: the row's section, and See All's grid inside its
   sides), and the side is `SimilarArtists.side(scaled, page:)`, the smaller of the two. It still grows with the text,
   so at AX5 the grid is one column. Tests: `aTileNeverOutgrowsThePage` and `test_a_tile_is_never_wider_than_the_page`.
8. **"Newest first" couldn't be chosen while a visit was drawn Newest first with Most played stored.** A Picker never
   sets the value it already shows, so the next artist opened in Most played anyway. **The items are two Toggles** (a
   menu's checkmark items, the drawn one ticked), and every tap chooses its own order, the ticked one's too. The pin
   is `AlbumOrderItems`' whole body, with no Picker left in the file.

**The nits:**
- **Fold keys are `FoldKey`** (UTF-16 units, as the rest of Core compares them) in `SimilarArtists.Library` and
  `AlbumPlays.of`. After Fold's NFKD the difference from String's comparison can't be observed with real names, so
  the rule is pinned by source.
- **A dimmed tile of theirs says why it does nothing**: its VoiceOver value is "Opens once deadwax is back"
  (`LastfmWords.opensOnceBack`, a new key in both iphone.json and mac.json, by hand; DeviceWordsTests adds it).
- **Two artists of yours with one id: the first wins**, as `ArtistJoin.claimed` keeps the first by release id
  (`twoLibraryArtistsWithOneIdGiveTheFirst`).
- **The visit's timing is Core's**: `LastfmVisit` takes A1's arrival and the albums' `Visit` together, event by event
  - begun, unasked, asking(pulled:), answered, waited, chose - and ArtistPageModel only reports each event where it
  happens. Its behaviour is tested: `anAnswerInsideTheWaitOrdersTheAlbums`, `anAnswerAfterTheWaitLeavesThemNewestFirst`,
  `onlyAPullJudgesAgain` and `aKeptAnswerOrNoAskDrawsTheAlbumsAtOnce`.
- The other nits' mutations are below, each now caught.

**Tests now:** AlbumPlaysTests 19 (was 10), SimilarArtistsTests 12 (was 8), tests/test_ios_lastfm_a2.py 15 (was 13).
test_ios_artist_look.py's rows pin takes `lines: lines`.

**test_ios_contract.py's Last.fm test was slow**, found on the full suite's rerun. It took about 25 minutes, because
A2's exported answers hold some 450 similar artists and albums, and each was checked with `fields()` read afresh
(three reads each, every read parsing all of DeadwaxCore, about 1.1 s). Now it reads each struct once, and
`assert_decodes` takes the read, so it runs in 9 s with the same assertions. Seen biting: LastfmAlbum's `mbid` made
required fails it, both at the field list and, with that loosened, at the decode ("LastfmAlbum needs ['mbid']").

**Each fault applied alone, its tests run, the file restored and `cmp`'d** (the Swift ones under
AlbumPlaysTests, SimilarArtistsTests, LastfmDecodeTests and LastfmPageTests, and every one under A2's Python tests):
- 1, the plays back at the line's end: `newestFirstIsThePagesOwnWithNothingAtTheEnds`,
  `test_most_played_plays_are_never_the_part_cut`. One line at every size (`lines` always 1): the same two. The rows

## Last.fm, slice A3 (2026-11-26)

Last.fm's third app slice, **A3** of ~/Desktop/Code/deadwax-plans/lastfm.md (2.6, 3.5-3.8, section 4's A3, checks
494-502, section 7, and section 8's binding answer: **Autoplay is off by default**): **Start Radio** and **Autoplay**,
on the iPhone and the Mac alike. The server's half is S5, main's **2.1.44** (notes/lastfm.md "S5"), already on this
branch: `GET /deadwax/lastfm/radio`, the songs of the asker's scope Last.fm calls similar to a song, the whole list at
once. Not in it: About (A4). What it leaves alone:
- src/ and ui/ are untouched; the app is still 0.13 (13); **ios/Deadwax.xcodeproj is untouched** (the new App file in
  the synchronized folder, the Core file and the tests found by folder).
- **No diff to DeadwaxAudio, App/AudioSessionController.swift or the engine**: a station's songs reach the engine as
  Add to Queue's do, through QueueController's edit path (`replaceUpcoming`, held for a join).
- **UpNext.swift and QueueController.swift gain one function each, additively** (`withStation`, `appendStation`); no
  existing function changed, so UpNextTests, UpNextTraceTests and UpNextPropertyTests - the web-traced vectors - run
  as they were.
- `DeadwaxClient` grows by one route, `lastfmRadio(songId:title:artist:scope:)` (the count 111 to 112), its answer
  `LastfmRadio`, read loosely.
- Nothing of R12's (NeedsLookScreen, EditAlbumSheet's queue bar, MacNeedsALook, App/Shared/Routes.swift).

### What was built

**Core (pure, tested on Linux and macOS):**
- `Station.swift` (new): `Station` - `kind` (`radio`, Start Radio's, its songs the list itself; `autoplay`, begun at a
  queue's end from its LAST entry), `seed`, `queueId` (UpNextState.id: a station belongs to its queue), `songs` (the
  answer's, at most `most` 100), `next` (where `take` stopped), `asks`, `asking`, `failure` (the entry playing as it
  failed, and when), and Autoplay's `added` (the ids it gave) and `floor` (the queue's next key as it first gave any).
  `lowWater` 2, `batch` 10, `tries` 3, `againSeconds` 30. `radio(_:)` and `autoplay(_:)` make one of a queue; `Ask` -
  the id, title and artist, trimmed as the route trims them (`PyText.strip`), nil for one missing or past the route's
  limits (ID_MAX 256, WORDS_MAX 500), so a 422 is never asked for; `mayAsk(playing:now:)` (no answer yet, none out,
  under three asks, and after a failure another entry playing or 30 s gone); `againAt`; `began()`; `answered(_:playing:
  now:)` - `.songs`, `.nothing` (`[]`, a definite nothing) or `.failed` (no answer, or `songs` null); `exhausted`;
  `take(_:here:)` - the next ten from the pointer, never a song the queue holds (by id, History's included, or by
  `SongTitle.key(title)` and `Fold.key(artist)`), never the seed (even once the queue lacks it), and with `here` given
  (offline) only songs on the device; every song looked at passed for good, so one taken out of the Queue isn't added
  back - but (after review) one passed only for not being on the device kept in `later`, looked at first by the next
  take, and counted by `exhausted`. `wantsMore(_:mode:lastfm:station:autoplay:)` - Last.fm on, Repeat Off, not a
  library's shuffle, a song playing, a station of this queue's or Autoplay on, and `following` (after review: every
  entry after the one playing but Repeat One's copies) at `lowWater` or under. `inList` (after review) - a radio's,
  or Autoplay's once it has given songs: what dims Shuffle. Autoplay's `start` (after review) - the source's count as
  it first gave, what turning it off takes out from. `split(_:_:_:)` - the Queue's list
  as the list's own rows under their own title (the source less Autoplay's songs: "From Mezzanine", not "Still to
  play") and Autoplay's, the list's tail: the longest run at its end of `.source` marks from `floor` on whose songs
  Autoplay gave; nothing split for a radio, another queue's station, a list with more than is drawn, or none; a list
  all Autoplay's is nil. (`autoplayKeys` went at review: withoutStation, from `start`, replaced it.)
  `Autoplay` - UserDefaults `deadwax-player-autoplay`, `on` alone on (`read`), `stored`.
- `UpNext.swift`: `withStation(_:_:_:)` - the songs at the end of this time round's list as the list's own (`source`
  grows; each mark `{key: nextKey + i, from: .source, at: the old source count + i, pass: the list's last song's}`;
  `nextKey` on), through `rebuilt` as withMore is; the same queue unless Repeat is Off, the queue has Up Next's account,
  a song playing and no `paged`, and there are songs. (After review) `withoutStation(_:from:)` - see "After review".
- `QueueController.swift`: `appendStation(_:)` - `edit { withStation($0, tracks, repeatMode) }`, an edit like Add to
  Queue's: held for a join in a song's last moments (D4) and made at the next tick, never a play. (After review)
  `removeStation(from:)` - `edit { withoutStation($0, from: start) }`, the same kind of edit.
- `Lastfm.swift`: `LastfmRadio` (`enabled` absent false, `unavailable` absent true, `why`, `songs` - `looseList`, a
  song without an id left out; null or not a list nil). `Routes.swift`: `lastfmRadio` (query `song_id`, `title`,
  `artist`, `scope`) with 30 s (`timeouts`: a cold scope's list is read a 2,000-song page at a time, and Last.fm's 4 s
  besides). `DeadwaxClient.swift`: `lastfmRadio(songId:title:artist:scope:)` - nothing asked without an `Ask`.
- `MacMenu.swift`: `State.lastfm`, `.autoplay`, `.station` (before `rowSize`, so MacCommands' state still ends with
  the Row Size store's); `Command.autoplay`, Controls' tick after Repeat's three while Last.fm is on (no key), enabled
  with something queued, ticked while on; Shuffle dimmed with a station while it is off.
- `LastfmWords.swift`: `startRadio` "Start Radio" (`dot.radiowaves.left.and.right`), `autoplay` "Autoplay"
  (`infinity`), `autoplayHint`, `autoplaySaid(_:)` ("Autoplay on" / "Autoplay off"), `noSimilarSongs`, `radioFailed`.
  `Info.swift`: `NowPlayingWords.more(... radio:)` - ", start radio" after Go to album.

**App:**
- `Models/PlayerModel+Station.swift` (new): `StationKeeper` (the player's `stations`, made with it): the station, the
  setting (read from UserDefaults once, written on each change), the ask (`client.lastfmRadio` with the scope the
  Shuffle uses, `ShuffleOf.library.scope(library: AlbumScope.albums(for: server.me))`; never offline; a seed without
  an ask answered `[]` at once), the retry (a DispatchWorkItem at `againAt`), the notices (a radio's: "No similar songs

  held (the queue it would be made against isn't the one in hand), then `wantsMore` - Autoplay's station begun from the
  last entry, its next songs taken (offline, `downloads.isHere` only) and appended, or its answer asked for.
  `setAutoplay` off (after review): `letAutoplayGo()` - Autoplay's station dropped and `player.removeStation(from:
  start)` - a radio's never; while an edit is held, nothing yet, and `check()` makes it once the held edit has landed,
  before `wantsMore`. PlayerModel's `startRadio(_:)`: `play(playlist: [song], at: 0)` - the existing call, in the tap,
  nothing awaited - then `stations.radioStarted(song)` (the station of the queue that play made, its seed checked to
  be the song, asked at once). `autoplay`, `setAutoplay`, `hasStation` (`has`: this queue's station, `inList`),
  `stationHoldsShuffle` (after review: `hasStation && !shuffle` - what dims every Shuffle), `stationSplit`.
- `Models/PlayerModel.swift`: `stations`, attached in init and connected with the downloads and the reach;
  `appendStation(_:)` - PlaylistPlay.plan at the Normalization setting's songs level, the albums remembered as Add to

  controller.removeStation(from:) }`, as a removal is made.
- `Player/QueueMenu.swift`: `QueueMenuRequest.radioSong` - one song, not queued as an album, not a playlist's whole
  (`wholeList`); Start Radio after Add to a playlist… while Last.fm is on, deadwax is reached and the album isn't gone -

- `Player/NowPlayingMenu.swift`: Start Radio after Go to album for the song playing, on the same terms; the button's

- `UpNext/UpNextScreen.swift`: the phone's foot - Autoplay after Repeat, the flat DWButtonStyle button Shuffle's and

  the Mac's chips in a `ViewThatFits`: the three on one line, else Autoplay on a line of its own under Shuffle and
  Repeat (`shuffleChip`, `repeatChip`, `autoplayChip`, `chipGap` 8), capped at xxxLarge.
- `Shared/MacCommands.swift`: the state's `lastfm`, `autoplay`, `station`; the tick after Repeat's submenu; its click
  the chip's own call.
- `Player/NowPlayingView.swift`, `Player/PlayerBar.swift`: Shuffle dimmed with a station while off
  (`stationHoldsShuffle`), as for `paged` - one line each.
  Now Playing's is inside the transport R4b pinned, so test_ios_now_playing_look.py's `TRANSPORT_DIGEST` moves with
  it (noted beside it) - the one pinned thing this slice changes, for 3.5's "as it is for paged" and check 497.

### Decisions, and where this departs from the plan

- **Autoplay is off by default** (section 8, answer 1): `Autoplay.read` is on only for a stored `on`.
- **`lowWater` 2 counts entries after the one playing**, as 3.5 says; so Autoplay's rows appear on the album's
  THIRD-to-last song (two follow it). Check 496 said "on its second-to-last song" - the spec's off-by-one, decided at
  review: lowWater stays 2, and docs/ios.md's 496 now says "when two songs are left after the one playing".
- **Autoplay's rows are told by the songs it gave and a floor key**, not by recorded keys: an append held for a join
  is made later against the queue as it is then, so its keys can't be known as the songs are taken. A row of the
  list's own, or one added with Add to Queue (`.added`), is never Autoplay's.
- **Start Radio from Now Playing restarts the song**: 3.5's tap is `play(playlist: [song], at: 0)`, a new queue; the
  song plays from its start. Kept at review, and said plainly in docs/ios.md and check 494.
- **Shuffle is dimmed with a station on Now Playing, the Mac's player bar and Controls too**, not only the Queue's
  chip (3.5 names the chip, "as it is for paged" - and paged dims all four). Kept at review, with the digest redone -
  and (after review) only while Shuffle is off, and only once the station's songs are in the list.
- **The top-up waits while an edit is held**, and runs again as the held edit lands (the queue changes).
- ~~A song skipped offline is passed for good~~ (changed at review: kept for later - see "After review").
- **Start Radio is left out for an album gone from the collection** (`request.gone`), as Add to a playlist… is.
- **The notices**: "Couldn't start the radio just now." only on a radio's FIRST failed ask - the retries are quiet.
- **The radio's notice on a song with no ask** (a title or artist blank or too long) is "No similar songs in your
  library.": nothing can be asked, so nothing will come.
- **`withStation` takes the pass of the list's last song**, so after Repeat All was turned off mid-round the songs
  follow that round; it doesn't move History's start or anything before the end.

### Words added (iphone.json and mac.json, by hand, the same seven in each)

`LastfmWords.startRadio` "Start Radio", `LastfmWords.autoplay` "Autoplay", `LastfmWords.autoplayHint` "Keeps playing
similar songs from your library when the queue ends.", `LastfmWords.autoplaySaid(on)` "Autoplay on",
`LastfmWords.autoplaySaid(off)` "Autoplay off", `LastfmWords.noSimilarSongs` "No similar songs in your library.",
`LastfmWords.radioFailed` "Couldn't start the radio just now.". None says "Up Next": the word is Queue.

### After review (2026-11-26)

The review found no binding rule broken, and seven things to fix; rebased onto ios's eb119050 (R12 and Search's field,
no conflicts) first. Each fix, then each new fault made alone and seen failing, then restored:

1. **Medium - Autoplay off left its songs in `source`.** Its rows went (withoutKey, a row at a time) but withStation's
   `source += tracks` stayed: the heading turned "Still to play", Repeat All's line said "the list", and Repeat All
   turned on at the last song queued 1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3, r1, r2, r3. **Fixed with one more additive Core function,
   `withoutStation(_:from:)`** (UpNext.swift; no existing function changed, every existing vector as it was): every
   entry after the song playing's unit whose mark is the list's with `at >= start` goes with its copies (any round:
   turning Repeat on keeps Autoplay's rows, decided - they're queued songs - so turning Autoplay off afterwards takes
   the later rounds' too); then the source's tail from `start` down to the last item an entry left still plays (a
   played or playing Autoplay song keeps its place, and so does everything before it - nothing at or before the index
   changes); `left` loses what's past the new end; `reached`, if taken out, moves to the unit before it after the song
   playing; `nextKey` stays. `Station.start` (the source count as Autoplay first gave - only withStation grows a
   non-paged queue's source, and the take never runs while an edit is held, so the held append lands at that count),
   `QueueController.removeStation(from:)` and `PlayerModel.removeStation(from:)` carry it; `autoplayKeys` went.
   WithoutStationTests: the queue as it was before Autoplay (marks, source, `left`, the whole Queue view, Repeat All's
   "Then Mezzanine again from the top.", the next round 1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3 - and the review's bug shown, rows alone
   taken out leaving "Still to play" and r1-r3 in the next round), the song playing and its Repeat One copies kept,
   Repeat All's later rounds, rows swiped out before, a roll-back's furthest unit, and the same queue for each guard.
2. **Low-medium - one offline top-up used the whole answer up.** `take` now keeps a song passed only for not being on
   the device in `later`, looks at `later` first, and `exhausted` counts it; a song kept for later that the queue has
   since got is passed for good. `offlineOnlySongsOnTheDeviceAndTheRestKeptForLater` (back online r2 and r5 come
   first) and `oneOfflineTopUpNeverUsesTheAnswerUp` (100 songs, 2 on the device: not exhausted, the next take ten).
3. **Low - Autoplay off while its append was held** landed the held withStation as ten plain rows. `setAutoplay(false)`
   now only records the setting while `player.holdsAnEdit`; `check()` makes the removal (`letAutoplayGo`) once the held
   edit has landed - the watch sees the queue change - before `wantsMore`. Pinned (test_ios_lastfm_a3.py); the Core
   half (a removal is itself a held edit, made at the join, never a play) is AppendStationTests'
   `autoplayOffIsAnEditHeldForTheJoinAndNeverAPlay`.
4. **Low - `following` undercounted after a roll-back across Repeat All's rounds.** It now counts every mark after the
   index but Repeat One's copies (`wantsMore` asks only under Repeat Off). `aRollBackAcrossRoundsCountsWhatItMovedBackDown`:
   the second round playing, rolled back to the first round's song 2, Repeat off - four to come (it was one).
5. **Fit - the Mac Queue panel's chips.** Worked out with tests/ios_fonts.py: a chip is 12 a side, its symbol (1.3 em,
   taken wide), the Label's gap (8, taken wide) and its words in the medium face at the subheadline's size; the row is
   400 less the panel's 1-point edge, the inset list's 20 a side and the row's 20 a side: 319. At the Mac's size (15)
   the three need 367 with "Repeat one" (the review's ~365) and 337 even with "Repeat" - more than 319, and more than
   the 335 of 16-a-side margins too - so `modes` is now a `ViewThatFits`: the three on one line, else Shuffle and
   Repeat (243 at 15, 312 at xxxLarge with "Repeat one") with Autoplay on a line of its own, capped at xxxLarge as the
   phone's foot is. The chips read no Row Size (it sizes rows, not words). `test_the_macs_chips_take_two_lines_where_
   the_three_dont_fit` holds it at every size from xSmall to xxxLarge and every Repeat word. Not measured on the Mac.
6. **UX - Shuffle dimmed from the moment an Autoplay station was made**, and with Shuffle on it couldn't be turned off.
   Decided: `has` is true for a radio, or for Autoplay's station once it has added songs (`Station.inList`); and every
   Shuffle - the Queue's foot, its chip and `toggleShuffle`, Now Playing's, the Mac's player bar, Controls

## Last.fm, slice A4 (2026-11-26)

Last.fm's fourth app slice, **A4** of ~/Desktop/Code/deadwax-plans/lastfm.md (3.9, section 4's A4, checks 503-504):
**About** at the foot of an artist's page and an album's, on the iPhone and the Mac alike - "About", Wikidata's one
line, the paragraph at four lines with More / Less, and the link ("More on Last.fm", "From Wikipedia"). The server's
half was there already: `GET /deadwax/describe/artist` and `/album` (server 2.0.13, the web's descriptions), Last.fm's
words first since S3 (main's **2.1.42**, notes/lastfm.md "S3"). No server change was needed. What it leaves alone:
- src/ and ui/ are untouched; the app is still 0.13 (13); **ios/Deadwax.xcodeproj is untouched** (the two new App files
  in the synchronized folder, the Core files and tests found by folder).
- **The engine files have no diff**, nor does anything of DeadwaxAudio's or the player's (A3's files): About plays
  nothing.
- Of the files A3 shares, only A4's own entries: Routes.swift's two endpoints, their line in `all` and their two
  timeouts; DeadwaxClient's `describe(_:)`; ClientTests' count (A3's 112 to 114) and its timeouts
  table; the words fixtures' six keys; test_ios_contract.py's ROUTE_COUNT and one test.

### What was built

**Core (pure, tested on Linux and macOS):**
- `AboutBlock.swift` (new - Core's `About.swift` is Info's About already, so the plan's "Core `About`" is `AboutBlock`
  and `AboutWords`), the web's lib/describe.ts and app/useDescription.ts:
  - `DescribeAnswer`: the route's five fields, read loosely (a field of the wrong kind is none); `unavailable` missing
    is read as true - unsure, kept a minute - as A1's answers are (the web reads it `=== true`; the route always sends
    it, so only a broken answer differs).
  - `of(_:)` (descriptionOf): the paragraph only with words and a source the app knows (`wikipedia`, `lastfm` - the
    route names Navidrome's words `lastfm` too, their link Last.fm's page), the subtitle trimmed as the web trims; nil -
    no block - with neither. `link(_:_:)` (linkFits): Last.fm's by A1's `LastfmLink.checked`; Wikipedia's https on
    `en.wikipedia.org` exactly (`percentEncodedHost`, so no escaped host passes), printable ASCII, no `\` or `@`, at
    most `LastfmLink.most` letters - a link that doesn't fit is dropped, the words kept (after review: no name or
    password before the host, rather than no `@`, and Wikipedia's credit kept as words - `credited(_:)`). `url(_:)` is
    the one URL the App opens.
  - `Ask`: only what the route takes - `mbid` by `MBID.of`, Navidrome's id 1 to `idMost` (256, the route's ID_MAX)
    letters - each sent only when there is one (an empty `mbid=` is the route's 422), none at all with neither (its
    NEEDS_AN_ID); `key` the kind and both ids.
  - `Question` (`unsettled`, `nothing`, `ask`) and the two pages' rules: `artist(...)` - nothing for an artist gone;
    unsettled until Navidrome's answer, then while who they are on MusicBrainz may still come from the library's
    folders (`indexKnown`, or the albums' own wait, `SearchPacing.ownedWaitMs`), then, with an mbid, until MusicBrainz's
    facts have settled (answered or not: the web's ArtistPage asks after its facts, and the server's Wikipedia side
    makes that same lookup); `album(...)` - nothing for an album gone (`gone || goneButHere`), unsettled until the album
    is in hand and, with a pressing to look up, while the library's folders haven't answered nor been waited for; the
    release group the first of `OwnedIndex.forRelease`'s folders that names one.
  - `Kept` (keptDescription / keepDescription): the session's answers by `Ask.key`, the 200 most recently used
    (`kept`), one unsure only `unsureKeptMs` (60 s); and each page's last question (rememberPageKey). `Showing`
    (useDescription): what a page draws, for which page - the session's answer at once, else its own ask's; while the
    question changes what it drew stays until a new answer replaces it; a page come back to while its ids settle draws
    the answer of its last question. `asks(_:kept:now:)`: the Ask to send, or nil when there is none or one is kept.
- `AboutWords.swift` (new): `heading` "About", `more`, `less`, `source(_:)` ("From Wikipedia", "More on Last.fm"),
  `spoken(_:)` - the heading, the subtitle and every word, VoiceOver's one label (after review: no heading - it is a
  header of its own - and Wikipedia's credit when it is words; `moreWords` "More…" added).
- `Routes.describeArtist` and `.describeAlbum` (114 routes now), each given 120 s (`artistFacts`'s: a
  description is a MusicBrainz lookup with its ten attempts, then Wikidata and Wikipedia at 8 s each, and the server
  bounds none of it but Last.fm's 4 s; nothing waits for the block). `DeadwaxClient.describe(_:)` picks the route by
  the kind.

**App:**
- `Models/AboutModel.swift` (new): one per page, ArtistPageModel's `about` and AlbumModel's. `ask(page:person:question:
  client:online:)` draws what the session has at once and - online, with a question settled and nothing kept - asks.
  The session is static and one person's (another's begins it again); one ask out per key, shared by every page
  asking it and never called off, its answer kept when it comes (a failure as none, unsure) for the person who asked;
  each ask takes the next number and only the newest lands. Offline nothing is asked: a kept answer draws, else nothing.
- `Shared/AboutSection.swift` (new): `AboutSection`, the phone's (the heading, the words, 20 above); `AboutBlockView`,
  the one VoiceOver element every page draws through (`.accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)`, the label
  `AboutWords.spoken`, More or Less and the link as actions; opened only for the words it was opened for - after
  review, the words alone are the element, `AboutSpoken`, the heading outside it);
  `AboutWordsView` (the subtitle, the paragraph at `AboutBlock.lines` with the whole measured unseen behind it so More
  shows only when the words run past four lines, and the foot of More / Less and the link - side by side, stacked at
  the accessibility sizes, the link up to three lines there); `AboutFaces` - the phone's (`.phone`) the only place the
  phone's sizes are named, each Mac page passing its own (the link's face named `credit`: test_ios_no_web_app.py
  refuses an argument labelled `link:` anywhere but Core's AlbumInfo); `AboutDrawn`, the spaces.
- The phone's artist page (ArtistView): `aboutQuestion` from the page's answer, its mbid (said, or chosen with Which
  artist is this?) and `model.factsSettled(for:)` (ArtistPageModel's new `factsFor`: the mbid whose facts settled, set
  only when the facts' task wasn't let go); `aboutKey` = `taskKey|` the question's token `|online`, its `.task(id:)`;
  About after Similar Artists, drawn once nothing above is held (`!arrival.holding`), before A1's foot line.
- The phone's album page (AlbumView): `aboutQuestion` from the album, its `musicBrainzId` and `search.ownedIndex` (the

- The Mac's artist page (MacArtistPage): after Similar Artists, `aboutSection` - the page's own `sectionHead` and the

- The Mac's album page (MacAlbumPage): under Properties, a `MacGroupBox` titled About, as Properties is. (Corrected

  `A4_PAGES` (AboutSection.swift).

### Decisions, and where this departs from the plan

- **The album's release group** is the first of `OwnedIndex.forRelease`'s folders that names one (the plan's
  `.first?.releaseGroupMbid`): a first folder without one doesn't hide a later one's.
- **The album page waits for the library's folders** before asking - the plan didn't say. (After review: the bridge's
  group first, and the folders' waited for until their ask ends; the first version waited 1.5 s and could draw
  Navidrome's words, then another's in their place - "After review".) An album no folder names a group for is asked by
  Navidrome's id alone, for good.
- **The artist page asks once MusicBrainz's facts have settled** (the web's way): the server's Wikipedia side makes the
  same lookup, so it is served from the server's cache rather than racing it.
- **Drawn only once nothing above it is held** on the artist page (A2's `arrival.holding`): the foot never stands under
  Play while the albums wait.
- **A failure is none, unsure**: no block, no words for it, kept a minute so Back draws at once and it is asked again
  soon - the plan's "absent with no words".
- **No header trait** on the element: the rule is one element per row, the heading inside its label, so VoiceOver's
  headings rotor won't stop on About. (Reversed after review: the heading is its own element, a header, outside the
  words' one - "After review".)
- **Not on the pages of what you don't have** (a MusicBrainz artist's page, an album you don't have): 3.9 names the
  artist page and the album page. docs/ios.md's line on Search's artist page "without their description" still holds.

keys in each.)

### After review

The coordinator's review of the first version (e3d8dc88) found seven things. Each is fixed in this one commit; where a
line above said otherwise it is corrected where it stands.

1. **The Mac album page squeezed About to a line, and More made its words vanish** (high). The page doesn't scroll and
   its songs' box has `.layoutPriority(1)`; About's four lines had no height of their own (their least one line), and
   opened, the ViewThatFits fell back to a ScrollView whose least is 0. The reviewer's probe at a 662-point page: with
   8, 12 or 20 songs the closed paragraph 16 points, More showing even for short words; opened, 0; at a 442-point page
   the songs' box 18. What was decided, for the Mac album page alone (the phone and the Mac's artist page are as they
   were):
   - **The four lines are fixed at their height** (`.fixedSize(horizontal: false, vertical: true)` on the block) and
     never grow in place. `AboutBlockView` takes `opens`: given, More does that instead of opening the words where they
     stand (and no Less). Its foot is always drawn under the words on that page (`AboutFaces.footLeast`, MacLook's
     small button, 22), so the block's height never waits on whether More shows - the measure - and the page's choice
     can't turn on it.
   - **More opens the whole words in a popover** (`AboutWhole` in AboutSection.swift, in the page's faces: the
     subtitle, every word - selectable - and the credit, 440 wide and 16 in, scrolling inside past 360). It is
     presented through Presenting.swift's new `appPopover` (`CarriedPopover`: the app's models carried on the Mac as a
     sheet's page is, its going said on `appPresentationGone` as it disappears - SwiftUI's popover has no onDismiss);
     test_ios_mac.py's list of SwiftUI presentations in Presenting.swift now ends in `popover`, five carried.
   - **The songs' box's least always wins.** About is `.layoutPriority(2)`, laid out before the box in what the box's
     least leaves: `ViewThatFits(in: .vertical)` of the block and one row - "About" as MacGroupBox's legend draws it,
     and **More…** (`AboutWords.moreWords`) opening the same popover. The box's least is taken less the row's height
     (`aboutLeast`: `MacAlbumAboutDrawn.rowTall`, 12 + 22 = 34, while there is an About), never About's drawn height
     (`aboutTall` is gone) - so the row is never pushed off the page nor drawn a sliver, and never 0.
   - **The arithmetic** (tests/test_ios_lastfm_a4.py's `test_the_mac_album_page_keeps_the_songs_least_and_about_on_it`,
     with tests/ios_fonts.py's faces): the block 22 + 14 + the subtitle's line at 12 (14.54) + 6 + four lines at 13
     (63.02) + 6 + 22 + 12 = 159.6; the row 34; around the box 54 (20 + 16 + 18), the hero 132, Properties 100 or 112.
     At the opening window's 662 (room 364-376) the box's least is untouched (114, 144, 180) and the block is offered
     184 to 262: the four lines at every Row Size, with 3 songs or 20. At the smallest window's 442 (room 144-156) the
     block never fits: the row, and the box's least 110 to 122. **A judgement**: the row is counted as Properties is, so
     at Small with four-line Properties the least stays 114, but at Medium and Large - whose least was 144-156 there
     before About - the songs give up to 34 for it (110-122).
   - **Probed**: the same stack (the hero, the box at its least and its whole with priority 1, Properties, About with
     priority 2 as ViewThatFits of the fixed block and the row, in the bundled faces) laid out by SwiftUI on this Mac
     (swiftc, ImageRenderer at 1x; scratch only, never committed - as "The letter bar beats momentum" did), every
     frame read: at 662 the block (161 tall - each line rounded to a whole point at 1x; 159.5 at 2x) at every size,
     3 or 20 songs, the box at or over its least (116 to 215); at 442 the row (34) and the box at its least (110-122,

3. **The album page could draw one answer, then replace it** (medium-low). Now:
   - The release group is the id bridge's first (`storeGroup`: `AlbumModel.store?.releaseGroupMbid`, the web's own
     source - AlbumPage.tsx asks once `storeFor` says the bridge has answered). **My addition**: with the bridge asked
     (a library of your own), the album counts as answered only once the bridge's word is in - `AlbumModel.bridgeSettled`
     (answered, failed, or not asked) - else the folders' group could draw and the bridge's replace it.
   - Without the bridge's group, the library's folders': the page holds unsettled while `/library/owned` is out -
     `ownedSettled`, SearchModel's new `ownedAnswers` (one more at each end of its ask: answered, the same as before, or
     failed - counted after the index it brings, in the same turn) against the count when the page asked
     (`ownedSince`). Asked by Navidrome's id alone only once it has answered without one, or failed. No fixed wait
     (`ownedWaited` and its sleep are gone from the album page; the artist page keeps its own, as decided).
   - `refreshOwned()` again as deadwax comes back (`ownedKey`: the page, online, and whether there is a client).
   - Core's `album(answered:gone:navidromeId:release:storeGroup:index:ownedSettled:)`, and the sequence tested:
     `theAlbumPageDrawsOneAnswerNeverTwo` - opened cold with `/library/owned` out longer than the old 1.5 s, the
     bridge's group in hand, and the folders' ask failing - each draws one answer and asks once.
4. **Tests that let mutations pass**: `eachQuestionHasATokenOfItsOwn` (each question's token its own, an ask's its key);
   `clamped = height measure()` and `whole = height measure()` pinned exactly, once each; both Mac About views
   compared whole (the artist page's `.padding(.horizontal, Drawn.side)` and `.padding(.bottom, Drawn.below)`, the album
   page's `.padding(.top, Drawn.propertiesAbove)` and its row).
5. **VoiceOver's headings rotor skipped About** (`.ignore` swallowed the heading's `.isHeader`). `AboutSpoken`, a
   ViewModifier, makes the words alone the one element - their label, More / Less and the link as actions - before the
   page's frame lays its heading beside them (`AboutWordsElement`), so ArtistSectionHead's, the Mac artist page's
   sectionHead's, MacGroupBox's legend and the row's heading keep their header trait. `AboutWords.spoken` no longer
   says "About" (it is read as the heading). Both devices.
6. **The `@` refusal on Wikipedia links**: a name or password before the host is refused (`parts.user == nil,
   parts.password == nil`), not every `@` - "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/@Home" passes; "https://en.wikipedia.org@
   evil.com/..." is still refused by the exact host and "https://someone@en.wikipedia.org/..." by the userinfo. With no
   usable link, Wikipedia's credit is drawn as plain words in the second colour (`AboutBlock.credited`, AboutCredit's
   Text - LastfmCredit's way), and read in the words' label, so its attribution never goes; Last.fm's credit only with
   its link (Navidrome's words come as `lastfm` and may be Deezer's, so "More on Last.fm" with nowhere to go would say
   the wrong thing).
7. **docs/ios.md** said Navidrome's words "are Last.fm's too"; they may be Deezer's (lastfm.md 2.8, describe.ts). It
   says so now, and that the link names only where it goes.

Words changed after review (iphone.json and mac.json, by hand, the same in each): `AboutWords.spoken` - "1994 studio
album by Portishead, Dummy is the debut album by Portishead." (no heading); `AboutWords.moreWords` "More…" added.
DeviceWordsTests adds it.

## The Library's line underlines what is chosen (27 Nov)

James, on the phone: **"on iOS in library, it's not immediately clear which of 'yours' or 'all' is selected, and most
others in that row. Ideas for improving that?"** The design session (App Design) showed him three ways
(~/Desktop/Code/deadwax-plans/mac-redesign/iLibraryLine.dc.html, kept for the record) and he chose the first: **"Yeah I
like the underline"**. The design is iphone-redesign.md's "Changed 27 Nov: the Library's line underlines what is
chosen", dw.css's new block (`.meta .opt`, `.opt.on`, `.opt svg`, `.pair`, and `.said`, option C's - copied into
ios/design/dw.css whole, at its end: the canvas has the credits block before it, which this copy doesn't yet), drawn on
iLibrary, iArtists and iPlaylists. It supersedes R2b's "white is where you are and purple is what a tap goes to".

What is his and what is the design session's: the underline is his choice of the three. The rest - grey until chosen,
the switch's own line, "a purple line means chosen; purple words mean a link" as one rule for the phone, the hairline
gone, the sizes - is the design session's, drawn and sent with the choice.

Built on the ios branch at b51a90a5. The app is still 0.13 (13), `__version__` untouched, no project change, no engine
file touched. Other slices ran beside it (the Library's top into iOS's navigation bar, the album, artist and
release-group bars, Speed A's models): none of their files is touched here - LibraryView.swift, LibraryTop.swift, Core's
TopClearance and DebugModel are as they were.

### What was built

**A choice** (`LineChoice`, LibraryLine.swift - `.meta .opt`): each of Grid, List, Yours and All. Until it is chosen, in
the line's third colour (DWPalette.t3, `--t3`, the count's own grey); chosen, white (DWPalette.text) over the accent's
2 pt line - and a word semibold too (`.opt.on`'s 600; a glyph's weight is the same either way, as the drawing's stroke
is). 3 either side of its words or glyph (the line as wide as the two, as `.opt.on`'s inset shadow is), 28 tall at
least, the line at its foot; 13 pt words (Typeface.Phone `.meta`, `.opt`'s font-size). A glyph is the same SF Symbol as
before (`square.grid.2x2`, `list.bullet`, medium) in a box 17 at least (`.opt svg`), where it had a 28 pt square -
since the review fitted to the drawing's ink (`resizable`, `scaledToFit`, a frame of PhoneLook.optInk's 12.75 scaled
with the line's words), so the box is what the line holds; on the Mac its own 13 pt symbol, as before (see "After
review").

**The line under it is the switch's own** - `DWChosenLine` (DWSegmented.swift), the overlay R1c drew inline in
DWSegmented's phone segment, now a ViewModifier of its own: the accent's DWFlat.chosenLine at the foot, hidden from
VoiceOver. DWSegmented's phone segment and LibraryLineEnd's choices both take it, so there is one lit line, not a
second drawn for the line. (PhoneStrip and Sources' strip still draw their own copy of it inline, as R1c and R7 left
them: outside this change.) It is NOT phone-only, as the first pass had it: the Mac's offline Library draws the line
(see "The Mac"), so DWChosenLine is in DWSegmented's pinned Mac half, re-pinned (see "After review").

**Pairs** (`.meta .pair`): Grid and List one pair, Yours and All the other, the two of a pair 6 apart, each choice
holding its half of that 6 inside its target (as PhoneStrip's words hold half their gap), so every point of a pair
answers a tap and the pair is as wide as drawn. **No hairline between Yours and All**: DWPalette.metaRule, PhoneLook's
sidesGap and sidesRule and the hairline's @ScaledMetric are gone. Grid and List's pair is 14 before Yours | All, on the
line's own 6, only where Yours | All follows.

**Purple words** are only the order with its caret (PhoneMetaLink, a Menu's label) and Playlists' New playlist… - as
they were; nothing in the line's end names the accent now.

**Nothing else in the line moved**: PhoneMeta, its four ways and its Layout are R2b's review's (a doc comment aside);
the count and the order lead, Grid and List then Yours | All trail; the callers (AlbumsScreen, ArtistsScreen,
PlaylistsScreen, SongsScreen) are unchanged.

**The sizes, as tokens** (PhoneLook, Core): `opt` 28 (`.meta .opt height`), `optPadding` 3 (`.opt padding-left`),
`optGlyph` 17 (`.opt svg width`), `optInk` 12.75 (drawn: the svgs' ink, after review), `pairGap` 6 (`.pair gap`),
`pairAfter` 14 (drawn: iLibrary's first `.pair`'s inline `margin-right: 14px` - in PHONE_FROM_DRAWINGS beside `meta`,
`metaTrail` and `optInk`). `meta` stays 32 and `metaGap` 6. They replace R2b's metaGlyph 28, metaGlyphGap 2,
metaGlyphsAfter 10, sidesGap 10 and sidesRule 12.

**VoiceOver**: as before - Grid and List each a button, the shown one selected; Yours | All a group, "Your library or
all music", the side shown selected. The line is decoration and never heard; the chosen one is also white where the
others are grey, and a word semibold.

### The fold

The line gives way inside itself exactly as R2b's review made it (MetaLine: one line, the count's noun dropped, then its
end folded, then folded with the noun dropped - PhoneMeta's ViewThatFits of the four, measured as drawn). What moves is
the end's width. Core's new `MetaLine.end(_:)` says it from its choices' own widths: each choice plus 3 either side, a
pair's two 6 apart, the pairs 6 + 14 apart, no pair with nothing in it - what LibraryLineEnd's HStacks draw (PhoneMeta
measures the real thing; `end` is for the arithmetic, as `fit` is). DWLookTests holds it
(`aQuietLinesEndIsItsChoicesAtTheirSpacing`, `aQuietLineFoldsAtItsNewEnd`), and test_ios_library_look.py holds Core's
body word for word and does the arithmetic with it.

In the bundled faces, with the glyphs in their box of 17 (the symbols fitted to the drawing's ink since the review,
so nothing here is a guess at a symbol's width): Albums' end is 142.5 where R2b's was 147.5 at the standard size (150.6
of 155.6 at xLarge) - each glyph's choice 23 where its box was 28, Grid and List 6 apart where they were 2, 20 before
Yours where they were 16, and 3 less for the hairline's room. Every other page's end (Yours | All alone) is 3 narrower
(70.5 of 73.5). Eight cells of R2b's tables moved, all on Albums' line with Yours | All, every one toward one line:

| size | count | order | R2b (375 / 393 / 402) | now |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| standard | 140 albums | Year, newest first | S S F | S **F** F |
| standard | 2318 albums | Year, newest first | S S S | S S **F** |
| standard | 12 of 2318 albums | Recently added | f S S | **S** S S |
| standard | 1234 of 2318 albums | Artist | S F F | **F** F F |
| standard | 1234 of 2318 albums | Recently added | f f S | f **S** S |
| standard | 1234 of 2318 albums | Year, newest first | f f f | f f **S** |
| xLarge | 140 albums | Year, newest first | f S S | **S** S S |
| xLarge | 12 of 2318 albums | Artist | S S F | S **F** F |

(F one line, S the count's noun dropped, f folded; two of them - 1234 of 2318 under "Recently added" at the standard
size, 140 under the longest at xLarge - back to what R2b's Noto Sans drew.) So at the standard size a library's count
still never folds the line on any of the three phones under any order; Find's count never folds it on 402 under any
order (R2b: but for a four-figure find under the longest); on 393 only a four-figure find under a Year order does (R2b:
under "Recently added" too); on 375, under "Recently added" only a four-figure find (R2b: any find in a four-figure
library), under "Year, oldest first" a four-figure library's, and under the longest every find, as R2b's. The other pages never fold at the standard size or at xLarge, as
before; folded, every end fits a line of its own at every size.

(The first pass, a1e16198, took the glyphs at 1.3 of the body's 17, the symbol drawn at its own size: its end was
152.7, and its seven moved cells all moved the other way. The review found that a guess: an SF Symbol at that size is
some 18-20 of ink, so the box never bound and the line's width was the guess's - at 1.2 four of the seven would not
have moved.)

### Departures from the brief and the drawing

- **The line is 32, not 34.** The brief said 34; iLibraryLine's sketches of the three ways draw `.meta` 34, but
  iLibrary, iArtists and iPlaylists - where the design says it is drawn - still draw 32, and the design says nothing
  else in the line moves. A 28 pt choice sits in 32 with 2 above and below.
- **"14 between the pairs" is 20 between the pairs' boxes**: the drawing's 14 is the first pair's margin in the line's
  flex row, whose own gap of 6 comes on top of it, so a browser draws 20 (R2b read `.views`' margin-right 10 the same
  way: 16). Between the glyph's ink and "Yours", about 28.
- **A glyph is fitted to the drawing's ink, not its own size** (after review): the symbol `resizable`, `scaledToFit`
  in a frame of 12.75 (PhoneLook.optInk) scaled with the line's words, in its box of 17 - its choice 23, as the
  drawing's is. The ink is the box's until xxxLarge, the line's cap, where it is 18.6 and the box grows to hold it
  (lookSquare a minimum on the phone), never cut. A resizable symbol keeps its weight (medium) and scales its stroke
  with it, as the drawing's stroke of 2 scales with its svg.
- **The pair's 6 is inside the targets**, half each - the drawing has no targets.
- The drawing writes VoiceOver's label "Grid, chosen" on the chosen glyph; the app says "Grid" with the selected trait,
  as every other choice in the app.

### The Mac

The Mac's own Library pages (MacAlbumsPage, MacArtistsPage, MacPlaylistsPage) draw neither PhoneMeta nor LibraryLineEnd,
and change nothing. Its Library root borrows the phone's pager in two places (LibraryView's `desk` is nil there): the
Songs page, whose line is PhoneMeta with the count alone - LibraryLineEnd(.songs, sides: nil) is empty, Yours | All
never showing on the Mac (`!Platform.mac && LibraryPages.sides(...)`) - so it is as it was; and the root's Downloaded
albums while deadwax can't be reached (LibraryRootList's `.downloaded` - LibraryView's `pager` passes no desk for it,
so AlbumsScreen draws the phone's page and its LibraryLineEnd), whose line ends in Grid and List: those take the new
look there too (grey, the chosen one white over the lit line, 6 apart), each its own 13 pt symbol as before, in its box
of 17 exactly (lookSquare is exact on the Mac), so 23 wide where they were 28. So the Mac draws DWChosenLine: the
first pass had it phone-only in test_ios_mac_halves.py and the Mac's half of DWSegmented pinned unchanged, which the
review found wrong - it is in the Mac's half now, re-pinned (see "After review").

### After review (27 Nov)

The review found no functional bug, but three things the tests claimed that the code didn't bear out:

1. **DWChosenLine is not phone-only.** Offline, the Mac's Library shows the Downloaded albums: LibraryView's `pager`
   passes no desk for `.downloaded`, so AlbumsScreen draws the phone's page, whose LibraryLineEnd's LineChoice takes
   DWChosenLine. It is out of test_ios_mac_halves.py's PHONE_ONLY, and DWSegmented's Mac half re-pinned on purpose:
   a804e4bbec16c8f3 (computed here, as the review had it), where 8d680fda0b85a713 was the switch's Mac half alone -
   unchanged, the difference DWChosenLine's.
2. **The glyphs drawn as the drawing draws them, so the tables stop resting on a guess.** The drawing's 17 px svg has
   12.75 of ink (its paths run 4 to 20 of the viewBox's 24, the stroke of 2 square-capped: 3 to 21). The symbol drawn
   at the body's size was some 18-20 of ink, so the 17 box never bound and the glyph's width was the test's guess
   (1.3 of 17) alone. Now PhoneLook.optInk 12.75 (drawn: held by PHONE_FROM_DRAWINGS, and worked out from the paths
   and dw.css's `.opt svg` stroke by test_ios_library_look.py), and the phone's symbol `resizable`, `scaledToFit` in a
   frame of it, a @ScaledMetric relative to the line's own words (Typeface.Phone `.meta`, the footnote): the box of 17
   binds at every size to xxLarge (16.7), and at xxxLarge, the line's cap, the ink is 18.6 and the box grows to it
   rather than cut it. The tables are recomputed from the bound box ("The fold"), and the test's SYMBOL and BODY are
   gone. The Mac's offline line keeps its own 13 pt symbol (`if Platform.mac`), in its exact box of 17.
3. **Stale words**: test_ios_library_look.py's docstring still said R2b's "white where you are and purple what a tap goes
   to"; it says what is drawn now.
